translation.quality: The source edition describes its English as machine-assisted and post-edited and cautions that errors may remain. These passages were extracted from the al-Tabari-labeled sections; they have not been independently checked against the Arabic.

x: What he meant by his saying, may his praise be glorified:
h
Disavowal from God and His Messenger
, is that this is
h
disavowal from God and His Messenger

. So, Baraa'ah is raised by an omitted word, which is (this), just as His statement: A Surah We have revealed (al-Nur 24:1) is raised by an omitted word, which is (this). If someone were to say: Baraa'ah is raised by the pronoun from its mention in His statement:
h
To those with whom you made a treaty
, and make it like a definite noun, raising what comes after it, since it had become, with its connection, which is His statement:
h
From God and His Messenger
, like a definite noun, and the meaning of the statement became: Baraa'ah
h
from God and His Messenger
h
to those with whom you made a treaty

from the polytheists, it would be a doctrine whose validity is not proven, even though the first statement is more pleasing to me, because it is the custom of the Arabs to imply for every thing witnessed, whether it is indefinite or definite, that thing witnessed, (this) and (this), so they say when they witness a good thing: (Good, by God), and an ugly thing: (Ugly, by God), meaning: This is good, by God, and this is ugly, by God, so I chose the first statement.
He said: A declaration of immunity
h
from God and His Messenger

to those with whom you have made a treaty, meaning to those with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty among the polytheists, because the treaties between the Muslims and the polytheists were a treaty between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one was responsible for concluding them except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or someone who made them by his command. However, he addressed the believers with this because they knew its meaning, and the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, treaties with his nation were their treaties, because they were satisfied with all his actions toward them, and they were Muslims with his treaties with them. So his treaty with them became like their treaties with themselves. Therefore, he said: To those with whom you have made a treaty among the polytheists, because it was a treaty and a covenant between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

The people of interpretation differed about whom God and His Messenger declared innocent of the covenant that was between him and the Messenger of God from the polytheists, so He permitted him to travel the earth for four months.

Some of them said: They are two types of polytheists: One of them had a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of less than four months, and he was given four months to travel. The other of them had an unspecified covenant, so he limited it to four months to explore for himself, and then he is at war after that with God, His Messenger, and the believers, and he is killed wherever he is found and taken prisoner, unless he repents.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, as a leader of the Hajj in the year nine, to establish the Hajj for the people, and the people of polytheism to their places of Hajj. Abu Bakr and the Muslims who were with him went out, and Surah Bara’ah was revealed to break the covenant between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists that they had made between him and them: that no one who came to the House should be prevented from entering it, and that no one should be afraid during the sacred month. This was a general covenant between him and the people of polytheism. And between that, there were covenants between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some tribes of the Arabs, specific to a specified term, so it was revealed about him and about those hypocrites who stayed behind from him in Tabuk, and according to the saying of some of them, God revealed in it the secrets of people who were hiding things other than what they showed, some of whom were named to us, and some of whom were not named to us, so He said:
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

, meaning: to the people of the general covenant from the polytheists of the Arabs, so travel freely in the land for four months, until His saying: Indeed, God is free from the polytheists and His Messenger, meaning: after this argument.

Others said: Rather, God Almighty granted a four-month reprieve to those polytheists who had a treaty with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). As for those who did not have a treaty with the Messenger of God, their term was fifty nights, which is twenty days of Dhul-Hijjah and the entire month of Muharram. They said: This was only the case because the term of those who had no treaty was until the end of the sacred months, as God said: And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). They said: The call to disavow was on the day of the greater Hajj, which was the Day of Surat al-Tawbah 9:1
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

. Sacrifice according to some people, and according to others the Day of Arafah, which was fifty days. They said: As for the postponement of the four months, it was only for the people of the treaty between them and the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) from the day Bara'ah was revealed.

They said: It was revealed at the beginning of Shawwal, so the end of their term was the end of the sacred months. Some of those who say this article say: The beginning of the postponement was for both groups one - I mean the one who had a covenant and the one who did not have a covenant - except that the term of the one who had a covenant was four months, and the one who did not have a covenant was the expiration of the sacred months, which is the expiration of Muharram.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

. So travel freely through the land for four months,” he said: God set a limit for those who made a treaty with His Messenger of four months, during which they may travel wherever they wish, and He set a deadline for those who do not have a treaty, which is the expiration of the sacred months from the Day of Sacrifice until the expiration of Muharram, so that is fifty nights.
h
So when the sacred months have passed
, He commands him to lay down the sword against those who have made a treaty.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When A declaration of freedom from God was revealed, up to And that God will disgrace the disbelievers, he said: A declaration of freedom from the polytheists who had a treaty with them on the day A declaration of freedom was revealed, so he made the period of those who had a treaty with them before A declaration of freedom was revealed, four months, and he ordered them to travel the earth for four months. And he made the period of the polytheists who had no covenant before Bara’ah was revealed, the passing of the sacred months, and the passing of the sacred months from the day Bara’ah was announced until the passing of Muharram, and they are fifty nights: twenty of Dhul-Hijjah, and thirty of Muharram, And when the sacred months have passed, until His saying: And sit in wait for them at every place of ambush, meaning: no covenant or protection remained for any of the polytheists since Bara’ah was revealed and the sacred months had passed, and the period of those who had a covenant from the polytheists before Bara’ah was revealed, is four months from the day Bara’ah was announced until ten of the first of Rabi’ al-Akhir, so that is four months.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about the verse: A declaration of immunity
h
from God and His Messenger

to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, before A declaration of immunity was revealed, he made a treaty with some of the polytheists from Mecca and others, so this was revealed: A declaration of immunity from God to everyone of the polytheists who had made a treaty with you. I will break the treaty that was between you and them, so I will grant them a four-month reprieve to travel wherever they wish on earth in safety. And the reprieve for those who had no treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the passing of the sacred months, from the day the declaration of immunity was announced, and it was announced on the Day of Sacrifice, so the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah and the Muharram were thirty, so that is fifty nights. So God commanded His Prophet when the Muharram was over to put the sword on those who had no treaty with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killing them until they entered Islam. And He commanded those who had a treaty when four days had passed from the Day of Sacrifice to put the sword on them also, killing them until they entered Islam. The period of those who had no covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was fifty nights from the Day of Sacrifice, and the period of those who had a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was four months: from the Day of Sacrifice until the tenth of the month of Rabiʿ al-Akhir.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Disavowal from God and His Messenger

, to his statement: And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment, he said: It was mentioned to us that Ali called the call to prayer, and ordered Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on them both, to lead the pilgrimage. And it was the year in which the Muslims and the polytheists performed the pilgrimage, and the polytheists did not perform the pilgrimage after that year. His statement:
h
Those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty
, to his statement:
h
Until their term

, he said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty at the time of Hudaybiyyah, and there were four months left of their term after the Day of Sacrifice, and God commanded His Prophet to fulfill their treaty
h
until their term

, and whoever had no treaty, the month of Muharram was over, and he threw away his treaty to everyone with a treaty, and he commanded that they be fought until they testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and nothing but that would be accepted from them.

x: Others said: The beginning of the delay of the polytheists was four months and its end for all of them was at the same time. They said: Its beginning was the day of the greater pilgrimage and its end was the end of the tenth of Rabiʿ al-Akhir.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: A declaration of immunity
h
from God and His Messenger

to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, he said: When this verse was revealed, he was absolved from the treaty of every polytheist, and no one made a treaty except those who had made a treaty, and he extended the duration of each one, So travel freely throughout the land for four months, for whoever had made a treaty in it, from the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal, and the ten days of Rabi’ al-Akhir.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others told us:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr as a leader of the Hajj season in the year nine, and he sent Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them both, with thirty or forty verses from Bara’ah, and he recited it to the people, giving the polytheists four months to roam the earth. So he recited Bara’ah to them on the Day of Arafah. The polytheists were given a period of twenty days from Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabiʿ Al-Awwal, and ten days from Rabiʿ Al-Akhir. He recited it to them in their homes and said: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.
b.via: Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So travel freely throughout the land for four months, twenty of Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten of Rabi' al-Akhir. That was their covenant that was made between them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Disclaimer
h
from God and His Messenger

, to the people of the treaty: Khuza’ah, Mudlij, and whoever had a treaty from them or others. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came from Tabuk when he had finished, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to perform Hajj, but he said: The polytheists will be present and will circumambulate naked, so I do not wish to perform Hajj until that does not happen. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may God have mercy on them, to tour the people in Dhu al-Majaz, and in their places where they used to trade, and in all the seasons, and they gave permission to the people of the treaty to be safe for four months, which are the consecutive months: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until the tenth of the month of Rabi’ al-Akhir, then they would have no treaty. And he gave permission to all the people to fight unless they believe.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

, he said: The people of the treaty are Mudlij, and the Arabs with whom he made a treaty, and whoever had a treaty. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came from Tabuk when he finished it and wanted to perform Hajj, then he said: There are polytheists who are present at the House, circumambulating naked, so I do not want to be exposed until that does not happen. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may God have mercy on them, and they circumambulated the people in Dhu al-Majaz, and in their places where they used to trade, and in the entire season, and they gave permission to the people of the treaty to be safe for four months, which are the sacred months that come and go in succession: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until the tenth of the month of Rabiʿ al-Akhir, then they have no treaty. And he gave permission to all the people to fight unless they believe. So the people all believed at that time, and no one was able to do so. He said: When he returned from Taif, he immediately went and invaded Tabuk, after he had come to Medina.

x: Others who said: (The beginning of the term for all polytheists and its end was one) said: Its beginning was on the day that Bara’ah was revealed, and the end of the sacred months, which is the end of Muharram.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: Then travel freely throughout the land for four months. He said: It was revealed in Shawwal, so these four months are: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi’dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram.

x: Others said: God only postponed the four months for the polytheists in the tourism, for those who had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that lasted less than four months. As for those who had a treaty that lasted more than four months, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that his treaty be completed for its duration.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: Al-Kalbi said:
m: The four months were only for those who had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of less than four months, so he completed the four months for him. And whoever had a treaty of more than four months, he is the one who was commanded to complete his treaty for him, and He said: Fulfill their treaty with them
h
until their term
(al-Tawbah 9:4).

b.v: Abu Jaʿfar may God have mercy on him said:
x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: The term that God set for the polytheists with whom we have a treaty, and He permitted them to travel freely in it by saying: Then travel freely throughout the land for four months, is only for the people of the treaty who supported the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and broke their treaty before its expiration. As for those who did not break their treaty and did not support anyone against him, God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet (blessings and peace of God Surat al-Tawbah 9:1
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

. be upon him) to complete the treaty between him and them until its term by saying: “Except for those among the polytheists with whom you made a treaty and then they did not fail you in anything and did not support anyone against you.
So fulfill to them their treaty
h
until their term
. Indeed, God loves the righteous.” (al-Tawbah 9:4) If he thought that the statement of God Almighty:
h
So when the sacred months have passed

, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5) indicates the opposite of what we said about that, since that indicated that the obligation upon the believers was after the end of the sacred months to kill every polytheist, then the matter in that is contrary to what he thought, and that is because the verse that follows that shows the correctness of what we said, and the corruption of what he thought of the one who thought that the passing of the sacred months permitted the killing of every polytheist, whether he had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or did not have a treaty with him, and that is His statement: “
h
How can there be a treaty with God and with His Messenger
, except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram?

So as long as they are upright with you, be upright with them. Indeed, God loves those who fear Him” (al-Tawbah 9:7), then these are polytheists, and God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers to be upright with them in their treaty, as long as they are upright with them by not breaking their peace treaty and not supporting their enemy against them. And then, in the agreed upon reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “When he sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, with the declaration of innocence to the people of the covenants between him and them, he ordered him among what he ordered him to announce among them: And whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his covenant is for its term,” the clearest evidence for the correctness of what we said. That is because God did not order His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to break the covenant of a people with whom he had a covenant for a term and they adhered to their covenant by not breaking it, and that He only gave a four-month reprieve to whoever had broken his covenant before the postponement, or whoever had a covenant for an unlimited term.

As for whoever had a limited term for his covenant, and did not make it a way for himself to break it, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to fulfill his covenant until its end. And with that he sent his crier to announce it to the people of the season from the Arabs.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said, Muharrir ibn Abi Hurairah told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: I was with Ali, may God have mercy on him, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to call out. When his voice became hoarse, I called out. I said: What were you calling out? He said: Four things: No one should circumambulate the Kaaba naked, whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his covenant is valid for its term, none will enter Paradise except a believing soul, and no polytheist will be punished after this year of ours.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Affan told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Al-Muharrir bin Abi Hurairah told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: And whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then his covenant is until his term.

x: Shu’bah narrated this hadith, and he differed with Qais regarding the term.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, they said: Uthman bin Umar told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Muharrir bin Abi Hurairah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I was with Ali when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him with the declaration of innocence to the people of Mecca, and I was calling until my voice became hoarse. I said: What were you calling? He said: We were ordered to call out: None will enter Paradise except a believer, and whoever has a treaty between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then his term is four months, and when the term comes, then God and His Messenger are free from the polytheists, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House, and no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year.

x: I fear that this report may be a mistake on the part of its transmitter regarding the term, because the report is consistent regarding the term to the contrary, along with the disagreement of Qais Shu’bah regarding this same hadith, as I have explained.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith al-A’war, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God have mercy on him, who said: I was commanded to do four things: I was commanded that no polytheist should approach the House after this year, that no man should circumambulate the House naked, that no one should enter Paradise except every Muslim soul, and that everyone who has a covenant should fulfill his covenant.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid ibn Yathi’, who said:
m: “‘Bara’ah’ was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent it to Abu Bakr, then he sent Ali to take it from him. When Abu Bakr returned, he said: ‘Has it been revealed about something? ’ He said: ‘No, but I have been ordered to deliver it, myself or a man from my family. ’ So he set out for Mecca, and he decreed four things among them: that no polytheist should enter Mecca after this year, that no one should circumambulate the Ka’bah naked, that no one should enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and that whoever had a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his covenant would last for its term.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me when Bara’ah was revealed, with four things: that no naked person should circumambulate the House, and no polytheist should approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs, and whoever has a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it shall remain until its term, and none shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul.

c: Ibn Wakiʿiq told us, he said, Ibn Abd al-Aʿla told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God have mercy on him, he said: I sent four things to the people of Mecca, then he mentioned the hadith.

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us, Hussain bin Muhammad told us, Sulayman bin Qarm told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr with the declaration of innocence, then he sent Ali after him and took it from him. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, has something happened? He said: No, you are my companion in the cave and at the pool, and no one will carry it out on my behalf except me or Ali! And what Ali sent with was four things: none will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, no one will circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is until its term.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Aamer, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, and he announced: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, no naked person shall circumambulate the House, and no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, then his term shall be until its term, and God is innocent of the polytheists and His Messenger.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Husayn ibn ʿAli, he said:
m: “When Baraʿah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, to perform Hajj for the people, it was said to him: O Messenger of God, why don’t you send to Abu Bakr! He said: No one will perform it on my behalf except a man from my family! Then he called ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, and said: Bring out this story from the beginning of Baraʿah, and announce to the people on the Day of Sacrifice when they gather in Mina: No disbeliever will enter Paradise, no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, no naked person will circumambulate the House, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it will last until its term. So ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, went out on the Messenger of God’s she-camel, al-ʿAdhbaʿ, until he caught up with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq on the road. When Abu Bakr saw him, he said: Is he a leader or someone commanded? He said: Someone commanded. Then they went, may God have mercy on them both, and Abu Bakr performed Hajj for the people. And the Arabs at that time in that year were at their stations of Hajj that they had been in during the Jahiliyyah. Then, when the Day of Sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, stood up and announced to the people what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had commanded him to do. He said: O people, none shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul. After this year, no polytheist shall perform Hajj, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Whoever had a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is his until its term. After that year, no polytheist performed Hajj, and no one circumambulated the House naked. Then they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was from “Bara’ah,” regarding those who were polytheists among the people of the general covenant and the people of the term until the appointed time.
b.via: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Husayn ibn ʿAli

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: “When these verses were revealed, up to the fortieth verse, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them with Abu Bakr and ordered him to perform the Hajj. When he set out and reached the tree of Dhu al-Hulayfah, Ali followed him and took them from him. Abu Bakr returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, has anything been revealed concerning me? He said: No, but no one but me or a man from me will convey it. Are you not satisfied, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave and that you are my companion at the Cistern? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God! So Abu Bakr set out with the Hajj, and Ali was calling to prayer with the declaration of innocence. On the Day of Eid al-Adha, he said: No polytheist shall approach the Sacred Mosque after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then his covenant is valid until its term. These are days of eating and drinking, and God does not admit anyone into Paradise except one who is a Muslim. They said: Surat al-Tawbah 9:1
h
A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty

. We are.” We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin except for stabbing and beating! So the polytheists returned, and blamed each other and said: What are you doing, since the Quraysh have become Muslims? So they became Muslims.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: I was commanded to do four things: that no polytheist should approach the House after this year, that no one should circumambulate the House naked, that no one should enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and that everyone who has a covenant should fulfill his covenant. Muammar said: And Qatada said the same.

x: These reports and similar ones have confirmed the truth of what we have said, and that the four-month period was only for those we have described. As for those whose covenant was for a known period, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers were not given a way to break it and support their enemies against them, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fulfilled his covenant for him until its period, based on God’s command to him to do so. And this is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent with it. As for the four months, they were more extended than those we mentioned. Their beginning was the day of the greatest punishment, and their end was the end of the tenth of Rabiʿ al-Akhir. So that was four consecutive months, in which the people of the covenant, whose situation we have described, were given the right to travel the earth, to go wherever they wished, and no Muslim would expose them to war, killing, or plunder.
If the matter is as you have described, then what is the meaning of His statement:
h
So when the sacred months have passed
, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). You know that their passing is like the passing of Muharram, and you claimed that the postponement of the people
h
from God and His Messenger
was four months, and that between the greatest day of Hajj and the passing of the sacred months is fifty days at most, so where are the fifty days in the four months?

The expiration of the sacred months was a term for those who had no covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the four months for those who had a covenant, either for an unlimited term, or for a limited term that he had broken, so by breaking it he became in the sense of someone whose betrayal was feared, so he deserved to be ostracized equally, except that he was given the right to prepare for himself and to explore for himself from the term of the four months. Do you not see that God says to the people of the four months, and describes them as people of a covenant: “
h
Disavowal from God and His Messenger

to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty. So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape God.” And He describes those for whom the expiration of the sacred months is a deadline, as people of polytheism, not people of a covenant, saying: And an announcement
h
from God and His Messenger

to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that God is disassociated from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. The verse, Except those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty.
The verse? Then He said:
h
So when the sacred months have passed

, kill the polytheists wherever you find them. So He commanded the killing of the polytheists with whom there is no covenant after the expiration of the sacred months, and the completion of the covenant of those with whom there is a covenant, if they have not broken their covenant by supporting the believers and introducing a deficiency in it upon them.
What is the evidence that the beginning of the postponement was on the day of the greater Hajj, and not that it was in Shawwal, as those who said that said?

Those who said that claimed that the postponement was from the time of the revelation of Bara’ah, and that cannot be correct, because the one for whom the period of travel was set for a limited time, if he does not know what was set for him, especially with a covenant that preceded it that was contrary to it, then it is like someone for whom that was not set, because if he does not know what he has in the period that was set for him and what he owes after its expiration, then he is as he was before the period that was set for him. And it is known that the people did not know what was set for them from that, except when the call to the season was made among them. And if that is the case, then it is correct that its beginning is what we said, and its expiration was what we described.

evidence.text: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr as a leader of the Hajj season in the year nine, and he sent Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them both, with thirty or forty verses from Bara’ah, and he recited it to the people, giving the polytheists four months to roam the earth.
He recited it to them in their homes and said: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.

x: As for his saying:
h
So travel freely in the land for four months
, he means: So travel in it, coming and going, safe and not afraid of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his followers.
So-and-so wandered the earth, wandering, traveling, and wandering. As for His statement:
h
And know that you will not cause failure to God

, He is saying to the people of the covenant, those who had a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the revelation of this verse: Know, O polytheists, that if you spread corruption in the land, and you chose that with your disbelief in God, over the acknowledgement of the Oneness of God and the belief in His Messenger, you will not cause failure to God, meaning: you will not cause failure to God by yourselves, because wherever you go and wherever you are on earth, you are in His grasp and authority. No minister will prevent you from Him, and nothing will come between you and Him if He intends for you a punishment that is either safe or secure, except belief in Him and in His Messenger, and repentance from disobeying Him.
He is saying: So hasten His punishment with repentance, and abandon the wandering that does not benefit you. As for his saying:
h
And that God will disgrace the disbelievers
, he says: Know that God will humiliate the disbelievers, and will cause them shame in this world and Hell in the Hereafter.
God Almighty says:
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger
to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage. We have explained the meaning of the call to prayer in the previous part of this book with its evidence.
And Sulayman bin Musa used to say about that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Sulayman ibn Musa Al-Shami claimed that his statement:
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger

, he said: (The announcement), Al-Qasas, is the opening of Al-Bara’ah until it ends: And if you fear poverty, then God will enrich you from His bounty, (al-Tawbah 9:28), so that is twenty-eight verses.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger
, he said: An announcement from God and His Messenger. He raised his statement:
h
And a call from God
, in apposition to his statement:
h
Disavowal from God
, as if he said: This is
h
disavowal from God
and His Messenger,
h
and a call from God
. As for his saying:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
, there is a difference of opinion among scholars about it.

x: Some of them said: It is the Day of Arafah.

Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid narrated, Haywah ibn Shuraih narrated, Abu Sakhr narrated, that he heard Abu Mu’awiyah al-Bajali from the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu al-Sahba’ al-Bakri say: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him about
h
the greater day of Hajj

. He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah may God be pleased with him to lead the Hajj for the people, and he sent me with him with forty verses from Bara’ah, until he came to Arafat and addressed the people on the Day of Arafat. When he had finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: Get up, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). So I got up and recited to them forty verses from Bara’ah, then we set out until we came to Mina, where I threw stones at the Jamarat and slaughtered the camel, then I shaved my head.

I knew that the people of the assembly had not attended Abu Bakr’s sermon on the Day of Arafat, so I began to follow the tents and recite them to them. From that, I think you thought it was the Day of Sacrifice, but it is the Day of Arafat.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I asked Abu Juhaifa about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
. He said: The Day of Arafah. I said: Is he from among you, or from the companions of Muhammad? He said: All of that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Arafah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Waleed Al-Shani, on the authority of Shihab bin Ibad Al-Asri, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Omar, may God have mercy on him, said:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Arafah. So I mentioned it to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and he said: I will tell you on the authority of Ibn Omar, that Omar said: The greatest limit is the Day of Arafah.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Omar bin Al-Waleed Al-Shanni told us, he said, Shihab bin Abbad Al-Asri told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I heard Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, say: This is the day of Arafah,
h
the greatest day of Hajj

, so no one should fast on it. He said: So I performed Hajj after my father, and I came to Madinah, and I asked about the best of its people, and they said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, so I went to him and said: I asked about the best of the people of Madinah, and they said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, so tell me about fasting on the day of Arafah! He said: I will tell you about someone who is a hundred times better than me, Omar - or Ibn Omar - used to forbid fasting on it and say: It is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Habib told us, on the authority of Maqal bin Dawud, he said:
m: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: This day of Arafah is
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, so no one should fast on it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ghalib bin Ubaid God told us, he said:
m: I asked Ata’ about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, and he said: The Day of Arafah, so he departed from it before dawn.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah told me, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon on the eve of Arafah, then he said: As for what follows, and he would not deliver a sermon without saying: As for what follows, for this is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Arafah.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Bakht, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Arafah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Tawus told me, on the authority of his father, he said,
m: we said: What is the greater Hajj? He said: The Day of Arafah.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon on the Day of Arafah and said: This is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

x: Others said: It is the day of sacrifice.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Musʿab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, he said:
m: I heard Ali say: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, he said:
m: I asked Ali about the greater Hajj, and he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Abi Awfa about the greater Hajj, he said: He said: The Day of Sacrifice.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ayyash al-Amiri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice. ... He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Malik, he said:
m: Abu Salamah and I entered upon ʿAbdullah ibn Awfa, he said: I asked him about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, and he said: The Day of Sacrifice is the day on which blood is shed.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Bayan, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abi Awfa about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice. ... He said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Umair told us, he said, I heard Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, and he was asked about his saying:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
, he said: It is the day on which blood is shed and hair is shaved.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: I heard Yahya Ibn Al-Jazzar narrating on the authority of Ali that he went out on the Day of Sacrifice on a white mule heading to the cemetery, and a man came taking hold of the reins of his mule, and asked him about the greater Hajj, and he said: It is this day of yours, let it go.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Malik bin Mughul,
m: and Shatir, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, he said: The day of the greatest punishment is the day of sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: He was asked about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya ibn Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Ali:
m: that a man met him on the Day of Sacrifice and took hold of his bridle, and asked him about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, he said: It is this day. Surat al-Tawbah 9:3
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger
to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger. So
h
if you repent
, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you cannot cause failure to God. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair,
m: and Ayyash Al-Amiri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: It is the day on which blood will be shed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Ibn Abi Awfa, he said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the day on which blood is shed, hair is shaved, and what is forbidden is made permissible.

c: Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me, he said, Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, he said:
m: Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba addressed us on the day of Eid Al-Adha on a camel and said: This is the day of Eid Al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, he said:
m: Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba gave us a sermon on the day of Eid al-Adha on a camel and said: This is the day of Eid al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, he said:
m: Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba gave us a sermon, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, he said,
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Juhaifa, who said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said:
m: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas and a man from the family of Shaiba disputed over the Greater Day of Hajj. Ali said: It is the Day of Sacrifice. The one from the family of Shaiba said: It is the Day of Arafah. So he sent for Saʿid ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice. Don’t you see that whoever misses the Day of Arafah has not missed the Hajj, but if he misses the Day of Sacrifice, he has missed the Hajj?

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said:
m: The greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. He said: I said to him: Abdullah bin Shaiba and Muhammad bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas differed on that. Muhammad bin Ali said: It is the Day of Sacrifice. Abdullah said: It is the Day of Arafah. Saeed bin Jubair said: Tell me, if a man misses the Day of Arafah, does he miss the Hajj? And if he misses the Day of Sacrifice, does he miss the Hajj?

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, a man told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qais bin Ubadah, he said:
m: Dhul-Hijjah is the tenth of the day of sacrifice, and it is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, he said:
m: h
The greater day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice. And the lesser Hajj is Umrah.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Had, he said:
m: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Hajabi, he said:
m: I asked Nafi’ bin Jubair bin Mut’am about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, he said: The Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: It was said: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the day on which blood is shed and the forbidden is made permissible.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj

is the Day of Sacrifice, on which everything forbidden is permissible. ... He said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, who said:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I asked Muhammad about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, and he said: It was a day that coincided with the Hajj of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Hajj of the people of the hair.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, Omar bin Dhir told us:
m: I asked Mujahid about
h
the greatest day of Hajj
, and he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice - and Ikrimah said:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice, the day on which blood is shed and the forbidden is made permissible - and Mujahid said: The day on which all of Hajj is gathered, and it is
h
the greatest day of Hajj
. ... He said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali:
h
The greatest day of Hajj

is the Day of Sacrifice. ... He said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said, Ali said:
m: The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Sacrifice. He said: Al-Zuhri said: The Day of Sacrifice is the greater day of pilgrimage.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Yunus and Amr informed me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman,
m: “on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me with Abu Bakr on the pilgrimage that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had commanded him to undertake before the Farewell Pilgrimage, with a group who would announce to the people on the Day of Sacrifice: No polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.” Al-Zuhri said: Humayd used to say: The Day of Sacrifice is the greatest day of pilgrimage.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abdul Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Sha’bi told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Shaddad about the greater Hajj and the lesser Hajj, and he said: The greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah. ... He said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said:

c: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Shaddad, and he mentioned something similar. ... He said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said:

c: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, he said:
m: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa say:
h
The greatest day of Hajj

is the day on which hair is laid down, blood is shed, and what is forbidden is made permissible. ... He said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ali, who said: The greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Ayyash al-Amiri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa,
m: that he was asked about
h
the greatest day of Hajj

, so he said: Glory be to God, it is a day on which blood is shed, what is forbidden is made permissible, and hair is placed on it, it is the day of sacrifice. ... He said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, who said: Al-Mughira bin Shu’bah addressed us on his camel and said: This is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater pilgrimage. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Hassan bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Tahman, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice, on which the forbidden is permissible.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told me, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: When that day came, he sat on his camel, and a man took hold of its reins - or: its bridle - and said: What day is this? He said: We kept silent until we thought that he would give it a name other than its name, then he said: Is it not the day of Hajj?

c: Sahl bin Muhammad Al-Sijistani told us, Abu Jaber Al-Harami told us, Hisham bin Al-Ghazz Al-Jarshi told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood at the Jamarat on the Day of Sacrifice during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said: This is the greatest day of pilgrimage.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani,
m: “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among us on a red, green she-camel and said: Do you know what day your day is? They said: The day of sacrifice! He said: You have spoken the truth, it is the day of the greater pilgrimage.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr ibn Murrah told me, Murrah told us,
m: a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about us, and he mentioned Surat al-Tawbah 9:3
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger
to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger. So
h
if you repent
, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you cannot cause failure to God. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment. something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on the authority of... he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali with four words when Abu Bakr led the people in Hajj. He called out in disavowal: This is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

. Beware, none shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul. Beware, no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Beware, no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year. Beware, whoever has a covenant between him and Muhammad, let his term be until its term. God is free from polytheists and so is His Messenger.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told me, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
The greater day of Hajj

, he said: The Day of Sacrifice, the day on which the pilgrim becomes free from ihram and the sacrificial animals are slaughtered. Ibn Umar used to say: It is the Day of Sacrifice. My father used to say: Ibn Abbas used to say: It is the Day of Arafah. I did not hear anyone say that it is the Day of Arafah except Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: Hajj is missed by missing the Day of Sacrifice, but it is not missed by missing the Day of Arafah, if he misses the day but not the night, he stands between it and the rising of dawn.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The Day of Sacrifice is
h
the greatest day of Hajj

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said,
m: “A man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me in this room of mine, I think he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us on the Day of Sacrifice on a red, green she-camel and said: Do you know what day this is? This is the Day of Sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj.”

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying: The day of the greater Hajj is the time and date of the greater Hajj. He said: That is all the days of Hajj, not a specific day.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The greatest day of Hajj
is the time of Hajj, all of its days.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The greater Hajj is all the days of Mina, and the gatherings of the polytheists when they were in Dhu al-Majaz, Ukaz, and Majannah, when it was announced to them: Muslims and polytheists should not meet after this year, and no one should circumambulate the House naked, and whoever had a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then his covenant is for its term.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said,
m: Sufyan used to say: (The Day of Hajj), (The Day of the Camel), and (The Day of Siffin), meaning: all of its days.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The greatest day of Hajj
, he said: During Hajj, meaning: all of its days.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said:
h
The greater day of Hajj

is the Day of Sacrifice, because of the convergence of reports from a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Ali called out what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him with of the message to the polytheists, and recited to them Bara’ah, on the Day of Sacrifice. This, “in addition to the reports that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said on the Day of Sacrifice: Do you know what day this is? This is
h
the greater day of Hajj

.” And then, (the day) is only added to the meaning by what it is in, like people saying: (the day of Arafah), which is the day people stand in Arafah, and (the day of sacrifice), which is the day they sacrifice, and (the day of breaking the fast), which is the day they break the fast.

Likewise (the day of Hajj) is the day they perform Hajj, and people perform Hajj and complete their rituals on the Day of Sacrifice, because on the night and day of the Day of Sacrifice, standing in Arafah is not missed until dawn, and on its morning one performs the acts of Hajj. As for the Day of Arafah, even if standing in Arafah is in it, standing in it is not missed until dawn on the night of Sacrifice, and the Hajj is all on the Day of Sacrifice. As for what Mujahid said: that the day of Hajj refers to all of its days, even if that is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, it is not the most common and well-known meaning in the speech of the Arabs. Rather, the most common meaning of the day among them is that it is from sunset until the same time the next day. Rather, the interpretation of the Book of God is based on the most common and well-known meaning from the speech of the one in whose language the Book was revealed.
The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which this day was called: The Greater Day of Pilgrimage.
Some of them said: It was called that because it was in a year in which the Hajj of Muslims and polytheists was combined.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: It was called the greatest pilgrimage because Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage that he performed, and the Muslims and polytheists gathered in it, so that is why it was called the greatest pilgrimage, and it also coincided with the feast of the Jews and Christians.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jadaan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal, who said:
m: The day of the greatest Hajj was the Farewell Hajj, on which the Hajj of the Muslims, Christians and Jews gathered, and it did not gather before it or after it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: His statement:
h
The Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage
, he said: It was only called the Greatest Pilgrimage because it was the day on which Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage, and the covenants were abandoned.

x: Others said: The greater Hajj is the Qur’an, and the lesser Hajj is the Ifrad.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abu Bakr al-Nahshali told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: It was said: The greater Hajj and the lesser Hajj. The greater Hajj is the Qiran, and the lesser Hajj is the Hajj itself.

x: Others said: The greater Hajj is Hajj, and the lesser Hajj is Umrah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The greater Hajj is Hajj, and the lesser Hajj is Umrah. ... He said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, who said: I said to him: This is the greater Hajj, but what is the lesser Hajj? He said: Umrah.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: It was said: The lesser Hajj is the Umrah in Ramadan. ... He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It was said: (The lesser Hajj) is Umrah. ... He said, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Asma, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, who said:
h
The greater day of Hajj
is the Day of Sacrifice, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Ala told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri:
m: The people of the pre-Islamic era used to call the lesser Hajj the Umrah.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The greater pilgrimage is Hajj, because it is greater than Umrah in that its work is greater than its work, so it was called the greater, for that reason. As for the lesser, it is Umrah, because its work is less than the work of Hajj, so it was called the lesser, because its work is less than its work. As for his saying:
h
God is innocent of the polytheists and His Messenger
, its meaning is: God is innocent of the covenant of the polytheists and His Messenger, after this argument.
The meaning of the statement:
h
And an announcement from God and His Messenger
to the people on the day of the greatest pilgrimage: that God and His Messenger are innocent of the covenant of the polytheists, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: God and His Messenger are innocent of the polytheists, meaning: after this argument.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
If you repent
, it is better for you.
But if you turn away, then know that you cannot cause failure to God. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.”
God Almighty says:
h
If you repent

, from your disbelief, O polytheists, and return to the Oneness of God and sincere worship of Him - without any gods or rivals - then returning to that is better for you, than remaining in polytheism in this world and the Hereafter. But if you turn away, he says, and if you turn away from belief in God and insist on remaining in your polytheism, then know that you will not cause failure to God, he says: So be certain that you will not prevent God from inflicting upon you His painful punishment and severe chastisement, for remaining in disbelief, as He did to those who came before you from the polytheists by sending down His vengeance upon them and bringing the punishment upon them immediately. And give good tidings to those who disbelieve, he says: And inform, O Muhammad, those who denied your prophethood and disobeyed the command of their Lord, of a painful punishment that will befall them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you repent
, he said: you believe.

evidence.text: I knew that the people of the assembly had not attended Abu Bakr’s sermon on the Day of Arafat, so I began to follow the tents and recite them to them.

x: God Almighty says: And an announcement from God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that God is free from the polytheists and His Messenger, except for the covenant with those polytheists with whom you have made a covenant, O believers, and they have not diminished anything from you, from the covenant that you made with them, nor have they supported anyone against you, from your enemy, so they aid them with their souls and bodies, nor with weapons, horses, or men, so fulfill their covenant with them until their term, meaning: fulfill their covenant that you made with them, and do not wage war against them until the expiration of the term of their covenant that is between you and them, Indeed, God loves the righteous, meaning: God loves the one who fears Him by obeying Him, performing His obligations, and avoiding His disobedience.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So fulfill their covenant with them until their term, meaning: until their appointed time.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: Except for those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty, meaning: the specific treaty until a specified term, and then they did not fail you in anything, the verse.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except for those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty and then they did not fail you in anything and did not support anyone against

you, the verse, he said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty at the time of Hudaybiyyah, and there were four months left of their term after the Day of Sacrifice. So God commanded His Prophet to fulfill their treaty with them until their term, and with those with whom he had no treaty until the end of Muharram, and to throw away the treaty of every one with whom he had a treaty, and He commanded him to fight them until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that nothing would be accepted from them except that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The period for those who had a treaty with the polytheists before the revelation of Bara’ah was four months, from the day the permission was given to Bara’ah until the tenth of Rabi’ al-Akhir, and that is four months. If the polytheists break their treaty and support an enemy, then they have no treaty. But if they fulfill their treaty that was between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not support an enemy against him, then he has been commanded to fulfill their treaty with them and to fulfill it.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
So when the sacred months have passed

, is when they have passed, gone, and departed. It is said: We skinned such-and-such a month, we skin it skinned and skinned, meaning we left it. And from this is their saying: A skinned sheep, meaning: stripped of its skin, taken out of it. By the sacred months he means Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram. Rather, what is meant in this place is the expiration of the sacred month alone, because the call to prayer was for the day of the greater pilgrimage, so it is known that they did not postpone all the sacred months - and we have demonstrated the correctness of that previously - but since it was connected to the other two sacred months before it, and it was a third for them, and they are all connected to each other, it was said:
h
So when the sacred months have passed

, and the meaning of the statement is: So when the three sacred months have passed for those who have no covenant, or for those who had a covenant and broke their covenant by supporting the enemies against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, or their covenant was for an unknown period.

Then kill the polytheists, meaning: kill them, wherever you find them, meaning: wherever you encounter them on earth, in the sanctuary and outside the sanctuary, in the sacred months and outside the sacred months, and capture them, meaning: take them prisoner, and besiege them, meaning: prevent them from moving around in the lands of Islam and entering Mecca, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, meaning: lie in wait for them in pursuit of killing them or taking them prisoner, at every place of ambush, meaning: every road and watchtower. It is a verb that comes from the saying: I monitored so-and-so, I monitor him, meaning: I watched him. If they repent, meaning if they return from their polytheism and denial of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the oneness of God and sincere worship of Him without any gods or rivals, and acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and establish prayer, meaning if they perform the prayer that God has imposed upon them within its limits, and give the zakat that God has imposed upon them from their wealth to its people, then leave their way, meaning if they let them do their work in your cities and enter the Sacred House, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, to whoever among His servants repents and returns to His obedience after what he was upon of disobedience, covering up his sin, Merciful to him, that He does not punish him for his previous sins before his repentance, after his repentance.

We have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who postponed it until the end of the sacred months. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.

Who said that? Abdul A'la bin Wasil Al-Asadi narrated that Ubayd God bin Musa narrated that Abu Ja'far Al-Razi narrated that Al-Rabi' narrated that Anas said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever departs this world with sincerity to God alone and worshipping Him without associating anything with Him, departs from it and God is pleased with him. He said: Anas said: It is the religion of God that the Messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord, before the chaos of hadiths and the differences of desires, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of God in the last of what God revealed. God said: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. He said: Their repentance is to abandon idols, worship their Lord, establish prayer, and give zakah. Then He said in another verse: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. (al-Tawbah 9:11) Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying:
h
So when the sacred months have passed
, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, until he finished the end of the verse.

Qatada used to say: Release the one whom God has commanded you to release, for people are three: a group of Muslims who are required to pay zakat, a polytheist who is required to pay the jizyah, and a belligerent who is safe from his trade among the Muslims if he gives a tenth of his wealth.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When the sacred months have passed, which are the four that I have counted for you, meaning: the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi’ Al-Awwal, and the tenth of Rabi’ Al-Akhir.

x: Those who said this article said: These were called the sacred months because God Almighty forbade the believers in them to shed the blood of polytheists, or to show them off except for a good cause.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr: that he informed him on the authority of Mujahid and Amr bin Shuaib
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when the sacred months have passed
, that they are the four about which God said: Then travel freely throughout the land, he said: They are the sacred months, because they believed in it until they traveled it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: “A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely throughout the land for four months,” he said: He set a period of four months for them, and He disavowed every polytheist.
