Then He commanded that when those sacred months had passed, Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, do not leave them wandering in the land, nor go out for trade, and make things difficult for them after that. Then He commanded forgiveness: “But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So when the sacred months have passed

, meaning: the four for which a deadline was set - for the people of the general covenant from the polytheists - then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, the verse.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And if any of the polytheists, whom I have commanded you to fight and kill after the sacred months have passed, seek your protection, O Muhammad, so that he may hear the Word of God from you, which is the Qur’an that God revealed to him, then grant him protection, meaning: grant him protection so that he may hear the Word of God and you recite it to him,
h
then escort him to his place of safety

, meaning: then return him after he has heard the Word of God if he refuses to submit and does not learn from what you have recited to him of the Word of God and believe, to his place of safety, meaning: to where he is safe from you and from those who are in your obedience, until he joins his home and his people from the polytheists, that is because they are a people who do not know, meaning: You do that to them, by granting them protection so that they may hear the Qur’an, and returning them if they refuse to submit to Islam to their place of safety, because they are an ignorant people who do not understand the proof from God, and do not know what they will have by believing in God if they believe, and what sin they will bear. The sin is in abandoning faith in God.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection, meaning: from those whom I ordered you to fight, then grant him protection.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then reward him until he hears the word of God. As for the word of God, it is the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection, he said: A person comes to you and hears what you say, and hears what was revealed to you, so he is safe until he comes to you and hears the words of God, and until he reaches his place of safety, wherever he came.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. Ibn Humayd narrated that Yaqub narrated on the authority of Jaʿfar on the authority of Saʿid that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight and met the enemy. The Muslims brought out a polytheist and pointed their spears at him. The man said: Take your weapons away from me and let me hear the words of God. They said: You bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and you renounce all rivals to Him and disavow Al-Lat and Al-ʿUzza. He said: Then I call you to witness that I have done it!

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then escort him to his place of safety

, he said: If what you recite to him and tell him does not agree with him, then inform him. He said: This is not abrogated. There is a difference of opinion regarding the ruling on this verse: is it abrogated or not?

x: Some of them said: It is not abrogated, and we have mentioned the statement of those who said that.
Others said: It is abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them
, abrogated by: Then either a favor from us afterwards or ransom
r
(Muhammad 47:4)
. ... He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, the same.

x: Others said: Rather, His statement,
h
Then kill the polytheists
, was abrogated by His statement,
h
Then if there is any favor from Us after that (Muhammad 47
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds
r
(Muhammad 47:4)
, it was abrogated by his statement:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them

x: The correct opinion in this regard, in my opinion, is that of those who said: It is not abrogated. We have shown that the meaning of abrogation is the negation of a ruling that had been established by another ruling. There is no valid argument for the obligation of God’s ruling on the polytheists to kill in any case, then abrogating it by not killing them in exchange for ransom, nor in the manner of showing favor to them. Since that was the case, and ransom, favor, and killing were the rulings of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding them from the first war he fought against them, which was from the day of Badr, it was known that the meaning of the verse is: So kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and take them for killing or for favor or ransom, and besiege them. If that is its meaning, then what we said about it is correct, and not anything else.

evidence.text: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And if any of the polytheists, whom I have commanded you to fight and kill after the sacred months have passed, seek your protection, O Muhammad, so that he may hear the Word of God from you, which is the Qur’an that God revealed to him, then grant him protection, meaning: grant him protection so that he may hear the Word of God and you recite it to him, then escort him to his place of safety, meaning: then return him after he has heard the Word of God if he refuses to submit and does not learn from what you have recited to him of the Word of God and believe, to his place of safety, meaning: to where he is safe from you and from those who are in your obedience, until he joins his home and his people from the polytheists, that is because they are a people who do not know, meaning: You do that to them, by granting them protection so that they may hear the Qur’an, and returning them if they refuse to submit to Islam to their place of safety, because they are an ignorant people who do not understand the proof from God, and do not know what they will have by believing in God if they believe, and what sin they will bear.

x: God Almighty says: How can it be, O believers in God and His Messenger, and in what sense, that the polytheists have a covenant and protection with their Lord with God and His Messenger, which is fulfilled for them, and they are left safe and secure for its sake, acting in the lands? Rather, its meaning is: They have no covenant, and it is obligatory upon the believers to kill them wherever they find them, except for those of them who gave the covenant at the Sacred Mosque, for God Almighty commanded the believers to fulfill their covenant with them, and to be steadfast with them in it, as long as they are steadfast in it towards the believers.
The people of interpretation differed about what they meant by his saying:
h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque
Some of them said: They are people from Juthayma bin Ad-Dail.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “How can the polytheists have a covenant with God and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So as long as they are upright with you, be upright with them.” They are Banu Judhaymah bin Ad-Dail.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abbad Ibn Jaʿfar,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except for those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty
, he said: They are Juthaymah, the Bakr of Kinanah.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: How can it be for the polytheists, who were on a general covenant with you, that you would not frighten them nor would they frighten you in the sanctuary or in the sacred month, a covenant with God and with His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque, and they are the tribes of Banu Bakr who had entered into the covenant of Quraysh and their agreement on the day of Hudaybiyyah, until the period that was between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Quraysh, and none broke it except this tribe of Quraysh, and Banu Ad-Dail from Bakr. So he ordered the covenant to be completed for those of Banu Bakr who had not broken their covenant until its term, so long as they were upright with you, the verse.

x: Others said: They are Quraysh.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement:
h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque
, they are Quraysh.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque
, meaning: the people of Mecca.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram

, he said: They were people who had a period of time with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was not appropriate for a polytheist to enter al-Masjid al-Haram, nor to pay the jizya to a Muslim. So if they are upright toward you, be upright toward them, meaning the polytheists with whom you made a treaty.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: “
h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram

. So as long as they are upright with you, be upright with them,” he said: These are Quraysh. And this abrogated the months that were set for them, and they were excused for not being upright, as God said. So He set for them after the conquest four months, during which they could choose from their affair: either to submit to Islam, or to go to any country they wished. He said: So they submitted to Islam before the four months, and before they were killed.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Thawr, the uncle of Muammar, told us, on the authority of Qatada: “Except for those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram. So as long as they remain upright with you, then remain upright with them.” He said: It is the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: So they did not remain upright, they broke their treaty, meaning: they aided Banu Bakr, the alliance of Quraysh, against Khuza’ah, the alliance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: They are a people from Khuza'ah.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque
, he said: The people of the treaty from Khuza’ah.

x: The most correct of these statements, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: They are some of the Banu Bakr of Kinanah, who had adhered to his covenant, and had no role in breaking the covenant that was between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Quraysh on the day of Hudaybiyyah, when they broke it with the help of their allies from Banu Ad-Dail, against the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Khuzaʿah. I said: This statement is the most correct of the statements on this matter, because God commanded His Prophet and the believers to fulfill the covenant with those who had made a covenant with him at the Sacred Mosque, as long as they adhered to their covenant. We have already explained that these verses were proclaimed by Ali in the year nine of the Hijra, and that was one year after the conquest of Mecca.

There was no unbeliever in Mecca from Quraysh or Khuza’ah at that time between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant, so he was commanded to fulfill his covenant with him as long as he adhered to his covenant, because those of them who were residents of Mecca had broken the covenant and were being fought before these verses were revealed. As for his saying: Indeed, God loves the righteous, its meaning is: God loves the one who fears God and is mindful of Him in performing His obligations, fulfilling His covenant with those with whom He has made a covenant, avoiding His disobedience, and refraining from betraying His covenants with those with whom He has made a covenant.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
How can these polytheists who broke their covenant or those of you who have no covenant have a covenant and a protection

, O believers, when if they prevail over you, they will overcome you, observing no pact of kinship or protection against you. I suffice with how as evidence of the meaning of the speech, because what is intended by the meaning is presented before it.

i: And the Arabs do the same, if they repeat the letter after its meaning has passed, they permit the deletion of the verb, as the poet said:
x: You told me that death is only in the villages, so how about when this is a plateau and a dune?

The verb was deleted after how because what is meant after it came before it. The meaning of the statement is: How can death be in the villages, when this is a plateau and a dune, from which no one can escape?
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
They do not observe any pact of kinship or covenant with you
Some of them said, meaning: They do not respect God or any covenant with you.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They do not observe in a believer except (al-Tawbah 9:10), he said: God.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not observe towards a believer any pact of kinship or covenant (al-Tawbah 9
:10), he said: Like his statement: (Gabriel), (Michael), (Israfil), as if he is saying: He adds (Jabr), (Mika), (Israf) to (El), he says: Abdullah,
h
They do not observe towards a believer any pact of kinship or covenant (al-Tawbah 9
:10), as if he is saying: They do not observe God.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except for a covenant, they do not fear God or anyone else.

x: Others said: Al-Il means kinship.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not observe towards a believer any kinship or covenant (al-Tawbah 9

:10), meaning: kinship or covenant. And his statement: And if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe towards you any kinship or covenant, he said: The kinship means kinship, and the covenant means the covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
They do not observe among you any pact of kinship or covenant
. “Peace” means kinship, and covenant means the covenant, meaning the people of the covenant from the polytheists, he says: their covenant.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah and Abda told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: Al-Il means kinship.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: They do not observe concerning a believer any kinship or covenant (al-Tawbah 9:10). He said: The kinship means kinship, and the covenant means the pledge.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
They do not observe concerning a believer any pact of kinship or covenant (al-Tawbah 9
:10): The pact means kinship, and the covenant means the covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: How, even if they gain dominance over you, meaning the polytheists, they will not observe in you, a covenant, kinship, or pact.

x: Others said: It means an oath.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not observe among you any pact of kinship or covenant
, he said, The pact means the oath, and the covenant means the pledge.

x: Others said: Al-Il is the covenant, but it was repeated because the two words differed, even though their meaning is the same. Surat al-Tawbah 9:8 How can it be, when if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe concerning you any pact of kinship or covenant. They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are wicked.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except, he said: a covenant.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
They do not observe among you any pact or covenant

, he said: They do not observe among you any covenant or pact. He said: One of them is from the other like the form of (Forgiving), (Merciful), he said: So the word is one, but it is separate. He said: And the covenant is (the pact).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: nor a covenant, he said: the covenant.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: nor a covenant, he said: (the covenant) is the pledge.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God Almighty mentioned about these polytheists whom He ordered His Prophet and the believers to kill after the sacred months had passed, and to besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush: that if they were to prevail over the believers, they would not be watched over them (except). And (Al-Il) is a name that includes three meanings: covenant, contract, oath, and kinship. It also means (God). So since the word includes these three meanings, and God did not specify one meaning over another, then it is correct to include that as He, the Most High, included its three meanings.

They do not respect God, nor kinship, nor covenant, nor pact in the believer. Evidence that it means kinship is the statement of Ibn Muqbil: People are corrupted by their successors, who have severed family ties and kinship ties.

Meaning: They cut off kinship, and Hassan bin Thabit said: By your life, you are to the Quraysh like the head of an ostrich is to the neck of an ostrich. As for its meaning if it means covenant, then the speaker says: We found them lying, O God, and the One of God and the Covenant does not lie.

Some of the Basrans who claim to have knowledge of the Arabic language have claimed that il, “ahd,” mithaq, and yamin are one and the same, and that dhimmah in this context is the resentment of someone who has no covenant, and the plural is dhimmah. Ibn Ishaq used to say: This verse refers to the people of the general covenant.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: How is it, even if they gain dominance over you, meaning: the polytheists who have no covenant with them for a period of time from the people of the general covenant, they do not observe any pact or covenant with you. As for His statement: They please you with their mouths, He is saying: They give you with their tongues something other than what they conceal in their souls of enmity and hatred for you, but their hearts refuse, meaning: Their hearts refuse to submit to you, by believing what they express to you with their tongues. God Almighty warns the believers against their affair, and urges them to kill them and invade them wherever they find them on God’s land, and not to fall short in their hatred with all that they are able to do, and most of them are wicked, He is saying: Most of them are disobedient to your covenant, breaking it, disbelieving in their Lord, and going against His obedience.

x: God Almighty says: These polytheists, whom God has commanded you, O believers, to kill wherever you find them, have bought a small amount of compensation from the worldly goods by abandoning the proofs that God has given them. This is because, according to what was reported about them, they broke the covenant that was between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by eating a meal that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb fed them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They have sold the signs of God for a small price
, he said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb fed his allies, and left the allies of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. As for His statement:
h
And they hindered from His path

, its meaning is: They prevented people from entering Islam, and they tried to turn the Muslims away from their religion. Indeed, evil was what they were doing. God Almighty says: These polytheists whose characteristics were described, evil was what they were doing, from purchasing disbelief for faith, and misguidance for guidance, and their hindering from the path of God those who believed in God and His Messenger, or those who wanted to believe.

x: God Almighty says: These polytheists whom I have commanded you, O believers, to kill wherever you find them, do not fear killing a believer if they are able to do so, except for a covenant. He says: Do not spare them, O believers, just as they would not spare you if they were to prevail over you. And those are the aggressors. He says: Those who transgress against you to what is not theirs through injustice and aggression.

God Almighty says: If these polytheists whom I have commanded you, O believers, to kill, return from their disbelief and polytheism with God, to belief in Him and His Messenger, and turn to His obedience, and establish the prayer, the prescribed prayer, and perform it within its limits, and give the obligatory charity, the one that is due to those who are entitled to it, then they are your brothers in religion, meaning: they are your brothers in the religion that God has commanded you with, which is Islam, and We explain the verses in detail, meaning: and We clarify the proofs and evidence of God to His creation, for a people who know, what He has explained to them, so We explain it to them in detail, without the ignorant who do not understand God’s explanation and His decisive verses. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah

, then they are your brothers in religion, meaning: If they abandon Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, “then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakat, he said: This verse forbids the blood of the people of the Qiblah.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Prayer and zakat were both made obligatory, no distinction was made between them. And he recited: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion, and he refused to accept prayer without zakat. And he said: May God have mercy on Abu Bakr, how knowledgeable he was!

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: You were commanded to establish prayer and pay zakat, and whoever does not pay zakat has no prayer. It was said: Then your brothers, so it was raised with the pronoun: They are your brothers, since they had been mentioned before, as He said: But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion (al-Ahzab 33:5), meaning: they are your brothers in religion.

x: God Almighty says: If these polytheists with whom you made a covenant from Quraysh break their covenants after they have agreed with you that they will not fight you or support any of your enemies against you, and attack your religion, meaning: and cast aspersions on your religion of Islam, so they slander and criticize it,
h
then fight the leaders of disbelief
, meaning: fight the leaders of disbelief in God, for
h
they have no oaths

, meaning: the leaders of disbelief have no covenant, perhaps they will desist, so that they will desist from attacking your religion and supporting you. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them regarding the meanings of the imams of disbelief.
Some of them said: He is Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Utba bin Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan bin Harb, and their peers. Hudhayfah used to say: He has not yet reached its people.
Mention of those who said they are the ones who were named:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if they break their oaths after their covenant

, to: perhaps they will desist, meaning the people of the covenant from the polytheists, he called them leaders of disbelief, and they are like that. God says to His Prophet: And if they break the covenant that is between you and them, then fight them, leaders of disbelief who have no oaths, perhaps they will desist.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if they break their oaths after their covenant
to: they desist, so among the leaders of disbelief were: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan, and Suhayl ibn Amr, and they were the ones who intended to expel him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The leaders of disbelief are Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Utbah ibn Rabi’ah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Bashar told us
m: - Ibn Wakee’ said, Ghundar told us, and Ibn Bashar said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us - on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief
, for
h
they have no oaths
, he said: Abu Sufyan is one of them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they break their oaths
, to desist, these are Quraysh. He says: If they break their covenant that they made regarding Islam, and attack it, then fight them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief
, meaning the leaders of the polytheists, the people of Mecca.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief

, Abu Sufyan bin Harb, Umayyah bin Khalaf, Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, and Suhayl bin Amr, and they are the ones who broke the covenant of God and intended to expel the Messenger. And by God, it is not as the people of doubts, innovations, and slander against God and His Book have interpreted it. Mentioning the narration on the authority of Hudhayfah as we mentioned on his authority:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, on the authority of Hudhayfah:
m: h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief
, he said: The people of this verse have not been fought after that.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Habib bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, who said:
m: I was with Hudhayfah when he recited this verse: Fight the leaders of disbelief, and he said: The people of this verse have not been fought yet.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, he said:
m: Hudhayfah recited:
h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief
, he said: The people of this verse have not been fought after that.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sala bin Zafar:
m: h
They have no oaths
, they have no covenant.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if they break their oaths
, he said: their covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they break their oaths
, their covenant that they made Surat al-Tawbah 9:12
h
And if they break their oaths after their covenant
and attack your religion,
h
then fight the leaders of disbelief
. Indeed, there are no oaths for them. Perhaps they will desist. regarding Islam.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sila, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They have no oaths
, he said: They have no covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharibi told me, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sila bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then fight the leaders of disbelief
, for
h
they have no oaths

, he said: They have no covenant. As for nakth, its root is naqd, and it is said: So-and-so broke his rope, meaning he broke it. And (oaths) is the plural of (oath). There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
They have no oaths
. The people of Hijaz, Iraq, and others read it as:
h
They have no oaths

, with the alif of oaths open, meaning: they have no covenants, based on what we have mentioned from the commentators’ statement about it. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it as: They have no faith, with a kasra on the alif, meaning: they have no Islam. It may be read in a different way. That is, by reading it in this way, he meant that they have no security - that is, do not trust them, but kill them wherever you find them - as if he meant the source of the saying of the speaker: (I trust him, so I trust him with trust).

x: The correct reading in this regard, which I do not permit reading with anything else, is the reading of those who read with the opening of the alif without the breaking of it, because of the consensus of the proof of the reading on the reading with it, and the rejection of the opposite, and because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on what I mentioned that its interpretation is: they have no covenant, and the oaths which are in the meaning of the covenant, can only be with the opening of the alif because it is the plural of oath which was based on a contract that was between the two parties to the agreement.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Habib bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, who said: I was with Hudhayfah when he recited this verse: Fight the leaders of disbelief, and he said: The people of this verse have not been fought yet.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: They have no oaths.

The people of Hijaz, Iraq, and others read it as: They have no oaths, with the alif of oaths open, meaning: they have no covenants, based on what we have mentioned from the commentators’ statement about it.
It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it as: They have no faith, with a kasra on the alif, meaning: they have no Islam.
It may be read in a different way.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, which I do not permit reading with anything else, is the reading of those who read with the opening of the alif without the breaking of it, because of the consensus of the proof of the reading on the reading with it, and the rejection of the opposite, and because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on what I mentioned that its interpretation is: they have no covenant, and the oaths which are in the meaning of the covenant, can only be with the opening of the alif because it is the plural of oath which was based on a contract that was between the two parties to the agreement.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in God and His Messenger, urging them to fight their enemies from the polytheists: Will you not fight, O believers, these polytheists who broke the covenant between you and them, and attacked your religion, and supported your enemies against you, and intended to expel the Messenger, from among them, so they expelled him, and they initiated the fighting against you the first time, meaning their action on the day of Badr, and it was said that their fighting was against the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Khuzaʿah, Do you fear them? He says: Do you fear them for yourselves, so you refrain from fighting them out of fear for yourselves from them, for God is more deserving that you fear Him, He says: God is more deserving that you fear His punishment by refraining from fighting them, and beware of His wrath upon you, than these polytheists who do not possess for you any harm or benefit except by God’s permission, if you are believers.

He says: If you acknowledge that the fear of God for you is more important than the fear of these polytheists for yourselves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths

, after their covenant, and intended to expel the Messenger, he said: they intended to expel him so they expelled him, and they initiated the fighting against you the first time, Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they began it against you the first time, he said: Fighting the Quraysh, the allies of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God commanded His Messenger to wage jihad against the polytheists, those of the people of the specific covenant who broke it, and those of the people of the general covenant, after the four months that He set for them a deadline, unless one of them transgresses during it, in which case he is killed for his transgression. So He said:
h
Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths
and intended to expel the Messenger? until His saying: And God is Acquainted with what you do.

x: God Almighty says: Fight, O believers in God and His Messenger, these polytheists who broke their oaths, violated their covenants between you and them, and expelled the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among them. God will punish them by your hands, meaning God will kill them by your hands, and will disgrace them, meaning He will humiliate them by captivity and subjugation, and will give you victory over them, meaning He will give you victory and supremacy over them, and will heal the hearts of a people who believe in God and His Messenger, meaning He will heal the disease in the hearts of a people who believe in God and His Messenger, by killing these polytheists by your hands, and by your humiliation and subjugation of them. And that disease is what was in their hearts against them of resentment for the harm and distress they had inflicted upon them.

It was said: God meant by His saying: And heal the hearts of a believing people, the hearts of Khuza’ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was because the Quraysh broke the covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by aiding Bakr against them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding this verse: And heals the hearts of a believing people, he said: Khuza’ah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And heals the hearts of a believing people, he said: Khuza’ah, he heals their hearts from Banu Bakr.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And heals the hearts of a believing people, Khuza’ah, the allies of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And heals the hearts of a believing people, he said: The allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Khuza’ah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: God Almighty says: And the anguish of the hearts of these believing people from Khuzaʿah will go away, for these people who broke their oaths from the polytheists, and their grief and distress with what is in it of anguish for them, by their early assistance to them, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And He will remove the anger of their hearts, when Banu Bakr killed them, and Quraysh helped them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: the same, except that he said: And Quraysh helped them against them. As for his saying:
h
And God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills

, it is the report of a subject, and therefore it is raised, and he made the three letters before that jussive in the way of recompense, as if he said: Fight them, for if you fight them, God will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them. Then he began and said:
h
And God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills

, because fighting does not require them to repent from God, but it requires them to be punished by God, and disgraced, and to heal the hearts of the believers, and to remove the anger from their hearts, so he made that jussive as a condition and recompense for fighting, and fighting did not require repentance, so he began the report with it and made it jussive. The meaning of the statement: God bestows His favor upon whomever He wills of His disbelieving servants, and He accepts him to repentance by guiding him to it. And God is Knowing, of the secrets of His servants, and who among them is worthy of repentance, so He accepts his repentance, and who among them is not worthy of it, so He abandons him. Wise, in directing His servants from a state of disbelief to a state of faith by guiding whomever He guides to that, and from a state of faith to disbelief, by abandoning whomever among them abandons His obedience and monotheism, and other matters of their affairs.

x: God Almighty says to the believers whom He commanded to fight these polytheists, who broke their covenant between them and Him, by His saying: Fight them; God will punish them by your hands, the verse, urging them to fight them: Or do you think, O believers, that God will leave you without a trial with which to test you, and without a test with which to test you, so that He may know who among you is truthful in his religion from who is lying in it, and God has not yet made evident those who strive, meaning: Did you think that you would be left without a test by which He may know who among you is His guardian and who strives in His cause, who is wasting God’s command in that and who is excessive, and has not taken besides God and His Messenger, meaning: and God has not yet made evident those among you who strive, and those who have not taken besides God and His Messenger, an intimate friend. It is something that enters into another other than itself.

It is said: So-and-so entered into such-and-such, so he is a confidant. Rather, what he meant in this place is: the inner circle of the polytheists. God forbade the believers from taking the polytheists as allies and confidants, to whom they divulge their secrets. And God is Aware of what you do, meaning: God is All-Aware of what you do, of taking those other than God, His Messenger, and the believers in Him as allies and confidants, after what He has forbidden you from doing. That is not hidden from Him, nor are any of your other deeds, and God will reward you for that, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. And similar to what I said about the meaning of al-Walijah, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: nor the believers as allies, he takes it upon himself, from the guardianship of the polytheists.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: Walijah, he said: an entrance.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Or do you think that you will be left alone
, to His statement: and a slave, he said: He refused to leave them without testing. And he recited:
h
Or do you think that you will be left alone
while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive? And he recited: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive?
r
(Al Imran 3:142)

, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? All the verses, (Al Baqarah: 214), he informed them that he would not leave them alone until he tested them and examined them. And he recited: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, “We believe” and they will not be tested?” They will not be tested. And We have certainly tested those before them, and God will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
r
(Al Ankabut: 1-3)
, God refused except to test.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Walijah, he said: It is disbelief and hypocrisy, or he said one of them. It was said: Or did you think? and he did not say: Have you thought? because it is an interrogative sentence in the middle of a sentence, so or was inserted to differentiate it from the interrogative sentence. Similar examples of this have been explained in more than one place in the book.

x: God Almighty says: It is not appropriate for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they are witnessing against themselves that they are disbelievers. He says: The mosques are only maintained for the worship of God in them, not for disbelief in Him. So whoever is a disbeliever in God, it is not his business to maintain the mosques of God.
As for their testimony against themselves of disbelief, it is as follows:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief

, meaning: It is not appropriate for them to maintain them. As for bearing witness against themselves of disbelief, the Christian is asked: Who are you? He says: Christian. The Jew says: Jew. The Sabean says: Sabean. The polytheist says, if you ask him: What is your religion? He says: Polytheist! No one would say that except the Arabs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: It was not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God. He said, It was not appropriate for them to maintain them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Bearing witness against themselves of disbelief. He said: The Christian is asked: Who are you? He says, Christian. The Jew is asked: What are you? He says, Jew. The Sabean is asked: What are you? He says, Sabian. And His saying:
h
Their deeds have become worthless

, meaning: their rewards have been nullified and lost, because they were not for God but for Satan. And in the Fire they will abide eternally, meaning: they will never remain in it, neither alive nor dead. There is a difference in the reading of his statement:
h
It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God

. So the majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: Mosques of God, in the collective. Some Meccans and Egyptians read it as: The Mosque of God, in the singular sense, meaning the Sacred Mosque.

x: They all agree on reading his statement, Only the mosques of God are maintained as a plural, because if it is read in this way, it can mean both the singular and the plural, because the Surat al-Tawbah 9:17
h
It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief
. Those -
h
their deeds have become worthless
, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. Arabs may refer to the singular as a plural, and the plural as a singular, like their saying, He has on a garment of immorality.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God.
So the majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: Mosques of God, in the collective.
Some Meccans and Egyptians read it as: The Mosque of God, in the singular sense, meaning the Sacred Mosque.

Abu Jaʿfar said: They all agree on reading his statement, Only the mosques of God are maintained as a plural, because if it is read in this way, it can mean both the singular and the plural, because the Surat al-Tawbah 9:17 It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief.

x: God Almighty says: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by the one who believes in the Oneness of God, who sincerely worships Him, “and the Last Day, meaning: the one who believes in God’s resurrection of the dead from their graves on the Day of Resurrection, and establishes prayer, the prescribed prayer, within its limits, and pays the obligatory zakat on his wealth to whomever God has made it obligatory for him, and fears none but God, meaning: and does not fear the punishment of anyone for his disobedience to Him, except God, then perhaps those will be among the [rightly] guided, meaning: it is fitting for those who have this description to be, in the sight of God, among those whom God has guided to the truth and to the right path.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day

, meaning: those who believe in the Oneness of God and the Last Day. He says: he acknowledges what God has revealed, and establishes prayer, meaning the five daily prayers, and fears none but God, meaning: then worships none but God. He said: Then it is those, meaning: those are the successful ones, like His statement to His Prophet: It is possible that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, (al-Isra’ 17:79): He says: your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, and it is intercession, and every ‘asa in the Qur’an is obligatory. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then he mentioned the saying of the Quraysh 106:We are the people of the Sacred Sanctuary, the water-givers of the pilgrims, and the maintainers of this House, and no one is better than us! So he said:
h
The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day

, meaning: your maintenance is not like that. “The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who maintain them with due right, “by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except God,” so those are its maintainers, It is hoped that those will be among the [rightly] guided, and It is hoped is true from God.

x: This is a rebuke from God, which He mentioned to a people who boasted about providing water and custodianship of the House. So He, may His praise be glorified, informed them that the pride lies in faith, the Last Day, and jihad in His cause, not in what they boasted about, such as providing water and custodianship. Thus came the traces and the interpretation of the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Muawiyah ibn Salam narrated to me, on the authority of his grandfather Abu Salam al-Aswad, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir al-Ansari, who said:
m: I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a group of his companions, and one of them said: I do not care if I do not do any work after embracing Islam, except providing water to the pilgrims!

x: Another said: Rather, maintaining the Sacred Mosque! And another said: Rather, jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said! Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and that was on a Friday - but when I have prayed the Friday prayer, I will go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him about the matter in which you differed. He said: So he did, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: Have you made the providing water to the pilgrims until His saying:
h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you considered the provision of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the

Last Day? Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib said when he was taken prisoner on the day of Badr: If you had preceded us in Islam, migration, and jihad, then we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque, provide water to the pilgrims, and free the captives! God said: Have you considered the provision of water to the pilgrims, to His statement: the wrongdoers, meaning that that was in polytheism, and I do not accept what was in polytheism.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you made the provision of water to the pilgrims

, to the wrongdoers, that is because the polytheists said: Maintaining the House of God and providing water is better than those who come and strive, and they were proud of the Sacred Sanctuary and were arrogant, because they were its people and its maintainers. So God mentioned their arrogance and their turning away, so He said to the people of the Sacred Sanctuary from the polytheists: My verses were recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels, arrogant, spending their time in idle chatter. (al-Mu’minun 23:66-67), meaning that they were arrogant about the Sacred Sanctuary. He said: Passing their time in idle chatter, because they used to spend their time in idle chatter and neglect the Qur’an and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the best of faith in God and striving with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the maintenance of the House by the polytheists and their providing water. And it would not have benefited them with God, despite their associating partners with Him, if they were to build His House and serve Him. God said: They are not equal before God,
h
and God does not guide the wrongdoing people

, meaning: those who claimed that they were the people of construction, so God called them wrongdoers, because of their associating partners with Him, so construction did not benefit them at all. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of al-Nu’man bin Bashir, that a man said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except providing water to the pilgrims!

x: Another said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except maintaining the Sacred Mosque!

Another said: Jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said! Umar rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices near the pulpit of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - and that was on a Friday - but when he prays the Friday prayer, we will enter upon him! Then the verse was revealed: Have you made the providing water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque until His saying:
h
They are not equal in the sight of God

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: It was revealed about Ali, Abbas, Uthman, and Shaibah. They spoke about that, and al-Abbas said: I see myself as abandoning our water-giving! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Continue with your water-giving, for there is good for you in it. ... He said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said:

c: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: It was revealed about Ali and al-Abbas, they spoke about that.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I was told on the authority of Abu Sakhr, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi say: Talhah ibn Shaybah from Banu Abd al-Dar, Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Ali ibn Abi Talib boasted, so Talhah said: I am the owner of the house, I have its key, if I wish I could sleep in it! Abbas said: I am the owner of the water supply and the one who takes care of it, if I wish I could sleep in the mosque! Ali said: I do not know what you are saying, I prayed towards the qiblah six months before the people, and I am the owner of jihad! Then God revealed:
h
Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims
and the maintenance of al-Masjid al-Haram? the whole verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: When the verse:
h
Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims

was revealed, “al-Abbas said: I see myself abandoning our provision of water! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Continue with your provision of water, for there is good in it for you.”

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God?
h
They are not equal in the sight of God

.” He said: Ali, Abbas, and Shaibah bin Othman boasted, and Abbas said: I am the best of you, I provide water to the pilgrims of the House of God! Shaibah said: I maintain the Mosque of God! Ali said: I migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I strive with him in the cause of God! Then God revealed: Those who believed and migrated and striven in the cause of God until permanent bliss.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims

? the verse, the Muslims turned to Al-Abbas and his companions who had been taken captive on the day of Badr, taunting them with polytheism. Al-Abbas said, By God, we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque, free the captives, protect the House, and provide water for the pilgrims! So God revealed,
h
Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims
? the verse.

x: The interpretation of the statement then is: O people, have you considered providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque to be like the faith of one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal to those, and their conditions and positions are not equal before God, because God Almighty does not accept any action other than belief in Him and the Last Day.
h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people

. He says: And God does not grant success to righteous deeds to one who disbelieves in Him and denies His Oneness. The noun was placed in the place of the source in his saying: like one who believes in God, since its meaning was known, as the poet said: By your life, it is not for young men to grow beards, but for young men, every young man is dewy. So he made the report of the young men “that”, and it is as they say: Generosity is Hatim’s, and poetry is Zuhair’s.

evidence.text: So God mentioned their arrogance and their turning away, so He said to the people of the Sacred Sanctuary from the polytheists: My verses were recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels, arrogant, spending their time in idle chatter.

x: This is a judgment from God between the groups of boasters, one of whom boasted of providing water, another of providing custodianship, and another of believing in God and striving in His cause. God the Almighty says: Those who believed in God, and believed in His Oneness from the polytheists, and emigrated the homes of their people, and fought the polytheists in the religion of God, with their wealth and their lives are greater in degree with God, and higher in status with Him, than those who provide water to the pilgrims and maintain the Sacred Mosque, while they are polytheists with God. And those, He says: and those whose characteristics We have described, that they believed, emigrated, and fought, are the successful ones, of Paradise, saved from the Fire.

God Almighty says: He gives good tidings to those who believed, emigrated, and struggled in the way of God, their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, for them, that He has had mercy on them so that He would not punish them, and of His pleasure for them, that He has been pleased with them for their obedience to Him, and their fulfillment of what He has charged them with, and gardens, meaning: and orchards, for them therein is lasting pleasure, that does not disappear or perish, fixed and permanent for them forever.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayr told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said:
m: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God Almighty says: I have given you something better than this! They say: Our Lord, what is better than this? He says: My pleasure.

x: God Almighty says, abiding therein, abiding therein, meaning in the gardens, forever, there is no end to that and no limit, Indeed, God has with Him a great reward, meaning that God Almighty has described these believers with the description He mentioned in this verse, a great reward, a reward for their obedience to their Lord and their performance of the deeds He has charged them with, “and that is the bliss that He has promised them that He will give them in the Hereafter.

God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: Do not take your fathers and brothers as intimate friends to whom you divulge your secrets, and expose to them the faults of Islam and its people, and prefer staying among them over migrating to the abode of Islam, if they prefer disbelief over faith, meaning: if they choose disbelief in God over belief in Him and acknowledging His Oneness, and whoever among you takes them as allies, meaning: whoever among you takes them as intimate friends rather than believers, and prefers staying with them over migrating to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the abode of Islam, then those are the wrongdoers, meaning: those among you who do that are those who disobeyed God's command, so they placed the guardianship in the wrong place, and disobeyed God in His command. It was said: This was revealed as a prohibition from God to the believers from befriending their relatives who did not migrate from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque? He said: They were commanded to emigrate, so Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib said: I will provide water for the pilgrims! And Talhah, the brother of Banu Abdul Dar, said: I am the owner of the Kaaba, so we will not emigrate! So the statement was revealed: Do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies until His statement: God brings about His command, with the conquest, in His command to them to emigrate. All of this was before the conquest of Mecca.

x: The Blessed and Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who have not migrated to the abode of Islam, and are residing in the abode of polytheism: If the residence is with your fathers, sons, brothers, wives, and relatives, and wealth you have acquired, meaning: you have earned it, and commerce in which you fear decline, because you have left your country, and dwellings in which you are pleased, and you have settled in them, are dearer to you, than migrating to God and His Messenger, from the abode of polytheism, and than striving in His cause, meaning: in support of the religion of God which He has chosen, then wait, meaning: then wait, until God brings about His command, until God brings about the conquest of Mecca, and God does not guide the wicked people, meaning: God does not guide to good those who have disobeyed Him and are in His disobedience. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Until God brings about His command, with the fat-ha.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then wait until God brings about His command, the conquest of Mecca.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And wealth that you have acquired
and commerce in which you fear decline, he says: you fear that it will decline so you sell it, and dwellings that please you, he said: they are palaces and homes.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And wealth that you have acquired
, he said: you have acquired it.

x: God Almighty says: God has certainly given you victory, O believers, in places of war where you have prepared yourselves to meet your enemy, and in many scenes where you and they meet,
h
and on the day of Hunayn
, meaning:
h
And on the day of Hunayn

also He gave you victory. And (Hunayn) is a valley, as mentioned, between Mecca and Taif. It was made genitive because it is a masculine name for a masculine. It may be omitted, and it is intended to be the name of the town in which it is located.

i: From this is the saying of the poet:
x: They supported their prophet and strengthened his resolve with Hanin on the day when heroes were helpless.

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Aban Al-Attar told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of Urwa, he said:
m: Hunayn is a valley next to Dhu Al-Majaz. When you were pleased with your great number, and they were, as we were told, twelve thousand that day. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that day: We will not be defeated because of our small number. It was said: This was said by a Muslim man, one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is the saying of God: When your great number pleased you, but it availed you nothing, meaning: your great number availed you nothing, and the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for you, meaning: the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for you. The letter ba here has the meaning of fi, and its meaning is: The earth became narrow for you in its vastness and spaciousness. It is said: (A spacious place), meaning wide. And the spacious area was called (Spacious) because of its spaciousness. Then you turned back in flight, from your enemy in defeat. Turning back, he says: And you turned your backs on them, and that is defeat. The Blessed and Exalted is He informs them that victory is in His hand and from Him, and that it is not due to great numbers or great force, and that He gives victory to the few over the many if He wills, and He leaves the many and the few alone, so He defeats the many. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

m: "Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: "
h
God has certainly helped you in many battlefields and on the day of Hunayn

," until he reached: "And that is the reward of the disbelievers," he said: "Hunayn," is between Mecca and Taif, where the Prophet of God fought Hawazin and Thaqif. He said: And it was mentioned to us that twelve thousand went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day: ten thousand of the Muhajireen and Ansar, and two thousand of the freed slaves. And it was mentioned to us that a man said on that day: We will not be defeated today due to the large number! He said: And it was mentioned to us that the freed slaves fled on that day with the people, and fled from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he got off his gray mule. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God said: O Lord, give me what You promised me! He said: And Al-Abbas was holding the reins of the Messenger of God's mule, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Call: O group of Ansar, O group of Muhajireen! So he began calling the Ansar, thigh by thigh, then he said: Call the people of Surat Al-Baqarah. He said: The people came in one group. The Prophet of God (peace be upon him) turned around and saw a group of Ansar. He said: Are there others with you? They said: O Prophet of God, by God, if you had gone to Barak al-Ghamad in Dhi Yaman, we would have been with you. Then God sent down His victory, defeated their enemy, and the Muslims retreated. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) took a handful of dirt - or a handful of pebbles - and threw it in the faces of the infidels, and said: May your faces be disfigured! So they were defeated. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) gathered the spoils and came to al-Ji'ranah, he divided the spoils of Hunayn with it, and brought together some people, including Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis, the Ansar said: This man has believed and preferred his people! report of this reached the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) while he was in a leather tent of his, so he said: O group of Ansar, what is this that has reached me? Were you not astray and then God guided you, and were you lowly and then God honored you, and were you and were you! Saad bin Ubadah may God have mercy on him said: Give me permission to speak! He said: Speak. He said: As for your saying: (You were astray and then God guided you), we were like that, (And were you lowly and then God honored you), the Arabs knew that there was no tribe of the Arabs more fortified for what was behind them than us! Umar said: O Saad, do you know who spoke? He said: Yes! I am speaking to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the Ansar were to take a valley and the people were to take a valley, I would take the valley of the Ansar, and if it were not for the migration, I would be one of the Ansar. He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: The Ansar are my burden and my family, so accept their good deeds and overlook their bad deeds. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O group of Ansar, are you not pleased that the people return with the camels and sheep, and you return with the Messenger of God to your homes? The Ansar said: We are pleased with God and His Messenger, and by God we only said that out of concern for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God and His Messenger believe you and excuse you.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: “It was mentioned to us that the mother of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who breastfed him, or his wet-nurse from Banu Sa’d ibn Bakr, came to him and asked him for the captives of the day of Hunayn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not own them, but I only have my share of them. But come to me tomorrow and ask me while the people are with me, for if I give you my share, the people will give you. So she came the next day, and he spread out a garment for her so she sat on it, then she asked him, and he gave her his share. When the people saw that, they gave her their shares.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: God has certainly given you victory in many battles, the verse, “that a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn said: O Messenger of God, we will not be defeated today due to fewness! And he was impressed by the large number of people, and they were twelve thousand. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched, and they were entrusted with the man’s word, and they fled from the Messenger of God, except for al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, who was killed that day in front of him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: Where are the Ansar? Where are those who pledged allegiance under the tree? So the people retreated, and God sent down the angels with victory. So they defeated the polytheists that day,” and that is His saying: Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Kathir ibn Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: “When the day of Hunayn came, the Muslims and the polytheists met, and the Muslims turned back that day. He said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one was with him except Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, holding the reins of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not spare any effort to hasten towards the polytheists. He said: So I came and took hold of his bridle, and he was on his grey mule, and he said: O Abbas, call the companions of the samura! And I was a man of high voice, so I announced in my loudest voice: Where are the companions of the samura! So they turned around like camels when they are herded to their young, saying: (Ya Labbayk, Ya Labbayk, Ya Labbayk), and the polytheists came. So they met with the Muslims, and the Ansar called out: (O group of Ansar), then the call was limited to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, so they called out: (O Banu al-Harith ibn Al-Khazraj), so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at their fighting while he was on his mule, as if he was tall, and said: This is when the battle is fierce! Then he took pebbles in his hand and threw them at them, then he said: They are defeated, by the Lord of the Kaaba, they are defeated, by the Lord of the Kaaba! He said: By God, their matter continued to be in retreat, and they were alone and weak, until God defeated them. He said: It was as if I could see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, running after them on his mule.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab:
m: "That day they captured six thousand captives, then their people came as Muslims after that, and they said: O Messenger of God, you are the best of people and the most pious of people, and Surat al-Tawbah 9:25 God has already given you victory in many battlefields,
h
and on the day of Hunayn

, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, became strait for you; then you turned back, fleeing. you have taken our children, our women, and our wealth! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have with me those whom you see, and the best of words are the most truthful. Choose: either your children and your women, or your wealth. They said: We did not consider ancestry equal to anything! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: These people came to me as Muslims, and we gave them the choice between children and wealth, and they did not consider ancestry equal to anything. So whoever has something of them in his possession and is willing to return it, let him do so, and whoever does not, let him give it to us, and let it be a loan to us until we obtain something, and we will give it to him in its place. They said: O Prophet of God, we are satisfied and we submit! He said: I do not know, perhaps there are among you those who are not satisfied, so order your leaders to report that to us.

c: So he reported it to us.
m: The mystics have accepted and submitted to him.

c: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, Muammil narrated to us, Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, Yaʿla bin Ataʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hammam, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman - meaning al-Fahri -
m: who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Hunayn. When the sun had set, I put on my cloak and mounted my horse until I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the shade of a tree. I said: O Messenger of God, it is time for the afternoon prayer. He said: Yes! So he called: O Bilal! O Bilal! So Bilal got up from under a tamarisk tree and approached as if his shadow was the shadow of a bird. He said: At your service and your pleasure, and my soul is your ransom, O Messenger of God! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Saddle my horse! So he brought out a saddle with its flaps stuffed with palm fibers, in which there was neither arrogance nor pride. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mounted, and we fought them day and night. When the two horses met, the Muslims turned their backs, as God said. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called: O servants of God. God, O group of emigrants!
