He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned from his horse, took a handful of dirt and threw it in their faces, and they turned and fled. Yaʿla ibn ʿAtaʿ said: Their sons told me on the authority of their fathers that they said: There was not one of us left whose eyes were not filled with that dirt. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Baraʿ and a man from Qays ask him: Did you flee from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn? Al-Baraʿ said: But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not flee, and the Hawazin were archers at that time, and when we attacked them they fled, so we attacked the spoils, and they met us with arrows. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his white mule - and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding its reins - and he was saying: I am the prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said: A man asked him: O Abu Ammarah, was the day of Hunayn an orphan? Al-Baraa’ said, and I was listening: I bear witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not turn his back that day, and Abu Sufyan was leading his mule. So when the polytheists surrounded him, he dismounted and began to say: I am the prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib No one was seen that day who was more severe than him. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated, on the authority of ʿAwf al-Aʿrabi, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Rahman, the freed slave of Umm Barthan, who said: A man who was one of the polytheists on the day of Hunayn narrated to me: When we and the companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him, met each other, they did not stop to milk a sheep for us until we defeated them. While we were leading them, we came to the owner of the gray mule, and we were met by white, handsome men who said to us: “May your faces be disfigured! Go back!” So we went back, and the people rode us, and that was it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Yaqub, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, he said:
m: God supported his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn with five thousand marked angels. He said: And on that day God called the Ansar believers. He said: So God sent down His tranquility upon the Messenger of God and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers that they had not seen.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And on the day of Hunayn
, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, he said: They were twelve thousand.

c: Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Adami told us, he said, Ma’n bin Isa told us, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Sa’ib Al-Ta’ifi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yazid bin Aamer, who said:
m: When the Muslims were exposed on the day of Hunayn, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck the ground with his hand and took a handful of dirt, and turned to the polytheists as they were following the Muslims, and threw it in their faces and said: Go back, may your faces be disfigured! He said: So we turned back, and no one met anyone except that he was wiping the dirt from his eyes. And on his authority, on the authority of Yazid bin Aamer Al-Suwai’i, he said: It was said to him: O Abu Hajiz, what did you find of the terror that God cast into the hearts of the polytheists? He said: Abu Hajiz was with the polytheists on the day of Hunayn, so he would take a pebble and throw it into a basin and it would make a sound, then he would say: There was something like this in our stomachs.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan bin Arfa narrated to us, saying: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman narrated to me, on the authority of Awf,
m: saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman, the freed slave of Umm Barthan - Umm Barthum - saying: A man who was among the polytheists on the day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: When we and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met on the day of Hunayn, they did not milk a sheep for us. He said: When we defeated them, we began to drive them behind them until we reached the owner of the white mule, and it was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Then handsome, white men met us at his place and said to us: May your faces be disfigured, go back! He said: So we fled, and they rode on our shoulders, and that was it.

x: God Almighty says: Then after the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for you, and the enemies turned their backs on you, God removed the calamity from you by sending down tranquility - which is security and peace - upon you. We have already explained that it is a fa’ila from sukun in what has already been said in this book of ours, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And He sent down soldiers you did not see, which are the angels mentioned in the hadiths that have already been mentioned,
h
and He punished those who disbelieved

, meaning: God punished those who denied His Oneness and the message of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by killing them, taking their families and children captive, stealing their money, and humiliating them. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers, meaning: This is what We did to them of killing and taking captive.
The recompense of the disbelievers, meaning: It is the reward of those who denied His Oneness and the message of His Messenger.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And He punished those who disbelieved
, meaning: He killed them with the sword.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawood Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id:
m: h
And He punished those who disbelieved
, he said: with defeat and killing.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He punished those who disbelieved
, and that is the recompense of the disbelievers, he said: whoever remained of them.

x: God Almighty says: Then God will be gracious in granting success to repent and return to Him, after His punishment with which He punished those of them who perished by the sword, upon whomever He wills, meaning: God will accept the repentance of whomever He wills of the living, and will accept him into His obedience, and God is Forgiving, of the sins of those who repent and return to Him from them and others, Merciful, of them, so He will not punish them after their repentance, nor will He hold them accountable for them after their repentance.
God Almighty says to those who believe in Him and His Messenger, and acknowledge His Oneness, that the polytheists are nothing but impure.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of impure and the reason for which they were called that.

Some of them said: He called them that because they are ritually impure and do not wash themselves. He said: They are impure and should not approach the Sacred Mosque, because a person in a state of ritual impurity should not enter the mosque.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The polytheists are unclean

, I do not know of Qatada who did not say: unclean means ritual impurity. And with it, “On the authority of Muammar, he said, ‘It has reached me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Hudhayfah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his hand, and Hudhayfah said, ‘O Messenger of God, I am in a state of ritual impurity.’ He said, ‘The believer is not impure.’”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, indeed,
h
the polytheists are unclean
, meaning: they are impure.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: The polytheists are nothing but the filth of a pig or a dog. This is a statement narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas from an unreliable source, so we disliked mentioning it. And His statement:
h
So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs

, means that He is saying to the believers: Do not let them approach the Sacred Mosque by entering the Sanctuary. Rather, He meant by that preventing them from entering the Sanctuary, because if they enter the Sanctuary, they have approached the Sacred Mosque.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of this.
Some of them said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ said:
m: The entire Haram is a qiblah and a mosque. He said: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque, he did not mean the mosque alone, rather he meant Mecca and the Haram. He said that more than once. It was mentioned about Omar bin Abdul Aziz in this regard:

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, he said, Abu Amr told us:
m: Omar bin Abdul Aziz wrote: (Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims), and he followed in his prohibition the words of God:
h
The polytheists are unclean

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The polytheists are impure. He said: Do not shake hands with them, and whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution. As for his saying,
h
After this year of theirs
, it is after the year in which Ali, may God have mercy on him, declared innocence, and that was the year in which Abu Bakr led the people on Hajj, which was the ninth year of the Hijra, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs

, which is the year in which Abu Bakr performed Hajj, and Ali, may God have mercy on him, called the call to prayer, and that was nine years after the migration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj al-Ju’a the following year, and he did not perform Hajj before it or after it. And His saying:
h
And if you fear poverty

, He says to the believers: And if you fear need and poverty, by preventing the polytheists from approaching the Sacred Mosque, then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. It is said: He provides for a family and children, and from it the poet said: The poor man does not know when he will become rich, and the rich man does not know when he will be dependent.

c: It was narrated from some of them
m: that some Arabs say in poverty: Aal ya’ul with the letter waw. It was mentioned on the authority of Omar bin Faid that he used to interpret his saying:
h
And if you fear poverty

, to mean: When you fear. And he would say: The people had feared, and that is similar to the saying of someone to his father: If you are my father, then honor me, meaning: When you are my father. This was said to them because the believers feared that if the polytheists stopped entering the sanctuary, their trade would be cut off, and that harm would come to them. God secured them from poverty, and compensated them for what they hated to be cut off from them with something better for them than it, which was the jizya. He said to them: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful to subdued.

x: Some people said: By sending rain upon them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, indeed,
h
the polytheists are unclean
h
so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs

, he said: When God banished the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque, Satan cast sadness into the hearts of the believers. He said: From where will you eat, when the polytheists have been banished and the caravans have been cut off from them! Then God said:
h
And if you fear poverty
, then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills, so He commanded them to fight the People of the Book, and He enriched them from His bounty.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed
, indeed,
h
the polytheists are unclean
, so let them not approach Al-Masjid Al-Haram
h
after this year of theirs

, he said: The polytheists used to come to the House, and bring food with them, and trade in it. When they were forbidden to come to the House, the Muslims said: Where will the food come from? So God revealed:
h
And if you fear poverty
, then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills, so He sent down rain upon them, and their goodness increased, until the polytheists left them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Ali bin Saleh, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
The polytheists are unclean
, the verse, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Hannad, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Waqid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: When the verse:
h
The polytheists are unclean
h
so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs

, was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were upset by that and said: Who will bring us our food, and who will bring us our provisions? Then the verse:
h
And if you fear poverty
, then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills, was revealed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Waqid,
m: the freed slave of Zaid ibn Khalidah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said: The polytheists used to come to them with trade, so this verse was revealed:
h
The polytheists are unclean
until His saying: Poverty, he said: poverty, Then God will enrich you from His bounty.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, he said: The Muslims said:
m: We used to gain from their trade and their sales, so the following was revealed:
h
The polytheists are unclean
until His saying: from His bounty.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard my father - I think he said: Abu Jaʿfar told us - on the authority of ʿAtiyya, he said: When it was said: (And no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year), they said: We used to take a share of their sales during the season! He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
O you who have believed, indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. And if you fear poverty, then God will enrich you from His bounty
, meaning: because of what they missed of their sales.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And if you fear poverty
, then God will enrich you from His bounty, he said: the jizya.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: The polytheists were expelled from Mecca, and that was difficult for the Muslims and they said: Surat al-Tawbah 9:28
h
O you who have believed
h
the polytheists are unclean
, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram
h
after this year of theirs
h
And if you fear poverty

, then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, God is Knowing and Wise. We used to get trade and provisions from them! So God revealed: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
And if you fear poverty

, God will enrich you from His bounty, that some Muslims used to gather the caravans, and when the Surah Bara’ah was revealed about fighting the polytheists wherever they were found, and that they should lie in wait for them at every ambush, Satan cast into the hearts of the believers: How will you live when you have been commanded to fight the people of the caravan? God knew what He knew of that, so He said: Obey Me, and carry out My command, and obey My Messenger, for I will enrich you from My bounty. So God entrusted them with that.

c: Muhammad ibn Umar told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The polytheists are unclean

to his statement: Then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills, he said: The believers said: We used to get from the merchandise of the polytheists! So God promised them that He would enrich them from His bounty, in exchange for them not letting them approach the Sacred Mosque. So this verse, with the beginning of Bara’ah, in the reading, and with the end of it in the interpretation: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, to his statement: with their own hands while they are humbled, when Muhammad and his companions were ordered to go to the Battle of Tabuk.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When God banished the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they used to come with sales that benefited the Muslims. So God, the Most High, revealed:
h
And if you fear poverty

, God will enrich you from His bounty, so He enriched them with this tax, the ongoing tribute, which they take month by month, year by year. No polytheist may approach the Sacred Mosque after their year under any circumstances, except the one who pays the tribute, or a slave of a Muslim man.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Abu al-Zubayr told us:
m: that he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say regarding his statement:
h
The polytheists are unclean
h
so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs
, unless he is a slave, or one of the People of the Covenant. ... He said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs
, he said: Except for a person who pays the jizya, or after that for a man from the Muslims.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abdul Aziz bin Jurayj, he said, Abu al-Zubayr told me:
m: that he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say about this verse:
h
The polytheists are unclean
, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque, unless they are slaves, or one of those who pay the jizyah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you fear poverty
, then God will enrich you from His bounty, he said: God enriched them with the ongoing jizyah, month by month, and year by year.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir:
m: h
The polytheists are unclean
, so they should not approach the Sacred Mosque
h
after this year of theirs
. He said: No polytheist or dhimmi should approach the Sacred Mosque
h
after this year of theirs

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
The polytheists are unclean
, so do not approach the Sacred Mosque
h
after this year of theirs

, even if you fear poverty. That is because the people said: The markets will be cut off from us, trade will be destroyed, and the amenities we used to gain from them will be gone! So God, the Almighty, said:
h
And if you fear poverty

, then God will enrich you from His bounty, from another source, If He wills until His saying: while they are humbled. So in this there is compensation for what you feared from the cutting off of those markets, so God compensated them with what He cut off from them from the matter of polytheism, what He gave them from the necks of the People of the Book from the jizya. As for his saying: Indeed, God is Knowing and Wise, its meaning is: Indeed, God is Knowing of what your souls tell you, O believers, of fear of poverty for it, by preventing the polytheists from approaching the Sacred Mosque, and other interests of His servants, Wise in His management of them and the management of all of His creation.

evidence.text: So this verse, with the beginning of Bara’ah, in the reading, and with the end of it in the interpretation: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, to his statement: with their own hands while they are humbled, when Muhammad and his companions were ordered to go to the Battle of Tabuk.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Fight, O believers, the people, who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, meaning: they do not believe in Paradise or Hell, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not follow the religion of truth, meaning: they do not obey God with the obedience of truth,
h
of those who were given the Scripture

, meaning the Jews and Christians. Everyone who obeys a king or has authority is his debtor. It is said: So-and-so owed so-and-so a debt, so he owes him a debt. Zuhair said: If you settled in the atmosphere of Banu Asad in the religion of Amr and Fadak came between us His saying:
h
Of those who were given the Scripture
, meaning those who were given the Book of God, and they are the people of the Torah and the Gospel, until they pay the jizyah.

And (al-jizya), the verb from: (So-and-so rewarded so-and-so what he owed), if he paid it, (he rewards him), and (al-jizya) is like (al-qa’dah) and (al-salah). The meaning of the words: until they give the tax on their necks, which they give to the Muslims to protect them. As for his saying: from hand, he means: from his hand to the hand of the one to whom he gives it. Likewise, the Arabs say about anyone who gives something to someone unwillingly or unwillingly: He gave it to him with his hand, and from hand. This is similar to their saying: I spoke to him face to mouth, and I met him hand to hand, and also: I gave it to him hand to hand. As for his saying:
h
And they are humiliated
, its meaning is:
h
And they are humiliated

and subjugated. The lowly and contemptible is called: Saghir. He mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his command to fight the Romans.
After it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led the Battle of Tabuk.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are subdued,” when Muhammad and his companions were ordered to go on the expedition to Tabuk.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the young ones that God meant in this place.
Some of them said: He should give it while standing and the recipient should sit.
Who said that?

c: Abdul Rahman bin Bishr Al-Naysaburi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Saad, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are subdued, he said: That is, you take it while you are sitting, and he is standing.

x: Others said: The meaning of his statement:
h
Until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are humbled
, is about themselves, with their own hands, walking with them, unwillingly. This is a statement narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, from a viewpoint that is questionable.
Others said: Giving them to him is the little ones.
The people of interpretation differed about who said: “Ezra is the son of God.”
Some of them said: It was one man, Phinehas.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: I heard Abdullah bin Ubayd bin Umair say:
h
And the Jews say
, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’ He said: One man said it. They said: His name is Phinehas. And they said: He is the one who said: Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich.
r
(Al Imran 3:181)
Others said: Rather, that was the saying of a group of them.

x: Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Salam bin Mishkam, Numan bin Awfa, Shas bin Qais, and Malik bin Al-Saif came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qiblah, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God? So God revealed concerning that, in their statement:
h
And the Jews say
, ‘Ezra is the son of God,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Messiah is the son of God.’ to
h
How are they deluded

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And the Jews say

, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’ They only said, He is the son of God, because Ezra was among the People of the Book, and they had the Torah, so they acted according to it as God willed them to act, then they lost it and acted unjustly, and the Ark was among them. So when God saw that they had lost the Torah and acted according to their whims, God lifted the Ark from them, and made them forget the Torah, and abrogated it from their chests, and God sent upon them a disease, so their stomachs became loose until a man could walk with his liver, until they forgot the Torah, and it was abrogated from their chests, and among them was Ezra. So they remained as long as God willed them to remain after the Torah was abrogated from their chests, and Ezra had previously been one of their scholars, so Ezra called upon God, and implored Him to return to him what had been abrogated from his chest of the Torah. While he was praying and supplicating to God, a light from God descended and entered his body, and what had been lost from his body of the Torah returned to him. He called out to his people, saying: O my people, God has given me the Torah and returned it to me! So he clung to them, teaching them. They stayed as long as God willed while he taught them. Then the Ark descended after that, after it had gone from them. When they saw the Ark, they showed what was in it to the one who Ezra was teaching them, and they found it to be the same. They said: By God, this Ezra was not given except that he is the son of God!!

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “And the Jews said, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’ They said that because the giants had defeated them and killed them, and they had taken the Torah, and their scholars who remained had gone, and they had buried the books of the Torah in the mountains. Ezra was a young boy who used to worship on the mountaintops, and he would not come down except on a feast day. So the young boy began to cry and say, ‘O Lord, You have left the Children of Israel without a scholar!’ He kept crying until his eyelashes fell off. Once he went down to the feast day, and when he returned, he saw a woman standing before him at one of those graves, crying and saying, ‘O you who fed you, and O you who clothed you!’ He said to her, ‘Woe to you! Who fed you, or clothed you, or gave you drink, or benefited you before this man?’ She said, ‘God!’ He said, ‘Indeed, God is alive and has not died!’ She said, ‘O Ezra, who taught the scholars before the Children of Israel?’ He said, ‘God!’ She said, ‘Then why are you crying over them?’ When he knew that he had been deprived, he turned back. She called him and said: O Ezra, when you wake up tomorrow, go to such and such a river and wash yourself in it, then go out and pray two rak'ahs, for an old man will come to you and whatever he gives you, take it. So when morning came, Ezra went to that river, washed himself in it, then went out and prayed two rak'ahs. The old man came and said: Open your mouth! So he opened his mouth and threw into it something like a huge coal, gathered together like bottles, three times. Then Ezra returned, and he was the most knowledgeable of people about Surat al-Tawbah 9:30
h
And the Jews say
, "Ezra is the son of God," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God." That is their statement with their mouths;
h
they imitate the statement of those who disbelieved before
. God's destruction!
h
How are they deluded

? the Torah, and said: O Children of Israel, I have come to you with the Torah! They said: O Ezra, I was not a liar! So he tied a pen to each of his fingers and wrote with all of his fingers, and he wrote the entire Torah. When the scholars returned, they were told about Ezra. Those scholars extracted their books that they had buried from the Torah in the mountains, and they were buried in a hole. They compared them to the Torah of Ezra, and they found it to be similar. They said: God did not give you this except that you are his son! There are different readings of this: The majority of the people of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians read it as: “And the Jews said, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’” They do not add a tanween to Ezra.

x: Some of the Meccans and Kufians read it as: Uzair ibn God, with the tanween of Uzair. He said: It is a proper noun, even though it is foreign, because of its lightness. However, it is not attributed to God, so it is like saying: Zayd ibn Abdullah, and he put the son in the place of the predicate. If it was attributed to God, the correct way would be, if the son was the predicate, the procedure and the tanween, so how is it when it is attributed to someone other than his father? As for those who left the tanween of Uzair, then since the ba’ of ibn was quiescent with the quiescent tanween, and two quiescent letters met, the first of them was deleted because it was too heavy to move.
To find me with the prince outside and on the canal, trampled by cunning If the peaceful one is covered, he will flee The letter noon was deleted for the consonant that preceded it.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who read: ʿUzair, son of God, with the tanween of ʿUzair, because the Arabs do not add a tanween to nouns if the son is an adjective for the noun, but they add a tanween if it is a predicate, like their saying: This is Zayd, son of ʿAbdullah, so they wanted to make the predicate of Zayd that he is the son of ʿAbdullah, and they did not want to make the son an adjective for him, and the son in this instance is the predicate of ʿUzair, because those whom God mentioned that they said that, only informed about ʿUzair that he was like that, and if they were lying and fabricating against God by saying that. And the Christians say, ‘The Messiah is the son of God.’ That is their statement with their mouths;
h
they imitate the statement of those who disbelieved before
, meaning the Jews’ statement, Ezra is the son of God.

He says: The statement of these people in lying about God and slandering Him and attributing the Messiah to God as a son is similar to the Jews’ lie and slander against God in attributing Ezra to God as a son. It is not appropriate for God to have a son, glory be to Him. Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are obedient to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They imitate the statement of those who disbelieved before
, meaning: they resemble.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They imitate the statement of those who disbelieved before them
, the Christians imitated the statement of the Jews before them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before, the Christians imitate the saying of the Jews regarding Ezra.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before, meaning: the Christians, they imitate the saying of the Jews.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They imitate the statement of those who disbelieved before

, meaning: They said what the idolaters said. It has been said that the meaning of this is: They are narrating with their words the words of the idolaters, who said: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other. There are different readings of this. The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: (yadahun), without a hamza. Asim read it: They imitate, with a hamza, and it is the language of Thaqif. They are two languages. It is said: I competed with him on such-and-such, I competed with him, and I competed with him on it, meaning I helped him and supported him.

x: The correct reading in this regard is to omit the hamza, because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions and the classical language.
As for his saying:
h
May God fight them
, its meaning, according to what was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas, is:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
May God fight them
, meaning: May God curse them. And everything in the Qur’an that says fight is a curse. Ibn Jurayj said about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his saying:
h
May God fight them
, meaning the Christians, is a word from the speech of the Arabs. As for those who know the Arabic language, they say: It means:
h
May God kill them

. The Arabs say: (May God kill you) and (May God kill her), meaning: May God kill you. They said: (May God kill you) is easier than (May God kill him). They mentioned that they say: May God make him miserable as long as he lives, meaning: May God make him miserable as long as he lives. They said: The meaning of his saying,
h
May God kill them

, is like his saying, The liars were killed, (al-Dhariyat 51:10), and The people of the trench were killed, (al-Buruj 85:4), one meaning of astonishment. If what they said is as they said, then it is one of the rare speeches that came in a way that is not analogical, because (faʿilat) hardly comes as a verb except from two, like their saying: (I quarrelled with so-and-so), and (I fought him), and the like. And they claimed that their saying (may God pardon you) is from it, and that its meaning is: may God pardon you, in the sense of praying for the one who prayed for him to pardon him from evil. His saying:
h
How are they deluded
? He says: What is the direction that leads them and makes them deviate? And how are they turned away from the truth? We have explained that with its evidence in what has passed before.

evidence.text: There are different readings of this: The majority of the people of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians read it as: “And the Jews said, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’”
Some of the Meccans and Kufians read it as: Uzair ibn God, with the tanween of Uzair.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who read: ʿUzair, son of God, with the tanween of ʿUzair, because the Arabs do not add a tanween to nouns if the son is an adjective for the noun, but they add a tanween if it is a predicate, like their saying: This is Zayd, son of ʿAbdullah, so they wanted to make the predicate of Zayd that he is the son of ʿAbdullah, and they did not want to make the son an adjective for him, and the son in this instance is the predicate of ʿUzair, because those whom God mentioned that they said that, only informed about ʿUzair that he was like that, and if they were lying and fabricating against God by saying that.
The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: (yadahun), without a hamza.
Asim read it: They imitate, with a hamza, and it is the language of Thaqif.
Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading in this regard is to omit the hamza, because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions and the classical language.

x: God Almighty says: The Jews took their rabbis, who are the scholars. I have explained the interpretation of this with its evidence in the previous part of this book of ours. The singular of them is (Habr), and (Habr) with the letter ha’ broken or opened. Yunus al-Jarmi, as mentioned about him, claims that he only heard it as Habr with a kasra on the ha. He uses as evidence the saying of the al-Nas 114:This is the ink of a scholar, meaning the ink of a scholar. Al-Farra’ mentioned that he heard it as Habra and Habra with a kasra or a fatha on the ha.
And the Christians (their monks), who are the owners of the monasteries and the people of diligence in their religion among them, such as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: They took their rabbis and monks, he said: their readers and scholars. Lords besides God, meaning: masters for them besides God, whom they obey in disobeying God, so they make lawful for them what they make lawful of what God has forbidden for them, and they forbid what they forbid for them of what God has permitted for them, such as:

c: Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahan told me, he said, Abd Al-Salam bin Harb Al-Mala’i told us, on the authority of Ghatif bin A’yan, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d,
m: “On the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting in Surat Bara’ah: “
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God
,” so he said: As for them, they did not worship them, but they were permissible for them and they were permissible for them.”

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, they said: Malik bin Ismail narrated to us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Abd al-Salam bin Harb, he said: Ghatif bin A’yan narrated to us, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, “On the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I had a cross of gold around my neck, and he said: O Adi, throw this idol off your neck! He said: So I threw it away, and I came to him while he was reciting Surah Bara’ah, and he recited this verse: “
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God

.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, we do not worship them! He said: Do they not forbid what God has permitted and you forbid it, and they permit what God has forbidden and you permit it? I said: Yes! He said: That is their worship.” The wording is from the hadith of Abu Kurayb.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abd Al-Salam bin Harb Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ghadif, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting Surat Al-Bara’ah. When he recited:
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God

, I said: O Messenger of God, did they not pray to them? He said: You have spoken the truth, but they used to make lawful what God made unlawful and consider it lawful, and they used to forbid what God made lawful for them and consider it unlawful.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Hudhayfah:
m: That he was asked about His statement:
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God
, did they worship them? He said: No, if they made something permissible for them, they made it permissible, and if they made something forbidden for them, they made it forbidden.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: It was said to Abu Hudhayfah, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: But they made permissible for them what was forbidden, so they made it permissible, and they made forbidden for them what was permissible, so they made it forbidden.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: It was said to Hudhayfah: What do you think of the statement of God: They took their rabbis as their own? He said: They did not fast for them nor pray for them, but if they made something permissible for them, they made it permissible, and if they made something forbidden for them that God had made permissible for them, they made it forbidden. That was their lordship. ... He said, Jarir and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari: They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. He said: They went to what God had made lawful and made it unlawful, and they went to what God had made unlawful and made it lawful, so they obeyed them in that. So God made their obedience their worship. If they had said to Him: Worship Us, they would not have done so.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: A man asked Hudhayfah and said: O Abu Abdullah, what do you think of His statement:
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God
, did they worship them? He said: No, if they made something permissible for them, they made it permissible, and if they made something forbidden for them, they made it forbidden.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Adi told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: They took their rabbis and monks as lords, he said: in obedience.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God
, meaning: They made their obedience seem attractive to them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God. Abdullah bin Abbas said: They did not order them to prostrate to them, but they ordered them to disobey God and they obeyed them, so God called them lords for that.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah:
m: They took their rabbis and monks as lords. He said: I said to Abu al-Aaliyah: How was the lordship that existed among the Children of Israel? He said: They did not curse our rabbis for anything that had passed. Whatever they commanded us to do, we obeyed, and whatever they forbade us from doing, we refrained from saying, and they found in the Book of God what they commanded and what they forbade, so they sought advice from men and threw the Book of God behind their backs.

c: Bishr bin Suwaid told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Hudhayfah:
m: They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, he said: They did not worship them, but they obeyed them in committing sins. As for his saying:
h
And the Messiah
, son of Mary, its meaning is: They took their rabbis and monks
h
and the Messiah
, son of Mary, as lords besides God. As for his statement:
h
And they were commanded only to worship one God
, what he means by it is: And these Jews and Christians who took the rabbis, monks,
h
and the Messiah

as lords were commanded only to worship one God, and to obey only one Lord, without various lords, and He is God to whom all things are to be worshipped, and all creation is to be obeyed, and who deserves judgment from all His creation for His Oneness and Lordship, There is no god but Him. The Most High says: Divinity is only due to the One Whom creation was commanded to worship, and all servants are obligated to obey Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him, meaning: To purify and sanctify God from what they associate with Him in His obedience and Lordship, those who say: Ezra is the son of God, and those who say: The Messiah is the son of God, those who take their rabbis as lords besides God.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, They took their rabbis and monks, he said: their readers and scholars.
He said: So I threw it away, and I came to him while he was reciting Surah Bara’ah, and he recited this verse: “They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God.”

x: God Almighty says: These people who take their rabbis, monks, and Jesus, son of Mary, as lords, want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, meaning that they try, by denying the religion of God with which He sent His Messenger, and by turning people away from it with their tongues, to invalidate it, which is the light that God made a radiance for His creation. But God refuses except to perfect His light, so that His religion is elevated, His word is made manifest, and the truth with which He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is completed. Even though the disbelievers dislike God’s completion of it, meaning those who deny it and reject it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, he said: They want to extinguish Islam with their words.

x: God Almighty says: God is He who refuses except to perfect His religion, even though those who deny and reject it hate it, Who has sent His Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with guidance, meaning: with an explanation of God’s obligations to His creation, and all that is necessary for them, and with the religion of truth, which is Islam, to make it prevail over all religions, meaning: to make Islam prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists hate it, with God making it prevail over them.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying:
h
So that He may make it prevail over all religions
Some of them said: That will be when Jesus comes out, when all religions will become one.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, Shaqiq told us, Thabit Al-Haddad Abu Al-Muqaddam told me, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That He may make it prevail over all religions
, he said: When Jesus, son of Mary, comes out.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, he said,
m: someone who heard Abu Jaafar tell me: To make him prevail over all religions, he said: When Jesus, peace be upon him, comes out, the people of every religion will follow him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: to teach him all the laws of religion, and to inform him of them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That He may make him prevail over all religions
, he said: So that God may make His Prophet prevail over all matters of religion, so that He may give it all to him, and nothing of it may be hidden from Him. The polytheists and the Jews hated that.

x: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, and have acknowledged the Oneness of your Lord, indeed many of the scholars and reciters from among Israel, from the Jews and Christians, devour the wealth of people unjustly, meaning: they take bribes in their rulings, and they distort the Book of God, and they write with their own hands and then say: (This is from God), and they take a small price for it from their lowest people, and they hinder [people] from the way of God, meaning: and they prevent whoever wants to enter Islam from entering it, by forbidding them from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly. As for the rabbis, they are from the Jews. As for the monks, they are from the Christians. As for the path of God, it is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment

God Almighty says: Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of people unjustly, and He also consumes it with them: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment, meaning: Give tidings to many of the rabbis and monks who devour the wealth of people unjustly, and who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God, of a painful punishment for them on the Day of Resurrection, painful from God. Scholars differed about the meaning of treasure.

Some of them said: It is all money on which zakat is due, but its zakat is not paid. They said: What he meant by his statement: and they do not spend it in the way of God is that they do not pay its zakat.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: All wealth on which zakat has been paid is not a treasure, even if it is buried. And all wealth on which zakat has not been paid is the treasure that God mentioned in the Qur’an, and its owner will be branded with it, even if it is not buried.

c: Al-Hasan bin Al-Junaid narrated to us, he said: Saeed bin Muslimah narrated to us, he said: Ismail bin Umayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: He said: All wealth from which zakat has been paid is not a treasure, even if it is buried. And all wealth from which zakat has not been paid, even if it is not buried, is a treasure.

c: Abu Al-Saib told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: Any wealth on which zakat has been paid is not a treasure, even if it is buried in the ground. Any wealth on which zakat has not been paid is a treasure with which its owner is branded, even if it is on the surface of the earth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said:
m: That which you pay zakat on is not a treasure. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Amri, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: That which you have paid zakat on is not a treasure, even if it is under seven earths. And that which you have not paid zakat on is a treasure, even if it is visible. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: What you pay zakat on is not a treasure.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: As for those who hoard gold and silver, these are the people of the Qiblah, and treasure is that which has not been paid its zakat, even if it is on the surface of the earth, even if it is little. And if it is a lot and its zakat has been paid, then it is not a treasure.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: I said to Amer: There is money on a shelf between the sky and the earth, and its zakat is not paid. Is it being hoarded? He said: It will be branded on the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: Any money that exceeds four thousand dirhams is a treasure, whether zakat is paid from it or not.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha, on the authority of Ja’dah bin Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God have mercy on him, who said: Four thousand dirhams or less is expenses, and whatever is more than that is treasure.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha, on the authority of Ja’dah ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Sha’bi told us, he said: Abu Hasin told me, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ja’dah bin Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God have mercy on him, regarding his statement:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver
, he said: Four thousand dirhams or less is spending, and anything above that is a treasure.

x: Others said: Treasure is all the money that is left over from what its owner needs.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ubayd God ibn Muadh told us, my father told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abd al-Wahid:
m: that he heard Abu Mujib say: “The hilt of Abu Hurayrah’s sword was made of silver, but Abu Dharr forbade him from it and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever leaves yellow or white, it will be branded with it.”

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-A’mash and Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, who said:
m: When the verse:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

and do not spend it in the way of God was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Destroy the gold! Destruction of the silver! He said it three times. He said: This was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? Umar said: I know that for you! He said: O Messenger of God, your companions were distressed and they said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? He said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps one of you in his religion.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Thawban,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Jaʿd, he said:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

and do not spend it in the way of God’, the Muhajirun said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? Umar said: Ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it! He said: I caught up with him on a camel and said: O Messenger of God, the Muhajirun said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a believing wife who helps each one of you in his religion.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said:
m: “A man from the people of the Suffa died, and a dinar was found in his waistband, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A cautery! Then another died, and two dinars were found in his waistband, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Two cautery!”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Sadi bin Ajlan Abu Umamah, he said:
m: “A man from the people of the Suffa died, and a dinar was found in his waistband, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A cautery! Then another died, and two dinars were found in his waistband, so the Prophet of God said: Two cautery!”

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim,
m: “On the authority of Thawban, he said: We were on a journey, and we were traveling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the emigrants said: We wish we knew which wealth is best so we could take it, since what was revealed about gold and silver was revealed! So Umar said: If you wish, I will ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that! They said: Yes! So he set out, and I followed him and put my camel on, and he said: O Messenger of God, when God revealed what was revealed about gold and silver, the emigrants said: We wish we knew which wealth is best so we could take it? He said: Yes! So one of you should take a tongue that remembers God, a heart that is grateful, and a wife who helps one of you in his faith.”

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying mentioned on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar: that every wealth on which zakat has been paid is not a treasure that its owner is forbidden to hoard, even if it is a lot, and that every wealth on which zakat has not been paid is subject to punishment and deserving of God’s threat, unless God favors him with His forgiveness, even if it is little, since it is something on which zakat is due. This is because God has made obligatory on five ounces of silver, through the tongue of His Messenger, a quarter of a tenth, and on twenty mithqals of gold, the same, a quarter of a tenth. So since this is what God has made obligatory on gold and silver through the tongue of His Messenger, it is known that a lot of money, even if it reaches thousands upon thousands, Surat al-Tawbah 9:34 O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of God.
h
And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment

. if it were - and its zakat is paid - from the treasures for which God has threatened its people with punishment, then the zakat we mentioned of a quarter of a tenth would not be due on it. This is because what was obligatory to give out in its entirety from the money, and it is forbidden to take it, its zakat is to give out all of it to its people, not a quarter of a tenth. This is like usurped money, which is forbidden for the usurper to keep, and it was made obligatory for him to take it out of his hand and return it to his hand, to purify himself from it: to return it to its owner. If the excess of the money was more than four thousand dirhams, or what was left over from the inevitable need of its owner, which its owner deserves by acquiring it - if he pays the people of the two shares their rights from it in charity - and God’s threat, then his Lord would not be required to pay him a quarter of a tenth of it, rather what was required of him was to give all of it to its people, and spend it on what he must spend it on, like what we mentioned about the obligation of the usurper of a man’s money to return it to its owner.
And then, in what follows:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told me, Suhayl ibn Abi Salih told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth, except that on the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be made with which his forehead, his brow, and his back will be branded, and on a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people, then he will see his path. And if they are camels, a flat, gurgling plain will be spread out for them, trampling him with their hooves - I think he said: and biting him with their mouths - returning the first to the last, until judgment is passed between the people. And if they are sheep, it is the same, except that they butt him with their horns and trample him with their hooves." In similar reports that we did not want to prolong mentioning, there is clear evidence that the threat is from God only for the money that did not fulfill the duties imposed on its owners from charity, not for its acquisition and hoarding. And in what we have explained of that, there is clear evidence that the verse is specific, as Ibn Abbas said, and that is what:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment
, he said: They are the People of the Book. And he said: It is specific and general.

x: What he meant by his saying: (It is specific and general) is that it is specific to Muslims, to those among them who did not pay the zakat on their wealth, and general to the People of the Book, because they are infidels and their expenditures are not accepted from them if they spend.
This indicates the correctness of what we said in interpreting this statement of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it until his statement

: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard, he said: They are those who do not pay the zakat on their wealth. He said: Every wealth on which zakat is not paid, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its depths, is a treasure. And every wealth on which zakat is paid is not a treasure, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its depths.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

, he said: The treasure is what is hoarded out of obedience to God and His obligation, and that is the treasure. He said: Zakat and prayer were both made obligatory, there was no distinction between them.

x: We only said: That is specific, because treasure, in the speech of the Arabs, means: everything that is gathered together, whether in the belly of the earth or on its surface.

i: This is indicated by the words of the poet:
x: I don't know if I feed their guests the filth of the earth while I have wheat stored away He means by this: I have the wheat, some of it gathered together.
And the Arabs also say about a gathered body: heaped up, because some of it is joined together. If that is the meaning of treasure for them, and his statement,
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

, means: And those who gather gold and silver together and do not spend it in the way of God, and it is general in recitation, and there was no statement in the verse about how much of that amount of gold and silver is that if gathered together, it would deserve the threat, it was known that the specificity of that was only realized, because the Messenger stopped at it, and that is as we explained that it is the money from which God’s right of zakat was not paid, and not anything else, because of what we have explained of the evidence for its correctness.
Some of the Companions used to say: It is general for every treasure, but it is specific to the People of the Book, and God meant them by it.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hasin told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, he said:
m: I passed by Ar-Rabadha and met Abu Dharr, so I said: O Abu Dharr, what brought you to this land? He said: I was in Ash-Sham, so I read this verse:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

3:100. Muawiyah said: This verse is not about us, rather this verse is about the People of the Book! I said: It is for us and for them! He said: So the talk was raised between me and him, so he wrote to Uthman complaining about me, so Uthman wrote to me to come to me! I came, and when I arrived in Madinah, the people rode me as if they had never seen me before that day, so I complained about that to Uthman, so he said to me: Move away quickly. I said: By God, I will never give up what I was saying! Abu Kuraib, Abu al-Sa’ib, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb, he said: We passed by al-Rabdhah, then he mentioned something similar on the authority of Abu Dharr.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ash’ath and Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said, Abu Dharr said:
m: I went out to Ash-Sham and read this verse:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver
and do not spend it in the way of God. Mu’awiyah said: It only refers to the People of the Book! I said: It is for us and among them.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Hisin told us, on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb, who said:
m: I passed by Ar-Rabadha and there I saw Abu Dharr. I said to him: What brought you to this place? He said: I was in Ash-Sham, and Muawiyah and I differed about this verse:
h
And those who hoard gold and silver

and do not spend it in the way of God. He said: It was revealed about the People of the Book! I said: It was revealed about us and them. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Hisham, on the authority of Hisin.

x: How is it said: And they do not spend it in the way of God, so the ha and the alif were used as a metaphor for one of the two types?

This has two possible meanings: One of them is that gold and silver refers to treasures, as if it were said: And those who hoard treasures and do not spend them in the way of God, because gold and silver are treasures in this context.

i: The other: that he dispensed with the report of one of them in the return of their mention, from the report of the other, because the speech indicates that the report of the other is like the report about it, and this is often found in the speech of the Arabs and their poetry, and from it the saying of the poet: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, and the opinion is different He said:
x: satisfied, and did not say: satisfied.

The other said: The crack of youth and black hair, unless disobeyed, is madness. He said: He disobeys, and he did not say: He disobeys in many things. And from this is the saying of God: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it (al-Jumuah 62:11), and he did not say: to them.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, and have acknowledged the Oneness of your Lord, indeed many of the scholars and reciters from among Israel, from the Jews and Christians, devour the wealth of people unjustly, meaning: they take bribes in their rulings, and they distort the Book of God, and they write with their own hands and then say: (This is from God), and they take a small price for it from their lowest people, and they hinder [people] from the way of God, meaning: and they prevent whoever wants to enter Islam from entering it, by forbidding them from it.
He said: I was in Ash-Sham, so I read this verse: And those who hoard gold and silver 3:100.

Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ash’ath and Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said, Abu Dharr said: I went out to Ash-Sham and read this verse: And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God.

x: God Almighty says: So give good tidings to those who hoard gold and silver, and do not pay God’s dues from them, O Muhammad, of a painful torment, on the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell. So (on the Day) is connected to (the painful torment), as if it was said: He gives them good tidings of a painful torment, with which God will torment them on the Day when it will be heated. What he means by his saying:
h
It will be heated over it

, is that the fire will be put into it and lit over it, that is, over the gold and silver that they have hoarded, in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, sides, and backs will be branded with it. Everything that is put into the fire is heated up. It is said: I heated the iron in the fire, I heat it up up. And His statement:
h
Then their foreheads will be branded with it
, meaning with the hoarded gold and silver, which will be heated in the fire of Hell, and God will brand with it.
He says: God will burn the foreheads of its hoarders, their sides, and their backs.
h
This is what you have hoarded
, meaning: And it will be said to them:
h
This is what you have hoarded

in this world, O disbelievers who have withheld their treasures from the obligatory duties of God in it for yourselves. So taste what you have been hoarding, meaning: And it will be said to them: So taste the punishment of God because you used to withhold from your wealth the rights of God and hoard it out of competition and boasting. And the word and it will be said to them was omitted from his statement:
h
This is what you have hoarded
, because the statement indicates this. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Hilal, he said:
m: Abu Dharr used to say: Give good tidings to the treasurers, cauterize them on their foreheads, cauterize them on their sides, and cauterize them on their backs, until the heat meets their insides. ... He said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala’ Ibn Al-Shakheer, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf Ibn Qays, who said: I came to Madinah, and while I was in a circle in which there were many of the Quraysh, a man came with coarse clothes, coarse body, and coarse face. He stood over them and said: Give glad tidings to the treasurers of a hot coal that will be heated in the fire of Hell, and it will be placed on the nipple of one of their breasts until it comes out of the hollow of his shoulder, and it will be placed on the hollow of his shoulder until it comes out of the nipple of his breasts, and he will shake. He said: So the people lowered their heads, and I did not see any of them respond to him at all. He said: And he turned away, so I followed him, until he sat against a pillar, and I said: I have never seen these people except that they disliked what I said! He said: These people do not understand anything.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Al-Hakam told us, Amr ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah Al-Jamali, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said:
m: I saw in the mosque of Medina a man with rough clothes and a shabby appearance, walking around the circles and saying: Give glad tidings to the owners of treasures, their sides will be branded, their foreheads will be branded, and their backs will be branded! Then he went away complaining and saying: What will the Quraysh do to me!!

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Abu Dharr said:
m: The owners of treasures will be given good report, they will be branded on their foreheads, branded on their sides, and branded on their backs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, he said: A snake will wrap itself around his forehead and his forehead will say: I am your wealth that you were stingy with!

“Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Thawban: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘Whoever leaves behind a treasure, it will appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair, following him and saying: Woe to you, what are you?’ It will say: ‘I am your treasure that you left behind!’ It will continue to follow him until it puts its hand in it and he bites it, then the rest of his body will follow it.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, ‘Abd Al-Razzaq narrated to us, Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: It has reached me that treasures will turn on the Day of Resurrection into a serpent that follows its owner while he flees from him, and it will say: ‘I am your treasure!’ It will not attain anything of it Surat al-Tawbah 9:35 The Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell and branded with it their foreheads, their sides, and their backs, [saying], "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard." except to take it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: By the One besides whom there is no god, a servant will not be branded with a treasure, touching dinar by dinar or dirham by dirham, but his skin will be expanded, and each dinar and dirham will be placed separately. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: There is no man who is branded with a treasure and a dinar is placed on a dinar or a dirham on a dirham, but his skin is made wider.

x: God Almighty says: The number of months of the year with God is twelve months in the Book of God, in which He wrote everything that will happen in His decree that He decreed, On the Day He created the heavens and the earth, of them four are sacred. He says: Of these twelve months, four are sacred months that the people of ignorance used to venerate and sanctify, and forbid fighting in them, so that if a man of them met his father's killer in them, he would not satirize him. They are: Rajab of Mudar, and three consecutive months, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram. And thus the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have become clear.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told us, he said: Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said: Musa bin Ubaidah Al-Rabdhi told us, he said: Sadaqah bin Yasar told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage in Mina in the middle of the days of Tashreeq, and he said: O people, time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth, and the number of months with God is twelve months, four of which are sacred, the first of which is Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha’ban, and Dhul-Qa’dah, and Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram.”

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Time has come back to the way it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth, and
h
the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth
, of which four are sacred, three consecutive, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha’ban.”

c: Yaqub told us, Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Bakra:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said: Behold, time has returned to its original state as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred, three of which are consecutive: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha’ban.”

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, a man in Bahrain told me:
