m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage: ‘Behold, time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth, and the number of months with God is twelve months, three consecutive: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.’”

c: Ibn Hamida told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: his saying:
h
The number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth

, of which four are sacred, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Three consecutive months: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.”

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon on the day of Mina: Beware, time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth, and the number of months with God is twelve months, four of which are sacred, three of which are consecutive: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban. This is the opinion of most interpreters.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
The number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth
. Of these, four are sacred.” As for four months, they are Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab. As for the Book of God, it is what is with Him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months, he said: The matter of the intercalation is known by it, what is missing from the year. Surat al-Tawbah 9:36 Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve [lunar] months in the register of God [on the day He created the heavens and the earth]. Of these, four are sacred.
h
That is the right religion
, so wrong not yourselves therein. And fight the polytheists collectively as they fight you collectively.
h
And know that God is with the righteous

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God, he said: It mentions the matter of the intercalation. As for his saying:
h
That is the upright religion
, its meaning is: This that I have informed you of, that the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God, and that four of them are sacred: it is the upright religion, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
That is the upright religion
, he said: the straight one.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
That is the right religion

, he said: The right command. He says: God Almighty said: And know, O people, that the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God in which He has written everything that will be, and that of these twelve months four months are sacred. That is the straight religion of God, not what the intercalator does by making permissible what he makes permissible of the months of the year, and forbidding what he forbids of them. As for his saying:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein
, its meaning is: Do not disobey God therein, and do not make permissible what God has forbidden you, lest you earn for yourselves what they cannot bear of God’s wrath and punishment, such as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein

, he said: Injustice is committing sins against God and abandoning His obedience. Then the people of interpretation differed about what the letter ha and the letter nun referred to in his saying: in them.

x: Some of them said: This applies to the twelve months, and he said: Its meaning is: Do not wrong yourselves in all the months.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve [lunar] months in the register of God [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth. Of these, four are sacred.
h
That is the right religion

, so do not wrong yourselves during them,” in all of them. Then He singled out four months from that and made them sacred, and magnified their sanctity, and made sin greater in them, and righteous deeds and reward greater.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So do not wrong yourselves therein
, he said: in all the months.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not wrong yourselves during the four sacred months, and the ha and nun refer to the four months.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: as for his statement:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein

, then wrongdoing in the sacred months is a greater sin and burden than wrongdoing in other than them, even though wrongdoing is great in any case, but God magnifies whatever He wills of His command. He said: God has chosen the best of His creation, He has chosen messengers from the angels, and messengers from the people, and He has chosen His remembrance from speech, and He has chosen the mosques from the earth, and He has chosen Ramadan and the sacred months from the months, and He has chosen Friday from the days, and He has chosen the Night of Decree from the nights, so magnify what God has magnified, for matters are only magnified by what God has magnified in the eyes of the people of understanding and reason.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not wrong yourselves by making the four months forbidden permissible, and their permissible months forbidden.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: The number of months with God is twelve months, until His saying:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein

, meaning: do not make what is forbidden permissible nor what is permissible forbidden, as the polytheists did, for the postponement, which they used to do, is an addition to disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray, the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: So do not wrong yourselves in them, he said: Wrong yourselves means that you do not deprive them as they are forbidden.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ali:
m: So do not wrong yourselves in them, he said: Wrong yourselves means that you do not deprive them as they are forbidden.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad,
m: something similar.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: Do not wrong yourselves during the four months by making permissible what is forbidden in them, for God has made them great and made their sanctity great. Rather, we said: This is more correct in its interpretation, because of His saying:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein

, so He brought out the metaphor for it in the same way as the metaphor for a group of between three and ten. This is because the Arabs say about between three and ten, when you are talking about it: (We did that on the three nights that have passed, and on the four days that remain), and when you are talking about what is above ten to twenty, they say: (We did that on the thirteenth that have passed, and on the fourteenth that have passed), so in His saying, may He be glorified:
h
So do not wrong yourselves therein

and bringing out the metaphor for the number of months in which He forbade the believers from wronging themselves in the same way as the small group number from three to ten, is clear evidence that (the ha and the nun), from mentioning the four months, is less than the twelve.
Because if that was a metaphor for (the twelfth months), it would have been: Do not wrong yourselves therein.

Why do you deny that this is a metaphor for the twelve, even though what you mentioned is what is known in the speech of the Arabs? You know that what is known in their speech is to use the letter ha’ as a metaphor for what is between three and ten, without the letter nun. The poet said: They became in ulcers and in their homes for seven nights without their fodder. He did not say: their fodder, as this is a metaphor for the seven?

Even if that is permissible, it is not the most eloquent and most familiar in her speech, and directing God’s speech to the most eloquent and most familiar is more appropriate than directing it to the most unknown.
If the matter is as you have described, then it must be permissible for us to wrong ourselves in other months of the year?

This is not the case, rather it is forbidden for us at all times and places, but God has made these months great in sanctity and honoured them over all other months of the year, so He has singled out sin in them for honour, just as He has singled them out for honour, and this is similar to His statement: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer (al-Baqarah 2:238). There is no doubt that God has commanded us to guard all the obligatory prayers in His statement: Guard strictly the prayers (al-Baqarah 2:238), and He has not permitted neglecting to guard them, by His command to guard the middle prayer, but He, the Most High, has increased its sanctity, emphasised its preservation, and made neglecting it more severe. The same is true of His statement: “
h
Of these four are sacred
h
That is the right religion
h
so do not wrong yourselves therein
.” As for His statement:
h
And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together

, He, the Most High, says: And fight the polytheists with God, O believers, all together, not differing, united and not separated, as the polytheists fight you all together, united and not separated, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together
. As for all together, it means all together, and your matter is united.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight the polytheists all together
, he said: all together.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And fight the polytheists all together

, meaning: all of them. The word kafa in every case is in one form, it is not mentioned or pluralized, because even if it is in the form of fa’ila, it is in the meaning of a verbal noun, like al-‘afiyya and al-‘aqiba. The Arabs do not include the alif and lam in it, because it is the last word in the sentence, with what is in it of the meaning of a verbal noun, just as they did not include it when they said: qama ma’an and qama jama’a. As for his statement:
h
And know that God is with the righteous

, its meaning is: Know, O believers in God, that if you fight all the polytheists, and fear God and obey Him in what He commands you and forbids you, and do not disobey His command and disobey Him, then God will be with you against your enemy and His enemy from the polytheists, and whoever God is with, nothing will overcome him, because God is with whoever fears Him, so he fears Him and obeys Him in what He commands him to do of His commands and prohibitions.

x: God Almighty says: The postponement is nothing but
h
an increase in disbelief

. The word nasi’ is derived from the saying: I postponed your days, and God postponed your life span, meaning: God increased the days of your life and the length of your life, so that you may remain alive. And every increase that occurs in something, the thing that occurs in that increase is due to what happened in it: nasi’. That is why milk is called nasi’ when it increases in water, and a pregnant woman is called nasu’ and the woman is postponed, due to the increase in her child, and it is said: I postponed the she-camel and I postponed it, if you urge it to move faster. It may be possible that: (Al-Nasi’), (Fa’il), was derived from (Maf’ul), as was said: (La’in) and (Qateel), meaning: cursed and killed. And its meaning would be: The delayed month is only
h
an increase in disbelief

. It is as if the first statement is more similar to the meaning of the speech, which is that its meaning is: The delay that the polytheists delay from the four sacred months, and their making the forbidden ones permissible, and the permissible ones forbidden, is an increase in their disbelief and denial of the rulings of God and His verses.

Some of the reciters used to read it as: The postponement is only without omitting the hamza and without extending it, thus misguiding those who disbelieve. There are different readings of this. The majority of the Kufians read it as: (He misleads thereby those who disbelieve) meaning: God misleads those who disbelieve by the intercalation that they innovated and created. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as: Those who disbelieve are led astray thereby, meaning: those who disbelieve are removed from the path of God which He made for His servants as a path that they follow to please Him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri:
m: (He misleads thereby those who disbelieve) meaning: He misleads people by the postponement that the disbelievers instituted.

x: The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings, and the people of knowledge of the Qur’an and understanding of it have read both of them, and they are close in meaning. Because whoever God leads astray is astray, and whoever goes astray is led astray by God’s leading him astray and abandoning him. So whichever of the two the reader reads, he is correct in that. As for the correct reading of al-Nasi’, it is the hamza, and its reading is based on the estimation of Fa’il because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions, and it is not permissible to differ from it in what they have agreed upon. As for his saying:
h
They will make it permissible
for a year, its meaning is: Those who disbelieved will make the postponement permissible, and the ha in his saying:
h
They will make it permissible

, refers back to it. The meaning of the statement: They make lawful those who delayed its prohibition from the four sacred months, one year, and they make it unlawful one year to match the number of what God has prohibited, meaning: to match by making lawful what they have made lawful from the months, and their prohibition of what they have prohibited from them, the number of what God has prohibited, “and they make lawful what God has prohibited.

Their evil deeds have been made attractive to them,” meaning: their evil and ugly deeds have been made attractive to them, and what contradicts God’s command and obedience, and God does not guide the disbelieving people, meaning: God does not guide to the good and beautiful actions, and what pleases God, the people who deny His Oneness, and the disbelievers in the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but He lets them down from guidance, just as He let these people down from the sacred months. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

, he said: The postponement is that (Junadah bin Awf bin Umayyah al-Kinani) used to come to the season every year, and his nickname was (Abu Thamama), so he would call out: (Behold, Abu Thamama is not favored nor criticized, behold, Safar of the first year is the year of halal), so the people would make it halal, so Safar would be forbidden one year, and Muharram would be forbidden one year, and that is the saying of the Most High:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
until His saying: the disbelievers. And His saying:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
, means: They would leave Muharram one year, and forbid it the next year.

x: This interpretation is from the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbas, and indicates the correctness of the reading of the one who reads al-Nasi by leaving out the hamza and leaving out the extension, and directing the meaning of the speech to it being an action, from the saying of the speaker: I forgot the thing, I made it forget it, and from the saying of God, They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: they abandoned God, so He abandoned them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

, he said: It is the sacred month. He used to make Safar sacred one year, and Safar another year, and Safar was added to the sacred months. They used to make Safar sacred once, and make it permissible another time, and God condemned that. Hawazin, Ghatafan, and Banu Salim used to do it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

. He said: The postponement was a man from Banu Kinanah, and he had an opinion among them, and he used to make the year of Muharram Safar, so they would raid in it, and they would take booty in it, and they would gain, and he would forbid it for a year. ... He said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
, the verse. There was a man from Banu Kinanah called al-Nasi’, and he used to make Muharram a month of Safar, and he would make spoils permissible in it, so this verse was revealed.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: There was a man from Banu Kinanah who would come every year during the season on his donkey and say: “O people, I do not criticize nor do I show favoritism, and there is no objection to what I say. We have forbidden Muharram and delayed Safar.” Then he would come the following year and say the same thing, and say: We have forbidden Safar and delayed Muharram! So his statement:
h
So that they may make up the number of what God has forbidden
, he said: meaning the four, and make permissible what God has forbidden, by delaying this sacred month.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

, “the postponement” is Muharram. Muharram was forbidden one year and Safar was forbidden another year, so the increase was (Safar), and they used to delay the months until they made Safar Muharram, so they made permissible what God had forbidden. Hawazin, Ghatafan, and Banu Salim used to venerate it, and they were the ones who used to do that in the pre-Islamic period.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
until His saying: the disbelievers.

x: Some people from among the people of misguidance deliberately added Safar to the sacred months. Their leader would stand up during the season and say: Behold, your gods have forbidden the sacred year, so they would forbid it that year. Then he would stand up the following year and say: Behold, your gods have forbidden Safar, so they would forbid it that year. They were called the two Safars. He said: The first to postpone were Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and they were three: Abu Thamama Safwan ibn Umayyah, one of Banu Fuqaym ibn al-Harith, then one of Banu Kinanah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

, he said: God imposed Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah. He said: The polytheists used to name the months: Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi’, Rabi’, Jumada, Jumada, Rajab, Sha’ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and Dhul-Hijjah, they would perform Hajj once in it, then they would remain silent about Muharram and not mention it, then they would go back and name Safar Safar, then they would name Rajab Jumada al-Akhira, then they would name Sha’ban Ramadan, then they would name Ramadan Shawwal, then they would name Dhul-Qa’dah Shawwal, then they would name Dhul-Hijjah Dhul-Qa’dah, then they would name Muharram Dhul-Hijjah, and they would perform Hajj in it, and its name among them was Dhul-Hijjah. Then they returned with a similar story, and they would perform Hajj every month for two years, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, coincided with the last of the two years in Dhul-Qi'dah. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed his Hajj, which coincided with Dhul-Hijjah. That was when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon: Surat al-Tawbah 9:37 The postponement is only an addition to disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and forbid it another year in order to correspond to the number of what God has forbidden. Thus they make lawful what God has forbidden. Their evil deeds have been made attractive to them. And God does not guide the disbelieving people. Time has returned to its original state as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

. He said: They performed Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah for two years, then they performed Hajj in Muharram for two years, then they performed Hajj in Safar for two years. So they performed Hajj every year in every month for two years, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr the last of the two years coincided with Dhul-Qa'dah, one year before the Hajj of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj the following year in Dhul-Hijjah, and that was when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon: Time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
. He said: They used to make the year thirteen months, and they would make Muharram Safar, and they would make the forbidden things permissible in it, so God revealed:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve go astray

, the verse, he said: This is a man from Banu Kinanah called Al-Qalmis, who was in the pre-Islamic era. And in the pre-Islamic era, they would not attack each other in the sacred month. A man would meet the killer of his father and not raise his hand against him. So when that happened, he said: Let us go out, they said to him: This is Muharram! So he said: We postpone it for the year, they are two Safars, and when the next year comes, we will complete them and make them sacred. He said: So he did that. So when the next year came, he said: “Do not fight in Safar, make it sacred along with Muharram, they are two sacred months. We postpone Muharram for the first year and complete it.” That is the postponement. And their opponents said: And the months of the pen are forgotten And God revealed:
h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
, to the end of the verse. As for his saying:
h
An increase in disbelief
, its meaning is
h
an increase in disbelief
due to the intercalation, to their disbelief in God before their innovation of the intercalation, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The postponement is only an increase in disbelief
, meaning: They increased their disbelief with it. As for his saying:
h
So that they may agree
, it is from the saying of the speaker: I agreed with so-and-so on such-and-such, I agree with him, meaning I agreed with him on it, supporting him, not opposing him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding this: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
So that they may agree on the number of what God has forbidden
, he said: they may resemble.

x: This is close in meaning to what we have explained, and that is that whatever resembles something agrees with it in the way in which it resembles it. The meaning of the statement is that they agree, in the number of months that they forbid, with the number of the four months that God has forbidden, and they do not increase or decrease from it, even if they bring it forward or delay it. Therefore, their number is in agreement with the number of what God has forbidden.

evidence.text: Some of the reciters used to read it as: The postponement is only without omitting the hamza and without extending it, thus misguiding those who disbelieve.
The majority of the Kufians read it as: (He misleads thereby those who disbelieve) meaning: God misleads those who disbelieve by the intercalation that they innovated and created.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as: Those who disbelieve are led astray thereby, meaning: those who disbelieve are removed from the path of God which He made for His servants as a path that they follow to please Him.

As for the correct reading of al-Nasi’, it is the hamza, and its reading is based on the estimation of Fa’il because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions, and it is not permissible to differ from it in what they have agreed upon.

Abu Jaʿfar said: This interpretation is from the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbas, and indicates the correctness of the reading of the one who reads al-Nasi by leaving out the hamza and leaving out the extension, and directing the meaning of the speech to it being an action, from the saying of the speaker: I forgot the thing, I made it forget it, and from the saying of God, They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: they abandoned God, so He abandoned them.

x: This verse is an urging from God, the Most High, to the believers among the companions of His Messenger, to invade the Romans, and that is the invasion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Tabuk. God Almighty says:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, What is the matter with you? What is your command, when you are told to go forth in the cause of God? He says: When the Messenger of God Muhammad says to you: Go forth, meaning: go out from your homes to your battlefield. The root of nafar is to leave one place for another due to a matter that has motivated one to do so. From this: nafaran ad-daba the animal fleeing. However, it is said from nafar to raid: So-and-so fled to such-and-such a border, fleeing in flight and in flight. I think that this is one of the differences by which they differentiate between the difference in what is being reported, even if the meanings of the report are the same.

The meaning of the statement is: What is the matter with you, O believers, when you are told: Go out as fighters, in the way of God, meaning: in jihad against the enemies of God, that you cling to the earth heavily? He says: You are clinging heavily to your land and your homes and sitting in them. It was said: Athaqaltum is due to the assimilation of thaa into taa, so an alif was added to it, to reach the point of speaking with it, because taa is assimilated into thaa. If the alif was dropped and it was started with, it would only be moving, so an alif was added to make the movement occur with it, as the Most High said: Until, when they all overtook it (al-A’raf 7:38), and as the poet said: She takes over the bed if he finds her sweet-tasting waist, if he continues kissing her It is from thickness, and its metaphor is the metaphor of you did it, from heaviness. And His statement:
h
Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter

God Almighty says: Are you satisfied with the portion of this world and its comforts, in exchange for the bliss of the Hereafter, and what is with God for the righteous in His gardens? What is the enjoyment of the life of this world compared to the Hereafter? He says: What do those who enjoy themselves in this world enjoy in its life and pleasures in comparison to the bliss of the afterlife and the honor that God has prepared for His friends and those who obey Him, except a little, insignificant. He says to them: So seek, O believers, the bliss of the Hereafter, and the honor of honor that is with God for His friends, by obeying Him and hastening to respond to His command to mobilize to fight His enemy. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: What is the matter with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God you cling heavily to the earth? They were commanded to go forth in the Tabuk expedition after the conquest, after Taif, and after Hunayn. They were commanded to go forth in the summer, when the palm trees were in full bloom, the fruits were good, they desired shade, and the way out was difficult for them.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God you adhere heavily to the earth? He said: This was when they were commanded to go forth in the Battle of Tabuk after the conquest and Hunayn and after Taif. He commanded them to go forth in the summer, when the palm trees were in full bloom, the fruits were good, they desired shade, and the way out was difficult for them. He said: They said: The heavy one, the one in need, the one in distress and preoccupation, and the one who is spread out in all of that, so God revealed: Go forth, whether light or heavy. (al-Tawbah 9:41) Surat al-Tawbah 9:38
h
O you who have believed
, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God you adhere heavily to the earth?
h
Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter
? But what is the enjoyment of the life of this world compared to the Hereafter except a little?

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of His Messenger, threatening them for not going out to fight against their enemy from al-Rum 30:If you do not go out, O believers, to those whom the Messenger of God has called upon you to fight, God will punish you immediately in this world, for your not going out to fight against them, with a painful punishment, and will replace you with another people, meaning: God will replace you with His Prophet, another people, who will go out when called upon, and will respond to him when called upon, and will obey God and His Messenger, and will not harm Him at all, meaning: And will not harm God, by not going out and disobeying Him, at all, because He has no need of you, rather you are the ones who need Him, and He is independent of you and you are the poor, and God is over all things competent, meaning: God Almighty says: God is capable of destroying you and replacing you with another people, and of everything He wills. It was mentioned that the painful torment in this place was the withholding of rain from them.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, he said, Abdul-Mu'min bin Khalid Al-Hanafi told me, he said, Najdah Al-Khurasani told me, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas, and he was asked about His statement:
h
If you do not go forth

, He will punish you with a painful punishment, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon a tribe of the Arabs to go forth, but they were reluctant to come to him, so he withheld the rain from them, and that was their punishment, so that is what His statement:
h
If you do not go forth
, He will punish you with a painful punishment is.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abdul-Mumin told us, on the authority of Najdah, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Their punishment was that the rain was withheld from them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
If you do not go forth
, He will punish you with a painful punishment. God called the believers to the battle of Tabuk before the Levant, with what God knows of the effort.

x: Some of them claimed that this verse was abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said:
m: He said:
h
If you do not go forth

, He will punish you with a painful punishment. And he said: It was not for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to stay behind the Messenger of God or to prefer themselves over himself. Until His saying: That God may reward them with the best of what they used to do. Then the verse that followed abrogated it:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once

. Until His saying: That they may beware. (al-Tawbah 9:120-122) Abu Jaʿfar said: There is no report of what ʿIkrimah and al-Hasan said, that the ruling of this verse that they mentioned was abrogated. It must be accepted, and there is no argument that negates the validity of that. A number of the Companions and Followers saw the confirmation of the ruling with that, and we will mention them later. It is possible that his statement,
h
If you do not go forth

, He will punish you with a painful punishment, refers to the specific people, and what is meant by it is those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called forth but did not go forth, according to what we mentioned from the narration on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas. If that is the case, then His statement,
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once

, is a prohibition from God to the believers from evacuating the lands of Islam without a believer residing therein, and an announcement from God to them that it is obligatory for some of them to go forth and not for others, and that is for those among them who are called forth and not for those who are not. If that is the case, then there is no abrogation in one of the two verses for the other, and the ruling of each one of them is valid in what it means.

x: This is an announcement from God to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He is the One who is entrusted with the victory of His Messenger over the enemies of His religion and making him prevail over them, whether they aid him or not, and a reminder from Him to them that He did this to him, even though he was few in number and the enemy was many, so how about him, even though he was many in number and the enemy was few? He, the Most High, says to them: If you do not go forth, O believers, with My Messenger when he calls you to mobilization and you support him, then God is his supporter and helper against his enemy, and He will do without you and without your support and support, just as He supported him, when those who disbelieved in God from Quraysh drove him out of his homeland and home, the second of two, meaning: they drove him out while he was one of the two, meaning: one of the two.

Likewise, the Arabs say: He is the second of two, meaning: one of two, and the third of three, and the fourth of four, meaning: one of three, and one of four. This is contrary to their saying: He is the brother of six, and the servant of seven, because the brother and the servant are not the six and the seven, and the third of three is one of the three. What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: the second of two, was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, because they were the two who fled from the Quraysh when they intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they hid in the cave. And his saying:
h
When they were in the cave
, he says: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, were in the cave. And the cave is a great hole in the mountain.

When he said to his companion, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companion Abu Bakr, Do not be sad, because he feared that the search would lead them to know where they were, so he was alarmed by that, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Do not be sad, because God is with us and God is our supporter, so the polytheists will not know about us and will not reach us. The Most High says: God has given him victory over his enemy while he was in this state of fear and small numbers, so how could He let him down and make him need you, when God has increased his supporters and the number of his soldiers? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Unless you support him, he mentioned who was at the beginning of his affair when he was sent, God says: So I will do that to him and support him, as I supported him at that time and he was the second of two.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
If you do not aid him - God has already aided him
, he said: He mentioned what happened at the beginning of his affair when he was sent, so God will do the same to him, He will aid him as He aided him then, the second of two
h
when they were in the cave

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you do not aid him
, God has aided him the verse, he said: So his companion was Abu Bakr, and as for the cave, it is a mountain in Mecca called: (Thawr).

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Aban Al-Attar told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, set out, Abu Bakr had a gift of sheep to bring to his family, so Abu Bakr sent Amir bin Fuhaira with the sheep to Thawr. Amir bin Fuhaira used to bring those sheep to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cave in Thawr, which is the cave that God named in the Qur’an.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim bin Jubair Al-Wasiti told me, he said, Affan and Jabban told us, they said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas,
m: “That Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told them, he said: While I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cave, and the feet of the polytheists were above our heads, I said: O Messenger of God, if one of them were to raise his foot, he would see us! He said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two people with God as their third?”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Abu Bakr stayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cave for three days.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: h
When they were in the cave
, he said: In the mountain called Thawr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr stayed there for three nights.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of his father:
m: That Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, when he gave a sermon, he said: Who among you recites Surat At-Tawbah? A man said: I will. He said: Recite. When he reached: When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve,’ Abu Bakr cried and said: I, by God, am his companion.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “So God sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God - that is - the highest.
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

God Almighty says: So God sent down His reassurance and tranquility upon His Messenger - and it has been said: upon Abu Bakr - And supported him with soldiers you did not see, meaning: He strengthened him with soldiers from Him from the angels, whom you did not see, And He made the word of those who disbelieved, which is the word of polytheism, the lowest, because it was subdued and humiliated, and God Almighty nullified it and annihilated its people, and everything that is subdued and defeated is lower than the victor, and the victor is the highest,
h
And the word of God is the highest
, meaning: And the religion of God and His monotheism and the saying there is no god but God, which is His word, the highest, over polytheism and its people, the victorious, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest
, which is associating partners with God,
h
and the word of God is the highest
, which is: There is no god but God. His saying:
h
And the word of God is the highest
, is the predicate of a subject, and is not rejected by his saying:
h
And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest
, because if that were conjoined with the first word, it would be in the accusative case. As for his saying:
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

, it means: And God is Exalted in Might, in His vengeance against the people who disbelieve in Him. No one can subdue Him, no one can overcome Him, and no one can help those He punishes. Wise, in His management of His creation and His disposition of them according to His will.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of (lightness) and (heaviness), which God commanded whoever has one of them to go out with Him.
Some of them said: The meaning of lightness that God meant in this place is youth, and the meaning of heaviness is old age.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: Old and young.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Old men and young men. ... He said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: Old men and young men, I did not hear a single excuse from God!! So he went out to the Levant, and fought until he died.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Al-Nu’man, he said:
m: There was a man from the Nakha’ tribe, and he was an old, fat man. He wanted to go on a raid, but Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas prevented him, so he said: God says: Go forth, whether light or heavy! So Sa’d gave him permission. So the old man was killed, and after ‘Umar asked about him, he said: What happened to the old man who seemed to be from Banu Hashim? They said: He was killed, O Commander of the Faithful!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, he said:
m: The young man and the old man. ... He said, Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Malik bin Mughol, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The young man and the old man. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: Old men and young men. ... He said, Habawayh, Abu Yazid, told us, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Hamid, on the authority of Bishr ibn Atiyah: old men and young men.

c: Al-Walid told us, he said, Ali bin Sahl told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Bakir bin Maruf, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan,
m: regarding his statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: young men and middle-aged men.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: young and old, rich and poor.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: Old men and young men.

c: Saeed bin Amr told me, Baqiyah told us, Harez told us, Hubban bin Zaid Al-Sharabi told me:
m: We set out with Safwan bin Amr, who was the governor of Homs before Al-Afsus, to Al-Jarajima. I met an old man with a heavy heart, his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, from Damascus, on his mount, among those who had raided. So I turned to him and said: O uncle, God has excused you! He raised his eyebrows and said: O son of my brother, God has called us to mobilization, light and heavy. He whom God loves He tests, then He returns him and tests him. God only tests those of His servants who are grateful and patient, and that is because they worship none but God.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Saleh:
m: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: Every old man and young man.

x: Others said: This means: busy and not busy.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam,
m: regarding his statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: busy and not busy.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: Go forth, rich and poor.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Abu Salih: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: rich and poor.

x: Others said: With us: activity and non-activity.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said,
m: my father told Surat al-Tawbah 9:41 Go forth, whether light or heavy,
h
and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God

. That is better for you, if you only knew. me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, meaning: Go forth with energy and without energy.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Light and heavy, he said: active and not active.

x: Others said: It means: riders and pedestrians.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said:
m: When the people set out for the paths of the Levant, they set out for them lightly, riding. And when the people set out for these coasts, they set out for them lightly or heavily, riding and walking.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: someone with a farm and someone without a farm.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: The heavy one is the one who has property, so he is heavy and hates to lose his property and go out, and the light one is the one who has no property, so God said: Go forth, whether light or heavy.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Al-Hadrami claimed that he mentioned that some people were thinking that one of them might be sick or old, and he would say: If I avoid it out of refusal, then I am sinful! So God revealed: Go forth, whether light or heavy.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: Ayoub witnessed Badr with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he did not miss a single Muslim expedition except that he was in another, except for one year. And Ayoub used to say: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and I did not find myself except light or heavy.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Harez bin Othman told us, on the authority of Rashid bin Saad, on the authority of someone
m: who saw Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, the knight of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a coffin of the money changers in Homs, and some of its bones were left over from it. So I said to him: God has excused you! He said: The Surah Al-Ba’uth has refused us, March out, whether light or heavy.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Harez told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Maysarah told me, Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me:
m: I came upon Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, the knight of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting on one of the money changers’ coffins in Homs, some of its bones were left over, intending to go on a raid. So I said to him: God has excused you! He said: Surat Al-Buhuth refused us: Go forth, whether light or heavy.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is that it is said that God, the Most High, commanded the believers to set out to fight His enemies in His cause, whether light or heavy. The light may include anyone for whom setting out is easy due to his physical strength, his physical health and youth, and anyone who has money and is free from work, and is able to ride a camel and mount. The heavy may include anyone who is otherwise, such as the weak, sick and ill, the one who is financially insolvent, the one who is busy with a farm and earning a living, the one who has neither a camel nor a mount, and the elderly with children. Since the light and heavy may be included in our description of the people with the attributes that we mentioned, and God, may He be glorified and exalted, did not single out one type over another in the Book, nor on the tongue of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did He establish any evidence for its specificity, it must be said: God, may He be glorified and exalted, commanded the believers from among the companions of His Messenger to go forth to fight in His cause, light and heavy, with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in every state of lightness and heaviness.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Masrouq, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, who said:
m: The first thing to be revealed in Bara’ah was: Go forth, whether light or heavy.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told us, Al-Qasim told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The first thing that was revealed in Bara’ah was: God has certainly helped you in many battlefields. He said: He makes them aware of His help and prepares them for the Battle of Tabuk.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God
That is better for you, if you only knew.”

God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger from the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Strive, O believers, against the disbelievers, with your wealth, so spend it in struggling against them for the religion of God that He has prescribed for you, until they submit to you, so they enter it willingly or unwillingly, or pay you the jizyah with their hands, if they are People of the Book, or you kill them, and yourselves, meaning: and with yourselves, so fight them with your hands, God will disgrace them and grant you victory over them, that is better for you, meaning: What I command you to do of going forth in the cause of God Almighty, light and heavy, and striving against His enemies with your wealth and yourselves, is better for you than being sluggish on the earth when you are called to action, and remaining there, and being content with a little of the enjoyment of worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter, if you are among the people of knowledge of the truth of what has been explained to you about the virtue of striving in the cause of God over sitting back from it.

The Most High says to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of his companions had asked his permission to stay behind when he went out to Tabuk, and he gave them permission: If what you are calling those who stayed behind from you to do, and those who asked your permission to not go out with you to your campaign to which you have called them, were a near gain, meaning: present booty, and a short journey, meaning: and a nearby, easy place, they would have followed you, and gone out with you to them. But you called them to a distant place, and you burdened them with a journey that was difficult for them, because you urged them in a time of heat, and a time of scorching heat, and when there was a need for shelter, and they will swear by God, if we were able, we would have gone out with you, the Most High says: And these people who asked your permission to not go out with you will swear to you, O Muhammad, as an apology from them to you falsely, so that you accept their excuse from them, and give them permission to stay behind from you, lying by God, if we were able, we would have gone out with you.

“He says: If we were able to go out with you, with the means, the vehicles, the appearance, and what a traveler and a fighter needs, and the health of the body and strength, we would go out with you to your enemy, destroying themselves, he says: they make it necessary for themselves, with their swearing by God as liars, to perish and be ruined, because they bring upon themselves the wrath of God, and earn themselves His painful punishment, and God knows that they are liars, in their swearing by God, If we were able, we would have gone out with you, because they were able to go out, with the means to do so, with what they had of money, which the fighter needs in his raid, and the traveler needs in his journey, and the health of the bodies and strength of the bodies. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: If it were an immediate offer, to his statement: they would be liars, that they could go out, but it was a delay from themselves and Satan, and a lack of interest in good.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: If it were a close offer, he said: It is the Battle of Tabuk.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God knows that they are liars, meaning: that they are capable.

x: This is a reproach from God Almighty: He reproached His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for allowing those of the hypocrites whom he had given permission to stay behind when he set out for Tabuk to fight the Romans. The Most High says:
h
God has pardoned you

, O Muhammad, for what you did in giving permission to these hypocrites who asked your permission to not go out with you and to stay behind you, before you knew their truthfulness from their lies. Why did you give them permission? For what reason did you give them permission? So that you may know who are truthful and who are liars, meaning: It was not appropriate for you to give them permission to stay behind when they said to you: If we were able, we would have gone out with you, until you knew who among them had an excuse for staying behind and who among them had no excuse. So your permission for whomever you gave permission to among them was based on your knowledge of his excuse, and you knew who was lying and who stayed behind out of hypocrisy and doubt in the religion of God.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: May God forgive you for giving them permission. He said: People said: Ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission. If he gives you permission, then sit down. If he does not give you permission, then sit down.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “
h
God has pardoned you

. Why did you give them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful?” The verse, he rebuked him as you hear, then God revealed what is in Surat An-Nur, so He gave him permission to give them permission if he wished, so He said: So if they ask your permission for any of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish of them. (al-Nur 24:62), so God made it a permission for that from that.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun Al-Awdi, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did two things for which he was not commanded to do anything: his permission for the hypocrites, and his taking of prisoners, so God revealed:
h
God has pardoned you for giving them permission
, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I read to Saeed bin Abi Arubah, he said: This is how I heard it from Qatada, his statement:
h
God has pardoned you for giving them permission
, the verse, then God revealed after that in Surat al-Nur 24:So if they ask your permission for any of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish of them, the verse, (al-Nur 24:62).

c: Saleh bin Mismar told us, he said, Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said, Musa bin Sarwan told us, he said:
m: I asked Muraq about his saying: God has forgiven you, he said: His Lord rebuked him.

x: This is an announcement from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the characteristics of al-Munafiqun 63:that among their signs by which they are known is their failure to fight in the way of God, by asking permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave them going out with him if they are called upon with false excuses. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: O Muhammad, do not give permission to anyone who asks your permission to stay behind when you go out to fight your enemy without an excuse, because no one asks your permission to do so except a hypocrite who does not believe in God and the Last Day. As for the one who believes in God and acknowledges His Oneness, the Resurrection, the Hereafter, reward and punishment, he will not ask your permission to abandon the fight and jihad against the enemies of God with his wealth and his life.

And God is Knowing of the righteous, meaning: God is All-Knowing of the righteous. He says: God is All-Knowing of the one who fears Him, so he fears Him by performing His obligations, avoiding His disobedience, and hastening to obey Him in fighting His enemy and jihad against them with his wealth and his life, and other than that of His commands and prohibitions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muntha told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Those who believe in God will not ask your permission

, this is a reproach to the hypocrites when they asked permission to stay away from jihad without an excuse, and God excused the believers and said: They did not go until they had asked His permission (al-Nur 24:62).

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Only those who do not believe in God nor acknowledge His Oneness ask your permission to stay behind and abandon jihad with you, without a clear excuse, and their hearts are in doubt, meaning: their hearts doubt the truth of God’s Oneness, and the reward of those who obey Him, and His punishment of those who disobey Him, so in their doubt they waver, meaning: they are confused in their doubt, and in the darkness of confusion they waver, not knowing right from wrong, so they act with insight. And this is the description of the hypocrites.
A group of scholars believed that these two verses were abrogated by the verse mentioned in Surat An-Nur.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said:
m: His statement,
h
Those who believe in God do not ask your permission to His statement

, So they are wavering in their doubt, was abrogated by the verse in al-Nur 24:The believers are only those who believe in God to Forgiving and Merciful (al-Nur 24:62). We have explained the abrogating and the abrogated, so there is no need to repeat it here.

x: God Almighty says: If these people who asked your permission, O Muhammad, to leave going out with you to fight your enemy, had wanted to go out with you, they would have prepared for it, meaning they would have prepared for going out, and they would have prepared for travel and the enemy, as they prepared for them, but God disliked their going out, meaning their going out for that purpose, so He held them back, meaning: the going out was so heavy on them that they found it easy to stay in their homes in opposition to you, and they found the travel and going out with you burdensome, so they left going out for that purpose, and it was said, ‘Sit with those who sit,’ meaning: sit with the sick and weak who do not find what they can spend, and with the women and children, and leave going out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the mujahidin in the way of God. God discouraged them from going out with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him, because He knew of their hypocrisy and deceit of Islam and its people, and that if they went out with them they would harm them and not benefit them.

He mentioned that those who asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to stay were: (Abdullah bin Ubay bin Salul), (Al-Jadd bin Qais), and whoever was like them. Likewise: Narrated Ibn Hamid, he said: Narrated to us Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ishaq, he said: Those who asked his permission, as far as I have been informed, were of noble people, among them: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and Al-Jadd bin Qais, and they were nobles among their people, but God, knowing them, prevented them from going out with them and corrupting his army.

God Almighty says: If these hypocrites had come out among you, O believers, they would have increased you only in chaos, meaning: By coming out among you, they would have increased you only in corruption and harm, and for that reason I discouraged them from coming out with you. We have explained the meaning of al-Khabal with its evidence previously. And they will place themselves among you, meaning: And they will hasten their mounts to walk among you. Its origin is from (Idaa’ al-Khail wa al-Rakab), which means to speed up the journey.

i: It is said of a camel when it speeds up its journey: (The camel has put down, put down, put down and place), and (its owner has put it down), if he strives with it and speeds it up, (Yuwadaa Idaa’an), and from this the rajaz poet said:
x: I wish I was a tree trunk in it, so I could hide and put it there As for the origin of al-Khalal, it comes from al-Khalal, which is the gap between people, in rows and elsewhere.

From this comes the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Stand together in rows so that the devils do not get in between you, as if they were the children of Hadhramaut. As for his saying:
h
They seek to cause you discord
, the meaning of
h
they seek to cause you discord

is that they seek for you something with which to disturb you from your path in your campaign, by discouraging you from it. It is said: (I sought evil for him), (I sought good for him) (abghee bughaan), if you sought it for him, meaning: (I sought it for him). Likewise (‘akmataka), (halabtaka), meaning: (I milked for you), (‘akmat lak), and if they mean: I helped you to seek and request it, they say: (abgheeta kada), (ahalbakta), (‘akmat lak), meaning: I helped you with it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they would have placed among you, among you, seek to cause you discord, with that.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will place discord among you
, meaning:
h
And they will place discord among you

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they would have placed themselves among you
, seeking to cause you discord, they would have made you slow. He said: Rafa’ah bin al-Tabut, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and Aws bin Qayzi.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they would have placed themselves among you

, he said: They would have hastened the alleys, among you, seeking to cause you discord, they would have slowed you down, Abdullah bin Nabtal, and Rafa’ah bin Tabut, and Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul. ... He said: Al-Husayn told us, he said:

c: Abu Sufyan told me, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they will hasten to place themselves among you, he said: They will hasten to place themselves among you, seeking to cause you discord thereby.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
If they had gone out with you

, they would not have increased you except in confusion, he said: These are the hypocrites in the Battle of Tabuk. God consoled His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers about them, so he said: What saddens you?
h
If they had gone out with you
, they would not have increased you except in confusion! They say: (He has gathered against you, and he did and he did), abandoning you,
h
and they would have placed themselves among you
, seeking to cause you discord, disbelief. As for his saying:
h
And among you are those who listen to them
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And among you are those who listen to your speech, who convey it to you, and who are their eyes upon you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And among you are those who listen to them
, who narrate your stories, spies who are not hypocrites.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And among you are those who listen to them
, he said: Those who speak, are spies, other than the hypocrites.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among you are those who listen to them
, they hear what they convey to your enemy.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And among you are those who listen to their words and obey them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And among you are those who listen to them
, and among you are those who listen to their words.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Those who asked permission, as far as I have been informed, were of noble character, among them Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and Al-Jadd bin Qais, and they were nobles among their people, but God, knowing about them, restrained them from going out with them and corrupting his army. And among his army were people who loved them and obeyed what they called them to, because of their noble character among them, so He said:
h
And among you are those who listen to them

x: According to this interpretation: Among you are people who hear and obey you. If they accompanied you, they would corrupt you by discouraging them from going with you. As for the first interpretation, its meaning is: And among you are those who listen to you and hear your speech, so they convey it to you and deliver it to you, they are eyes upon you.

The most correct of the two interpretations in my opinion is the interpretation of those who said: Its meaning is: (And among you are those who listen to your talk to them, who convey it from you, they are spies for them), because most of the speech of the Arabs in their saying: (listening), is a description of the one described by it as listening to the talk, as God Almighty said in more than one place in His Book: (listening to lies) (al-Ma’idah 5:41), describing with that a people who hear lies from talk. But if they describe a man as listening to a man’s generosity and his commands and prohibitions and accepting them from him and referring to him, then you are describing him as: (listening to him and obedient), and you would hardly say: (He is listening and obedient). As for his statement: And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers, its meaning is: God is All-Knowing of those who direct their actions in ways other than their intended meanings, and put them in places other than their proper ones, and of those who ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for an excuse, and of those who ask his permission out of doubt in Islam and hypocrisy, and of those who listen to the conversation of the believers in order to inform the hypocrites, and of those who listen to it in order to be pleased with what the believers are pleased with, and to be displeased with what displeases them.
Nothing of the secrets and open secrets of His creation is hidden from Him. We have explained the meaning of injustice in more than one place in this book, so there is no need to repeat it here.

God Almighty says: These hypocrites sought to cause discord for your companions, O Muhammad. They sought to turn them away from their religion, and they were keen to return them to disbelief by discouraging them from it, as Abdullah bin Abi Bakr did with your companions on the day of Uhud, when they turned away from you with those of his people who followed him. That was their seeking of what they had sought for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of discord before. And by his saying: before, he means before this, and they turned things upside down for you, he says: and they circulated among you and inwardly the opinion of the one who sent you with the religion of God, by discouraging you, and denying what you bring to them and rejecting it from you, until the truth came, he says: until God's victory came, and God's command appeared, he says: and God's religion appeared, which He commanded and made obligatory for His creation, which is Islam, while they were averse, he says: and the hypocrites were averse to the appearance of God's command and His victory for you.

And now, God will make you and His religion prevail over the disbelievers among the Romans and others who disbelieve in Him, and they are reluctant to do so. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they turned matters upside down for you

, meaning: to make your companions abandon you and turn your matter back on you, until the truth came and the command of God became apparent. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of people who were named specifically.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they turned matters upside down for you

, he said: Among them are Abdullah bin Abi bin Salul, Abdullah bin Nabtal, the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, Rafa’ah bin Rafi’, and Zaid bin Al-Tabut Al-Qaynuqa’i. Abdullah bin Ubayy’s discouragement of his companions from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this raid was like the one who:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri,
m: Yazid bin Ruman, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, Asim bin Umar bin Qatada, and others, each of them narrated what he had heard about the Battle of Tabuk, and some of the people narrated what others had not narrated, and all of their hadiths gathered in this hadith: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to prepare for the Battle of the Romans, and that was at a time of hardship for the people, intense heat, and drought in the land, and when the fruits were ripe and the shade was dear, so the people loved to stay in their fruits and shade, and hated to depart from it, given the state of the time they were in. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rarely went out on a battle except that he referred to it and informed that he intended something other than the one he was facing, except for the Battle of Tabuk, for he made it clear to the people, due to the distance of the distance, the harshness of the time, and the large number of the enemy who faced him, so that the people would prepare for it with his preparation. So he ordered the people to wage jihad, and informed them that he intended the Romans. So the people prepared.” Despite their hatred for that face, they greatly appreciated the mention of the Romans and their invasion. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out on his journey, so he ordered the people to prepare and pack, and he urged the wealthy to spend and carry loads for the sake of God. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) set out, he camped at Thaniyat al-Wada', and Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Abi Salul camped further down from him, parallel to Dhubab - a mountain in the cemetery below Thaniyat al-Wada' - and it was claimed that he was not the smaller of the two armies. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) set out, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Ubayy stayed behind with those who stayed behind from the hypocrites and the suspicious. Abdullah bin Ubayy was the brother of Banu Awf bin al-Khazraj, Abdullah bin Nabtal was the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, and Rifa'ah bin Zayd bin al-Tabut was the brother of Banu Qaynuqa'. They were among the great hypocrites, and they were among those who plotted against Islam and its people. He said: And among them - according to what Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri - God revealed: They had sought discord before, the verse.

x: It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qais. And He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And among them

, and among the hypocrites, is he who says, ‘Give me permission,’ stay, so that I will not go with you, and do not tempt me, meaning: and do not test me by making me see the women of the yellow people and their daughters, for I am infatuated with women, so I go out and sin by doing so. Thus, the report of the people of interpretation became clear.
He mentioned the narration of that on the authority of the one who said it:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Give me permission and do not tempt me

, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Fight Tabuk, and take the daughters of the yellow ones and the women of the Romans as booty!’ So the grandfather said: ‘Give us permission, and do not tempt us with the women.’”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, they said:
