m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go on a raid and you will take the daughters of the yellow ones as booty, meaning the slave girls of the Romans, then he mentioned something similar. ... He said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement:
h
Give me permission and do not tempt me
, he said: He is Al-Jadd bin Qais, who said: The Ansar have learned that if I see women I will not be patient until I am tempted, but I will help you with my money.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri,
m: Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada and others, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day while he was preparing to go to Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah: ‘Would you like to fight the yellow ones this year, O Jadd? ’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, or
h
give me permission and do not tempt me

, for by God my people know that there is no man more amazed by women than I am, and I fear that if I see the women of Banu Al-Yasr I will not be able to resist them! ’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and said: ‘I have given you permission! ’ This verse was revealed about Al-Jadd ibn Qays: ‘
h
And among them is he who says
h
Give me permission and do not tempt me

.” ’ The verse means: If he only feared temptation from the women of Banu Al-Yasr, but that was not the case, then the temptation that he fell into by staying away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and preferring himself over himself, is greater.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And among them is he who says

, ‘Give me permission and do not put me to trial,’ he said: “He is a man from the hypocrites called Jadd ibn Qays. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘This year we will attack the yellow people and take from them concubines and slave girls.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, give me permission and do not put me to trial. If you do not give me permission, I will be put to trial and stay away!’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry, and God said: ‘Indeed, they have fallen into trial. Indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.’” He was from Banu Salamah, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Who is your master, O Banu Salamah? They said: Jadd ibn Qays, but he is a miserly coward! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What disease is worse than miserliness? But your master is the white, curly-haired young man, Bishr ibn al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them is he who says
, ‘Give me permission and do not put me to trial,’ he says: Give me permission and do not expel me. Unquestionably, they have fallen into trial, meaning: they have fallen into hardship.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And among them is he who says

, ‘Give me leave and do not put me to trial,’ and do not make me sin. Unquestionably, they have fallen into sin.” And His statement: And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers, meaning: Indeed, the Fire will surround those who disbelieved in God, denied His signs, and belied His messengers, surrounding them and gathering them all together on the Day of Resurrection. He says: It is sufficient for Al-Jadd bin Qais and his likes among the hypocrites to be disgraced by its burning.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, if you are pleased with God’s opening of the land of the Romans to you in this raid of yours, Al-Jadd bin Qais and his peers and followers from the hypocrites will be upset. And if a calamity befalls you with the remnants of your army, Al-Jadd and his peers will say: We have already taken our precautions by staying behind from Muhammad and abandoning his followers to his enemy, “before, meaning before this calamity befalls him, and they turn away while they are rejoicing, meaning: and they turn away from Muhammad while they are rejoicing at the calamity that befell Muhammad and his companions, with the remnants of his companions and their defeat from him, and the killing of those of them who were killed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
If good befalls you
, it distresses them, meaning:
h
If good befalls you
on your journey to Tabuk, it distresses them, he said: The grandfather and his companions.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We have already taken our matter before, he warned us.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We have already taken our matter before, he said: We have been warned.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If good befalls you
, it distresses them, if it was a victory for the Muslims, it would be great for them and distress them.

x: God Almighty says, educating His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who stayed behind you, Nothing will happen to us, O you who doubt their religion, except what God has decreed for us, in the Preserved Tablet, and decreed for us. He is our Protector, meaning: He is our helper against His enemies. And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning: And in God let the believers put their trust, for if they put their trust in Him, and do not hope for victory from anyone other than Him, and do not fear anything other than Him, He will suffice them in their affairs, and grant them victory over those who wronged and plotted against them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites whose characteristics I have described to you and whose situation I have made clear to you: Do you expect from us anything but one of two things that are better than the others? Either victory over the enemy and a conquest for us by our defeating them, in which there is reward, spoils, and safety, or killing us by our enemy, in which there is martyrdom, winning Paradise, and salvation from the Fire. Both of these are things that we love and do not hate. And we are waiting for you that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, meaning: And we are waiting for God to afflict you with a punishment from Himself that will destroy you, or by our hands, so that we will kill you, Then wait, for we are with you waiting, meaning: So wait, for we are with you waiting to see what God will do with us, and to what the matter of each group of us and you will come to.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things
? He said: Conquest or martyrdom. And he said another time: He said: Killing, so it is martyrdom and life and provision. Or He will disgrace you by our hands.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do you await for us anything but one of two good things

? He said: He is killed in it, life and provision, or he is victorious, in which case God will give him a great reward. It is like His statement: And whoever fights in the way of God to and is killed or victorious, then We will give him a great reward (al-Ma’idah 5:74).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except one of the two good things
, he said: Killing in the way of God, and triumphing over His enemies. ... He said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:

c: It was reported to me on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Killing in the way of God, and appearing.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: One of the two good things: being killed in the way of God, and being victorious over the enemies of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: With a punishment from Him, meaning death, or by Our hands, he said: killing.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things
? except victory or being killed in the way of God, And we await for you that God will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands, meaning killing.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites: Spend your money however you wish on this journey of yours and others, and in whatever condition you wish, willingly or unwillingly, for if you spend it, God will not accept your expenditures from you, and you are in doubt about your religion, and ignorant of the prophethood of your Prophet, and poorly aware of God’s reward and punishment, Indeed, you were a people of transgressors, meaning: outside of faith in your Lord. His statement,
h
Spend willingly or unwillingly

, is taken as a command, and its meaning is a reward. The Arabs do that in places where it is appropriate to use in which means reward, as God Almighty said, Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them (al-Tawbah 9:80). It is in the form of a command, and its meaning is a reward.

i: From this is the saying of the poet:
x: Treat us well or badly, we are not to be blamed or criticized if you offend us.
Likewise, his saying:
h
Spend willingly or unwillingly
, means: If you
h
spend willingly or unwillingly

, it will not be accepted from you. It was said: This verse was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qais, when he said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, offered him to go out with him to conquer al-Rum 30:(This is my money, with which I will help you).

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, Al-Jadd bin Qais said: When I see women, I cannot be patient until I am tempted, but I will help you with my money! He said: So it was revealed about him: Whether you
h
spend willingly or unwillingly
, it will never be accepted from you, he said: Because of his saying (I will help you with my money).

x: God Almighty says: What prevented these hypocrites, O Muhammad, from accepting their expenses that they spent on their travel with you, and on other paths, except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. The first an is in the accusative case, and the second is in the nominative case, because the meaning of the statement is: What prevented the acceptance of their expenditures is their disbelief in God. And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, meaning: They do not come to it except reluctantly. However, they do not hope for a reward for performing it, nor do they fear punishment for abandoning it. Rather, they perform it out of fear for themselves for abandoning it from the believers. So if they feel secure from them, they do not perform it. And they do not spend, meaning: They do not spend anything from their money, except while they are reluctant, that they spend it in the way in which they spend it, which strengthens Islam and its people.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: O Muhammad, do not be impressed by the wealth of these hypocrites or their children in this worldly life.
h
God only wants to punish them with it in the Hereafter
. He said: The meaning of that is to bring it forward, and it is delayed.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So do not let their wealth or their children impress you
, he said: This is one of the old sayings, he says: Do not let their wealth or their children impress you in this worldly life, God only wants to punish them with them in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God only wants to punish them with it in the Hereafter

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: God only wants to punish them with it in this worldly life, because of the obligations He imposed on them in it.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Salman Al-Ansari, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: God only wants to punish them with it in the life of this world, he said: By taking zakat and spending in the way of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world
, with the calamities in it, it is a punishment for them and it is a reward for the believers.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard, in our view, is the interpretation that we mentioned from Al-Hasan. Because that is the apparent meaning of the revelation, so diverting its interpretation to what its apparent meaning indicates is more appropriate than diverting it to an inner meaning that does not indicate its correctness. Rather, he directed that to the presentation, while it is delayed, because he did not know of a way to direct God’s punishment of the hypocrites with their wealth and children in this worldly life, and he said: How can He punish them with that in this world while they are happy in it? And he went away from directing it to the fact that it is a great punishment for him, obligating him to do what God has obligated him to do in it of his rights and obligations, since he was obligating it and it was taken from him while he was not in a good mood, nor hoping for a reward from God, nor from taking from him praise or thanks, out of boredom with it and hatred.
As for his saying:
h
And their souls will depart while they are disbelievers

, it means that their souls will depart, and they will die in their disbelief in God and their denial of the prophethood of the Prophet of God, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is said: (So-and-so’s soul was ruined, and was ruined), so whoever says (was ruined) says: (was ruined), and whoever says (was ruined) says: (was ruined), (was ruined), and from it it is said: (So-and-so was ruined in front of the people, was ruined) if he preceded them and went ahead of them. And it is said: (falsehood was ruined) if it went away and was destroyed.

God Almighty says: And these hypocrites swear to you, O believers, by God, falsely and wrongfully, out of fear of you: Indeed, they are of you in religion and faith. God Almighty says, belying them: And they are not of you, meaning: They are not of your religion and faith, rather they are people of doubt and hypocrisy, but they are a people who are afraid, meaning: But they are a people who fear you, so out of fear of you they say with their tongues: (Indeed, we are of you), so that they may feel safe among you and not be killed.

God Almighty says: If these hypocrites could find a refuge, meaning: a fortress in which they could be squeezed, or a stronghold in which they could be detained, or caves. They are caves in the mountains, the singular of which is maghārah, and it is a muf’al, from gharār al-rajūl fī al-shay’, yaghwār fīh, if he entered, and from this it is said, gharāt al-‘ayn, if it enters the pupil. Or an entrance means: a passage in the ground into which they enter. He said, Or an entrance, because it is from enter, enter. His saying:
h
They turned back to him
, meaning:
h
they turned back to him

, fleeing from you, while they were running, meaning: while they were speeding up their pace. It was said: Al-Jamah is a walk between two walks, and from it is the saying of Muhalhil: I have been so wild in their blood that I have seen their nobles extinguished. God described them with this description because they stood among the companions of the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in their disbelief, hypocrisy, and enmity towards them and their belief in God and His Messenger, because they were among their people and clan, in their homes and with their wealth, and they were not able to abandon that and separate from it.

So they treated the people with hypocrisy, and defended themselves, their wealth, and their children with disbelief and the claim of belief, while in their souls there was hatred for the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) and the people of belief in him and enmity towards them. So God said, describing them with what was in their hearts: If only they could find a refuge or caves Al-An’am 2:17. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If they could find a refuge
, “refuge” means a place of protection in the mountains, and cave holes means caves in the mountains. And his statement: or an entrance, and entrance means a passageway.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If they could find a refuge or caves or a place of entrance

, they would turn to it, rushing headlong into it. “Refuge” means a place of protection. Or caves means two caverns. Or a place of entrance means going into the earth, which is a tunnel in the earth, which is a passageway.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
If they could find a refuge or caves or a place of entrance
, he said: A place of protection to which they could flee from you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If they could find a refuge or caves or a place of entry
, he said: A place of protection for them, they would flee to it from you. Ibn Abbas said: His statement:
h
If they could find a refuge
, a place of protection, or caves, he said: caverns, or a place of entry, he said: a tunnel in the ground.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
If they could find a refuge
or caves or an entrance, he says:
h
If they could find a refuge
, fortresses, or caves, dens, or an entrance, flocks, they would turn to it, rushing headlong into it.

x: God Almighty says: Among the hypocrites whose description I have described to you, O Muhammad, in these verses, is he who criticizes you concerning the charity, meaning: he finds fault with you in the matter of it, and criticizes you for it. It is said: So-and-so slandered so-and-so, slanders him, and slanders him if he criticizes him and pinches him, and likewise hamza backbiting him, and from it it is said: So-and-so is a slanderer and backbiter, and from it the saying of Ru’bah: I brought my neck and my eyes closer together in the shadow of my false and misleading era And from it the other said: If I find you showing me a smile even when I am absent, then you are the one who criticizes and backbites. If they are given from it, they will be satisfied, meaning: It is not their fault in their finding fault with you and their slandering you because of it, but their anger is for themselves.

If you give them from it what pleases them, they will be satisfied with you, but if you do not give them from it, they will be angry with you and criticize you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities
, he said: They criticize you.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities

, meaning they question you and ask you. Ibn Jurayj said: And Dawud ibn Abi Asim informed me, he said: Charity was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he distributed it here and there until it was gone. He said: A man from the Ansar saw him and said: This is not justice! So this verse was revealed.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities
, meaning:
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities

. “And it was mentioned to us that a man from the desert, who had recently met a Bedouin, came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was distributing gold and silver, and said: O Muhammad, by God, if God has commanded you to be just, you have not been just! So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you! Who will be just with you after me? Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of this man and his likes, for my nation will be like this man, they recite the Qur’an but it does not go beyond their collarbones, so if they go out, kill them, then if they go out, kill them, then if they go out, kill them.” And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will not give you anything nor will I withhold it from you, I am only a treasurer.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them is he who criticizes you concerning the charities, he said: He criticizes. ... He said, Muhammad bin Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distributing, Ibn Dhi Al-Khuwaisira Al-Tamimi came to him and said: Be just, O Messenger of God! He said: Woe to you, who will be just if I am not just! Umar bin Al-Khattab said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off his head! He said: Leave him, for he has companions, one of whom would consider his prayer insignificant compared to their prayer, and his fasting insignificant compared to their fasting. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target. He looks at its point and sees nothing, then he looks at its head and finds nothing, then he looks at its blade and finds nothing. The dung and blood have already passed. Their sign is a black man, one of his hands - or he said: his hands - like a woman’s breast - or like a piece of cloth that is dripping - they will emerge at a time of hiatus among the people.” He said: Then the verse was revealed:
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities
. Abu Saeed said: I bear witness that I heard this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I bear Surat al-Tawbah 9:58
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities

. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry. witness that when Ali, may God have mercy on him, killed them, the man was brought with the description that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: “
h
And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities

. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry,” he said: These are the hypocrites. They said: By God, Muhammad only gives it to whom he loves, and he does not give it to anyone except his own desires! So God informed His Prophet, and informed them that it came from God, and that this is a command from God, not from Muhammad: The charities are only for the poor, the verse.

x: God Almighty says: If only those who criticize you, O Muhammad, regarding the charity, were satisfied with what God and His Messenger gave them of gifts and what He apportioned to them of shares, and said, ‘God is sufficient for us,’ meaning: and they said: God is sufficient for us, God will give us of His bounty and so will His Messenger, meaning: God will give us from the bounty of His treasuries and His Messenger from charity and other things, Indeed, we are desirous of God, meaning: and they said: We are desirous of God that He may expand upon us from His bounty, so that we may be independent of charity and other things from people’s connections and need for them.
God Almighty says: Charity is only for the poor and the needy, and those whom God Almighty has named. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the poor and the needy.
Some of them said: The poor means the needy person who refrains from asking, and the destitute means the needy person who asks.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Charity is only for the poor and the needy. He said: The poor is the one who sits in his house, and the needy is the one who strives.

c: Al-Muntha told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
, he said: The needy are those who go around, and the needy are the poor Muslims.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Jarir ibn Hazim, he said, a man told me, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd:
m: that he was asked about the poor, he said: The poor are those who are self-sufficient, and the needy are those who ask.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muqal bin Ubaid God al-Jazari told us:
m: I asked al-Zuhri about his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor
, he said: Those who are in their homes and do not ask, and the needy, those who go out and ask.

c: Al-Harith told us, Al-Qasim told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abdul-Warith bin Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The poor person is the one who does not ask, and the needy person is the one who asks.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
, he said: The poor are those who do not ask people, people of need, and the needy are those who ask people.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told me, he said, Abdul Warith told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The poor are those who do not ask, and the needy are those who ask.

x: Others said: The poor person is the one in need, and the needy person is the one who is healthy.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
. He said: The poor is the one who is suffering from a disease, and the needy is the healthy person in need.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
. As for the poor, he is the one who has a time limit, and as for the needy, he is the one who does not have a time limit.

x: Others said: The poor are the poor immigrants, and the needy are those Muslims who did not immigrate and are in need.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hakam, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim:
m: h
Zakat is only for the poor

, he said: the poor immigrants, and the needy, those who did not immigrate. ... He said, Abdul Aziz told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: (The alms are only for the poor emigrants), Sufyan said: He means: And the Bedouins are not given anything from it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: It was said: Charity is only for the poor immigrants. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: She used to give charity to the poor immigrants
h
and in the way of God

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: and Saʿid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, they said: There were some people from the emigrants, one of whom had a house, a wife, a slave, and a camel, on which he would perform Hajj and fight, so God attributed to them that they were poor, and He gave them a share in the zakat.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Charity is only for the poor immigrants
h
and in the way of God

x: Others said: The poor means the one who has little income.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: Umar said:
m: The poor person is not the one who has no money, but the poor person is the one who is not accustomed to earning. Yaqub said: Ibn Ulayyah said: (Akhlaq) means the distorted, according to us.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: That Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, said: The poor person is not the one who has no money, but the poor person is the one who is inclined to earn. And some of them said: (The poor person) is from the Muslims, and (the poor person) is from the People of the Book.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Omar bin Nafi’ told us, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah regarding his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
, he said: Do not say to the poor Muslims poor, rather poor means the poor people of the Book.

x: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: The poor is the one who is poor and in need, and despite his need he refrains from asking people and being humble to them, in this context, and the needy is the one who is in need and is humble to people by asking them. We said that this is the case, even though the two groups were only given for poverty and need, not for humiliation and begging, because of the consensus of all scholars that the poor is only given from the obligatory charity for poverty, and that the meaning of poverty among the Arabs is humiliation, as God the Most High said: And humiliation and destitution were imposed upon them (al-Baqarah 2:61), meaning by that: disgrace and humiliation, not poverty. So since God the Most High has classified those to whom He has divided from the obligatory charity into a portion based on poverty, and made them into two categories, it is known that each category of them is different from the other.

Since this is the case, there is no doubt that the one to whom it is divided by the name of the poor is not the one to whom it is divided by the name of poverty and poverty. The poor person who is given that by the name of the absolute poor is the one in whom there is no poverty, and the one who is given by the name of poverty and destitution is the one who combines poverty with his poverty, which is humiliation in asking and begging. The interpretation of the statement, since that was its meaning: Charity is only for the poor: the abstinent among them who do not ask, and the humble among them who ask.

c: It was narrated from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what we have said about that.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told me, on the authority of Sharik bin Abi Namir, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The poor person is not the one who is refused a morsel or two, or a date or two. Rather, the poor person is the one who is too modest to do so. Read, if you wish, ‘They do not ask people insistently’ (al-Baqarah 2:273).” The meaning of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The poor person is only the one who is self-sufficient, is in the manner in which people have come to call the poor poor, not in detailing the poor person from the needy person. What indicates that this is the case is his, may God bless him and grant him peace, quoting God’s statement: Read, if you wish, They do not ask people insistently (al-Baqarah 2:273), and that is in describing the one whom He began mentioning and describing as poor, saying: “For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God, unable to move about in the land. The ignorant think them rich because of their self-restraint. You will recognize them by their mark. They do not ask people insistently” (al-Baqarah 2:273). His saying:
h
And those who work on it

, they are the ones who work to collect it from its people and give it to those who deserve it. They are given that through work, whether they are rich or poor. And the people of interpretation said the same as we Surat al-Tawbah 9:60 Alms are only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect them and those whose hearts are to be reconciled and to free captives and those in debt and in the cause of God and for the wayfarer - an obligation imposed by God. And God is Knowing and Wise. said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Maqal bin Ubaid God told us:
m: I asked Al-Zuhri about those who work on it, and he said: The messengers.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And those who work on it
, he said: Its collectors, those who collect it and strive in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And those who work on it
, meaning those who work on it. Then the people of interpretation differed about the amount that the worker is given from that.

x: Some of them said: He should be given the price.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Hassan bin Saleh, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: Those who work on it are entitled to an eighth of the charity.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Muslim bin Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
and those who work on it
, he said: The workers eat from the eighth share.

x: Others said: Rather, he is given according to his work.

Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Abdul-Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated, on the authority of Al-Akhdar bin Ajlan, who said: Ata’ bin Zuhair Al-Amiri narrated, on the authority of his father: That he met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and asked him about charity: What kind of wealth is it? He said: The wealth of the lame, the one-eyed, the blind, and everyone who is stranded. So he said to him: The workers have a right, and so do the mujahideen! He said: The mujahideen are a people for whom it is permissible,
h
and those who work on it
are according to their work. Then he said: Charity is not permissible for the rich, nor for the one who has a healthy heart.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said:
m: It is for the worker on it if he works according to what is right. Neither Umar, may God have mercy on him, nor those people gave the worker the price. Rather, they imposed it according to the extent of his work.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And those who work on it
, he said: The workers were given.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The worker is given according to the extent of his work and the wage of his peers. We said: This is more correct, because God, the Most High, did not divide the charity of wealth among the eight categories into eight shares, but rather He knew that the charity would not go beyond these eight categories to others. Since this is the case, as we will explain later, and as we have explained in another place, it is known that whoever is given a right from it, is given according to the effort of the giver in it. If this is the case, and the worker is given according to his work, not according to the need that is removed by the gift, it is known that what he was given from it is only compensation for his effort and work, and that it is only the amount he deserves as compensation for his work that is not removed by the gift, but is removed by dismissal.

As for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, they are people who used to reconcile with Islam those who were not right to support it, in order to reform themselves and their clan, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Uyaynah ibn Badr, Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, and their counterparts from the tribal leaders. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement: and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, they were people who used to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had become Muslims. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give them charity, and if he gave them charity and they gained something good from it, they would say: This is a good religion! But if it was otherwise, they would criticize him and abandon him.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer:
m: Those whose hearts were to be reconciled from Banu Umayyah were: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, from Banu Makhzum: al-Harith ibn Hisham, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Yarbu’, from Banu Jumah: Safwan ibn Umayyah, from Banu Amir ibn Lu’ayy: Suhayl ibn Amr, and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza: Hakim ibn Hizam, from Banu Hashim: Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from Banu Fazarah: Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Badr, from Banu Tamim: al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, from Banu Nasr: Malik ibn Awf, from Banu Salim: al-Abbas ibn Mirdas, and from Thaqeef: al-Ala’ ibn Haritha. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave each man of them one hundred camels, except Abd al-Rahman ibn Yarbu’ and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, for he gave each man fifty.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Safwan ibn Umayya said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to me, and he was the most hated of people to me, and he continued to give to me until he was the most beloved of people to me.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: There were people whom he used to win over with gifts, Uyaynah bin Badr and those who were with him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled, those who are to be reconciled to Islam.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: As for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, they are people from among the Bedouins and others, whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to reconcile with gifts so that they would believe.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muqal bin Ubaid God told us,
m: I asked Al-Zuhri about his statement: and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, so he said: Whoever converts to Islam from among the Jews or Christians. I said: Even if he is rich? He said: Even if he is rich.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Maqal bin Ubaid God Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri:
m: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled, he said: He is a Jew or a Christian. Then the scholars differed about the existence of the conciliator today or not, and whether someone today is given charity for conciliating people to Islam?

x: Some of them said: The conciliation of hearts has become invalid today, and no one has a share in the obligatory charity except for those who need it, in the way of God, or who work on it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled, he said: As for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, it is not today.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: There are no people today whose hearts are to be reconciled. They were only during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Habban ibn Abi Jabalah, who said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said, and Uyaynah ibn Hisn came to him: The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve (al-Kahf 18:29), meaning: Today is not a day to reconcile.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Today is not a day to reconcile.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The hearts of those who were to be reconciled were only during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but when Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, took office, the bribes were cut off.

x: Others said: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled, in every age, and their right to charity.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, who said:
m: Among the people today are those whose hearts are to be reconciled.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar,
m: the same.

x: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that God made charity in two meanings: one of them is to fill the need of the Muslims, and the other is to aid and strengthen Islam. Whatever aids Islam and strengthens its causes is given to the rich and the poor, because it is not given to those who are given it because of their need for it, but rather it is given to them as aid for the religion. This is like what is given to those who are given for jihad in the way of God, for it is given to those who are rich or poor, for the sake of conquest, not to fill their need. Likewise, those whose hearts are to be reconciled are given it even if they are rich, in order to improve their situation by giving them the matter of Islam and seeking to strengthen and support it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to those whose hearts are to be reconciled, after God had granted them conquests, and Islam had spread and its people had become strong.

So there is no argument for someone who argues by saying: (No one can be reconciled to Islam today, because its people are prevented by the large number of those who wanted them), and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to those whom he gave from them in the situation described. As for his saying: and in the necks, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning.
Some of them, and they are the majority, said: They are the slaves who are being freed, and they are given from it to free their slaves.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Dinar, on the authority of Al-Husayn:
m: That a freed slave stood up to Musa Al-Ash'ari, may God have mercy on him, while he was delivering a sermon to the people on Friday, and said: O Emir, urge the people against me! So Abu Musa urged him against him, and the people threw a turban, a sheet, and a ring at him, until they threw a great deal of black. When Abu Musa saw what was thrown at him, he said: Surat al-Tawbah 9:60 Alms are only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect them and those whose hearts are to be reconciled and to free captives and those in debt and in the cause of God and for the wayfarer - an obligation imposed by God. And God is Knowing and Wise. Gather it! So it was gathered, then he ordered it to be sold. He gave the freed slave his freed slave's rights, then he gave the surplus for the slaves, and he did not return it to the people, and he said: The people were only given for the slaves.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muqal bin Ubaid God told us,
m: I asked Al-Zuhri about his statement:
h
And for the slaves
, he said: The freed slaves.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And for the slaves
, he said: The slaves who are being freed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And in the slaves, he said: They are the freed slaves.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: There is nothing wrong with freeing a slave from zakat.

x: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is the statement of those who said: He meant by the slaves, in this case, the freed slaves, because of the consensus of the evidence on that, for God made zakat a right that is obligatory upon the one upon whom He made it obligatory from his wealth, and he pays it from it, and no benefit of worldly goods returns to him from it, nor is there any compensation for it. And the one who frees a slave from it, the loyalty of the one who freed him returns to him, and that is a benefit that returns to him from it. As for the indebted ones, those who borrowed money not for the sake of disobeying God, and then could not find anything to pay off their debts in terms of property or honour. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Those who are in debt are those whose house is burned down, or whose property is lost in a flood, and whose dependents are in debt. This is one of those who are in debt.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Uthman bin al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: and the debtors, he said: Whoever’s house burned down, his money was taken away by a flood, and he owed money to his family.

c: Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said:
m: Those in debt are those who borrow money without extravagance. The imam should pay it on their behalf from the public treasury. ...He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Maqal bin Ubaid God told us, he said: Al-Zuhri asked us about those in debt, he said: Those who are in debt. ... He said, Maqal told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, who said, a servant of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz who served him for twenty years told me: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz wrote: That the debtors be given - Ahmad said: I think most of the time: from the alms. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said: Those in debt are those who borrow money for a non-extravagance purpose.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: As for those in debt, they are people who are drowned in debt, but not due to poverty, extravagance, or corruption.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: The debtor is the one who is in debt.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the debtors, he said: He is the one whose wealth is lost by a flood or fire, and whose dependents are in debt. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said: The one who borrows for a non-corrupt purpose. ... He said, my father told me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said: Those in debt are those who borrow money without corruption. The imam should pay it on their behalf.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They are people who have been burdened with debts without corruption or extravagance, so God has given them a share in this verse. As for his saying:
h
And in the way of God

, he means: and in spending in support of God’s religion, His path, and His law that He has legislated for His servants, by fighting His enemies, and that is the conquest of the infidels. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And in the way of God
, he said: The one who fights in the way of God.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: a man who worked on it, or a man who bought it with his money, or in the way of God, or a wayfarer, or a man who had a neighbor to whom he gave charity and he gave it to him as a gift.” ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person, except for three: in the way of God, or a wayfarer, or a man who had a neighbor and gave him charity, so he gave it to him.” As for his saying:
h
And the wayfarer

, he is the traveler who passes from one country to another. And the path is the road, and the one who strikes it is called the wayfarer, because he sticks to it, as the poet said: I am the son of war, you raised me as a child until I grew up and became mature for my own good. The Arabs do the same, they call the intransitive noun for something by which it is known: his son. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, he said:
m: The wayfarer is the one who travels from one land to another.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Mandil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the wayfarer
, he said: The wayfarer has a right to zakat even if he is rich, if he is cut off from it.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Muqal bin Ubaid God told us:
m: I asked Al-Zuhri about the wayfarer. He said: A wayfarer comes to me in need. I said: What if he is rich? He said: What if he is rich.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the wayfarer
, the guest, he was given a right in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: The wayfarer is the traveler, whoever he is, rich or poor, if his expenses are lost or damaged, or something happens to them, or he does not have anything with him, then his right is obligatory.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, that he said:
m: Concerning the rich man who travels and is in need during his journey, he said: He takes from the zakat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, who said:
m: The wayfarer is the one who travels from one land to another. And His statement: A duty from God, He, the Most High, says: A portion that God has divided for them, and He has made it obligatory for them from the wealth of those who have wealth. And God is Knowing, of the interests of His creation in what He has imposed for them, and in other than that, nothing is hidden from Him. So with His knowledge of the obligation of what He has imposed of charity, and what is in it of interest, Wise, in His management of His creation, no defect enters into His management. Scholars differed on how to divide the alms mentioned by God in this verse. Is there a right to each of the eight categories in it, or is it up to the owner of the money and the one who is in charge of dividing it, so that he can give all of it to whomever he wants from the eight categories? Most scholars said: The one in charge can divide it and put it in any of the eight categories he wants. God named the eight categories in the verse to inform His creation that charity does not go from these eight categories to others, not to require it to be divided among the eight categories that He mentioned.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Hudhayfah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy and those who collect it
, he said: If you wish, you can make it into one category, or two categories, or three.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said:
m: If you put it in one category, it will suffice for you. ... He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar: Charity is only for the poor. He said: Whichever category you give from this, it will suffice you. ... He said: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abdul Muttalib, on the authority of Ata’:
h
Zakat is only for the poor

, the verse. He said: If you were to put it in one of these categories, it would suffice you. And if you were to look at a poor Muslim household that was self-sufficient and help them with it, that would be more pleasing to me. ... He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Charity is only for the poor and the needy, and those who collect it, “
h
and the wayfarer

,” so whichever of these categories you give it to, it will suffice you. ... He said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy and those who collect it

. He said: This is only something I know, so whichever of these categories you give it to will suffice for you. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim: Alms are only for the poor. He said: Whichever of these categories you put it in, it will suffice you. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Surat al-Tawbah 9:60 Alms are only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect them and those whose hearts are to be reconciled and to free captives and those in debt and in the cause of God and for the wayfarer - an obligation imposed by God. And God is Knowing and Wise. on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: If you put it in one category of what God has named, it will suffice you. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, who said: If you put it in one category of what God has named, it will suffice you. ... He said, Khalid bin Hayyan Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Burqan, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran: Charity is only for the poor. He said: If you give it to one category of these, it will suffice for you. ... He said, Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Masoud, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
h
Zakat is only for the poor and the needy

, the verse. He said: I know who its people are. ... He said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar: that he used to take the obligatory charity and put it in one category.

x: Some of the later scholars used to say: If the owner of the wealth is in charge of dividing it, he must divide it into six categories, because those whose hearts he wants to reconcile have gone, and the share of the workers is nullified by his dividing it. He claims that it is not sufficient for him to give less than three people from each category. He used to say: If the imam is in charge of dividing it, he must divide it into seven categories, and nothing else is sufficient for him.

God Almighty says: Among these hypocrites are a group who harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and criticize him, and they say, ‘He is an ear,’ a listener, who hears what everyone says, so he accepts it and believes it. It is from their saying: (A man of ear), like (Fa’lah), if he is quick to listen and accept, as it is said: (He is certain, and certain) if he is certain of everything that happened. Its origin is from (Adhanah lahu ya’dhan), if he listened to him. And from it is the hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has not given ear to anything as He has given ear to a prophet who chants the Qur’an, and from it is the saying of Adi bin Zaid: O heart, be comforted by my concern, for my concern is in hearing and ears. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Nabtal bin Al-Harith.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: God mentioned their deception - meaning the hypocrites - and their harm to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said:
h
And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say

, ‘He is an ear,’ verse. The one who said that statement, as far as I have heard, was Nabtal ibn al-Harith, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and this verse was revealed about him, because he said: Muhammad is only an ear! Whoever tells him something, he believes it! God says: Say, ‘He is an ear of good for you,’ meaning: he hears good and believes it. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Say, ‘It is a good omen for you.’ The majority of the reciters of the regions read this: “Say: ‘It is a good ear for you,’” by adding the ear to the good, meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad: It is a good ear, not an evil ear.

c: It was reported on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: that he read it as: “Say: ‘Aa’ishah khair lakum’ (Say: “Aa’ishah is better for you”), with the tanween of aa’ishah (Say: Aa’ishah is better for you), and aa’ishah becomes its predicate, meaning: Say: Who among you, O hypocrites, will hear what you say and believe you, if Muhammad is as you have described him, that if you come to him and deny what he has mentioned about you of your harming him and your faults towards him, he will hear from you and believe you, that is better for you than that he should lie to you and not accept from you what you say. Then he denied them and said: Rather, it is not accepted except from the believers, who believes in God
h
and believes in the believers

x: The correct reading in my opinion is the reading of the one who read: Say, ‘It is a good ear for you,’ by adding the ear to the good, meaning: Say, ‘It is a good ear for you, not an evil ear. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who annoy the Prophet and say
, ‘He is an ear,’ meaning, he hears from everyone.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say
, ‘He is only an ear,’ he said: They used to say: (Muhammad is only an ear, he does not narrate anything from us, but he is only an ear who hears what is said to him).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they say, ‘He is an ear.’ We say whatever we want and swear, and he believes us.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: He is the one who gives permission, he said: They say: We say whatever we want, then we swear to him and he believes us.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. As for his saying:
h
He believes in God
, he is saying:
h
He believes in God
alone, with no partner for Him. And his saying:
h
And believes in the believers

, he is saying: And he believes in the believers, not the disbelievers nor the hypocrites. This is a denial from God to the hypocrites who said: Muhammad listened! God Almighty says: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only a good listener, who believes in God and what came from Him,
h
and believes in the believers

, not the hypocrites and disbelievers in God. It was said: And He believes in the believers, meaning: And He believes in the believers, because the Arabs say, as we have been told about them: (I believed in him, and I believed him), meaning: I believed him, just as it was said: He has given you some of what you are hastening, (al-Naml 27:72), meaning: He has given you some, and just as He said: For those who fear their Lord (al-A’raf 7:154), meaning: For those who fear their Lord. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He believes in God
h
and believes in the believers
, meaning:
h
He believes in God
h
and believes in the believers
. As for his saying:
h
And a mercy to those of you who believe

, the readings differed in its reading: So the majority of the people of the countries read it as: And a mercy to those who believe, meaning: Say, It is a good ear for you, and it is a mercy to those of you who believe. So he raised mercy, in conjunction with ear. Some Kufians read: mercy, in apposition to good, with the interpretation: Say, goodness is your ear, and mercy is your ear.

x: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it: And mercy, in the nominative case, in apposition to the ear, meaning: And it is a mercy for those among you who believe. And God made it a mercy for those who followed it and were guided by its guidance, and believed in what it brought from their Lord, because God saved them from misguidance through it, and caused them to inherit His gardens through following it.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And those who harm the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment

God Almighty says: For these hypocrites who criticize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: He is an ear, and their likes among those who deny him, and who speak falsehood and slander about him, there is a painful punishment from God for them in the fire of Hell.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Say, ‘It is a good omen for you.’
The majority of the reciters of the regions read this: “Say: ‘It is a good ear for you,’” by adding the ear to the good, meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad: It is a good ear, not an evil ear.

It was reported on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read it as: “Say: ‘Aa’ishah khair lakum’ (Say: “Aa’ishah is better for you”), with the tanween of aa’ishah (Say: Aa’ishah is better for you), and aa’ishah becomes its predicate, meaning: Say: Who among you, O hypocrites, will hear what you say and believe you, if Muhammad is as you have described him, that if you come to him and deny what he has mentioned about you of your harming him and your faults towards him, he will hear from you and believe you, that is better for you than that he should lie to you and not accept from you what you say.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in my opinion is the reading of the one who read: Say, ‘It is a good ear for you,’ by adding the ear to the good, meaning: Say, ‘It is a good ear for you, not an evil ear.

As for his saying: And a mercy to those of you who believe, the readings differed in its reading: So the majority of the people of the countries read it as: And a mercy to those who believe, meaning: Say, It is a good ear for you, and it is a mercy to those of you who believe.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it: And mercy, in the nominative case, in apposition to the ear, meaning: And it is a mercy for those among you who believe.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: These hypocrites swear to you, O believers, by God, to please you regarding what you have heard about them harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their mention of him by slandering and criticizing him, and their secret agreement with the people of disbelief against you, by God and false oaths: that they did not do that, and that they are on your religion, and with you against those who oppose you, seeking thereby your pleasure. God Almighty says: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him, by repentance and turning back from what they said and concealed, if they are believers, meaning: if they believe in the Oneness of God, acknowledging His promise and His threat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They swear to you by God to please you

, the verse, he mentioned to us that a hypocrite said: By God, these are the best and most noble of us, and even if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys! A Muslim man heard him and said: By God, what Muhammad says is true, and you are worse than a donkey! The man went to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sent for the man and called him and said to him: What made you say what you said? He began to curse and swear by God that he had not said that. The Muslim man began to say: O God, the truthful one is true and the liar is a liar! So God revealed concerning that:
h
They swear to you by God to please you
, but God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers.

x: God Almighty says: Didn’t these hypocrites who swear falsely to God to please the believers, while they persist in hypocrisy, know that whoever fights God and His Messenger, and opposes them and opposes them by opposing them, then for him is the fire of Hell, in the Hereafter, to abide therein, meaning: remaining therein and residing forever? That is the great disgrace, meaning: his remaining in the fire of Hell and his abiding therein is great humiliation and disgrace. The reading was: Fan, with the opening of the alif of an, meaning: Did they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger will have the fire of Hell, and the operation of ya’lamu in it, as if they made the second an repeated on the first, and relied on it, since the report was with it without the first.

Some of the grammarians of Basra chose the kasra in this, over the beginning, because of the entry of the letter fa in it, and its entry in it, according to him, is evidence that it is the answer to the consequence, and that if it was an answer to the consequence, the choice in it would be the beginning.

The reading that I do not approve of other than it is opening the alif in both letters, I mean the first and second an, because that is the reading of the regions, and for the reason that I mentioned regarding the Arabic language.

evidence.text: The reading was: Fan, with the opening of the alif of an, meaning: Did they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger will have the fire of Hell, and the operation of ya’lamu in it, as if they made the second an repeated on the first, and relied on it, since the report was with it without the first.

Abu Jaafar said: The reading that I do not approve of other than it is opening the alif in both letters, I mean the first and second an, because that is the reading of the regions, and for the reason that I mentioned regarding the Arabic language.

x: God Almighty says: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts, meaning: revealing to the believers what is in their hearts. It was said: God revealed this verse to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because when the hypocrites criticized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned something about his affair and the affair of the Muslims, they said: (Perhaps God will not divulge our secret!), so God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell them: Mock, threatening them and warning them: Indeed, God will bring out what you fear. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed to them. He said: They say the saying among themselves, then they say: Perhaps God will not reveal our secret to us.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: We were pleased with this. As for his saying: Indeed, God will bring out that which you fear, he means by it: God will make manifest upon you, O hypocrites, that which you feared to make manifest, so God made that manifest upon them and disgraced them, so this surah was called: Al-Fadihah.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: This surah was called Al-Fadihah, exposing the hypocrites.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you ask, O Muhammad, these hypocrites about what they said of falsehood and lies, they will surely say to you: We only said that in jest, and we were engaging in a conversation in jest and mockery! God says to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, was it God and the verses of His Book and His Messenger that you were mocking?
Ibn Ishaq used to say: The one who said this statement, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The one who said this statement, as far as I have been informed, was Wadi’ah ibn Thabit, the brother of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, from Banu Amr ibn Awf. Ali bin Dawud narrated, Abdullah bin Saleh narrated, Al-Layth narrated, Hisham bin Saad narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: A hypocrite said to Awf bin Malik during the Battle of Tabuk: What is the matter with these reciters of ours? We have the most greedy stomachs, the most lying tongues, and the most cowardly when fighting! Awf said to him: But you are a hypocrite! I will tell the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So Awf went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to tell him, but he found that the Qur’an had preceded him. Zaid said: Abdullah bin Umar said: Then I looked at him clinging to the saddle of the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) camel, and the stones were hitting him, saying: We were only babbling and playing! The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Was it at God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? He did not say anything more.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Hisham bin Saad told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, he said: A man said
m: in a gathering during the Battle of Tabuk: We have never seen anyone like these reciters of ours, more greedy in stomachs, more lying in tongues, and more cowardly in combat! A man in the gathering said: You have lied, but you are a hypocrite! I will tell the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)! This reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Qur’an was revealed. Abdullah bin Omar said: I saw him clinging to the saddle of the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) camel, and stones were hitting him, and he was saying: O Messenger of God, we were only idly talking and joking! And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was saying: “Was it at God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuses. You have disbelieved after your belief.”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you ask them

, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and joking’ until his statement: that they were criminals, he said: So there was a man whom God, if He wills, He pardoned, saying: “O God, I hear a verse that I am concerned with, which makes the skins shudder and the hearts tremble. O God, make my death a killing in Your cause, so that no one will say, ‘I was washed, I was shrouded, Surat al-Tawbah 9:65
h
And if you ask them

, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and joking." Say, "Was it at God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking?" I was buried.’” He said: So he was killed on the day of Yamamah, and there was no one among the Muslims who did not find someone else.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you ask them

, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and joking,’ the verse, he said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on his way to Tabuk, and before him were some hypocrites, they said: ‘This man hopes to conquer the palaces and fortresses of Syria! Far from it, far from it!’ So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Hold back the caravan for me!’ So he came to them and said: ‘You said such and such, you said such and such.’ They said: ‘O Prophet of God, we were only conversing and joking,’ so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed about them what you hear.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if you ask them

, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and joking.’ He said: “While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on the Tabuk expedition, and a group of hypocrites were walking in front of him, they said: ‘He thinks that he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of the Romans!’ So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they had said, and he said: ‘Bring these people to me!’ So he called them and said: ‘You said such and such!’ So they swore: ‘We were only conversing and joking!’”

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb and others, they said:
m: “A man from the hypocrites said: I do not see these reciters of ours except that they are the most greedy in their bellies, the most lying in their tongues, and the most cowardly in the encounter! So that was reported to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he had departed and mounted his camel, and he said: O Messenger of God, we were only joking and playing!
