So he said: “Was it at God and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?” until his saying: criminals, and his feet were being blown away by stones, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pay attention to him, and he was clinging to the Messenger of God’s rope, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We were only joking and playing, he said: A man from the hypocrites said: (Muhammad tells us that so-and-so’s she-camel is in such-and-such a valley, on such-and-such a day! How does he know what the unseen is?)

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

evidence.text: Ali bin Dawud narrated, Abdullah bin Saleh narrated, Al-Layth narrated, Hisham bin Saad narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: A hypocrite said to Awf bin Malik during the Battle of Tabuk: What is the matter with these reciters of ours?

Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Hisham bin Saad told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, he said: A man said in a gathering during the Battle of Tabuk: We have never seen anyone like these reciters of ours, more greedy in stomachs, more lying in tongues, and more cowardly in combat!

Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb and others, they said: “A man from the hypocrites said: I do not see these reciters of ours except that they are the most greedy in their bellies, the most lying in their tongues, and the most cowardly in the encounter!

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to those whose description I have described to you: Do not make excuses, falsely, by saying: We were just joking and playing, “You have disbelieved,” meaning: You have denied the truth by saying what you said about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him, after your belief, meaning: after your belief in him and your acknowledgment of him, If We pardon one group of you, We will punish another group. He mentioned that he meant by the sect in this place, one man.
Ibn Ishaq used to say:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The one who was pardoned, as far as I have been informed, was Makhshi ibn Hamir al-Ashja’i, an ally of Banu Salamah, and that was because he denied some of what he had heard from them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Hibban told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b:
m: If We pardon a group of you, he said: A group, meaning a man.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: If We pardon a group of you, by denying what was denied to you by disbelief, We will punish a group for their disbelief and mockery of the verses of God and His Messenger.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, some of them said:
m: There was a man among them who did not agree with them in speaking, he would walk away from them, so this verse was revealed: If We pardon one party of you, We will punish another party, so he was called a party and he is one.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If a group of you repents and God forgives them, God will punish a group of you for abandoning repentance. As for his saying: Because they were criminals, its meaning is: We will punish a group of them for committing the crime, which is disbelief in God, and their slander of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

God Almighty says: The hypocrites, men and women, and they are those who show the believers faith with their tongues, but conceal disbelief in God and His Messenger, some of them are from others, meaning: they are one group, and their command is one, in their declaration of faith, but their internal disbelief, they command those who come before them, to do evil, which is disbelief in God and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought, and denying him, and they forbid what is right, meaning: they forbid them from believing in God and His Messenger, and in what he brought them from God.
And His statement:
h
And they withhold their hands
, meaning:
h
And they withhold their hands
from spending in the way of God, and they refrain from giving charity, thus preventing those for whom God has imposed on their wealth what He has imposed of zakat from their rights, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And they hold back their hands, he said: They do not extend them to spend in a rightful way.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And they hold their hands back, they do not extend them for good.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they withhold their hands
, he said: They withhold their hands from all good. As for his saying:
h
They forgot God

, so He forgot them, its meaning is: They abandoned God by not obeying Him and following His command, so God abandoned them from His success, guidance, and mercy. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of forgetfulness is abandonment, with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They forgot God

, so He forgot them, they forgot the good, but they did not forget the evil. His saying: Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked ones, meaning: Those who deceive the believers by showing them with their tongues faith in God, while they are inwardly disbelieving, are those who depart from the obedience of God, and are outside the faith in Him and in His Messenger.

x: God Almighty says: God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers, by God, the fire of Hell, that He will burn them all in it, abiding therein forever, meaning: remaining therein forever, neither living nor dying, it is sufficient for them, meaning: it is sufficient for them as punishment and reward for their disbelief in God, and God has cursed them, meaning: God has distanced them and crushed them from His mercy, and for them is an enduring punishment, meaning: for both groups, meaning the people of hypocrisy and disbelief, with God, an enduring punishment, permanent, that does not go away or perish.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who said: We were only conversing and joking: Were you mocking at God and the verses of His Book and His Messenger?
h
Like those before you

, from the nations who did what you did, so God destroyed them and hastened for them disgrace in this world, along with what He has prepared for them of punishment and chastisement in the Hereafter. God Almighty says to them: Beware lest the punishment of God befall you like what befell them, for they were stronger and more powerful than you, and had more wealth and children than you. So enjoy their portion, meaning: enjoy their share and portion of their worldly life and religion, and were satisfied with that portion in this world in exchange for their portion in the Hereafter, and you, O hypocrites, have followed their path in enjoying your portion.

He says: You have done with your religion and your worldly life, as the nations who were before you, whom I destroyed because they disobeyed My command, enjoyed their property, meaning as those before you did with their share of their worldly life and their religion. And you have plunged, in lying and falsehood against God, like those who plunged, meaning: And you have also plunged, O hypocrites, like those nations before you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told me, on the authority of Saʿid bin Abi Saʿid Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will take as the nations before you took, cubit by cubit, span by span, and fathom by fathom, to the extent that if one of them entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it! Abu Hurairah said: Read the Qur’an if you wish: “
h
Like those before you

who were stronger than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. So you enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share, and you plunged into it as they plunged into it.” They said: O Messenger of God, as the Persians and the Romans did? He said: Are there any people except them?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Umar ibn Ata’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like those before you
, the verse, he said, Ibn Abbas said: How similar tonight is to last night!
h
Like those before you

, these are the Children of Israel, we likened them to them, I do not know except that he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will follow them until even if one of them entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. ... Ibn Jurayj said: Ziyad ibn Saʿd informed me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will follow the ways of those before you, inch by inch, cubit by cubit, and span by span, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it! They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? The People of the Book? He said: Their mouth!”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said that he said:
m: So whoever.
b.via: Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said that he

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Then enjoy their morals, he said: their religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He warned you against introducing something new into Islam, and he knew that some people from this nation would do that, so God said about that: ‘Then enjoy their way of life, and you enjoyed your way of life as those before you enjoyed their way of life, and you plunged into it as they plunged into it.’ They thought that the tribulation that had befallen the Children of Israel before them would not befall them, and that the tribulation would return as it began.” As for his statement:
h
These are the ones whose deeds have become worthless

, its meaning is: These are the ones who said: We were only conversing and playing, and they did in that the actions of the nations that perished before them. Their deeds have become worthless, meaning: Their deeds have gone in vain, and there is no reward for them except the Fire, because they were in what angers and dislikes God. And those are the losers, meaning: And those are the ones who were deceived by their deal, by selling the bliss of the Hereafter for their small and insignificant share of this world.

x: God Almighty says: Has not the report of those before them reached these hypocrites who conceal their disbelief in God and forbid belief in Him and His Messenger? He says: The report of the nations who were before them, when they disobeyed Our Messengers and opposed Our command. What happened to them from Our punishment? Then He, the Most High, mentioned those nations to which He said to these hypocrites, Did not their report reach them? He said, The people of Noah. Therefore, He lowered the people because He translated them from those who, and those who is in the position of lowering. The meaning of the words: Did not these hypocrites receive report of the people of Noah and what I did to them, when they denied My Messenger Noah and disobeyed My command? Did I not drown them in the flood? And 'Aad, he says: And the story of 'Aad, when they disobeyed My Messenger Hud, did I not destroy them with a violent, furious wind?

And the story of Thamud, when they disobeyed My Messenger Salih, did I not destroy them with the earthquake, so that I may leave them in their courtyards in ruins? And the story of the people of Abraham, when they disobeyed him and rejected what he brought them from God of the truth, did I not take away their blessings and destroy their king Nimrod? And the story of the companions of Midian, son of Abraham, did I not destroy them with the punishment of the Day of Shadow when they denied My Messenger Shu'aib? And the story of their land being overturned, so that its highest part became its lowest, when they disobeyed My Messenger Lot, and denied what he brought them from Me of the truth? God Almighty says: Do these hypocrites, who mock God, His verses, and His Messenger, feel secure that He will not take revenge on them, hasten their humiliation and punishment in this world, as did their predecessors among the nations, and that what befell them for their denial of My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will befall them for their denial of Our Messengers, when they came to them with clear proofs?
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the overturned lands, he said: The people of Lot, their land was turned upside down, and its top was turned to the bottom.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And the overturned cities, he said: They are the people of Lot.

x: If what I mean by the overthrown ones is the people of Lot, then how was it said the overthrown ones and made it plural and not singular?
It was three villages, so it was collected for that reason, and for that reason it was collected with the ta’, according to the saying of God: And the overturned I am inclined to (al-Najm 53:53).
How is it said:
h
Their messengers came to them with clear proofs
, when the one to whom they were sent was only one?

The meaning of this is: A messenger came to every village of the destroyed ones, calling them to God, so the messengers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom he sent to them to call to God about his message, were messengers to them, just as the Arabs said to a people who were attributed to Abu Fadik the Kharijite: (al-Fadikat), and (Abu Fadik) is one, but when his companions were attributed to him and he was their chief, they were called by that, and were attributed to their chief. So is his saying:
h
Their messengers came to them with clear proofs
. It may be possible to say that this means: The people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and all the other nations mentioned by God in this verse were given clear proofs by their messengers from God.

And His statement: God would not wrong them, God Almighty says: God did not destroy these nations that He mentioned that He destroyed except because of their crimes and wronging themselves, and their deserving of a great punishment from God. It was not injustice from God to them, nor was He Almighty imposing a punishment on someone who did not deserve it, because God is wise, there is no flaw in His plan, nor any error in His judgment. But the people whom He destroyed wronged themselves by disobeying God and denying His messengers, until they angered their Lord, so the word of punishment came true for them and they were punished.

God Almighty says: As for (the believing men and believing women), who are those who believe in God and His Messenger and the verses of His Book, their description is that some of them are supporters and helpers of others, enjoining what is right, meaning: they command people to believe in God and His Messenger and in what He brought from God, [and forbidding what is wrong…], establishing prayer, meaning: they perform the obligatory prayer, and giving zakat, meaning: they give the obligatory zakat to its people, and obeying God and His Messenger, so they obey the command of God and His Messenger and refrain from what He has forbidden them from, those - God will have mercy on them, meaning: these are the ones who have this description, whom God will have mercy on, and He will save them from His punishment and admit them into His Paradise, not the people of hypocrisy and denial of God and His Messenger, who forbid what is right, enjoin what is wrong, and restrain their hands from committing His disobedience. His disbelief in Him, nothing prevents Him from taking revenge on him, and no one supports Him against him, Wise, in taking revenge on them, and in all His actions.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an about enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, “enjoining what is right” is a call from polytheism to Islam, and forbidding what is wrong is a prohibition against the worship of idols and devils. ... He said, Abdullah told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: (establishing prayer), he said: the five daily prayers.

x: God Almighty says: God promised those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged him and what he brought from God, of men and women, gardens beneath which rivers flow, meaning: orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow, abiding therein, meaning: remaining therein forever, residing, its delights never departing from them nor perishing, and pleasant dwellings, meaning: and homes in which they will dwell pleasantly.
And (its goodness) is that, as we have been told, it is like:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Jisr,
m: “On the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: I asked Imran bin Husayn and Abu Hurayrah about a verse in the Book of God, the Blessed and Exalted: ‘And good dwellings in gardens of perpetual bliss.’ They said: It has fallen on the expert! We asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: A palace in Paradise made of pearls, in it are seventy houses of red rubies, in each house are seventy houses of green emerald, in each house are seventy beds.”

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari narrated to us, he said, Qara bin Habib narrated to us, on the authority of Jisr bin Farqad, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn and Abu Hurayrah, they said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse: ‘And good dwellings in gardens of perpetual bliss.’ He said: A palace of pearls. In that palace are seventy houses of red rubies. In each house are seventy houses of green emerald. In each house are seventy beds. On each bed are seventy mattresses of every color. On each bed is a wife from the houris. In each house are seventy tables. On each table are seventy types of food. In each house are seventy female servants. And the believer is given strength in one morning that which would come from all of that together.” As for his saying:
h
In the Gardens of Eden
, he means: These are the good dwellings that God Almighty described,
h
in the Gardens of Eden
. And fi is related to masakin. It was said:
h
Gardens of Eden
, because they are gardens of eternity and residence, from which no one departs. It was said: It was called
h
Gardens of Eden

because it is the abode of God which He has chosen for Himself and for whomever He wills of His creation, from the saying of the Arabs: So-and-so resided in such-and-such a land, meaning he resided there and was immortal there. And from this is the mine, and it is said: He is in a mine of truth, meaning that he is in a firm origin. And some narrators recited the verse of Al-A’sha: If they host his dream, they will be added to Rajih, who has returned. He recites: He has weighed. And as we said about that, Ibn Abbas and a group with him, as mentioned, interpreted it.
b.via: Imran bin Husayn and Abu Hurayrah

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Gardens of Eden
, he said: (The man’s place of residence), in which he will be.

c: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, on the authority of Abu al-Dardaʿ, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God opens the remembrance in the three hours remaining of the night. In the first hour of them, He looks into the book which no one else looks into, and He erases what He wills and confirms. Then in the second hour, He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is in His house which no eye has seen and which has not crossed the mind of man. It is His dwelling place, and none of the children of Adam dwell with Him except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. Then He says: Blessed is he who enters you and remembers in the third hour.”

c: Musa bin Sahl told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Al-Layth bin Saad told us, he said, Ziyadah bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Eden is His home - meaning: the home of God - which no eye has seen and has not crossed the mind of man. It is His dwelling place, and none of the children of Adam will inhabit it with Him except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘Blessed is he who enters you.’”

x: Others said: The meaning of
h
Gardens of Eden
is gardens of grapes and vineyards.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Abi Sarij Al-Razi told me, he said, Zakariya bin Adi told us, he said, Ubaid God bin Amr told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith:
m: that Ibn Abbas asked Kaab about the
h
Gardens of Eden

, and he said: They are vineyards and Surat al-Tawbah 9:72 God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and pleasant dwellings in
h
Gardens of Eden
. And approval from God is greater. That is the great attainment. grapes, in Syriac.

x: Others said: It is the name of the two sides of Paradise and its middle.
Who said that?

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Aʿmash, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of ʿAbdullah, who said:
m: Aden means the two valleys of Paradise.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Shu’bah, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Gardens of Eden

, he said: The two depths of Paradise. Ibn Bashar said in his hadith, so I said: What are its two depths? And Ibn al-Muthanna said in his hadith, so I said to al-A’mash: What are the two depths of Paradise? He said: Its middle.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah,
m: and Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah:
h
Gardens of Eden

, he said: The two valleys of Paradise. ... He said, Abd al-Rahman told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Abi Sarij told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha,
m: and Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of both of them, or on the authority of one of them, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah:
h
Gardens of Eden
, he said: The two valleys of Paradise.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Gardens of Eden
, he said: The two depths of Paradise.

x: Others said: Aden is the name of a palace.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Abda Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Awn bin Musa Al-Kinani, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: h
Gardens of Eden
. And what do you know about the
h
Gardens of Eden
? A palace of gold, which none shall enter except a prophet, a truthful person, a martyr, or a just judge. And he raised his voice with it.

c: Ahmad bin Abi Surayj told us, Abdullah bin Asim told us, Awn bin Musa told us:
m: I heard Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan say:
h
Gardens of Eden
, and what do you know about the
h
Gardens of Eden
? A palace of gold, which none shall enter except a prophet, a truthful person, a martyr, or a just judge. Al-Hasan raised his voice with it.

c: Ahmad told us, Yazid told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Ataʿ, on the authority of Nafiʿ bin Asim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said:
m: There is a palace in Paradise called Aden, around which are the towers and the spirit. It has fifty thousand doors, and on each door is a door. None shall enter it except a prophet or a friend.

c: Al-Hasan bin Naseh told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, he said,
m: I heard Ya’qub bin Asim narrating, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: Indeed, in Paradise there is a palace called Aden, which has five thousand doors, and on each door are five thousand inkwells. None will enter it except a prophet, a truthful person, or a martyr. It was said: It is the city of heaven.

x: Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman al-Maharbi, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding the
h
Gardens of Eden

, who said: It is the city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, prophets, martyrs, and imams of guidance, and the people are around them after that, and the gardens are around it. It was said: It is the name of a river.

x: Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Maharibi, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Sa’ib Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: Aden is a river in Paradise, and its gardens are on both its banks. As for his saying:
h
And the pleasure of God is greater
, its meaning is: And the pleasure of God with them is greater than all of that, and this is what the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will say to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise! They will say: At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure! He will say: Are you satisfied? They will say: Why should we not be satisfied, when you have given us what you have not given to any of your creation? He will say: I will give you something better than that. They will say: O Lord, what is better than that? He will say: I will bestow upon you My pleasure, and I will never be angry with you after that.”

c: Ibn Humayd narrated that Yaqub narrated to me, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shammar, who said:
m: The Qur’an will come on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a pale man, to a man when his grave is opened, and will say: Rejoice in the honor of God! Rejoice in the pleasure of God! He will say: Who can give good tidings like you? And who are you? He will say: I am the Qur’an that kept you awake at night and made you thirsty during the day! So he will carry it on his neck until he meets his Lord with it, and it will stand before Him and say: O Lord, this is Your servant, reward him well on my behalf! For I kept you awake at night and made you thirsty during the day, and I would command him and he would obey Me, and I would forbid him and he would obey Me. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, will say: Then he will have the robe of honor. He will say: O Lord, increase it, for he deserves it! He will say: Then he will have My pleasure. He said:
h
And the pleasure of God is greater

. The report about God’s pleasure for the believing men and women began with the fact that it is greater than everything that He, the Most High, has mentioned, so it was raised, even though pleasure is among what He has promised them. It was not linked in the syntax to gardens and good dwellings, so that it would be known that God prefers His pleasure for the believers over all the rest of what He has apportioned to them from His grace and given them from His honor, similar to the saying of the speaker in the other speech: I gave you and connected you with such and such, and honored you, and My pleasure after being away from you is better for you. “That is the great triumph,” these are the things that were promised to the believing men and women, that is the great triumph. He says: It is the great victory, and the great salvation, because they have attained eternal dignity, and have been saved from humiliation in Hellfire, so it is the great triumph than which there is nothing greater.

evidence.text: And some narrators recited the verse of Al-A’sha: If they host his dream, they will be added to Rajih, who has returned.

x: God Almighty says: O Prophet, fight the disbelievers, with the sword and weapons, and the hypocrites.
The interpreters differed regarding the description of the jihad that God commanded His Prophet to do against the hypocrites.
Some of them said: He ordered him to fight them with his hand and tongue, and with everything he could fight them with.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman and Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Hasan bin Salih, on the authority of Ali bin al-Aqmar, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Jundub, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites
, he said: With his hand, and if he is unable to do so, then with his tongue, and if he is unable to do so, then with his heart, and if he is unable to do so, then let him frown in his face.

x: Others said: Rather, he ordered him to fight them with his tongue.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet,
h
fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them
, so God commanded him to fight the disbelievers with the sword, and the hypocrites with the tongue, and to remove gentleness from them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told me, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites
, he said: (the disbelievers), by fighting, and (the hypocrites), by speaking harshly to them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them
, meaning: Fight the disbelievers with the sword, and be harsh upon the hypocrites with words, which is fighting them.

x: Others said: Rather, he ordered him to implement the limits on them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Fight the infidels and the hypocrites, he said: Fight the infidels with the sword, and the hypocrites with the limits, establish the limits of God upon them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them, he said: God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and to be harsh upon the hypocrites in the limits.

x: The most correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is what Ibn Masʿud said: that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight the hypocrites in the same way that He commanded him to fight the polytheists.
How did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, leave them living among his companions, even though he knew about them?

God, the Most High, only commanded fighting those among them who openly declared disbelief and then continued to declare it. As for those among them who, if it was discovered that they had spoken a word of disbelief and accepted it, denied it and returned from it and said: I am a Muslim, then the ruling of God regarding everyone who openly declared Islam with his tongue is that his blood and wealth are protected by that, even if he believed otherwise. God, the Most High, was entrusted with their secrets and did not leave it to people to search for secrets. Therefore, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, despite his knowledge of them and God’s knowledge of their inner selves and the belief in their hearts, would allow them to be among the Companions, and a Muslim would not treat their jihad as a jihad against someone who had waged war against him on the basis of associating partners with God, because if one of them was discovered to have said a word in which he disbelieved in God and then accepted it, he would deny it and declare Islam with his tongue. So, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would not accept it except for what he showed him of his words, when he was present with him and his intention to carry out the ruling on him, without what he had previously said of his words before that, and without the belief of his conscience, which God did not permit anyone to accept in the ruling, and he took it upon himself to accept it without his creation.
And His statement: And be harsh with them, God Almighty says: And be severe with them in jihad, fighting, and terror. His saying:
h
And their abode is Hell

, meaning: Their Surat al-Tawbah 9:73 O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. dwellings are Hell, which is their abode and their abode. And wretched is the destination, meaning: And wretched is the place to which they will be led, Hell.
The people of interpretation differed about the one about whom this verse was revealed, and the statement he made, about whom God informed that he would swear by God that he did not say it.
Some of them said: The one about whom this verse was revealed is Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin Al-Samit.
And what he said was: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said:

c: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father:
m: h
They swear by God that they did not say it

, but they did say the word of disbelief. He said: “It was revealed about Al-Jalas ibn Suwaid ibn As-Samit, who said: ‘If what Muhammad brought is true, then we are worse than donkeys!’ His wife’s son said to him: ‘By God, O enemy of God, I will tell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what you said, for if I do not do so I fear that a calamity will befall me and I will be held accountable for your sin!’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Al-Jalas and said: ‘O Jalas, did you say such and such?’ So he swore that he did not say it, and then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: ‘
h
They swear by God that they did not say it

, but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam and intended what they did not attain. They did not resent it except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah Al-Dareer told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: “This verse was revealed: ‘
h
They swear by God that they did not say it

- but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam’, about Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin As-Samit. He and his wife’s son Mus’ab came from Quba’. Al-Jalas said: If what Muhammad brought is true, then we are worse than our donkeys that we are on! Mus’ab said: By God, O enemy of God, I will tell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what you said! So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I feared that something would be revealed in the Qur’an, or that a calamity would befall me, or that I would be confused by his sin. I said: O Messenger of God, Al-Jalas and I came from Quba’, and he said such and such, and were it not for the fear that I would be confused by his sin, or that a calamity would befall me, I would not have told you. He said: So he called Al-Jalas and said to him: O Al-Jalas, did you say what Mus’ab said? He said: So he swore, and God, the Most High, revealed: ‘They swear by God What they said, and they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam,” the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The one who said that statement, as far as I have heard, was Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin Al-Samit, and a man who was in his care, called Umair bin Saeed, took it back from him, and he denied it, and he swore by God that he had not said it. Then when the Qur’an was revealed about him, he repented and stopped, and his repentance was good, as far as I have heard.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The word of disbelief, one of them said: (If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys)! A man from the believers said to him: What he said is true, and you are worse than a donkey! He said: The hypocrites intended to kill him, so that is what He said: And they intended what they did not attain.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Jadhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Ayyub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Raja told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the shade of a tree, and he said: ‘A man will come to you and look at you with the eyes of a devil, so when he comes, do not speak to him.’ It was not long before a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: ‘Why are you cursing me, you and your companions?’ So the man went and brought his companions, and they swore by God that they had not said or done, until he forgave them, and God revealed: ‘They swear by God that they did not say,’ then He described them all until the end of the verse.”

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul.
They said: And the word that he said is what:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They swear by God that they did not say it

, to his statement: Who is there to protect us and who is there to help us? He said: It was mentioned to us that two men fought, one of them from Juhayna, and the other from Ghifar, and Juhayna were allies of the Ansar, and the Ghifarites prevailed over the Juhayni, so Abdullah bin Ubayy said to the Aws: Help your brother, for by God, our situation and the situation of Muhammad are like the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and he said:
h
If we return to Medina

, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble (al-Munafiqun 63:8). So a man from the Muslims went to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sent for him and asked him, and he began to swear by God that he did not say it, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
h
They swear by God that they did not say it
, but they did say the word of disbelief.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They swear by God that they did not say it
, but they did say the word of disbelief, he said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God the Most High informed us Surat al-Tawbah 9:74
h
They swear by God that they did not say it
, but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam and intended what they did not attain. They only resented it because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. So
h
if they repent

, it will be better for them, but if they turn away, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And they do not resent it except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. So
h
if they repent

, it will be better for them, but if they turn away, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. They will have on earth neither protector nor helper. about the hypocrites that they swear falsely by God about a word of disbelief that they uttered, that they did not say it.

It is possible that this statement is what was narrated from ʿUrwah: that Al-Jalas said it, and it is possible that the one who said it was ʿAbdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and the statement is what Qatadah reported that he said. We do not know which of these is which, since there is no report of either of them that requires proof, and by which one can reach certain knowledge of it, and its knowledge is not something that can be attained by the innate mind. So the correct statement is to say about it as God the Most High said:
h
They swear by God that they did not say it

, but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam. As for his saying: And they intended to do what they did not attain, the people of interpretation differed about what they intended to do, and what was the thing they intended to do.
Some of them said: He is a hypocrite, and what he intended to do was to kill his wife’s son who heard what he said and feared that he would reveal it to him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The hypocrite intended to kill him, meaning to kill the believer who said to him: (You are worse than a donkey)! So that is what he said: And they intended what they did not attain.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: The one they were about to do was a man from Quraysh, and the one they were about to do was kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And they intended that which they could not attain, he said: A man from Quraysh intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was called Al-Aswad.

x: Others said: The one who was concerned was Abdullah bin Abi bin Salul, and his concern that he did not achieve was his saying:
h
If we return to Medina
, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble (al-Munafiqun 63:8), from the words of Qatada, and we have mentioned it. And His statement:
h
And they did not resent anything except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty

, tells us that the hypocrite about whom God mentioned that he said the word of disbelief was poor, so God enriched him by killing a slave of his, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him his blood money. So when he said what he said, God the Most High said: And they did not resent anything, meaning: they did not find fault with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father:
m: And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. Al-Jalas had killed a freed slave of his, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered blood money for him, and he became independent. That is what he said: And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. ... He said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money should be twelve thousand for a client of Banu Adi ibn Ka’b, and this verse was revealed about him: And they did not resent him except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty, he said: After God bin Abi, it was blood money, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, paid it for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, Amr told us, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah: A client of Banu Adi bin Kaab killed a man from the Ansar. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money should be twelve thousand, and in it was revealed: And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. Amr said: I did not hear this from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from Ikrimah, meaning: The blood money should be twelve thousand.

c: Salih bin Mismar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Awqi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta’ifi narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the blood money twelve thousand. That is what he said: And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty, he said: By taking the blood money. As for His statement:
h
If they repent

, it will be better for them, the Most High says: If these people who said the word of disbelief repent from what they said and then go back on it, their going back and repenting from that will be better for them than hypocrisy. But if they turn away, meaning: If they turn away from repentance, and do it and persist in their disbelief, God will punish them with a painful punishment, meaning: He will punish them with a painful punishment in this world, either by killing or by a quick disgrace for them in it, and He will punish them in the Hereafter with the Fire. And His statement:
h
And they will have no protector or helper on earth

, meaning: And if God punishes them in this worldly life, what will these hypocrites have, any protector who will support him in order to prevent him from God’s punishment, nor any helper who will support him from God and save him from His punishment. They were people of honor and strength with their clans and people, and they protected themselves with them from those who wanted to harm them. So God, the Most High, informed us that those who protected them from those who wanted to harm them from their clans and allies will not protect them from God nor will they support them from Him, if they need their support. He mentioned that the person about whom this verse was revealed repented from his hypocrisy.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father:
m: h
If they repent
, it will be better for them. He said: Al-Jalas said: God has made an exception for me to repent, so I repent. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted it from him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father:
m: h
If they repent

, it will be better for them, the verse. Al-Jalas said: O Messenger of God, I see that God has made an exception for me in repentance, so I repent! So he repented, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted it from him.

x: God Almighty says: And among these hypocrites whose description I have described to you, O Muhammad, He who has made a covenant with God, meaning: God has given a covenant, If He gives us from His bounty, meaning: If God gives us from His bounty, provides us with wealth, and is generous to us from Him, we will give in charity, meaning: We will give in charity from that wealth that our Lord has provided us, and we will be among the righteous, meaning: And we will work in it as the righteous do with their wealth, by maintaining ties of kinship with it, and spending it in the way of God. God the Most High says: So God provided for them and gave them from His bounty, But when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it, from the bounty of God that He gave them, so they did not believe in it, nor did they maintain any ties of kinship from it, nor did they spend from it in the right of God, and they turned away, meaning: and turned away from their covenant that they had made with God, and they were turning away, from it, so God made it a consequence for them, “hypocrisy in their hearts,” because of their stinginess with the right of God that He imposed upon them in what He gave them from His bounty, and their breaking the promise that they promised God, and their breaking His covenant in their hearts, until the Day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to God, from charity and spending in His cause, and because they used to lie, in what they said, and He forbade them from repenting from it, because He, the Most High, made a condition for their hypocrisy that He made it a consequence for them until the Day they meet Him, which is the day of their death and departure from this world.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of this verse.
Some of them said: He meant a man called Tha’laba bin Hattab, from the Ansar.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty,’ the verse. That is because a man called Tha’laba bin Hattab, from the Ansar, came to a gathering and called them to witness, saying: If God should give me from His bounty, I would give every person his due, give charity from it, and uphold the ties of kinship from it! So God tested him and gave him from His bounty, but God broke His promise to him, and he angered God by breaking His promise. So God related his case in the Qur’an:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God
, the verse until His statement: They lie.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hisham bin Ammar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Shuaib told us, he said, Ma’an bin Rafa’ah Al-Salami told us, on the authority of Abu Abdul Malik Ali bin Yazid Al-Alahani: that he informed him on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman: that he informed him on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili,
m: “On the authority of Tha’laba bin Hatib Al-Ansari: that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask God to grant me wealth! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you, Tha’laba, a little for which you can express gratitude is better than a lot that you cannot bear! He said: Then he said it again, and he said: Are you not satisfied to be like the Prophet of God? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I wanted the mountains to move Surat al-Tawbah 9:75
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, "If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous." with me in gold and silver, they would move! He said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, if I ask God to grant me wealth, I will give every person with a right his right! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, grant Tha’laba wealth! He said: So he took sheep, and they grew like worms grow, and the city became too small for him, so he moved away from it, and he descended One of its valleys, until he began to pray the noon and afternoon prayers in congregation, and leave the rest. Then it grew and multiplied, so he moved away until he left the prayers except for the Friday prayer, and it grew like a worm, until he left the Friday prayer. So he began to meet the riders on Friday, asking them about the report, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What has Thaʿlaba done? They said: O Messenger of God, he has taken sheep and the city has become too small for him! They told him about his situation, and he said: Woe to Tha'laba, woe to Tha'laba, woe to Tha'laba! He said: Then God revealed: Take from their wealth a charity (al-Tawbah 9:103), and the obligatory charity was revealed to him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent two men to collect the charity, a man from Juhayna and a man from Sulaym. He wrote to them how to collect the charity from the Muslims, and he said to them: Go to Tha'laba and to so-and-so, a man from Banu Sulaym, and take their charity! So they went out until they came to Tha'laba, and asked him for the charity, and he read to him the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: This is nothing but a jizya! This is nothing but a sister of the jizya! I do not know what this is! Go until you are done and then come back to me. So they went, and As-Salami heard about them, so he looked at the best teeth of his camels, and set them aside for charity, then he met them with them. When they saw them, they said: This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you. He said: Yes, take it, for my soul is content with that, and it is only for me! So they took it from him. When they had finished their charity, they returned until they passed by Tha’laba. He said: Show me your letter! He looked at it and said: This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah! Go, so that I may see what I think. So they went until they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he saw them, he said: Woe to Tha’laba! Before he spoke to them, he prayed for blessings for As-Salami. They told him what Tha’laba had done and what As-Salami had done, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed concerning him: “
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity and be among the righteous. ’” until His saying: and because of what they used to deny. And with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from among Tha’laba’s relatives, and he heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: Woe to you, Tha’laba! God has revealed such and such concerning you! Then Thaʿlaba went out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to accept his charity. He said: God has prevented me from accepting your charity. So he began to throw dirt on his head. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is your work. I ordered you and you did not obey me! When he refused to die, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to his home. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and did not accept anything from him. Then he went to Abu Bakr when he was appointed caliph and said: You know my status with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and my position among the Ansar, so accept my charity! Abu Bakr said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it, and I accept it! So Abu Bakr died and did not accept it. When ʿUmar took over, he came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity! He said: Neither the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor Abu Bakr accepted it, and I accept it from you! So he died and did not accept it. Then ʿUthman, may God have mercy on him, took over, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it, and I accept it from you. May God be pleased with them both, and I accept it from you! But he did not accept it from him. And Tha’laba died during the caliphate of Uthman, may God have mercy on him.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty’ the verse, he told us that a man from the Ansar came to a gathering of the Ansar and said: If God should give him wealth, he would give to every person entitled to it his due! So God gave him wealth, and he did with it what you hear. He said: But when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it, until His statement: and because they used to lie. He told us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated that when Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with the Torah to the Children of Israel, the Children of Israel said: The Torah is too much, and we do not have time for it, so ask your Lord for us to gather the matter so that we may preserve it and devote ourselves to it for our livelihood! He said: O people, take it easy, take it easy! This is the Book of God, the light of God, and the protection of God! He said: So they repeated it to him, and he repeated it to them, he said it three times. He said: God revealed to Moses: What do My servants say? He said: O Lord, they say such and such. He said: I command you with three things, if you adhere to them, they will enter Paradise because of them: to stop dividing the inheritance and not wrong others in it, not to let their eyes enter the houses until permission is given to them, and not to eat food until they perform ablution for prayer. He said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned with them to his people, and they were happy, and they saw that they would do them. He said: By God, the people did not stay long before they turned away and were cut off. When the Prophet of God narrated this story about the Children of Israel, he said: Guarantee me six things, and I will guarantee you Paradise! They said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: ((When you speak, do not lie, and when you make a promise, do not break it, and when you are entrusted, do not betray, and restrain your eyes, your hands, and your private parts: your eyes from betrayal, your hands from theft, and your private parts from adultery.))

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Three things, if they are found in someone, he becomes a hypocrite, even if he fasts, prays, and claims to be a Muslim: if he speaks, he lies, if he is entrusted, he betrays, and if he makes a promise, he breaks it.”

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is two men: one of them is Tha’laba, and the other is Mu’tab bin Qushair.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God
, ‘If He should give us from His bounty,’ the verse. And among those who made a covenant with God were: Tha’laba ibn Hattab and Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, and they were from Banu Amr ibn Awf.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty,’ he said, two men went out to a group of people and said: By God, if God provides us with provision, we will give in charity! But when God provided them with provision, they were stingy with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty,’ two men went out to a group of people and said: By God, if God should provide us with provision, we will surely give in charity! But when He provided for them, they were stingy with it, So He made hypocrisy follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed to fulfill what they promised God, when they said: We will surely give in charity, but they did not do so.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity’ 1:106, he said: These are a group of hypocrites, but when He gave them that, they were stingy with it, and when they were stingy with that, He followed that with hypocrisy until the Day they meet Him, from which they will have no repentance, forgiveness, or pardon, just as happened to Iblis when he prevented him from repenting.

x: In this verse, there is clarification from God, may He be glorified, about the sign of the hypocrites, I mean in His saying:
h
So He made hypocrisy follow them in their hearts until the Day they meet Him
, because they failed to fulfill what they promised God and because they used to lie.
A group of the Companions and Followers used to say something similar to this, and the report was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Some of those who said that said:

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Yazid, he said, Abdullah said:
m: Consider the hypocrite with three things: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he makes a covenant he betrays it. And God revealed confirmation of that in His Book:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God
, ‘If He should give us from His bounty’ until His saying: they lie.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Subaih ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmaira, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, who said:
m: Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite: When he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays that trust. He said: And he recited this verse:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God
, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give alms and be among the righteous,’ to the end of the verse.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, he said:
m: I heard Subaih bin Abdullah Al-Absi say: I asked Abdullah bin Amr about the hypocrite, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, he said, Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi told us, he said, Abdul Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, he said, Uthman ibn Hakim told us, he said,
m: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi say: I used to hear that the hypocrite is known by three things: lying, breaking his oath, and betrayal. So I looked for them in the Book of God for a time but could not find them, then I found them in two of the Book of God, His statement:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God until he reached and because of what they used to lie
, and His statement: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth (al-Ahzab 33:72), this verse.

c: Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf narrated to me, Shababah narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Muharram narrated to us,
m: I heard Al-Hasan say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things in whomever they are found, he is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim: if he speaks, he lies, if he makes a promise, he breaks it, and if he is entrusted, he betrays.” So I said to Al-Hasan: O Abu Saeed, if a man owes me a debt and he meets me to pay it, but I do not have it, and I fear that he will imprison me and kill me, so I promised him that I would pay it at the beginning of the new moon, but I did not do it. Am I a hypocrite? He said: This is what it says in the hadith. Then he narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that when his father was dying, he said: Marry so-and-so to me, for I promised him that I would marry him to you, lest I meet God with one-third of hypocrisy! I said: O Abu Saeed, what if a man is one-third hypocrite and two-thirds believer? He said: This is what the hadith says. He said: So I performed Hajj and met Ata bin Abi Rabah, and I told him the hadith that I heard from Al-Hasan, and what I said to him and he said to me. He said to me: Are you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Joseph, peace be upon him? Did they not promise their father but broke their promise? Did they not speak to him but denied him? Did he not entrust them but they betrayed him? Were they not prophets? Was their father a prophet and their grandfather a prophet? He said: So I said to Ata: O Abu Muhammad, tell me about the origin of hypocrisy and the origin of this hadith. He said: Jabir bin Abdullah told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only said this hadith about the hypocrites in particular, those who spoke to the Prophet but denied him, and entrusted them with his secret but betrayed him, and promised to go out with him on a campaign but broke it. He said: Abu Sufyan left Mecca, and Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place, so go out to him and keep it secret. He said: A hypocrite wrote to him: Muhammad wants you, so be on your guard. So God revealed: Do not betray God and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know (al-Anfal 8:27), and He revealed about al-Munafiqun 63:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, ‘If He should give us from His bounty’ until: So He punished them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him because they broke what they promised God and because they used to lie. So when you meet Al-Hasan, greet him and tell him the origin of this hadith and what I told you. He said: So I went to Al-Hasan and said: O Abu Saeed, your brother Ata greets you, so I told him the hadith that had happened and what he had said to me. Al-Hasan took my hand and lifted it and said: O people of Iraq, are you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from me and did not accept it until he had deduced its origin. Ata’ is truthful. This is the hadith, and this is specifically about hypocrites.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Three things, whoever has them, even if he prays and fasts and claims to be a Muslim, is a hypocrite.’ So it was said to him: ‘What are they, O Messenger of God?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.’”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Mubashar told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Harun bin Riyab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wa’il:
m: When death approached him, he said: So-and-so proposed to me for my daughter, and I had said to him something about her that was similar to the waiting period. By God, I will not meet God with a third of hypocrisy, and I bear witness to you that I have married her to him.

x: Some people said: The covenant that these hypocrites made with God was something they intended in their hearts, but did not speak about it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us:
m: I heard Mu’tamir bin Sulayman Al-Taymi say: I rode the sea, and a strong wind struck us, so some of us made vows, and I intended to do so, but I did not speak about it. So when I arrived in Basra, I asked Abu Sulayman, and he said to me: O my son, do it. Mu'tamir said: And Kahams told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Thabit, who said regarding his statement:
h
And among them are those who made a covenant with God

, the verse, he said: It is only something they intended in their souls and did not speak about it. Have you not heard his statement: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations and that God is Knower of the unseen?

evidence.text: He said: And he recited this verse: And among them are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give alms and be among the righteous,’ to the end of the verse.

x: God Almighty says: Didn't these hypocrites who disbelieve in God and His Messenger secretly, and show their belief in them to the people of faith in them openly, that God knows their secret, which they conceal in themselves, of disbelief in Him and His Messenger, and their private conversations, meaning: and their private conversations, when they whisper among themselves to slander Islam and its people, and mention them in a way other than what they should be mentioned in, so they fear God's punishment that He will bring it upon them, and His power that He will inflict upon them, for their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and their faultfinding of Islam and its people, so they desist from that and repent from it, and that God is Knower of the unseen, meaning: Didn't they know that God is Knower of what is hidden from the hearing, sight, and senses of His creation, of what their souls conceal, but which has not appeared to their apparent limbs, so that this prevents them from deceiving His friends with hypocrisy and lying, and deters them from concealing other than what They show it, and show the opposite of what they believe?

God Almighty says: Those who criticize those who volunteer to give charity to the poor and needy with what God has not obligated them to give from their wealth, and they criticize them for it by saying: (They only gave it in charity for show and reputation, and they did not seek the face of God), and they criticize those who do not find anything to give in charity except their effort, and that is their capacity, so they belittle them and say: (God was indeed rich from the charity of these people!), mocking them, So they mock them, God mocked them. We have explained the description of God’s mockery of those among His creation whom He mocks in other places, so there is no need to repeat it here. And for them is a painful punishment, meaning: And for them from God on the Day of Resurrection is a painful, grievous punishment. He mentioned that the meaning of his saying: those who volunteer among the believers is Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Asim ibn Adi al-Ansari, and that the meaning of his saying: and those who find nothing but their effort is Abu Aqil al-Arashy, the brother of Banu Anif.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity
, he said: Abd al-Rahman bin Awf came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with forty pieces of gold, and a man from the Ansar came to him with a sa’ of food.

x: Some of the hypocrites said: By God, Abd al-Rahman did not bring what he brought except to show off! And they said: Indeed, God and His Messenger do not need this sa’!

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity and those who find nothing but their effort

, that is, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the people one day and called out to them: ‘Collect your charity! ’ So the people collected their charity. Then a man from the last of them came with some dates and said: ‘O Messenger of God, this is a saʿ of dates. I spent the night drawing water from a jug until I got two saʿ of dates, so I kept one of them and brought you the other. ’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to scatter it among the charity. Some men mocked him and said: ‘By God, God and His Messenger are independent of this! What would they do with your saʿ of anything? ’” Then ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, a man from Quraysh from Banu Zuhrah, said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Is there anyone left from the people of this charity? ’ He said: ‘No. ’ So ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf said: ‘I have one hundred ounces of gold. ’” In charity. Omar bin Al-Khattab said to him: Are you crazy? He said: I am not crazy! He said: So did we know what you said? He said: Yes! I have eight thousand, as for four I lend to my Lord, and as for the four thousand I keep! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: May God bless you in what you have withheld and in what you have given! The hypocrites hated it and said: (By God, Abdurrahman bin Awf did not give his gift except to show off)! They were lying, he only gave it voluntarily, so God revealed his excuse and the excuse of his poor friend who brought the saa of dates, so God said in His Book: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily concerning the charity
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:17)

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Those who slander the voluntary givers among the believers, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with his charity of four thousand, so the hypocrites slandered him and said: A show-off, “And those who find nothing but their effort,” he said: A man from the Ansar hired himself out for a sa’ of dates, he had nothing else, so he brought it and they slandered him and said: God was independent of this sa’!

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: His statement, Those who slander Surat al-Tawbah 9:79 Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily in charity and those who find nothing to give except their effort, so they ridicule them - God will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment. the believers who give freely, the verse, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with half of his wealth, and sought to draw closer to God with it, but the hypocrites slandered him and said: He only gave that for show and to be heard! Then a man from the poor Muslims called Habhab, Abu Aqil came and said: O Prophet of God, I spent the night the reward of a jug of dates on two sa’s of dates. As for one sa’, I kept it for my family, and as for one sa’, here it is! The hypocrites said: (By God, God and His Messenger are free from this!) So God revealed in that Qur’an, Those who slander, the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
