Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity

, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf gave half of his wealth in charity, and he had eight thousand dinars, so he gave four thousand dinars in charity, and some of the hypocrites said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf is indeed a great hypocrite! So God said:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity

, and a man had two sa's of dates, so he brought one of them, and some of the hypocrites said: God is indeed independent of this sa'! So the hypocrites used to slander them and mock them, so God said: And those who find nothing except their effort and ridicule them - God will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal Al-Anmati told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Omar bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give charity, for I want to send an expedition. He said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf said: O Messenger of God, I have four thousand, two thousand of which God has loaned, and two thousand for my family. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless you in what you have given, and bless you in what you have withheld! A man from the Ansar said: I have two sa’s of dates, one sa’ for my Lord, and one sa’ for my family! The hypocrites slandered and said: Ibn Awf did not give this except to show off! And they said: Was God not independent of this sa’? Then God revealed: ‘Those who slander the believers who give freely’, to the end of the verse.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Saad told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity

, he said: “The people were afflicted with great hardship, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to give charity. Abd al-Rahman came with four hundred ounces, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bless what you have withheld. The hypocrites said: Abd al-Rahman did nothing but show off and be seen! He said: A man came with a saʿ of dates, and said: O Messenger of God, I hired myself for two saʿs, so I went with a saʿ of them to my family, and I came with a saʿ of dates. The hypocrites said: God is independent of this saʿ! So God revealed this verse: “And those who find nothing except their effort, so they ridicule them - God will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment.” Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Those who criticize the believers who give charity voluntarily, the verse. The believers who gave charity voluntarily were Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who gave charity of four thousand dinars, and Asim ibn Adi, the brother of Banu Ajlan. This was because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, encouraged charity and urged it. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf stood up and gave charity of four thousand dirhams, and Asim ibn Adi stood up and gave charity of one hundred wasqs of dates. They criticized them and said: This is nothing but showing off! The one who gave charity with all his effort was Abu Uqayl, the brother of Banu Anif, al-Arashy, an ally of Banu Amr ibn Awf. He brought a sa’ of dates and emptied it into charity, so they laughed at him and said: God is independent of Abu Uqayl’s sa’!!

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam Abdullah told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Wa'il, on the authority of Abu Mas'ud, who said:
m: When the verse on charity was revealed, we were carrying loads - Abu al-Nu'man said: We were working - he said: Then a man came and gave a lot in charity. He said: Then a man came and gave a sa' of dates in charity, so they said: God is not in need of this sa'! Then the verse was revealed: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily concerning their charity and those who find nothing except their effort. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Zaid bin Habbab narrated, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, he said:

c: Khalid bin Yasar narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Uqayl, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I spent the night carrying the jareer on my back with two sa’s of dates. I returned with one of them to my family so that they could provide for them, and I brought the other to draw near to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, and he said: Sprinkle it in charity. So the hypocrites mocked him and said: God was indeed independent of the charity of this poor man! So God revealed: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily concerning their charity, and the two verses.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, he said:
m: “A man stood in the neighborhood and said: My father or uncle told me and said: I witnessed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Who gives charity today, I will bear witness for him before God on the Day of Resurrection? He said: And I have a turban on me. He said: So I took off one or two garments to give them in charity. He said: Then I was overtaken by what overtakes the son of Adam, so I tied it on my head. He said: Then a man came, the shortest of height, blackest of blacks, or darkest of eyes, leading a she-camel the likes of which I have never seen in Al-Baqi’. He said: Is it charity, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes! He said: Here it is! So he threw down its halter - or: its reins - He said: Then a man sitting there nudged him and said: By God, he gives it in charity, and it is better than him! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at him and said: Rather, he is better than you and it! He said that three times, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik told me, saying:
m: The one who gave a sa’ of dates in charity, and the hypocrites slandered him: (Abu Khaithama al-Ansari).
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Raja Abu Sahl Al-Abadani told us, he said, Amer bin Yasaf Al-Yamami told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer Al-Yamami, he said:
m: “Abdur-Rahman bin Awf came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with four thousand dirhams and said: O Messenger of God, I have eight thousand. I have come to you with four thousand, so I will spend it in the way of God, and I will keep four thousand for my family. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless what I have given and what I have kept! Another man came and said: O Messenger of God, I spent the night paying water in two sa’s, one of which I have left for my family and the other I have brought to you, so I will spend it in the way of God. He said: May God bless you in what I have given and in what I have kept! Some hypocrites said: By God, Abdur-Rahman only gave for show and reputation, and God and His Messenger were independent of so-and-so’s sa’! So God revealed: “Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily in charity” meaning Abdur-Rahman bin Awf; And those who find nothing but their effort meaning the owner of the sa’, and mock them, God will mock them. And for them is a painful punishment.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Muslims to collect their zakat, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand and said: This is my money that God has lent me, and I have the same amount left. So he said to him: May you be blessed in what you have given and in what you have withheld! The hypocrites said: He only gave to show off, and the owner of a sa’ only gave to show off. God and His Messenger are independent of this! And God does not do anything with a sa’!”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity

, until His statement: and for them is a painful punishment, he said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded the Muslims to give charity, so Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I found my wealth abundant, so I will take half of it. He said: So I came carrying a lot of money, and a man from the hypocrites said to him: Show off, Umar! He said: Yes, I show off to God and His Messenger, but as for others, no! He said: And a man from the blades did not have anything, so he risked himself to drag the jarir on his neck with two sa’s that night, so he left a sa’ for his family and came with a sa’ to carry, and one of the hypocrites said to him: God and His Messenger are independent of your sa’! This is what God Almighty said:
h
Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity and those who find nothing but their effort

, this is the Ansari, and ridicule them, God will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment. We have explained the meaning of insinuation in the speech of the Arabs with its evidence and what it contains in language and reading in what was said. As for his saying: the volunteers, its meaning is: the volunteers. The ta’ was assimilated into the ta’, so it became a double ta’, as it was said: And whoever volunteers good (al-Baqarah 2:158), meaning: volunteers. As for (effort), the Arabs have two dialects for it. It is said: (He gave me from his effort), with a damma on the jim, and this is, as mentioned, the language of the people of Hijaz, and from (his effort) with a fatha on the jim, and this is the language of Najd. The reading of the regions is with the damma, and this is the choice we have, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings on it. As for the people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs, from the narrators of poetry and the people of Arabic, they claim that it is open and closed with one meaning, and the difference in that is due to the difference in the language in it, just as their languages differed in (اْؤج), and (اْؤج) with the dammah and the fathah, from (ؤجت).

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi
m: regarding this: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Effort and effort are effort in work and effort in sustenance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: the same. ... He said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Isa bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Effort is in work, and effort is in killing.

evidence.text: The reading of the regions is with the damma, and this is the choice we have, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings on it.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Pray to God for these hypocrites, whose characteristics are described in these verses, for forgiveness, or do not pray for it for them. This is a statement that was issued as a command, and its interpretation is report, and its meaning is: If you seek forgiveness for them, O Muhammad, or do not seek forgiveness for them, God will not forgive them. And His statement:
h
If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times

, God will not forgive them, meaning that if you ask for their sins to be covered by His pardoning them and not disgracing them with them, then God will not cover them and will not pardon them, but He will disgrace them with them before all witnesses on the Day of Resurrection. That is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, meaning that the Most High says: This action of God towards them, which is His not pardoning them for their sins, is because they denied the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger.

And God does not guide the wicked people, meaning that God does not guide those who prefer disbelief in Him and disobeying Him over belief in Him and His Messenger to believe in Him and His Messenger. It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will increase my seeking forgiveness for them to more than seventy times, hoping that God will forgive them. Then the verse was revealed: ‘It is the same for them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them - never will God forgive them’ (al-Munafiqun 63:6).” Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Abda bin Sulayman narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father: “Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said to his companions: If you did not spend on Muhammad and his companions, they would have dispersed from around him! He is the one who said: ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble’ (al-Munafiqun 63:8).
So God revealed: ‘
h
Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them
- even
h
if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times
, God will not forgive them’. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will add more than seventy!’ So God revealed: ‘It is the same to them
h
whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them
’ (al-Munafiqun 63:8). But God, the Blessed and Exalted, refused to forgive them.”

c: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: “Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul called the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to attend his father’s funeral. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Who are you? He said: Hubab bin Abdullah bin Ubayy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Rather, you are Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul. Indeed, Hubab is the devil. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was said to me: ‘Whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them, if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.’ So I seek forgiveness for them seventy and seventy and seventy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his shirt on him, and it was covered in sweat.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times

, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will add more than seventy times of asking forgiveness! So God revealed in the surah in which the hypocrites are mentioned: God will never forgive them, (al-Munafiqun 63:6), as a firm statement.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: ... He said, Al-Husayn told us, Hisham told us, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: “When ‘Abdullah bin Ubayy became seriously ill, his son went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: My father is dying, so I would like you to witness it and pray over him! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is your name? He said: Al-Hubab bin ‘Abdullah. He said: Rather, you are ‘Abdullah bin ‘Abdullah bin ‘Abbi, for ‘Al-Hubab’ is the name of Satan. He said: So he went with him until he witnessed it and put his shirt on him, which was covered in sweat, and prayed over him. It was said to him: Are you praying over him while he is a hypocrite? He said: God said: ‘
h
If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times
, God will not forgive them,’ and I will ask forgiveness for him seventy and seventy times! Hisham said: I am not sure about the third.”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them until His statement

: the wicked people, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when this verse was revealed: I hear my Lord has given me permission regarding them, so by God I will ask forgiveness more than seventy times, perhaps God will forgive them! Then God said, out of the intensity of His anger with them: “It is the same to them
h
whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them
. Never will God forgive them. Indeed, God does not guide the wicked people” (al-Munafiqun 63:6), the verse.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them
, even
h
if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times

, God will not forgive them. So the Prophet of God said: My Lord has given me a choice, so I will add more than seventy to them! So God revealed: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them (al-Munafiqun 63:6).

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “When the verse: ‘
h
If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times
, God will not forgive them,’ was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will add more than seventy!’ God said: ‘It is the same to them
h
whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them
. God will never forgive them.’” (al-Munafiqun 63:6)

x: God Almighty says: Those whom God left behind from fighting with His Messenger and the believers in him and from fighting his enemies rejoiced, at their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God, meaning: at their sitting in their homes, in opposition to the Messenger of God, meaning: at their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God in his sitting and his position. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go forth to fight the enemies of God, but they disobeyed his order and sat in their homes. And his saying: Khilaf is a source from the saying of the speaker: (So-and-so disagreed with so-and-so, so he disagrees with him in disagreement), so its source came in the estimation of (fa’al), just as it is said: (Qataluhu, so he fights him in fighting), and if it was a source from (Khalafu), the reading would have been: (By their seat behind the Messenger of God), because the source of (Khalafu) is (Khalaf), not (Khilaf), but as I have explained, it is a source of (Khalaf), so it was read: (Khilaf Rasool God), and this is the reading that the countries read, and it is correct according to us.

i: Some of them interpreted this to mean: “After the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,” and cited as evidence for that the words of the poet:
x: After the spring, their disagreement began, as if the Shawatibs had spread a mat between them.
This is close to the meaning of what we said, because they remained after him in disagreement with him. And His statement:
h
And they hated to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God

, the Most High says: And these people who stayed behind hated to fight the infidels with their wealth and their lives, in the cause of God, meaning: in the religion of God that He has prescribed for His servants to support Him, and inclining toward ease and comfort, and preferring comfort over fatigue and hardship, and being stingy with money to spend it in obedience to God. And they said, ‘Do not go forth in the heat.’ That is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to this expedition, which was the expedition of Tabuk, in intense heat. The hypocrites said to one another, Do not go forth in the heat. So God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, to them, O Muhammad, The fire of Hell, which God has prepared for those who disobey His command and disobey His Messenger, is more intense in heat, than this heat in which you advise one another not to go forth in.

He says: The one who is more intense in heat is more likely to be warned against and protected from than the one who is less harmful, if they only understood, He says: If these hypocrites understood God’s admonition and pondered the verses of His Book, but they do not understand from God. They are wary of the least disliked and least harmful heat, but they are subjected to the most disliked and most severe affliction for those who encounter it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting behind the Messenger of God until his statement

: understand. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the people to set out with him, and that was in the summer. Some men said: O Messenger of God, the heat is intense, and we cannot go out, so do not set out in the heat! God said: Say, ‘The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood.’ So God ordered him to set out.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Ala told us, he said,
m: Muhammad Surat al-Tawbah 9:81 Those who stayed behind rejoiced at their stay behind the Messenger of God,
h
and they hated to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God

, and they said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood." bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: In their seat, contrary to the Messenger of God, he said: It is the Battle of Tabuk.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others, they said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in intense heat to Tabuk, and a man from Banu Salamah said: Do not go out in the heat! So God revealed: Say, ‘The fire of Hell,’ the verse.
b.via: Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he mentioned what some of them said to each other, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered jihad, and decided to march to Tabuk, despite the intense heat and barrenness of the land. God Almighty says: And they said, ‘Do not go forth in the heat.’ Say, ‘The fire of Hell is more intense in heat.’

evidence.text: And his saying: Khilaf is a source from the saying of the speaker: (So-and-so disagreed with so-and-so, so he disagrees with him in disagreement), so its source came in the estimation of (fa’al), just as it is said: (Qataluhu, so he fights him in fighting), and if it was a source from (Khalafu), the reading would have been: (By their seat behind the Messenger of God), because the source of (Khalafu) is (Khalaf), not (Khilaf), but as I have explained, it is a source of (Khalaf), so it was read: (Khilaf Rasool God), and this is the reading that the countries read, and it is correct according to us.

x: God Almighty says: These people who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God, so let them laugh happily for a little while in this fleeting world for their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God, and their distraction from obeying their Lord, for they will cry for a long time in Hell in place of their little laughter in this world, as a reward, meaning: a reward from Us to them for their disobedience, for leaving the group when they were called to fight their enemy, and for sitting in their homes in opposition to the Messenger of God, for what they were earning, meaning: for what they were committing of sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: h
So let them laugh a little and weep much
, he said, God Almighty says: The world is short, so let them laugh in it as much as they wish, and when they reach the Hereafter, they will weep endlessly. That is much.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim:
m: So let them laugh a little, he said: in this world, and let them weep much, he said: in the hereafter.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman and Yahya told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So let them laugh a little and weep much
, he said in the afterlife.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
So let them laugh a little and weep much

, he said: Let them laugh a little in this world, and weep much in the Fire. And he said regarding this verse: And then you will not enjoy [yourselves] except a little (al-Ahzab 33:16), he said: Until their appointed times. One of these two hadiths traces it back to Rabiʿ ibn Khathim.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: So let them laugh a little, he said: Let them laugh in this world, and let them weep much, in the Hereafter in the fire of Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So let them laugh a little, meaning in this world, and weep much, meaning in the Fire. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you knew what I know, you would laugh a little and weep much. It was mentioned to us that at that time he was called out, or it was said to him: Do not despair, My servants.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razeen, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Huthaim,
m: So let them laugh a little, he said: in this world, and let them weep much, he said: in the hereafter. ... He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Razin: So let them laugh a little, he said: In this world, then when they reach the Hereafter they will cry a crying that will not stop. That is a lot.

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So let them laugh a little and weep much
, he said: They are the hypocrites and the disbelievers, who have taken their religion as a joke and a game. God Almighty says: So let them laugh a little, in this world, and weep much, in the Fire.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
So let them laugh a little in this world

, and so let them weep much on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed, until he reached: Is there any reward for the disbelievers for what they used to do? (al-Mutaffifin 83:29-36).

x: The Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If God returns you, O Muhammad, to a group of these hypocrites from this expedition of yours, and they ask your permission to go out with you in another one other than it, then say to them, You will never go out with me nor will you fight an enemy with me, for you were satisfied to sit back the first time, and that was when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Tabuk,
h
then sit with those who stayed behind

, meaning: So sit with those hypocrites who stayed behind in opposition to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because you are from them, so follow their guidance and do what they did in disobeying God, for God has become angry with you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what Qana said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, the heat is intense, and we cannot go out, so do not set out in the heat!” - and that was during the Battle of Tabuk - and God said: “Say: The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood.” So God ordered him to go out. Some men stayed behind, and their souls overcame them, and they said: By God, we have not done anything! So three of them set out and joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they came to him, they repented, then they returned to Medina, and God revealed:
h
If God returns you to a group of them

, until His saying: And do not stand at his grave, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who stayed behind are doomed. Then God revealed their excuse when they repented, and He said: God has accepted the repentance of the Prophet, the Muhajireen, and the Ansar, until His saying: Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful (al-Tawbah 9:117-118).”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If God returns you to a group of them
, to his statement:
h
Then sit with those who stayed behind
, meaning: with the women. He mentioned to us that they were twelve men from the hypocrites, and what was said about them was said.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So sit with those who stay behind, and those who stay behind are the men.

x: The correct interpretation of his statement, those who dissent, is what Ibn Abbas said. As for what Qatada said about women, this is a meaningless statement. Because the Arabs do not gather women if there are no men with them, with the letter ya and the letter noon, nor with the letter waw and the letter noon. If it meant women, it would have been said: So sit with the ones who stay behind, or with the ones who stay behind. But its meaning is what we said, that it was intended: So sit with the sick men and the people of their time, and the weak among them, and the women. And if men and women gather in the report, then the Arabs have more males than females, and that is why it was said: So sit with the ones who stay behind, and the meaning is what we mentioned. If the meaning of this was directed to: So sit with the people of corruption, from their saying: (A man left his family behind, leaving behind a bad person), if he became corrupt, and from their saying: (He is a bad person), it would be a school of thought.

Its origin, if this meaning is intended by it, is from their saying: (The milk left behind, leaving behind a bad person), if it became bad from being left in the water skin for a long time until it spoiled, and from their saying: (The fasting person’s mouth has changed), if its smell has changed.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not pray, O Muhammad, for any of these hypocrites who died and did not go out with you, ever, and do not stand at his grave, meaning: and do not take charge of his burial and his burial. From the saying: So-and-so took care of so-and-so’s matter, meaning he took care of his matter. They disbelieved in God, meaning they denied the oneness of God and the message of His Messenger, and they died as outsiders of Islam, abandoning God’s commands and prohibitions. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over Abdullah bin Ubayy.
Who said that?
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Sufyan ibn Wakee’, and Suwar ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying:

c: Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Nafi’ informed me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: “Ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when his father died and said: Give me your shirt so that I may shroud him in it, pray over him, and seek forgiveness for him - so he gave him his shirt - and when you have finished, let me know. When he wanted to pray over him, Umar pulled him and said: Has not God forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites? He said: Rather, give me a choice and said: ‘Pray for forgiveness for them or do not pray for them.’ He said: So he prayed over him. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: ‘
h
And never pray over any of them who dies

, nor stand at his grave.’ He said: So he stopped praying over them.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Abu Usamah narrated on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, his son Abdullah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, so he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, stood up and took hold of the Prophet’s garment, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Ibn Salul! Will you pray over him, while God has forbidden you to pray over me?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My Lord has given me a choice, and He said: “Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them,” and I will add more than seventy.’ He said: ‘He is a hypocrite!’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, and God revealed: ‘
h
And never pray over any of them who dies

, nor stand at his grave. ’” Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said, Amer told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah: The head of the hypocrites died in Medina, and he left instructions that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, should pray over him, and that he should be shrouded in his shirt, so he shrouded him in his shirt, and prayed over him, and stood at his grave, so God Almighty revealed:
h
And never pray over any of them who dies
, nor stand at his grave.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to pray over Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, took hold of his garment and said:
h
And never pray over any of them who dies
, nor stand at his grave.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Abdullah bin Ubayy, who had been put in his grave. He took him out and placed him on his knees, dressed him in his shirt, and spat on him from his saliva. And God knows best.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masʿud, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas:
m: He said: “I heard Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called to pray over him, so he stood over him. When he stood over him intending to pray, I turned until I stood in front of him and said: O Messenger of God, are you praying over the enemy of God, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who said on such and such a day, such and such!! Count his days, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was smiling, until they became too many for him, and he said: Stop it, O Umar, for I was given a choice and I chose, and it was said to me: ‘Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.’ If I knew that if I increased it to seventy, he would be forgiven, I would have increased it!” He said: Then he prayed over him and walked with him, and he stood over his grave until he finished. He said: I was amazed at myself and my audacity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God and His Messenger know best, so by God It was only a short time before these two verses were revealed:
h
And never pray over any of them who dies
, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray over a hypocrite after that, nor did he stand at his grave, until God took him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, he said:
m: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died, his son Abdullah ibn Abdullah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him for his shirt, so he gave it to him, and he shrouded his father in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, he said:
m: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died, he mentioned something like the hadith of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Salamah.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And never pray over any of them who dies

, nor stand at his grave, the verse. He said: “Abdullah bin Ubayy was sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sick, to visit him, but Umar forbade him from doing so. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him, and when he entered upon him, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Love for the Jews has destroyed you!’ He said: ‘O Prophet of God, I was not sent to you to rebuke me, but I was sent to you to ask forgiveness for me!’ He asked him for his shirt to be shrouded in it, so he gave it to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for him, and he died and was shrouded in the shirt of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he breathed into his skin, and lowered him into his grave, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: “
h
And never pray over any of them who dies

,” the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was spoken to about that and he said: ‘And what does my shirt avail him from God - or: my Lord - and he prayed over him - and I hope That a thousand of his people would surrender to him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: “Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sick. When he entered upon him, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Love for the Jews has destroyed you!’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I only sent to you to ask forgiveness for me, and I did not send to you to rebuke me!’ Then Abdullah asked him to give him his shirt so that he could be shrouded in it, so he gave it to him, and he prayed over him and stood at his grave, so God, the Most High, revealed: ‘
h
And never pray over any of them who dies
, nor stand at his grave.’”

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not be impressed by the wealth and children of these hypocrites, so that you pray for one of them when he dies and stand at his grave, because of the abundance of his wealth and children, for I only gave him what I gave him of that in order to torment him with it in this world with sorrows and worries, with what I oblige him to pay in it of provisions, expenses, and zakat, and with what befalls him in it of misfortunes and calamities, and their souls shall depart, meaning: and he shall die and his soul shall leave his body, and he shall be separated from what I gave him of wealth and children, so that this will be a regret for him at his death, and a burden upon him then, and a burden upon him in the Hereafter, because he died denying the Oneness of God and the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And their souls will perish, in this worldly life.

x: God Almighty says: And when He sends down to you, O Muhammad, a surah from the Qur’an, that it is said to these hypocrites: Believe in God, meaning: believe in God, and fight with His Messenger, meaning: fight the polytheists with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, those of them who are wealthy ask your permission, meaning: those of them who are rich and wealthy ask your permission to stay behind you and stay with their families, “and they say: Leave us,” meaning: and they say to you: Leave us, we will be among those who stay in their homes with the weak and sick of the people, and those who are not able to go out with you on a journey. And similar to what we said about the meaning of length, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Those of means ask your permission, he said: meaning the wealthy.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Those of them who have wealth, meaning the rich.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And when a surah is revealed, ‘Believe in God and strive with His Messenger,’ those of means among them ask your permission. Among them were Abdullah bin Ubayy and Al-Jadd bin Qais, so God condemned them for that.

x: God Almighty says: These hypocrites - who, when it is said to them: Believe in God and fight with His Messenger, the wealthy among them ask your permission to stay behind from the conquest and go out with you to fight the enemies of God from among the polytheists - were satisfied to be in their homes, like women who are not obligated to fight, so they sit in their homes and houses, and a seal has been placed upon their hearts, meaning: God has sealed the hearts of these hypocrites, so they do not understand, from God's admonitions, so they learn from them. We have explained the meaning of nature and how hearts are sealed in the past, so there is no need to repeat it here. And similar to what we said about the meaning of the ones who leave was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They were satisfied to be with the ones who stayed behind
, he said: The ones who stayed behind are the women.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
They were satisfied to be with the ones who stayed behind
, meaning the women.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawayh Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah:
m: h
They were satisfied to be with the women
. He said: The women. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: With the women. He said: With the women.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They were satisfied to be with the women
, meaning: with the women.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Al-Hasan:
m: h
They were satisfied to be with the women
. They said: The women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
They were satisfied to be with the women
. He said: With the women.

x: God Almighty says: These hypocrites whose stories I have told did not fight the polytheists, but the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed in God and His Messenger with him, are the ones who fought the polytheists with their wealth and their lives, so they spent their wealth in their struggle, and they exhausted themselves in fighting them and gave it up, and those, meaning: for the Messenger and those who believed with him, who fought with their wealth and their lives, are the good things, and they are the good things of the Hereafter, and that is: its women, its gardens, and its pleasures.

i: Its singular is (Khaira), as the poet said:
x: The assemblies of the ribs have stabbed the ribs of India, the best of queens.
And the best of everything is the virtuous. And those are the successful ones, meaning: And those are the ones who will remain in Paradise, remaining therein, and winning therein.

God Almighty says: God has prepared for His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for those who believe with him, gardens, which are orchards, with rivers flowing beneath their trees, abiding therein, meaning: remaining therein, not dying therein, nor departing from it. That is the great attainment, meaning: that is the great salvation and abundant fortune.

God Almighty says: And came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the excuse-makers from among the desert Arabs came so that permission might be given to them, in staying behind, and sat, from coming to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fighting with him, those who denied God and His Messenger, and told lies, and made false excuses from them. God Almighty says: A painful punishment will befall those among them who denied the Oneness of God and the Prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

And the excuse-makers came, and you know that the excuser, in the speech of the Arabs, is only: the one who excuses in a matter, but does not exaggerate in it or make it a ruling? This is not the description of these people, but rather their description is that they had striven hard to seek what would enable them to rise with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to confront their enemy, and they were keen on that, but they did not find a way to it, so it is more appropriate and deserving of being described as: they excused, than as being described as they excused. And if they are described with that, then the correct reading in that is what Ibn Abbas read, and that is what: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Isqah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: Ibn Abbas used to read: (And those who have excuses have come), with a light pronunciation, and he would say: They are the people of excuse. With the approval of Mujahid and others?

The meaning of that is not what you have gone to, and that its meaning is: And the Arabs who apologized came, but (Taa) when it was next to (Dhal) was assimilated into it, so they became a doubled Dhaal, because the point of articulation of one of them is close to the other, as it was said (yadhkirun) in (yathakkarun), and (yadhakkar) in (yathakkaran), and the ‘ayn of (al-mu’adhdhireen) moved to the fatha, because the movement of the Taa in (al-mu’adhdhireen), which is the fatha, was transferred to it, so it was moved with what it was moved with.

And the Arabs have directed the meaning of (apology) to (excuse), so he says: (Fulan has apologized for such-and-such), meaning: he excused, and from that is the saying of Labid: Until the year, then peace be upon you both. Whoever cries for a full year has apologized. He said: He has apologized, meaning: he has excused himself. However, the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of these people whom God described as having come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with excuses.
Some of them said: They were lying in their apology, so God did not excuse them.
Who said that?

c: Abu Ubaidah Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Al-Hussein, he said:
m: Qatada used to recite: And there came the excuse-makers from among the bedouins, he said: They excused themselves with lies.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the excuse-makers came from among the Bedouins, he said: A group of Banu Ghafar came and apologized, but God did not excuse them. Those we mentioned among them said: These people were people who only apologized with falsehood, not with truth. So it is not permissible to describe them as having excuses, unless they are described as having excused themselves in their false apology. As for the truth - according to what those we have mentioned said - it is not permissible to describe them with it.

x: Some of them used to say: They came with excuses and were not serious, offering what they did not want to do. So whoever directed it to this interpretation, there is no problem in that, but I do not know of anyone among the people of knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur’an who directed his interpretation to that, so I recommend saying it. And then, what is upon it from the reading of the regions, the emphasis on (dhal), I mean from his saying: those who are excused, so in that is evidence of the correctness of the interpretation of those who interpreted it to mean an apology, because the people who were described with that were not charged with a matter for which they were excused, but rather they were two groups: either a diligent and obedient one, or a hypocritical and immoral one, disobeying the Surat al-Tawbah 9:90 And the excuse-makers from among the bedouins came to be permitted to speak, and those who denied God and His Messenger sat down.

A painful punishment will afflict those among them who disbelieved. command of God. So there is no one in the two groups described as being excused for being with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but rather he is an exaggerated excuser, or an apologist. If that is the case, and the evidence from the readings is unanimous on the emphasis on the dhal of al-mu’adhreen, it is known that its meaning is what we described of the interpretation. It was mentioned on the authority of Mujahid that he agreed with Ibn Abbas on this matter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Hamid, he said:
m: Mujahid read: (And those who have excuses will come), with a light pronunciation, and he said: They are the people of excuse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The excused ones, as far as I have heard, were a group of Banu Ghafar, among them: Khafaf bin Ayma bin Rahdah, then the story was about the people of excuse, until it ended with His saying: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them, the verse.

evidence.text: And if they are described with that, then the correct reading in that is what Ibn Abbas read, and that is what: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Isqah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: Ibn Abbas used to read: (And those who have excuses have come), with a light pronunciation, and he would say: They are the people of excuse.

And then, what is upon it from the reading of the regions, the emphasis on (dhal), I mean from his saying: those who are excused, so in that is evidence of the correctness of the interpretation of those who interpreted it to mean an apology, because the people who were described with that were not charged with a matter for which they were excused, but rather they were two groups: either a diligent and obedient one, or a hypocritical and immoral one, disobeying the Surat al-Tawbah 9:90 And the excuse-makers from among the bedouins came to be permitted to speak, and those who denied God and His Messenger sat down.
If that is the case, and the evidence from the readings is unanimous on the emphasis on the dhal of al-mu’adhreen, it is known that its meaning is what we described of the interpretation.

x: God Almighty says: There is no blame upon the people of this time and those who are unable to travel and fight, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find the means to reach their destination, hardship, which is sin. He says: There is no blame upon them if they were sincere to God and His Messenger in their absence from jihad with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no way against the doers of good, He says: There is no way against the one who was sincere to God and His Messenger in his absence from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from jihad with him, for an excuse that can be excused, so that he is punished by it. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, He says: God covers the sins of the doers of good, He covers them with His forgiveness for them, Merciful, towards them, that He does not punish them for them.
He mentioned that this verse was revealed about Aaidh bin Amr Al-Muzani.
Some of them said about Abdullah bin Mughaffal. It was mentioned that it was revealed about Aaidh bin Amr.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill or upon those who do not find anything to spend if they are sincere to God and His Messenger, it was revealed about (A’idh bin Amr). It was mentioned that it was revealed about Ibn Mughaffal.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick to his statement

: grief that they do not find anything to spend, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the people to go out to fight with him, and a group of his companions came to him, among them was Abdullah bin Mughaffal Al-Muzani, and they said: O Messenger of God, give us some mounts. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: By God, I do not find anything to mount you on! So they turned away, weeping, and it was difficult for them to sit out of jihad, and they did not find any money or a mount. So when God saw their eagerness for His love and the love of His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the sick or upon those who do not find anything to spend to his statement: so they do not know.

x: God Almighty says: And there is no way for the group of people who, when they come to you, to be carried, and ask you for loads, to reach their destination to fight with you against the enemies of God, O Muhammad, you said to them: I do not find a load to carry you on, they turned away, meaning: they turned away from you, and their eyes overflowed with tears of grief, and they weep from grief that they do not find what to spend, and carry with it for the jihad in the way of God.
Some of them mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of people from Muzaynah.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may mount them, you say, ‘I find nothing on which to mount you,’ he said: They are from Muzaynah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may carry them, he said: They are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: in a reading, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may carry them, to his statement: grieved that they do not find what they can spend, because: they are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And there is no blame upon those who

, when they come to you that you may carry them, he said: They are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of ʿUrwah, on the authority of Ibn Mughaffal Al-Muzani, who was one of the people about whom the verse was revealed:
h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may mount them, the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They turned away while their eyes were overflowing with tears out of grief
, he said: Among them was Ibn Muqrin. Sufyan said: The people said: Among them was Arabadh bin Sariyah.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Arabadh bin Sariyah.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Thawr bin Yazid, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Amr Al-Salami and Hajar bin Hajar Al-Kila’i, they said,
m: we entered upon Arabadh bin Sariyah, and he is the one about whom the verse was revealed:
h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may mount them, the verse.
b.via: Abd Al-Rahman bin Amr Al-Salami and Hajar bin Hajar Al-Kila’i

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, al-Walid told us, he said, Thawr told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr,
m: and Hajar ibn Hajar, something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about seven people from different tribes.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb and others, he said:
m: “Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to ask him to mount them, so he said: I do not find anything to mount you on! So God revealed: ‘Nor upon those who, when they come to you that you may mount them’, the verse. He said: They were seven men: from Banu Amr bin Awf: Salim bin Umair, from Banu Waqif: Harmi bin Amr, from Banu Mazin bin An-Najjar: Abd al-Rahman bin Kaʿb, whose kunya was Abu Laila, from Banu Al-Muʿalla: Salman bin Sakhr, from Banu Haritha: Abd al-Rahman bin Yazid, Abu Ubla, who was the one who gave his property in charity and God accepted it from him, and from Banu Salamah: Amr bin Ghanmah, and Abdullah bin Amr Al-Muzani.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon those who
, when they come to you that you may carry them, to his statement: in grief, Surat al-Tawbah 9:92
h
And there is no blame upon those who

, when they come to you that you may mount them, you say, "I cannot find anything on which to mount you," and they turn away while their eyes overflow with tears out of grief that they cannot find anything to spend. and they are the weepers, they were seven. Part 10 of Volume 6 is done. Followed, God willing, by the eleventh part of the sixth volume. The first: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: The way is only against those who ask your permission al-Tawbah 9:93

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, in a reading, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them, to his statement: grieved that they do not find what they can spend, because: they are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah.

x: God Almighty says: What is the way to punish those who have an excuse, O Muhammad? Rather, it is for those who ask your permission to stay behind you and abandon jihad with you, and they are people of wealth, strength, and energy for jihad and conquest, out of hypocrisy and doubt in God's promise and threat. They were content to be with those who stayed behind, meaning: They were content to sit after you with the women, who are the ones who stayed behind, behind the men in the houses, and to abandon conquest with you. And God has sealed their hearts, meaning: God has sealed their hearts with what they have earned of sins, so they do not know, the evil end of their fate, for staying behind you and abandoning jihad with you, and the ugly praise they will receive in this world and the great affliction in the Hereafter.

God Almighty says: He apologizes to you, O believers in God, for these who have stayed behind against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who have abandoned the jihad against the polytheists with you from the hypocrites, with falsehoods and lies, when you return to them from your journey and jihad, Say, to them, O Muhammad, Do not apologize, we will not believe you, meaning: We will not believe you in what you say, God has informed us of your report, meaning:

c: God has informed us
m: of your report, and informed us of your affair that which we have known of your lies, And God and His Messenger will see your work, meaning: And God and His Messenger will see your work afterward, will you repent from your hypocrisy, or will you persist in it? Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning: then you will be returned after your death, to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning: the One who knows the secret and the public, from whom nothing is hidden from the inner and outer aspects of your affairs, and He will inform you of what you used to do, so He will inform you of all your deeds, both the bad and the good, and He will reward you for them: the good of them for the good, and the bad of them for the bad.

x: God Almighty says: O believers in God, these hypocrites who rejoiced in their position in opposition to the Messenger of God will swear to you, If you return to them, meaning: if you return to them from your raid, to turn away from them, so do not rebuke them, so turn away from them, God Almighty says to the believers: So leave their rebuke, and leave them to what they have chosen for themselves of disbelief and hypocrisy, Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell, meaning: They are unclean, and their refuge is Hell, meaning: and their destination is Hell, which is their abode in the Hereafter, as a reward for what they used to earn, meaning: as a reward for the deeds they used to do in this world of disobeying God.
He mentioned that this verse was revealed about two hypocrites who said:

c: What - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to me, he said, my uncle narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will swear to you by God when you return to them to expose themselves to to for what they used to earn

, and that is “that it was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you not raid the yellow people, perhaps you will capture the daughter of the great Roman, for they are beautiful!” Two men said: You know, O Messenger of God, that women are a temptation, so do not tempt us with them! So give us permission! So he gave them permission. When they set out, one of them said: It is nothing but fat for the first eater! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out, and nothing was revealed to him about that. When he was on some of the way, it was revealed to him while he was on some water: If it had been a short excursion and a short journey, they would have followed you, but the distance was too great for them (al-Tawbah 9:42) and it was revealed to him: God has pardoned you, why did you give them permission? (al-Tawbah 9:43) and it was revealed to him: Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission (al-Tawbah 9:44). 44] And it was revealed to him: Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. A man who had fought with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that, so he came to them while they were behind them and said: Do you know that a Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after you? They said: What did you hear? He said: I do not know, except that I heard him say: Indeed, they are unclean! A man called Makhshy said: By God, I would have liked to be flogged a hundred times and not be with you! So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What brought you? He said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is being blown away by the wind, and I am in a cocoon!! Then God revealed to him: And among them are those who say, ‘Give me leave and do not put me to trial’ (al-Tawbah 9:49), And they say, ‘Do not go forth in the heat’ (al-Tawbah 9:81). And about the man who said, I wish I could be flogged a hundred times, God revealed to him: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down to them informing them of what is in their hearts (al-Tawbah 9:64). A man with the Messenger of God said: If these people are as they say, then there is no good in us! When that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to him: Are you the one who said the word that you heard? He said: No, by Him who sent down the Book to you! So God revealed about him: They have certainly said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam (al-Tawbah 9:74), and God revealed about him: “And among you are those who listen to them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers” (al-Tawbah 9:47).

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik told me: Abdullah ibn Kaʿb said:
m: I heard Kaʿb ibn Malik say: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Tabuk, and sat with the people, and when he had done that, those who had stayed behind came and began to apologize to him and swear to him, and they were about eighty-odd men, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted their outward expressions, and pledged allegiance to them, and sought forgiveness for them, and entrusted their secrets to God, and my hadith confirmed it. Ka'b said: By God, God has never bestowed upon me a greater blessing, after He guided me to Islam, than the truthfulness of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I hope that I do not lie about him and perish as those who lied perished. God said to those who lied when He sent down the revelation, the worst thing He said to anyone: “They will swear to you by God when you return to them that you will turn away from them. So turn away from them. Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.” Until His saying: Indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people.

x: God Almighty says: These hypocrites swear to you, O believers in God, as an excuse of falsehood and lies, “so that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people.” He says: If you, O believers, are pleased with them and accept their excuse, since you do not know whether they are truthful or lying, then your pleasure with them will not benefit them with God, because God knows of the secrets of their affairs what you do not know, and of the hidden beliefs of theirs what you are ignorant of, and that they are in disbelief in God... meaning that they are the ones who have departed from faith to disbelief in God, and from obedience to disobedience.

God Almighty says that the Bedouins are more ungrateful to the Oneness of God, and more hypocritical, than the urban dwellers in the villages and cities. God Almighty described them thus because of their rudeness, the hardness of their hearts, and their lack of encounters with good people. Therefore, they are harder-hearted and less knowledgeable about the rights of God. And his saying:
h
And it is more appropriate that they do not know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger
, he says:
h
And it is more appropriate that they do not know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger
, and that is, according to what Qatada said: the Sunnah.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is more likely that they do not know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger
, he said: They have less knowledge of the Sunnah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: A Bedouin sat with Zaid ibn Suhan while he was talking to his companions, and his hand had been injured on the day of Nahavand, so he said: By God, your talk pleases me, but your hand makes me doubt! Zaid said: What makes you doubt my hand? It is the left! The Bedouin said: By God, I do not know, is it the right hand that is cut off or the left? Zaid ibn Suhan said: God has spoken the truth: The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger. And His statement:
h
And God is All-Knowing
, All-Wise, means:
h
And God is All-Knowing

, of those who know the limits of what He revealed to His Messenger, and the hypocrites among His creation, and the disbelievers among them, none of them is hidden from Him, Wise, in His management of them, and in His forbearance in punishing them, with His knowledge of their secrets and their deception of His friends.

x: God Almighty says: And among the Bedouins are those who consider their expenditures that they spend in jihad against a polytheist, or in helping a Muslim, or in some of the things that God has urged His servants to do, a loss, meaning: a loss that is incumbent upon them, for which they do not hope to receive a reward, nor do they ward off punishment from themselves, and they await for you the evil consequences, meaning: and they await for you the evil consequences, that the days and nights will turn towards something bad and the arrival of something beloved, and the victory of an enemy over you. God Almighty says: upon them is the evil consequences, meaning: God has made the evil consequences happen to them, and the calamity will befall them, not upon you, O believers, nor with you, and God is All-Hearing, of the supplications of those who supplicate, All-Knowing of their planning, and what is coming down upon them from God's punishment, and what they will end up with from His painful punishment.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God: And among the desert Arabs are those who consider what they spend as a loss and await for you a misfortune, he said: These are the hypocrites among the desert Arabs, who only spend to show off, to avoid going to war or fighting or fighting, and they consider their spending a misfortune. Do you not see that He says: “and await for you a misfortune. Upon them is the misfortune”? There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: upon them is a circle of evil with the opening of the seen, meaning an adjective for the circle, even though the circle is added to it, like their saying: He is a man of evil and a man of truth, from ka’anhu if it is opened as a source from their saying: I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil.

x: Some of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: (upon them is the circle of evil), with a damma on the seen, as if he made it a noun, just as one says: upon him is the circle of affliction and torment. And whoever says: (upon them is the circle of evil) with a damma, does not say: (This is the evil man) with a damma, and (the evil man), and the poet said: I was like a bad wolf, when he saw blood on his companion one day, he referred to the blood Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading of this, according to us, is with the opening of the seen, meaning: upon them is the circle that will harm them with harm. Just as one says: (He is a man of truth), as an adjective.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: upon them is a circle of evil with the opening of the seen, meaning an adjective for the circle, even though the circle is added to it, like their saying: He is a man of evil and a man of truth, from ka’anhu if it is opened as a source from their saying: I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil, I made him evil.

Some of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: (upon them is the circle of evil), with a damma on the seen, as if he made it a noun, just as one says: upon him is the circle of affliction and torment.

And whoever says: (upon them is the circle of evil) with a damma, does not say: (This is the evil man) with a damma, and (the evil man), and the poet said: I was like a bad wolf, when he saw blood on his companion one day, he referred to the blood Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading of this, according to us, is with the opening of the seen, meaning: upon them is the circle that will harm them with harm.

x: God Almighty says: And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and acknowledge His Oneness, and in the resurrection after death, and reward and punishment, and they intend what they spend in jihad against the polytheists, and in their travels with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as drawing closer to God. And (drawing closer) is the plural of (drawing closer), which is what brings him closer to God’s pleasure and love,
h
and the prayers of the Messenger

, meaning by that: And he seeks with what he spends, while seeking his closeness to God, the supplication of the Messenger and his asking for forgiveness for him. We have previously demonstrated in our book that one of the meanings of prayer is supplication, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And the prayers of the Messenger
, meaning: the Prophet’s seeking of forgiveness, peace be upon him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God and the Last Day and regard what they spend as means of drawing closer to God and prayers of the Messenger, he said: The supplication of the Messenger, this is the second of God’s desert Arabs.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And among the bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day, he said: They are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah, and they are the ones about whom God said: “And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may mount them, you say, ‘I find nothing on which to mount you,’ and they turn away while their eyes overflow with tears out of grief” (al-Tawbah 9:92). He said: They are Banu Muqrin, from Muzaynah. He said, Hajjaj narrated to me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said: His statement: The bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, then he made an exception and said: And among the bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day, the verse.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Bukhtari bin Al-Mukhtar Al-Abdi, who said,
m: I heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Muqal say: We were ten sons of Muqrin, and the following was revealed about us: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God and the Last Day, to the end of the verse.

x: God said: Indeed, it is a means of drawing near to them. God Almighty says: Indeed, the prayers of the Messenger are a means of drawing near to them from God. It may be possible that its meaning is: Indeed, his spending that he spends in this way is a means of drawing closer to God.
