God will admit them into His mercy, meaning: God will admit them into those whom He has shown mercy to and whom He has admitted through His mercy into Paradise. Indeed, God is Forgiving, for what they have committed, Merciful, towards them despite their repentance and reform, that He will not punish them.

God Almighty says: And those who preceded mankind first in believing in God and His Messenger, of the Muhajireen, who migrated from their people and clan, and left their homes and homelands, and the Ansar, who supported the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, against his enemies from among the people of disbelief in God and His Messenger, and those who followed them with goodness, meaning: and those who followed their path in believing in God and His Messenger, and migrating from the land of war to the land of Islam, seeking God’s pleasure,
h
God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying:
h
and the first to forefront
Some of them said: They are those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the Pledge of Ridwan, or who were aware of it. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The first immigrants are those who witnessed the pledge of allegiance under the tree.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The first immigrants, who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan.

c: Al-Harith told me: Abdul Aziz told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The first immigrants, those who were before the pledge of allegiance until the pledge of allegiance, they are the first immigrants, and those who were after the pledge of allegiance, they are not among the first immigrants.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Ismail and Mutraf told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: h
And the first to forefront
among the Muhajireen and the Ansar, they are those who pledged the Pledge of Ridwan.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The two migrations were separated by the Pledge of Ridwan, which is the Pledge of Hudaybiyyah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr ibn Awn told us: Hisham told us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid and Mutraf told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: They are those who pledged allegiance to the Pledge of Ridwan.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abthar Abu Zubayd told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The first immigrants are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan.

x: Others said: Rather, they are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Uthman Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of a client of Abu Musa, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said:
m: The first immigrants are those who prayed facing the two qiblas with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir, on the authority of a client of Abu Musa, he said:
m: I asked Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari about his statement:
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar
, he said: They are those who prayed toward both qiblas.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: I said to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: Why were they called the first immigrants? He said: Whoever prays with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing both qiblas, is one of the first immigrants.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: The first immigrants are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar
, he said: They are those who prayed toward both qiblas.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abbas bin Al-Waleed told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: the same. Surat al-Tawbah 9:100
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar
and those who followed them with good conduct -
h
God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him
. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. That is the great attainment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the first to forefront
, he said: They are those who prayed towards the two qiblas.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Muadh told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: The first immigrants, those who prayed towards the two qiblas.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar

, he said: They are those who prayed toward both qiblas. As for those who followed the first immigrants and the Ansar with goodness, they are those who submitted their Islam to God and followed their methods of immigration, support, and good deeds, such as:

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Abu Maʿshar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, who said:
m: Umar passed by a man who was reciting this verse:
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar

and those who followed them with good conduct. He said: Who taught you this verse? He said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught it to me. He said: Do not leave me until I take you to him! So he came to him and said: Did you teach this man this verse? He said: Yes! He said: And did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?! He said: Yes! He said: I used to think that we had been raised to a status that no one after us would attain! Ubayy said: Confirmation of that is in the beginning of the verse at the beginning of Al-Jumuʿah, the middle of Al-Hashr, and the end of Al-Anfal. As for the beginning of al-Jumuah 62:And others of them have not yet joined them (al-Jumuah 62:3), and the middle of al-Hashr 59:And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith’ (al-Hashr 59:10), and as for the end of al-Anfal 8:And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are from you (al-Anfal 8:75). Abu Kuraib narrated, Al-Hasan bin Atiyah narrated, Abu Maʿshar narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab passed by a man reciting,
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar

, until he reached, And they were pleased with him. Umar took him by the hand and said, Who taught you this? He said, Ubayy bin Kaʿb! Umar said, Do not leave me until I take you to him! When he came to him, Umar said, Did you teach this man this verse like this? He said, Yes! He said, “Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He said, Yes! He said, I used to think that we had been raised to a level that no one after us would attain! My father said: Yes, this verse is confirmed in Surat al-Jumuah 62:And others of them have not yet joined them to And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise (al-Jumuah 62:3), and in Surat al-Hashr 59:And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith’ (al-Hashr 59:10), and in al-Anfal 8:And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are from you (al-Anfal 8:75), to the end of the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Omar
m: regarding this matter: Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to me, he said, Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Habib bin Al-Shaheed, and on the authority of Ibn Amir Al-Ansari: that Omar bin Al-Khattab recited:
h
And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar

and those who followed them with good conduct, so he raised the Ansar and did not add the waw in those who, so Zaid bin Thabit said to him: And those who followed them with good conduct, so Omar said: Those who followed them with good conduct, so Zaid said: The Commander of the Faithful knows best! Omar said: Bring me Ubayy bin Ka’b. So he went to him and asked him about that, so Ubayy said: And those who followed them with good conduct, so Omar said: Then we will follow Ubayy.

x: The reading is in the accusative case of the Ansar, in conjunction with the Muhajireen. It was mentioned about Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read: Al-Ansar in the nominative case, in conjunction with Al-Sabiqeen.

The reading that I do not permit other than it is the accusative case in al-Ansar, because of the consensus of the proof from the readings on it, and that the one who came first was from both groups, the Muhajireen and the Ansar. The intention was only to report on the one who came first from both groups, not to report on everyone. The addition of the waw in those who followed them in goodness, because that is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of all the Muslims, on the condition that those who followed in goodness, is not the Muhajireen and the Ansar. As for the forerunners, they are in the nominative case because of the reference to their mention in His statement,
h
God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him

. The meaning of the words: God is pleased with all of them because they obeyed Him and responded to His Prophet’s commands and prohibitions, and the first of the Muhajireen and Ansar, and those who followed them in goodness, were pleased with Him because He gave them a great reward for their obedience to Him and their belief in Him and in His Prophet, peace be upon him.

And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, which they will enter, abiding therein, remaining therein, forever, neither dying therein nor leaving therein. That is the great attainment.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading is in the accusative case of the Ansar, in conjunction with the Muhajireen.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that I do not permit other than it is the accusative case in al-Ansar, because of the consensus of the proof from the readings on it, and that the one who came first was from both groups, the Muhajireen and the Ansar.

x: God Almighty says: And among the people around your city are hypocrites, and among the people of your city are also hypocrites like them. His saying:
h
They were trained in hypocrisy

, means: they were trained in it and were trained in it. And from it: (a rebellious devil, and a rebellious one), which is the evil and obstinate one, and from it it was said: (So-and-so rebelled against his Lord), meaning: he rebelled, and became accustomed to disobeying Him and became accustomed to it.
Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among the people of Medina are those who persist in hypocrisy
, he said: They persisted in it, they did not repent as the others repented.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And among the people of Medina are those who persist in hypocrisy

, meaning: they persist in it and refuse to do anything else. Do not teach them, he says to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Do not teach them, O Muhammad, you are those hypocrites whose characteristics I have described to you from among the Bedouins and the people of Medina around you, but
h
we know them
, as:

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites
” to his statement:
h
We know them

, he said: So what is the matter with people who burden themselves with the knowledge of people? So-and-so is in Paradise and so-and-so is in Hell! So if you ask one of them about himself, he says: I do not know! By my life, you know yourself better than you do the deeds of people, and you have undertaken something that the prophets before you did not undertake! The Prophet of God, Noah, peace be upon him, said: And I have no knowledge of what they used to do
r
(Ash-Shu’ara’: 112)
, and the Prophet of God, Shu’aib, peace be upon him, said: “The remainder from God is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you”
r
, and God said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: Do not teach them,
h
We know them
. And His saying:
h
We will punish them twice
, means: We will punish these hypocrites twice, once in this world, and the other in the grave. Then the people of interpretation differed about what is in this world. What is it?

x: Some of them said: It is their disgrace. God disgraced them by revealing their affairs and revealing their secrets to the people through the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi narrated to us, saying, my father narrated to us, saying, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites
, and among the people of Madinah are those who persist in hypocrisy until His statement:
h
A great punishment

, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up as a preacher on Friday and said: ‘Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite, go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite.’ So he brought some of them out of the mosque and disgraced them. ‘Umar met them as they were coming out of the mosque, so he hid from them out of shame that he had not attended the Friday prayer, and he thought that the people had left. And they hid from ‘Umar, thinking that he had learned of their affair. ‘Umar came and entered the mosque, and found that the people had not prayed, so a man from the Muslims said to him: ‘Be of good cheer, ‘Umar, for God has disgraced the hypocrites today! This is the first punishment, when He brought them out of the mosque, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave.’”

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: h
We will punish them twice

. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would deliver a sermon and mention the hypocrites, and he would punish them with his tongue. He said: And the punishment of the grave.”

x: Others said: What befalls them of captivity, killing, hunger and fear in this world.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, he said: killing and captivity.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, with hunger and the punishment of the grave. He said:
h
Then they will be returned to a great punishment
, on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muntha told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn, Al-Qasim, and Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
We will punish them twice
, he said: hunger and killing, and Yahya said: fear and killing.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: With hunger and killing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, he said: with hunger and the punishment of the grave.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, he said: hunger and killing.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is, We will punish them with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave,
h
then they will be returned to a great punishment

. “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, confided to Hudhayfah twelve men from the hypocrites, and he said: Six of them will be sufficient for you with the debility, a lamp from the fire of Hell, which will take hold of one of them until it reaches his chest, and six will die a death.” It was mentioned to us that when a man died, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, would look at Hudhayfah, and if he prayed for him, he would pray for him, otherwise he would leave him. It was mentioned to us that Umar said to Hudhayfah: I ask you by God, am I one of them? He said: No, by God, and I will not believe anyone else after you!

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, he said: The punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ told us, they said: Badal bin Al-Muhabbir told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
We will punish them twice
, he said: A punishment in this world, and a punishment in the grave.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: The torment of this world, and the torment of the grave, then they will be returned to the torment of the Fire.

x: Others said: Their punishment was one of the two times: their misfortunes in their wealth and children, and the other time in Hell.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
We will punish them twice

, he said: As for the punishment in this world, it is wealth and children. And he recited the statement of God: “So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world” (al-Tawbah 9:55), with the calamities that befall them, it is a punishment for them, and it is a reward for the believers. He said: And punishment in the Hereafter, in the Fire,
h
Then they will be returned to a great punishment
, he said: the Fire.

x: Others said: Rather, one of the two times is the limits, and the other is the torment of the grave. This was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas from a source other than Murtadha.

Others said: Rather, one of the two times is taking zakat from their money, and the other is the torment of the grave. This was mentioned on the authority of Sulayman ibn Arqam, on the authority of al-Hasan.
Others said: Rather, it is one of the two times, their punishment due to the anger that enters them regarding the matter of Islam.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
We will punish them twice

, he said: The punishment that was promised to them twice, as far as I have heard, is their grief over what they are in regarding the matter of Islam, and the anger that enters them without any reason, then their punishment in the grave when they reach it, then the great punishment to which they are returned, the punishment of the Hereafter, and eternity in it.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is that God informed us that He will punish those who persist in hypocrisy twice, and He did not provide us with evidence that would lead us to knowledge of the description of those two punishments. It is possible that some of what we have mentioned about those who said what we have been informed about. We do not have knowledge of which of that is which. However, in His statement, may He be glorified and exalted,
h
Then they will be returned to a great punishment
, there is evidence that the punishment both times is before they enter the Fire. The most likely of the two times is that it is in the Surat al-Tawbah 9:101
h
And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites
and among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy. You do not know them, but
h
We know them
h
We will punish them twice
h
then they will be returned to a great punishment
. grave.
And His statement:
h
Then they will be returned to a great punishment
, meaning: Then these hypocrites will be returned, after God has punished them twice, to
h
a great punishment
, and that is the punishment of Hell.

God Almighty says: And among the people of Medina are hypocrites who have become accustomed to hypocrisy, and among them are and others who have acknowledged their sins, meaning: they have admitted their sins, they have mixed righteous deeds, meaning, may His praise be glorified, by the righteous deeds that they have mixed with the bad deeds: their acknowledgment of their sins, and their repentance from them, and the other bad deeds: is their failure to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he went out to fight, and their abandonment of jihad with the Muslims.
How is it said: They mixed a good deed with a bad one, when the statement is: They mixed a good deed with a bad one?
The Arabs differed on this.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was said like this, and it is permissible in Arabic for it to be with another, just as you say the water and the wood were equal, meaning: with the wood, and and I mixed the water and the milk. Another denied that it was similar to their saying: The water and the wood were equal, and he argued for that by saying that the verb in mixing is an agent in the first and second, and it is permissible to present each one of them before the other, and that presenting the wood before water is not permissible in their saying: The water and the wood were equal, and that was, in his view, evidence that it contradicts mixing.

The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is that it is in the same sense as their saying: I mixed water and milk, meaning: I mixed it with milk. Perhaps God will accept their repentance, he says: Perhaps God will accept their repentance. Perhaps from God is obligatory, but its meaning is: God will accept their repentance. However, in the speech of the Arabs, it is as you have described. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, he says: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Pardoning to whoever repents from his sins, and He covers them for him. Merciful, that is, He does not punish him for them.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of this verse and the reason for which it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed about ten people who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, including Abu Lubaba. Seven of them tied themselves to the pillars when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, as repentance for their sin.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “
h
And others acknowledged their sins

. They mixed a good deed with another bad one,” he said: “They were ten men who stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was about to return, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them when he returned in the mosque. When he saw them, he said: Who are these people who tied themselves to the pillars? They said: This is Abu Lubabah and his companions who stayed behind from you, O Messenger of God, and they swore that no one would release them until you release them and excuse them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And I swear by God that I will not release them nor excuse them until God is the one who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the battle with the Muslims! When that reached them, they said: And we, by God, will not release ourselves until God is the one who releases us! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: “
h
And others acknowledged their sins

. They mixed a good deed with another bad one. Perhaps God will release them.” May God forgive them,” and may is obligatory from God. So when it was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and released them and excused them.

x: Others said: Rather, there were six of them, one of whom was Abu Lubaba.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And others have acknowledged their sins

. They have mixed a good deed with another bad one. Perhaps God will forgive them.” to His statement: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on the expedition to Tabuk, and Abu Lubabah and five others with him stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Abu Lubabah and two other men with him thought and regretted, and were certain of their destruction, and said: “We will be in peace and security with the women, while the Messenger of God and the believers are with him in jihad! By God, we will tie ourselves to the pillars and not release them until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, releases us and excuses us.” So Abu Lubabah set out and tied himself and two other men with him to the pillars of the mosque, and three men remained who did not tie themselves. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from his expedition, and his way was in the mosque, so he passed by them and said: Who are these who tied themselves to the pillars? They said: This is Abu Lubabah and his companions, who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), so they made a covenant with God that they would not release themselves until you were the one to release them and be pleased with them, and they confessed their sins. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: By God, I will not release them until I am ordered to release them, and I will not excuse them until God is the one to excuse them, and they stayed behind from me, and they preferred themselves over fighting the Muslims and jihad against them! So God revealed in His mercy: “
h
And others have acknowledged their sins

. They mixed a righteous deed with another evil. Perhaps God will accept their repentance. Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.” And perhaps from God is obligatory, so when the verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) released them, excused them, and forgave them.

x: Others said: Those who tied themselves to the masts were eight.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam:
m: h
And others acknowledged their sins

. They mixed good deeds with bad ones. Perhaps God will accept their repentance. Indeed, Surat al-Tawbah 9:102 And others have confessed their sins. They have mixed a righteous deed with another evil. Perhaps God will accept their repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. God is Forgiving and Merciful.” He said: They are the eight who tied themselves to the masts, including Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Lubaba.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed, who said:
m: Those who tied themselves to the masts: Hilal, Abu Lubaba, Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Qais.

x: Others said: There were seven.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And others acknowledged their sins

. They mixed a righteous deed with another evil. Perhaps God will forgive them.” He mentioned to us that they were seven men who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. As for four, they mixed a righteous deed with another evil: Jadd bin Qais, Abu Lubabah, Haram, and Aws, and all of them were from the Ansar, and they are the ones about whom it was said: Take from their wealth a charity that will purify them, the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They mixed a good deed with another bad one, he said: They are a group of those who stayed behind from Tabuk, among them Abu Lubaba, and among them Jadd ibn Qays, he repented to them, Qatada said: And they are not three.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And others acknowledged their sins
, he said: They are seven, including Abu Lubaba, they were absent from the Battle of Tabuk, and they are not the three.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, “
h
And others have acknowledged their sins

. They mixed a good deed with another bad one,” “It was revealed about Abu Lubabah and his companions. They stayed behind from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from his battle, and he was close to Madinah, they regretted staying behind from the Messenger of God and said, ‘We will be in the shade and food and women, while the Prophet of God is in jihad and shelter! By God, we will tie ourselves to the pillars, then we will not release them until the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, releases us and excuses us! ’” And they tied themselves up, and three remained who did not tie themselves to the pillars. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from his battle, and passed by the mosque, which was his way, and he saw them, so he asked about them, and it was said to him, Abu Lubabah and his companions, they stayed behind from you, O Prophet of God, and they did to themselves what you see, and they made a covenant with God. That they will not release themselves until you are the one to release them! The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not release them until I am ordered to release them, and I will not excuse them until God excuses them, for they have preferred themselves over fighting the Muslims! Then God revealed:
h
And others have acknowledged their sins
, to Perhaps God will forgive them, and Perhaps is obligatory from God, so the Prophet of God released them and excused them.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse refers specifically to Abu Lubaba, and the sin he confessed to and was forgiven for was what happened to him regarding Banu Qurayza.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
m: h
And others acknowledged their sins
, he said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba, he said to Banu Qurayza what he said.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And others confessed their sins, he said: Abu Lubaba, when he said to Qurayza what he said, pointed to his throat: Muhammad will slaughter you if you submit to the judgment of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And others confessed their sins, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said, if you accept his judgment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Abu Lubaba tied himself to a column and said: I will not absolve myself until God and His Messenger absolve me! He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, absolved him. And this verse was revealed about him:
h
And others have acknowledged their sins
, mixing them with a righteous deed, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And others confessed their sins, he said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Abu Lubaba, because he did not go to Tabuk.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: Al-Zuhri said:
m: “Abu Lubabah was among those who stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. He tied himself to a pole and said: ‘By God, I will not release myself from it, nor will I taste food or drink, until I die or God accepts my repentance!’ So he remained for seven days without tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious. He said: ‘Then God accepted his repentance, and it was said to him: You have accepted your repentance, O Abu Lubabah!’ He said: ‘By God, I will not release myself until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, releases me!’ He said: ‘The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and released him with his hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: ‘O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I leave the home of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I give away all of my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger!’ He said: ‘A third will suffice you, O Abu Lubabah.’”

x: Some of them said: This verse refers to the Bedouins.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And others have acknowledged their sins
. They have mixed a good deed with another bad one.” He said: They are from the Bedouins.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Abi Zainab, he said:
m: I heard Abu Uthman say: There is no verse in the Qur’an that I think is more hopeful for this nation than His statement:
h
And others have acknowledged their sins to
: And God is Forgiving and Merciful.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: This verse was revealed about those who admitted that they had made a mistake in staying behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not fighting with him and going out to conquer the Romans when he set out for Tabuk, and that those about whom this was revealed were a group, one of whom was Abu Lubabah. Rather, we said: This is more correct in that, because God, the Most High, said:
h
And others have acknowledged their sins

, so He informed about the confession of a group of their sins, and the one who confessed his sin, who was tied to the mast during the siege of Qurayzah, was none other than Abu Lubabah alone. So since that was the case, and God, the Most High, described in His statement:
h
And others have acknowledged their sins

, the confession of their sins as a group, it is known that the group that He described with that is not one, so it became clear from that that since this description was only for a group, and there was no group that did that, according to what the people of biography and report transmitted and the people of interpretation agreed upon, except a group of those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, what we said about that is correct.
And we said: Among them was Abu Lubabah, because the authoritative people of interpretation agreed upon that.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, take from the wealth of those who have confessed their sins and repented from them, a charity that purifies them from the filth of their sins, and sanctifies them with it, meaning: and makes them grow and raises them from the lowly ranks of the hypocrites with it, to the ranks of the people of sincerity, and pray for them, meaning: your supplication and seeking forgiveness are reassurance for them, that God has pardoned them and accepted their repentance, and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning: God hears your supplication if you supplicate for them, and other words of His creation, All-Knowing of what you ask for them by your supplication to your Lord for them, and other matters of His servants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “They came with their wealth - meaning Abu Lubaba and his companions - when they were released, and they said: O Messenger of God, this is our wealth, so give it in charity on our behalf, and ask forgiveness for us! He said: I was not commanded to take anything from your wealth! So God revealed: ‘Take from their wealth a charity by which
h
you purify them
and sanctify them,’ meaning by zakat: obedience to God and sincerity, ‘and pray for them,’ meaning: ask forgiveness for them.”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released Abu Lubabah and his two companions, Abu Lubabah and his two companions went with their wealth and brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Take from our wealth and give it in charity on our behalf, and pray for us - they said: Ask forgiveness for us - and purify us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not take anything from it until I am ordered. Then God revealed: ‘Take from their wealth a charity by which
h
you purify them

and cause them to grow, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayers are a reassurance for them. ’ He said: Ask forgiveness for them for the sins they had committed. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a portion of his wealth and gave it in charity on their behalf.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, released Abu Lubaba and those who had tied themselves to the pillars, they said: O Messenger of God, take alms from our wealth to purify us! So God revealed:
h
Take alms from their wealth

to purify them, the verse. Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Ya’qub on the authority of Ja’far on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr who said: Those who had tied themselves to the masts said when he pardoned them: O Prophet of God, purify our wealth! So God revealed:
h
Take alms from their wealth
in order to purify them and sanctify them thereby. And when one of the three fell ill, the other two fell ill as well. Two of them were blind, and the other kept praying until he went blind.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The four: Jadd bin Qais, Abu Lubaba, Haram, and Aws, are those about whom it was said: “
h
Take alms from their wealth

in order to purify them and sanctify them with it, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayers are a reassurance for them.” That is, dignity for them. They had promised themselves that they would spend, strive in jihad, and give in charity.

c: Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj told us, he said,
m: I heard Abu Muadh, he said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, he said, I heard al-Dahhak, he said: “When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released Abu Lubabah and his companions, they came to the Prophet of God with their wealth and said: O Prophet of God, take from our wealth and give it in charity on our behalf, purify us, and pray for us - they said: Ask forgiveness for us - so the Prophet of God said: I will not take anything from your wealth until I am ordered to do so! So God Almighty revealed: ‘Take from their wealth a charity that will purify them’, from the sins they committed, ‘and pray for them’, he said: Ask forgiveness for them. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did what God ordered him to do.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement:
h
Take alms from their wealth
, Abu Lubaba and his companions, and pray for them, he said: Ask forgiveness for them, for the sins they had committed.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: “
h
Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to Surat al-Tawbah 9
h
Take alms from their wealth

in order to purify them and sanctify them thereby, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocations are a comfort to them. And God is Hearing and Knowing. grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them,” he said: These were people from among the hypocrites who had stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. They admitted their hypocrisy and said: O Messenger of God, we have doubted, acted hypocritically and had suspicions, but we must repent again and give charity from our wealth! So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Take from their wealth a charity by which
h
you purify them
and cause them to grow, after He said: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave, (al-Tawbah 9:84). The Arab scholars differed on the reason for raising Tazakihim.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said:
h
You purify them
with it is raised in the beginning, and if you wish, you can make it an attribute of charity, then you bring it as an emphasis, and likewise
h
you purify them

. Some grammarians of Kufa said: If his saying, purifies them, refers to the Prophet, peace be upon him, then the preferred form is to make it jussive, because there is no reference to charity, and purifies them is a new sentence. If charity purifies them
h
and you purify them with it
, then it is permissible to make both verbs jussive and nominative.
The correct statement in this regard is that his saying,
h
You purify them
, is related to charity, because the readings agree on raising it, and that is evidence that it is related to charity. As for his saying,
h
And you purify them with it
, it is a new report, meaning:
h
And you purify them with it
, so that is why it is raised.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement: Indeed, your prayer is a reassurance for them.
Some of them said: May God have mercy on them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Indeed, your prayer is a comfort to them, meaning: mercy for them.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: Your prayer is a dignity for them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Your prayer is a reassurance for them, meaning: dignity for them. There are different readings of this. So the city read it: (Your prayers are a comfort to them) meaning: your supplications. The people of Iraq and some of the Meccans read: Your prayer is a comfort to them, meaning: your supplication.

x: It seems that those who read it with Tawhid saw that reading it with Tawhid is more correct, because in Tawhid there is a meaning of gathering and large number that is not in His statement: (Indeed, your prayers are a reassurance for them), since (the prayers) is a gathering of what is between three and ten in number, not what is more than that. And what they said about that, according to us is as they said, and with Tawhid according to us is the reading, not the reason, because that is more in number than (the prayers), but what is meant by it is the report about the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prayers that they are a reassurance for these people, not the report about the number. And if that is the case, then Tawhid in (the prayer) is more appropriate.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement in this regard is that his saying, You purify them, is related to charity, because the readings agree on raising it, and that is evidence that it is related to charity.
So the city read it: (Your prayers are a comfort to them) meaning: your supplications.

Abu Jaʿfar said: It seems that those who read it with Tawhid saw that reading it with Tawhid is more correct, because in Tawhid there is a meaning of gathering and large number that is not in His statement: (Indeed, your prayers are a reassurance for them), since (the prayers) is a gathering of what is between three and ten in number, not what is more than that.

And what they said about that, according to us is as they said, and with Tawhid according to us is the reading, not the reason, because that is more in number than (the prayers), but what is meant by it is the report about the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prayers that they are a reassurance for these people, not the report about the number.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, the Most Great, with which He informed the believers: that accepting the repentance of the hypocrites who repent, and taking charity from their money if they give it, are not up to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that when the Prophet of God refused to release those who tied themselves to the pillars from those who stayed behind from the conquest, and when he did not accept their charity after God had released them when He had permitted him to do so, he only did that because that was not up to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that that was up to God, the Most High, the Most Great, not Muhammad, and that Muhammad only does what he does of leaving, releasing, taking charity, and other actions of his, by the command of God. Then He, the Most High, said: Do not these people who have stayed behind from jihad with the believers, who have tied themselves to the pillars, who say: “We will not release ourselves until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who releases us,” who ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to take the charity of their money, know that that is not up to Muhammad, but up to God, and that it is God who accepts the repentance of those of His servants who repent or returns it, and takes the charity of those who give charity or returns it to Him, not to Muhammad, so that they direct their repentance and charity to God, and intend thereby His face, not to Muhammad or anyone else, and sincerely repent to Him, and intend Him with their charity, and know that God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful?
He says: The One who turns to His servants to pardon them if they return to His obedience, the Most Merciful to them if they turn to His pleasure from His punishment.
Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: The others said, meaning those who did not repent from those who stayed behind: These, meaning those who repented, were with us yesterday, neither speaking nor sitting with us, so what is wrong with them? Then God said: Indeed, it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities, and indeed, it is God who is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said:
m: A man who used to visit Hammad and would not sit except with him informed me - Shuʿbah said: Al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab said: He is Qatadah, or Ibn Qatadah, a man from Muharrib - he said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn al-Saʿil - who was his neighbor - he said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud say: There is no servant who gives charity except that it falls into the hand of God, and He is the One who places it in the hand of the beggar. And he recited this verse: He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah bin Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Qatada, he said, Abdullah said:
m: Charity falls into the hand of God before it falls into the hand of the beggar. Then he recited this verse: He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Wakiʿ narrated to us, he said: ʿIbad bin Mansur narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Qasim:
m: that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, and He nurtures it for one of you as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel of food becomes like Mount Uhud. Confirmation of that is in the Book of God: ‘He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities,’ and ‘God destroys interest and gives increase for charities.’” (al-Baqarah 2:276) Sulayman ibn Umar ibn al-Aqta’ al-Raqi told us, he said:

c: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: and I do not think that he except raised it, he said: God accepts charity, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: God accepts charity if it is from good things, and He takes it with His right hand. A man gives charity equivalent to a morsel, and God raises it for him as one of you raises his young camel or his foal, and it grows in the palm of God - or he said: in the hand of God - until it becomes like a mountain.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities

? He mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, no man gives charity and it falls into the hand of the beggar until it falls into the hand of God!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And that God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful, meaning: if they are upright.

evidence.text: And he recited this verse: He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.
Then he recited this verse: He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who have confessed their sins to you and who have stayed behind from jihad with you, Work for God in a way that pleases Him, in obeying Him and performing His duties, for God will see your work and so will His Messenger, meaning: God will see your work if you work, and His Messenger and the believers will see it in this world, and you will be returned, on the Day of Resurrection, to the One who knows your secrets and your public affairs, and nothing of your inner and outer affairs is hidden from Him, and He will inform you of what you used to do, meaning: He will tell you what you used to do, what was sincere, what was hypocritical, what was obedience, and what was disobedience to God, and He will reward you for all of that with your reward, the good-doer for his good, and the evil-doer for his evil.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And say, ‘Work, and God will see your work, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers.’ He said: This is a threat.

x: God Almighty says: And among those who stayed behind when you set out to face your enemy, O believers, were others. He raised his statement: Others, in apposition to his statement:
h
And others have confessed their sins

, they mixed good deeds with bad ones. “And others are deferred,” meaning: they are deferring the command and judgment of God. It is said: (I postponed it, I postpone it, and it is postponed), with or without the hamza, and they are two languages with the same meaning. The recitation has been read with both of them. It was said: By these others, he meant a group of people who had stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. They regretted what they had done, and did not apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he arrived, and did not tie themselves to the pillars.
So God postponed their matter until their repentance was valid, so He accepted their repentance and forgave them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Three of them - meaning: those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk - did not tie themselves to the pillars, they were postponed for a week, not knowing whether they would be punished or repentance would be granted to them, so God revealed: God has certainly accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the emigrants until His saying: Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful (al-Tawbah 9:117-118).

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed - meaning His statement: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and sanctify them - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from their wealth - meaning from the wealth of Abu Lubabah and his two companions - and gave it in charity on their behalf. The three who opposed Abu Lubabah remained, and they were not trusted, and were not mentioned in anything, and their excuse was not revealed, and the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for him, and they are the ones about whom God said: “
h
And others are awaiting the command of God

, whether He will punish them or forgive them. And God is Knowing and Wise.” So the people began to say: They are doomed! Since no excuse was revealed for them. And others began to say: Perhaps God will forgive them! So they became deferring to the command of God, until the following was revealed: God has certainly forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship, who went out with him to Syria, “after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.” Then He said: And as for the three who were left behind, meaning those who deferred to the command of God. Repentance was revealed to them, and they were immersed in it. Then He said: Until, when the earth, with all its vastness, became strait for them and their souls became strait for them, until His saying: Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful. (al-Tawbah 9:117-118) Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah,
h
And others are awaiting the command of God
, he said: They are the three who stayed behind.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And others are awaiting the command of God
, he said: Hilal bin Umayya, Murarah bin Rib’i, and Ka’b bin Malik, from the Aws and Khazraj.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And others are awaiting the command of God

, Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn Rib’i, and Ka’b ibn Malik, from the Aws and Khazraj. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. ... He said, Al-Hussein told us, Heshim told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, the same. Al-Husayn narrated that he heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd told us, he heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And others are deferred to the command of God

, they are the three who stayed behind from repenting - meaning: other than Abu Lubabah and his companions - and God did not send down an excuse for them, so the earth became narrow for them despite its vastness. And the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were divided into two groups: A group said: They are doomed! when God did not send down about them what He sent down about Abu Lubabah and his companions. And another group said: Perhaps God will pardon them! And they were deferring to the command of God. Then God sent down His mercy and forgiveness and said: God has already accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhajireen (al-Tawbah 9:117), and He sent down: And about the three who stayed behind (al-Tawbah 9:118), and the verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And others are awaiting the command of God
. He said: We were told that they were the three who were left behind: Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murarah ibn Rabi’ah, a group of the Ansar.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And others are awaiting the command of God
, he said: They are the three who stayed behind.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And others are awaiting the command of God

, either He will punish them or He will forgive them, and they are the three who stayed behind, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, postponed their matter until their repentance from God came to them. As for his statement: Either He punishes them, it means: Either God prevents them from repenting by abandoning them, so He punishes them for the sins they died upon in the Hereafter, or He turns to them in forgiveness, meaning: Or He guides them to repentance so they repent from their sins, so He forgives them, and God is Knowing and Wise, meaning: God is the One with knowledge of their situation and what they will come to in terms of repentance and remaining in sin, Wise, in His management of them and the management of those other than them from among His creation, no flaw enters into His judgment.

evidence.text: The recitation has been read with both of them.

x: God Almighty says:
h
And those who built a mosque to cause harm
, and they are, as mentioned, twelve people from the Ansar.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Az-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada and others. They said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came - meaning from Tabuk - and stopped at Dhu Awan, a town one hour from Madinah. The people of the Masjid Ad-Dhirar had come to him while he was preparing to go to Tabuk. They said: O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for those who are sick and in need, and for rainy nights and wintery nights, and we would like you to come and pray for us in it! He said: I am on the verge of a journey and busy - or something to that effect from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If we had come back, we would have come to you, God willing, and prayed for you in it. When he arrived at Dhi Awan, report of the mosque reached him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn Ad-Dakhshum, the brother of Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn 'Adi - or his brother: Asim ibn 'Adi - the brother of Banu Al-Ajlan, and said: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressing it, and demolish it and burn it!

So they went out quickly until they reached Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the people of Malik ibn Ad-Dakhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: Give me time until I bring you fire from my people! So he entered to his people, took a palm frond, set it on fire, then they went out quickly until they entered the mosque and its people were in it, and they burned it and demolished it, and dispersed from it. And what was revealed about them in the Qur'an was: And those who took a mosque for the purpose of causing harm and disbelief to the end of the story. It was built by twelve men: Khadham bin Khalid, from Banu Ubayd bin Zayd, one of Banu Amr bin Awf, from whose house he brought out the mosque of Al-Shaqaq, and Tha’laba bin Hattab, from Banu Ubayd, who belonged to Banu Umayyah bin Zayd, and Mu’tab bin Qushair, from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, and Abu Habeeba bin Al-Az’ar, from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, and Ibad bin Hanif, the brother of Sahl bin Hanif, from Banu Amr bin Awf, and Jariyah bin Amir, and his two sons: Mujammi bin Jariyah, and Zayd bin Jariyah, and Nabtal bin Al-Harith, who are from Banu Dhubay’ah, and Bahzaj, who belonged to Banu Dhubay’ah, and Bajad bin Othman, who belonged to Banu Dhubay’ah, and Wadi’ah bin Thabit, who belonged to Banu Umayyah, the people of Abu Lubabah bin Abdul Mundhir.

The interpretation of the statement is: And those who built a mosque to harm the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and to disbelieve in God, because they opposed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) thereby, and to divide the believers thereby, so that some of them would pray in it instead of the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and some of them in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), so that they would differ because of that and separate,
h
and as an ambush for those who had fought God and His Messenger before

, meaning: and preparing it for Abu ʿAmir the disbeliever, who opposed God and His Messenger, disbelieved in them, and fought the Messenger of God, before, meaning before they built that mosque. That is because Abu ʿAmir was the one who was the party of the parties - meaning: the party of the parties to fight the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) - and when God abandoned him, he went to the Romans seeking victory from their king over the Prophet of God, and he wrote to the people of the mosque of harm ordering them to build the mosque that they had built, according to what was reported about him, so that he could pray in it, according to what he claimed, when he returned to them.

So they did that. This is the meaning of God Almighty’s saying: And as a watch for those who fought against God and His Messenger before. “And they will swear, ‘We intended only good’,” God Almighty says: And they will swear by its construction, We intended only good, except to be kind to the Muslims, and to benefit and provide for the weak and the sick, and for those who are unable to go to the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray in it, and that is the good deed. And God bears witness that they are liars, in their oath and their saying, We built it only intending good! But they built it intending evil by its construction, to harm the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to disbelieve in God, and to divide the believers, and to lie in wait for Abu Amir the wicked. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who built a mosque to cause harm

, they were people from the Ansar who built a mosque, so Abu Amir said to them: Build your mosque, and prepare whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and I will bring an army from the Romans, and I will expel Muhammad and his companions! So when they finished building their mosque, they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: We have finished building our mosque, so we would like you to pray in it, and invoke blessings upon us! So God revealed about it: “Never stand in it. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy of standing in it” until His saying: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people (al-Tawbah 9:108-109).

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief and to cause division among the believers

, he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, built the mosque of Quba, some men from the Ansar came out, including Bahzaj, the grandfather of ʿAbdullah ibn Hunayf, Wadiʿah ibn Hizam, and Mujammiʿ ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Bahzaj: Woe to you! What did you want to see? He said: O Messenger of God, by God, I only wanted goodness! And he was lying. The Messenger of God believed him and wanted to excuse him, so God revealed: “
h
And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief and to cause division among the believers

and to lie in wait for him who wages war against God and His Messenger,” meaning a man from among them called Abu ʿAmir, who was at war with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had Surat al-Tawbah 9:107 And those who took a mosque as a place of harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as an ambush for those who fought God and His Messenger before - they will surely swear, "We intended only good." And God bears witness that they are liars. gone to Heraclius, so they lay in wait for Abu ʿAmir to come and pray in it, and he had left Medina.” Fighting against God and His Messenger, And they will swear, ‘We intended nothing but good,’ and God bears witness that they are liars.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: And as an ambush for those who fought against God and His Messenger before. He said: Abu Amir the monk went to Caesar, and they said: If he comes to pray in it, they thought that he would prevail over Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And those who have taken a mosque for the purpose of causing harm and disbelief
, he said: the hypocrites, for those who wage war against God and His Messenger, by Abu Amir the monk.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. ... He said, Abu Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Warqaʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And those who have taken a mosque to cause harm and disbelief and division among the believers, he said: It was revealed about the hypocrites. And His statement:
h
And as an ambush for those who had fought God and His Messenger before
, he said: He is Abu ʿAmir the monk.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid bin Amr told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And those who took a mosque out of harm and disbelief, he said: They are Banu Ghanim bin Awf.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief
, he said: They are a tribe called: (Banu Ghanim).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief

, he said: They are a tribe called Banu Ghanim. He said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: And as an ambush for him who wages war against God and His Messenger, Abu Amir the monk, went to Ash-Sham, and those who built the mosque of harm said: We only built it for Abu Amir to pray in it.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who have taken a mosque for the purpose of causing harm

, the verse, some hypocrites deliberately built a mosque in Quba, to imitate the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray in it. It was mentioned to us that he called for his shirt to come to them, until he informed him of that. As for his statement:
h
And as an ambush for those who wage war against God and His Messenger

, there was a man called Abu Amir, who fled from the Muslims and joined the polytheists, so they killed him because of his conversion to Islam. He said: When he came, he prayed in it, so God revealed: Never stand therein, for a mosque founded on righteousness, the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
And those who have taken a mosque for the purpose of causing harm and disbelief
, they are some hypocrites who built a mosque in Quba to cause harm to the Prophet of God and the Muslims,
h
and as an ambush for those who wage war against God and His Messenger

, they used to say, When Abu Amir returns from Caesar of the Romans, he prays in it! And they used to say, “When he returns, he appears before the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as an ambush for those who fought God and His Messenger before, he said: The Quba Mosque, they all used to pray in it, and there was a man from the leaders of the hypocrites called Abu Amir, Abu Hanzala, the one washed by the angels, and Saifi, and Wahq. These three were among the best of the Muslims, so Abu Amir fled, he and Ibn Abd Yalil from Thaqeef, and Alqamah ibn Alathah from Qays, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they joined the ruler of the Romans. As for Alqamah and Ibn Abd Yalil, they returned and pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and converted to Islam. As for Abu Amir, he converted to Christianity and stayed. He said: Some hypocrites built the Mosque of Harm for Abu Amir. They said: Until Abu Amir comes to them and prays in it. They also wanted to create division among the believers, and to separate their congregation because they used to pray together in the Mosque of Quba. They came to deceive the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of God, perhaps a flood will come and cut between us and the valley, and stand between us and the people, and we will pray in our mosque, and when the flood goes away we will pray with them!” He said: And they built it out of hypocrisy. He said: “And their mosque collapsed during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” He said: And the people threw straw and garbage on him, so God revealed:
h
And those who have taken a mosque for harm and disbelief
and division among the believers, so that all the believers would not pray in the Quba Mosque,
h
and as an ambush for those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, on behalf of Abu Amir, and they will swear, ‘We intended nothing but good,’ and God bears witness that they are liars.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Layth,
m: that Shuqaiq did not attend the prayer in the mosque of Banu ʿAmir, so it was said to him: The mosque of Banu so-and-so, they have not prayed yet! He said: I do not like to pray in it, because it was built to cause harm, and every mosque that was built to cause harm, or to show off, or to gain reputation, its origin goes back to the mosque that was built to cause harm.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not stand, O Muhammad, in the mosque that these hypocrites built, to cause harm and division among the believers, and to lie in wait for those who wage war against God and His Messenger. Then God Almighty swore, saying: A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more deserving that you stand in it, you, in it. He means by his saying: It was founded on piety, that its foundation and origin were started on piety and obedience to God. From the first day, that is, its construction began. It is more worthy for you to stand in it, that is, more worthy for you to stand in it praying. It was said that the meaning of his saying: from the first day is the beginning of the first day, just as the Arabs say: I have not seen him since such-and-such day, meaning its beginning, and from the first day means: from the first days, like the saying of the speaker: I met every man, meaning all men.
The people of interpretation differed about the mosque that he meant by his saying:
h
A mosque founded on piety from the first day
Some of them said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which his pulpit and grave are located today.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ubayd God, he said:
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Hurairah sent me to Ibn Umar, to ask him about the mosque that was founded on piety, which mosque is it? The mosque of Medina, or the mosque of Quba? He said: No, the mosque of Medina. ... He said, Al-Qasim bin Amr Al-Anqazi told us, on the authority of Al-Darawardi, on the authority of Uthman bin Ubaid God, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Zaid bin Thabit, and Abu Saeed, who said: The mosque that was founded on piety is the mosque of the Messenger. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Rabia bin Othman, on the authority of Othman bin Ubaid God bin Abi Rafi’, who said: I asked Ibn Omar about the mosque that was founded on piety. He said: It is the mosque of the Messenger. ... He said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Kharijah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Zayd, who said: It is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Kharijah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Zayd, who said: It is the mosque of the Messenger.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saad told us, Hamid Al-Kharrat Al-Madani told us,
m: “I heard Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman say: Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Saeed passed by me, so I said: How did you hear your father say about the mosque that was founded on piety? He said to me: My father said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I entered upon him in the house of one of his wives, and I said: O Messenger of God, which mosque was founded on piety? He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and threw them on the ground, then he said: This is your mosque! I said: Is this how you heard your father say it?”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: The mosque that was founded on piety is the mosque of the greatest Prophet.

c: Humaid bin Mas’adah told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, who said:
m: The mosque that was founded on piety from the first day is the largest mosque in Medina.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, he said,
m: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: the greatest.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: It is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Surat al-Tawbah 9:108 Never stand therein.
h
A mosque founded on piety from the first day
is more worthy for you to stand therein.
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
; and God loves those who purify themselves.
