c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid - he
m: said: I think it was on the authority of his father - he said: The mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was founded on piety.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the Quba Mosque.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
A mosque founded on piety from the first day
, meaning the Quba Mosque.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
A mosque founded on piety from the first day
, meaning the Quba Mosque.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Salih bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, he said:
m: The Quba Mosque, which was founded on piety, was built by the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: The mosque that was founded on piety is the Quba Mosque.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah bin al-Zubayr,
m: those among whom the mosque was built, which was founded on piety, are the sons of Amr bin Awf.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of the authenticity of the report on this from the Messenger of God.
The novel mentioned that:

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us
m: - Abu Kurayb said: Wakee’ narrated to us, and Ibn Wakee’ said: My father narrated to us - on the authority of Rabi’ah ibn Uthman al-Taymi, on the authority of Imran ibn Abi Anas, a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: “Two men differed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the mosque that was founded on piety. One of them said: It is the mosque of the Prophet! The other said: It is the mosque of Quba! So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him, and he said: It is this mosque of mine.” The wording is from the hadith of Abu Kurayb, and the hadith of Sufyan is similar to it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Na’eem told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Aamer Al-Aslami, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d, on the authority of Abu Ka’b:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the mosque that was founded on piety, and he said: This is my mosque.”

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told me: Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: “Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One man said: It is the mosque of Quba!

x: Another said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace! The Messenger of God said: It is this mosque of mine.”

c: Bahr bin Nasr Al-Khawlani told me, he said,
m: it was read to Shu’ayb bin Al-Layth, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: Two men disputed, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Sahbal bin Muhammad bin Abi Yahya told me, he said,
m: I heard my uncle Anis bin Abi Yahya narrating, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mosque that was founded on piety is this mosque of mine, and in it is all good.
b.via: Sahbal bin Muhammad bin Abi Yahya

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Anis, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Safwan bin Isa told us, Anis bin Abi Yahya told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed:
m: “A man from Banu Khudri and a man from Banu Amr bin Awf disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety. Al-Khudri said: It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Awfi said: It is the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is this mosque of mine, and in it is all good.”

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
, and God loves those who purify themselves.

God Almighty says: Among those present at the mosque, which was founded on piety from the first day, are men who love to clean their seats with water when they go to the toilet, and God loves those who purify themselves with water. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hammam ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said:
m: “When the verse: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the purification that God has praised you for? They said: O Messenger of God, we wash away the traces of feces.”

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of Quba: God has praised you well for purification, so what do you do? They said: We wash away the traces of feces and urine.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: “When the verse: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

’ was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O group of Ansar, what is this purification for which God has praised you? They said: We clean ourselves with water when we come from the toilet.”

c: Jabir bin Al-Kurdi told me, he said, Muhammad bin Sabeq told us, he said, Malik bin Mughol told us, on the authority of Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to us and said: ‘Will you not tell me, for God has praised you for purification?’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, we find written in our Torah that one should clean oneself with water.’”

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya ibn Rafi’ told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, who said,
m: I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam narrating more than once, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the people of Quba’, he said: God has praised you for purification with goodness - meaning his statement: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
’ - they said: We find it written with us in the Torah, istinja’ with water.”

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Yahya bin Rafi’ told us, he said, Malik bin Mughul told us, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam - Yahya
m: said: I do not know it except from his father - he said, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of Quba: God has praised you for purification! They said: We find it written for us in the Torah, to clean ourselves with water.” And about it was revealed:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
b.via: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam - Yahya

c: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said, Ismail bin Subaih Al-Yashkari told us, he said, Abu Uwais Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Shurahbil bin Sa’d, on the authority of Uwaim bin Sa’idah,
m: who was one of the people of Badr, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of Quba: I hear that God has praised you for purification, so what is this purification? They said: O Messenger of God, we do not know anything, except that we saw our Jewish neighbors washing their backsides after defecating, so we washed as they did.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amara told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Saeed told us, he said, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Shurahbil ibn Saad, he said:
m: I heard Khuzaymah ibn Thabit say: This verse was revealed:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
, and God loves those who purify themselves. He said: They used to wash their backsides from excrement.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: Some people from Quba used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
, and God loves those who purify themselves.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Shababah bin Suwar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muslim Al-Qari, he said:
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: Should I pour water over my head? - while he is in a state of ihram - he said: Didn’t you hear God say: (Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves)?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Dawud,
m: and Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said, “When the verse: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of Quba’: What is this that God has praised you for? They said: There is not one of us who does not clean himself after relieving himself.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid Al-Madani, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ismail Al-Ansari:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Uwaim bin Sa’idah: What is this that God praised you for: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
, and God loves those who purify themselves’? He said: We are about to wash our anuses with water!”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Katheer, he said:
m: “The hadith of this verse began with men from the Ansar from the people of Quba: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
, and God loves those who purify themselves.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them, and they said: We cleanse ourselves with water.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Asbagh bin Al-Faraj told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, he said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of Uwaim bin Sa’idah, from Banu Amr bin Awf,
m: and Ma’n bin Adi, from Banu Al-Ajlan, and Abu Al-Dahdah. As for Uwaim bin Sa’idah, he is the one who has reached us that “it was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Who are those about whom God said: ‘In them are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves’? The Surat al-Tawbah 9:108 Never stand therein.
h
A mosque founded on piety from the first day
is more worthy for you to stand therein.
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

; and God loves those who purify themselves. Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes, men, among them is Uwaim bin Sa’idah.’ We have not been informed that he named a man among them other than Uwaim.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, he said, Al-Hasan told us:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

, and God loves those who purify themselves,’ the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this that God mentioned to you about purification, and praised you for it? They said: We wash the traces of feces and urine.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, who said,
m: I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam narrating, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina - or he said: The Messenger of God came to us - he said: God has praised you for purification, so will you not tell me? They said: O Messenger of God, we find it written about us in the Torah, to cleanse ourselves with water.” Malik said: He meant his statement:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves

, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them: What is this purification of yours that God mentioned? They said: O Messenger of God, we used to clean ourselves with water during the Age of Ignorance, but when Islam came, we did not abandon it. He said: Do not abandon it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: There were men from the Ansar in the Quba Mosque who would purify their lower parts with water. They would enter the palm trees while the water was running and perform their ablution. So God praised them for that and said:
h
In it are men who love to purify themselves
the verse.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: A group of people from Quba performed ablution with water, so the following verse was revealed about them: In them are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves. It was said: And God loves those who purify themselves, but it is actually: those who purify themselves. However, the ta’ was assimilated into the ta’, so it was made a double ta’, because the point of articulation of one of them is close to the other.

evidence.text: Bahr bin Nasr Al-Khawlani told me, he said, it was read to Shu’ayb bin Al-Layth, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: Two men disputed, and he mentioned something similar.

x: There is a difference in the reading of his statement:
h
Is he who laid the foundation of his building

Some of the people of Medina read it as: Is he who founded his building on piety towards God and His pleasure better than he who founded his building on piety towards God and His pleasure? in a way that did not name the agent in both letters. The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: Is he who founded his building on piety to God and His pleasure better, or he who founded his building? describing whoever as the doer who founded his building.
They are two readings that agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. However, his reading with the verb directed to from, since he was the founder, is more pleasing to me.

The interpretation of the statement then is: Which of these people who built mosques is better, O people, in your view: those who began building their mosque out of fear of God, by obeying Him in building it, performing His obligations, and being pleased with God for building what they built of it, and doing what they did, are better, or those who began building their mosque on the edge of a collapsing cliff? He means by his saying:
h
On the brink of a precipice

, on the edge of a precipice. And the cliff is one of the wells, unless a well is built for it. Har means reckless. It is actually (ha'ir), but it was changed, so its ya was delayed and it was said (har), just as it was said (huwa shaki al-silah), and (sha'ik), and it is more correct than (har yahur fahuwa ha'ir), and it was said: (huwa min har yahar), if it collapsed. And whoever made it from this language said: (hart ya jarf), and whoever made it (from har yahur), said: (hart ya jarf).

This is an example. God Almighty says: Which of these two groups is better? Which of these two buildings is more solid? The one who began the foundation of his building with obedience to God, and knew from him that his building is obedience to God, and God is pleased with him, or the one who began it with hypocrisy and misguidance, and without insight into the correctness of his action or his error, so he does not know when the error of his action and the enormity of his sin will become clear to him, so he demolishes it, just as a building comes on the edge of a well with no one to hold back the water of floods from it or other waters, rich in soil scattered about, and the floods will soon demolish it and scatter it? God Almighty says: Then it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell, meaning: The crumbling cliff with its construction was scattered into the fire of Hell, as: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then it collapsed with him, meaning its foundations, into the fire of Hell.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: So he collapsed with it, meaning: He was proud of it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Is he who founded his building on piety towards God until his statement
: and it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell, he said: By God, he did not stop before falling into the fire. It was mentioned to us that a spot of it was dug out, and smoke was seen from it.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: Banu Amr ibn Awf asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for permission to build it, so he gave them permission. They finished it on Friday, and prayed in it on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. He said: It collapsed on Monday. He said: He had given them three days, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, and it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell, the mosque of the hypocrites. It collapsed before he finished it before he fell into the fire. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that men dug a hole in it, and they saw smoke coming out of it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah Al-Danaaj, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, on the authority of Jabir,
m: regarding his statement: And those who built a mosque to cause harm, he said: I saw smoke coming out of the mosque that was built to cause harm during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Marzouq Al-Basri told us, he said, Abu Salamah told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Abdullah Al-Danaaj, he said, Talq Al-Anzi told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: I saw smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm.

c: Salam bin Salem Al-Khuza'i told me, he said, Khalaf bin Yasin Al-Kufi told us, he said:
m: I performed Hajj with my father at that time - meaning: the time of the Umayyads - and we passed by Madinah, and I saw the Mosque of the Two Qiblas - meaning the Mosque of the Messenger - and in it was the qibla of the Holy House. Then, in the time of Abu Ja'far, they said: The ignorant enters and does not know the qibla! So this building that you see was built by the hand of Badr Al-Samad bin Ali. And I saw the Mosque of the Hypocrites that God mentioned in the Qur'an, and in it was a stone from which smoke was coming out, and today it is a garbage dump. His saying:
h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people

, means: God does not guide to the right path in his actions, whoever builds his building in a place other than its right and proper place, and whoever is a hypocrite who disobeys in his actions the command of God and the command of His Messenger.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: Is he who laid the foundation of his building?

Some of the people of Medina read it as: Is he who founded his building on piety towards God and His pleasure better than he who founded his building on piety towards God and His pleasure? in a way that did not name the agent in both letters.

The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: Is he who founded his building on piety to God and His pleasure better, or he who founded his building? describing whoever as the doer who founded his building.
Abu Jaafar said: They are two readings that agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
However, his reading with the verb directed to from, since he was the founder, is more pleasing to me.

x: God Almighty says: The building of those who built a mosque for harm and disbelief will continue to be doubtful meaning: Their mosque that they built will continue to be doubtful in their hearts meaning: doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts, they think that they were doing good in building it,
h
unless their hearts are cut out

meaning: unless their hearts give charity and they die, and God is Knowing of what these hypocrites who built the mosque of harm are upon, of their doubt in their religion, and what they intended in building it and wanted, and what it will lead to in the Hereafter, and in this life as long as they live, and other than that of their affairs and the affairs of others, Wise in His management of them and the management of all His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their structure which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts
, meaning: suspicion,
h
unless their hearts are cut out
, meaning death.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Doubt in their hearts, he said: doubt in their hearts,
h
unless their hearts are cut out
until they die.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their structure which they have built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts until their hearts are cut out
, meaning: until they die.

c: Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me, he said, Abu Qutaybah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Unless their hearts are cut out
, he said: Unless they die.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Unless their hearts are cut out
, he said: They die.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Unless their hearts are cut out
, he said: They die.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. ... He said, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan: Their structure which they have built will always be a source of doubt in their hearts, they said: doubt in their hearts.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Razi told us, he said, Abu Sinan told us on the authority of Habib:
m: Their structure which they have built will always be a source of doubt in their hearts, he said: anger in their hearts. ... He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Unless their hearts are cut out
, he said: They die. ... He said, Ishaq al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Habib:
h
Unless their hearts are cut out

, unless they die. ... He said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi: Doubt in their hearts. He said: Disbelief. I said: Is Mujammi’ ibn Jariyah an unbeliever? He said: No, but it is a grudge.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Their structure which they have built will always be a source of doubt in their hearts, he said: a grudge in their hearts.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Their structure which they have built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts

, there will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts, and they will be satisfied with what they have done, just as the calf was made beloved by the companions of Moses. And he recited, And they made the calf drink into their hearts because of their disbelief, (al-Baqarah 2:93), he said, its love,
h
unless their hearts are cut out
, he said, that will continue to be in their hearts until they die, meaning the hypocrites.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Doubt in their hearts, he said, doubt. He said, I said: O Abu Imran, do you say this when you have read the Qur’an? It is only a grudge. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
Unless their hearts are cut out

x: Some of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina, Basra and Kufa read it as: except that God cuts their hearts, with a damma on the ta’ of cut, on the basis that halam is the subject, and with the meaning: except that God cuts their hearts.

Some of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it as: Except that their hearts are cut off, with the opening of the ta’ of cut off, on the basis that the verb refers to the hearts. Meaning: Except that their hearts are cut off, then one of the two ta’s was deleted. It was mentioned that Al-Hassan used to recite: Until their hearts are cut out, meaning: until their hearts are cut out. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading it is: Even if their hearts were cut off, and based on that, whoever reads it read: Unless you cut off, with a damma on the ta’.

My opinion on this matter is that the fat-ha on the ta’ and the damma are close in meaning, because hearts do not break when they are broken, except by God breaking them apart, and God does not break them apart except when they are broken apart. They are two well-known readings, and a group of readers have read each one of them, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in his reading. As for reading it: until you cut off, it is a reading that is contrary to the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and I do not see reading it differently from what is in their Qur’ans as permissible.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Unless their hearts are cut out.

Some of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina, Basra and Kufa read it as: except that God cuts their hearts, with a damma on the ta’ of cut, on the basis that halam is the subject, and with the meaning: except that God cuts their hearts.
Some of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it as: Except that their hearts are cut off, with the opening of the ta’ of cut off, on the basis that the verb refers to the hearts.
He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading it is: Even if their hearts were cut off, and based on that, whoever reads it read: Unless you cut off, with a damma on the ta’.
They are two well-known readings, and a group of readers have read each one of them, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in his reading.
As for reading it: until you cut off, it is a reading that is contrary to the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and I do not see reading it differently from what is in their Qur’ans as permissible.

x: The Almighty says: God has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for Paradise, a true promise binding upon Him, meaning: He promised them Paradise, the Most High, a promise binding upon Him to fulfill for them, in His revealed books: the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an, if they fulfilled what they promised God, and fought in His cause and in support of His religion against His enemies, and killed and were killed. And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? The Almighty says: And who is better at fulfilling what he has guaranteed and stipulated than God?

Then rejoice, meaning He says that to the believers: So rejoice, O believers, who have been true to God in what they promised by selling your lives and your wealth for what you sold them to your Lord for, for that is the great success, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, he said:
m: There is no Muslim but that he has a pledge of allegiance to God around his neck, and he fulfilled it or died upon it, in the statement of God: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers to His statement: And that is the great attainment, then He made them sweet and said: The repentant, the worshippers to And give good tidings to the believers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, meaning: in exchange for Paradise. ... He said, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yasar, on the authority of Qatada: that he recited this verse: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. He said: God made them the eighth, so He charged them a high price.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: that he recited this verse: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, he said: He sold them and charged them a high price.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others, they said:
m: “Abdullah bin Rawahah said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Set a condition for your Lord and for yourself as you wish!’ He said: ‘I set a condition for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I set a condition for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your wealth from.’ They said: ‘If we do that, what will we have?’ He said: ‘Paradise!’ They said: ‘Profit in the sale, we do not take a break and we do not ask for a break!’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, God has purchased from the believers,’ the verse.” ... He said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ubaid bin Tufail Al-Absi told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and a man asked him about his statement: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives, the verse, the man said: Shall I not attack the polytheists and fight until I am killed? He said: Woe to you! Where is the condition? Those who repent and worship.
b.via: Muhammad bin Kaʿb Al-Qurazi and others

evidence.text: He said, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yasar, on the authority of Qatada: that he recited this verse: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise.

Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan: that he recited this verse: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, he said: He sold them and charged them a high price.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, God has purchased from the repentant, worshipping believers their lives and their properties. However, He raised it, since it was initiated after another like it was completed. The Arabs do that, and we have already explained that in His statement: Deaf, dumb, blind (al-Baqarah 2:18), which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
The meaning of
h
those who repent
is those who return from what God hates and is angry with to what He loves and is pleased with, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, he said, Al-Hasan said
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
Those who repent
, he said: They repented to God from all sins.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: that he read the repentant, the worshippers, he said: they repented from polytheism, and were innocent of hypocrisy.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, he said:
m: Al-Hasan recited: The repentant, the worshippers, he said: They repented from polytheism and were innocent of hypocrisy.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: h
Those who repent
from polytheism.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan recite this verse:
h
Those who repent
and worship God. Al-Hasan said: They repented, by God, from polytheism and were innocent of hypocrisy.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who repent
. He said: They repented from polytheism, then did not act hypocritically in Islam.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
Those who repent

, he said: Those who repented from sins, then did not return to them. As for his saying: The worshippers, they are those who humble themselves out of fear of God and humility before Him, so they strive to serve Him, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The worshippers are people who took from their bodies during their night and day.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, he said, Al-Hasan said
m: regarding God’s statement: The worshippers, he said: They worshipped God in all their circumstances, in prosperity and adversity.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The worshippers, he said: The worshippers of their Lord. As for his saying: those who praise, they are those who praise God for everything He has tested them with, good and evil, such as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Hamidoon are people who praise God in every situation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Tha’laba, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: Those who praise are those who praise God for all their lives, in good times and bad.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Al-Hamidon, he said: Al-Hamidon for Islam. As for his saying: the travelers, it refers to the fasting people, as:
Muhammad bin Isa al-Damaghani and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the ‘travelers’ and he said: They are the fasting ones.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said, Hakim bin Hizam told us, he said, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Harun, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: The wanderers are the fasting ones.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of al-A’mash,
m: on Surat al-Tawbah 9:112 The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the fast-breakers, the bowers, the prostraters, the enjoiners of what is right and forbidders of what is wrong, and the maintainers of the limits set by God.
h
And give good tidings to the believers
. the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones. ... He said, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, Asim told me, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubaid God told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, he said:
m: Travel is fasting.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father - and Israel, on the authority of Ash’ath - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, he said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Abi Al-Sha’tha’, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, who said: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The travelers, he said: He means by the travelers, the fasting ones.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones. ... He said, Abdullah told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an, He mentioned tourism, they are the fasting ones. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Abu Amr Al-Abdi, who said: The travelers are those believers who fast continuously.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: The travelers are those who fast during the month of Ramadan.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones. ... He said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: Everything in the Qur’an that says the travelers refers to the fasting people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: those who travel, meaning those who fast.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said,
m: Ibn Numayr, Ya’la, and Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’, he said: The travelers are the fasting ones.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: the same. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, who said, Amr told us: And that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Travel was among the Children of Israel, and if a man traveled for forty years, he would see what the travelers before him had seen. Then a prostitute’s son traveled for forty years and did not see anything, so he said: O Lord, what if my parents did evil and I did good? He said: Then I see what the travelers before him had seen. Ibn Uyaynah said: If he abandons food, drink, and women, then he is a traveler.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The travelers are people who took from their bodies, fasting for the sake of God.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The tourism of this nation is fasting. His saying: those who bow and prostrate, means those who pray, those who bow and prostrate in their prayer, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Those who bow and prostrate, he said: the obligatory prayer. As for his saying:
h
Those who enjoin what is right

and forbid what is wrong, it means that they enjoin people to follow the truth in their religions, to follow the right path and guidance, and to act, and they forbid them from evil. This means that they forbid people from every action and word that God has forbidden His servants from.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hassan
m: regarding this matter: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
h
Those who enjoin what is right
means there is no god but God, and those who forbid what is wrong means polytheism.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, he said, Al-Hasan said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who enjoin what is right
, he said: They did not enjoin people to do good until they were among its people, And those who forbid what is wrong, he said: They did not forbid what is wrong until they had stopped doing it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: Everything mentioned in the Qur’an, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, enjoining what is right is a call from polytheism to Islam, and forbidding what is wrong is a prohibition against the worship of idols and devils.

x: We have already demonstrated the correctness of what we said: that enjoining what is right is everything that God or His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has commanded His servants to do, and forbidding what is wrong is everything that God or His Messenger has forbidden His servants to do. Since that is the case, and there is no indication in the verse that it is intended specifically rather than generally, nor is there any report from the Messenger, nor is there any innate intellect, then the generality is more appropriate, as we have explained in more than one place in our books.
As for his saying:
h
And those who preserve the limits of God

, he means: those who perform God’s obligations, who abide by His commands and prohibitions, who do not waste anything that He has obligated them to do, and do not commit anything that He has forbidden them to commit, like the one who:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those who preserve the limits of God
, meaning those who stand up to obey God. And it is a condition that He imposed on the people of jihad, if they fulfill God’s condition and He fulfills their condition for them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those who preserve the limits of God
, he said: Those who stand up for the obedience of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Suhayl, he said, Al-Hasan said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who preserve the limits of God
, he said: Those who uphold the command of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And those who preserve the limits of God
, he said: the obligations of God. As for his saying:
h
And give good tidings to the believers

, it means: And give good tidings to those who believe in what God promised them if they fulfill God’s covenant, that He will fulfill for them what He promised them of admitting them into Paradise, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hudha bin Khalifa told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives, until he concluded the verse. He said: Those who fulfilled their pledge,
h
those who repent

, those who worship, those who praise, until he concluded the verse. He said: This is their work and their conduct in prosperity, then they met the enemy and were true to what they had pledged to God.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And give good tidings to whoever does these actions - meaning his saying:
h
those who repent
and worship, to the end of the verse - even if they do not fight.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And give good tidings to the believers
, he said: those who did not fight.

evidence.text: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, he said: I heard Al-Hasan recite this verse: Those who repent and worship God.

x: God Almighty says: It was not appropriate for the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed in him, to seek forgiveness, meaning: to ask for forgiveness for the polytheists, even if the polytheists for whom they sought forgiveness were relatives, after it had become clear to them that they were companions of Hellfire, meaning: after they died in their polytheism and idol worship, and it had become clear to them that they were among the people of Hellfire, because God had decreed that no polytheist would be forgiven, so it was not appropriate for them to ask their Lord to do what they knew He would not do. If they say: So Abraham sought forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist? Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. So when it became clear to him and he knew that he was an enemy of God, he left him and abandoned him, and stopped seeking forgiveness for him, and preferred God and His command over him, so he disowned him when his command became clear to him.
The interpreters differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed regarding Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to seek forgiveness for him after his death, but God forbade him from doing so.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said:
m: “When Abu Talib was on his deathbed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon him and Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, and said: ‘O uncle, say: There is no god but God, a word with which I can argue for you before God!’ Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya said to him: ‘O Abu Talib, do you turn away from the religion of Abdul Muttalib?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will seek forgiveness for you as long Surat al-Tawbah 9:113
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists
, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. as I am not forbidden from doing so!’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists
,’ and the verse was revealed: ‘Indeed, you do not guide whom you love,’ (al-Qasas 28:56).”

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, he said, my uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said, Saeed ibn al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: “When Abu Talib was about to die, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and found Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughira with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O uncle, say: There is no god but God, a word that I will bear witness for you with before God!’ Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: ‘O Abu Talib, do you reject the religion of Abdul Muttalib?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept presenting it to him and repeating that statement to him, until Abu Talib said the last thing he said to them: ‘He is on the religion of Abdul Muttalib,’ and he refused to say: ‘There is no god but God.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By God, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so!’ Then God revealed: ‘
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

,’ and God revealed about Abu Talib, so he said to the Messenger of God: ‘Indeed, you do not You guide whom you love. Verse (al-Qasas 28:56) Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: “
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

,” he said: The believers say: Should we not ask forgiveness for our fathers, when Abraham asked forgiveness for his father when he was an unbeliever? So God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him, the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Abraham sought forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, and I will continue to seek forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from him!’ His companions said: ‘We will seek forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sought forgiveness for his uncle!’ So God revealed: ‘
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

,’ until His saying: ‘He disavows him.’” Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Yazid ibn Harun narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab who said: “When Abu Talib was about to die, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and with him were Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O uncle, you are the person with the greatest right over me, and the best of them in my hand, and you have a greater right over me than my father. So say a word that will make intercession for me obligatory on the Day of Resurrection. Say: There is no god but God.’” Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd Al-A’la on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thawr.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed regarding the mother of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was because he wanted to seek forgiveness for her, but he was prevented from doing so.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah, who said:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Mecca, he stood at his mother’s grave until the sun became hot on him, hoping that he would be given permission to ask forgiveness for her, until this was revealed: ‘
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

, even if they were relatives,’ until His saying: ‘He disavows him.’” ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a place, and I think he said: A grave. So he sat down next to it and began to address it, then he said, weeping, so I said: O Messenger of God, we have seen what you have done! He said: I asked my Lord for permission to visit my mother’s grave, and He gave me permission, and I asked Him for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but He did not give me permission. So he was never seen weeping more than that day.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It was not for the Prophet and those who believed

, to: that they are companions of Hellfire, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to seek forgiveness for his mother, but God forbade him from doing so, so he said: And Abraham, the friend of God, sought forgiveness for his father! So God revealed: It was not for Abraham’s seeking forgiveness, to: for he was compassionate and forbearing.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed because some people of faith were asking forgiveness for their dead polytheists, so they were forbidden from doing so.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

, the verse. So they used to ask forgiveness for them until this verse was revealed. When it was revealed, they stopped asking forgiveness for their dead, and it did not forbid them from asking forgiveness for the living until they died. Then God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him, the verse.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

, the verse, “It was mentioned to us that some men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Prophet of God, there were among our fathers those who treated neighbors well, maintained family ties, freed the captives, and fulfilled their obligations. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?” He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes! By God, I will ask forgiveness for my father, just as Abraham asked forgiveness for his father! God then revealed:
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

, until he reached Hellfire. Then God excused Abraham, saying: “And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him.” He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God said: Words were revealed to me and they entered my ears and settled in my heart: I have been commanded not to ask forgiveness for one who died a polytheist. Whoever gives excess of his wealth, it is better for him, and whoever withholds, it is worse for him. And do not…” Blame God for the lack of it. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of his saying:
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is: It was not for them to seek forgiveness, and likewise the meaning of His statement:
h
And it is not for a soul to believe
h
and it is not for a soul to believe
, except by permission of God
r

. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Its meaning is: It was not appropriate for them to ask forgiveness for them. He said: And likewise when (an) comes with (kan), then all of them have the interpretation of: it should, It is not for a prophet to take spoils
r
(Al Imran 3:161)
, it was not appropriate for him, this is not from his morals. He said: That is why (an) was used to indicate the future, because (yanbaghi) requests the future.
As for his saying:
h
And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him
, the scholars differed regarding the reason for which it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions used to seek forgiveness for their dead polytheists, thinking that Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, had done that, when God revealed His words, reporting on Abraham:
“He said, ‘Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He has been to me ever Gracious.’”
We mentioned the narration from some of those we attended, and we will mention from those who did not mention it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Khalil, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists. I said: Can a man ask forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists? He said: Did not Abraham ask forgiveness for his father? He said: So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness was not until
h
he disassociated himself from him

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Ali:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek forgiveness for his parents while they were polytheists, until the following verse was revealed:
h
And it was not Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father
, until His saying:
h
He disassociated himself from him

. It was said: And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise, meaning: except after a promise, just as one says: This matter was only because of such-and-such a reason, meaning: after that reason, or because of it. So too is his saying: except because of a promise, because of a promise and after it.

x: Some people have interpreted the words of God: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, the verse, as meaning that God forbade asking forgiveness for the polytheists after their death, because He said: After it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. They said: No one can know that except by dying in disbelief. As for when he is alive, there is no way to know that, so the believers may ask forgiveness for them.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Umar al-Raqi narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of al-Shaibani, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: A Jewish man died and he had a Muslim son, but he did not go out with him. This was mentioned to Ibn Abbas, who said: He should have walked with him and buried him, and prayed for his well-being as long as he was alive, but when he died, he left him to his own affairs! Then he said: “
h
And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him

,” he did not pray. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Fadil narrated, on the authority of Dhirar ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: A Christian man died, and his son entrusted him to the people of his religion. So I went to Ibn Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: What would have happened if he had walked with him, protected him, and asked forgiveness for him? Then he recited: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him, the verse.

x: Others interpreted repentance in this context to mean prayer.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Kathir bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Burqan, he said, Habib bin Abi Marzuq told us, on the authority of ʿAta’ bin Abi Rabah, he said:
m: I would not neglect praying for anyone from the people of this qiblah, even if she were an Ethiopian woman pregnant from fornication, because I have not heard God withhold prayer from anyone except the polytheists. God says: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.

x: Others interpreted it to mean seeking forgiveness, which is a supplication.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Asma bin Zamil, on the authority of his Surat al-Tawbah 9:
m: 114 And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him

. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. father, he said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: May God have mercy on a man who seeks forgiveness for Abu Hurairah and his mother. I said: And for his father? He said: No, for my father died as a polytheist.

x: We have shown that the meaning of seeking forgiveness is the servant’s asking his Lord to forgive sins. Since that is the case, and the servant’s asking his Lord for that may be during prayer or otherwise, neither of the two opinions that we have mentioned is invalid, because God has made it general in forbidding seeking forgiveness for the polytheist, after it has become clear to him that he is one of the people of Hell, and He has not specified a specific situation in which seeking forgiveness for him is permissible. As for his saying: After it became clear to them that they are the people of Hellfire, its meaning is what I have explained, that is: after they knew that he died as a disbeliever and that he was one of the people of Hellfire. It was said: The people of Hell, because they are its inhabitants and its people who are in it, just as it is said to the inhabitants of a house: These are the people of this house, meaning: its inhabitants.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: After it became clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire, he said: It became clear to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when Abu Talib died, repentance had ceased for him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It became clear to him when he died, and he knew that repentance had been cut off from him, meaning in his statement: after it became clear to them that they were companions of Hellfire.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement:
h
It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists (al-Ma’idah 5
:72), saying: If they die as polytheists, God says: Indeed, whoever associates others with God - God has forbidden him Paradise (al-Ma’idah 5:72).

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
, he disavowed him.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: When it became clear to him that he had died as a polytheist, he disavowed him and stopped asking forgiveness for him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died,
h
but when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
, he disavowed him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died, and when he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died, but when he died, he did not seek forgiveness for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him
,” meaning: He sought forgiveness for him while he was alive, but when he died, he stopped seeking forgiveness for him.

c: Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me, he said, Abu Asim and Abu Qutaybah Muslim bin Qutaybah told us, they said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him
, he said: When he died.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he said: His death while he was an unbeliever.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. ... He said, Ibn Abi Ghania told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam: When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him, he said, when he died and did not believe.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar:
m: When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him, his death while he was an unbeliever. ... He said, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him
, he said: When he died.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, when he died in his polytheism, he disavowed him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And it was not Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father
, that Abraham, may God’s prayers be upon him, hoped that his father would believe as long as he was alive, but when he died in his polytheism, he disavowed him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him, he said: His death while he was an unbeliever.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died. Then, when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he did not seek forgiveness for him. ... He said, Abu Ahmad told us, Abu Israel said, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he said: So when he died.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: When it becomes clear to him in the Hereafter. This is because his father clings to him when he wants to cross the bridge, and he passes by him, until when he is about to cross it, Abraham turns around and sees his father in the form of a monkey or a hyena, so he lets go of him and disowns him at that time.
Who said that?

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, Abdullah bin Sulaiman told us:
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: Abraham will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Lord of my parents, Lord of my parents! And when it is the third time, he will take his hand, turn to him while he is a hyena, and disown him. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair who said: You will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on one plain, hearing the caller and seeing with your eyesight. He said: Hell will roar and there will not remain a close angel or a sent prophet except that he will fall on his knees, his limbs trembling! He said: I thought it was saying: Myself, myself! And the bridge will be struck over Hell like the edge of a sword, a slippery slope, and on its sides are angels with hooks like the thorns of the Sa’dan tree. He said: They will pass like lightning, like the wind, like birds, like the best riders, like the best men, and the angels will say: O Lord, save, save! Some will be safe and some will be scratched and some will be crushed in the Fire. Then Ibrahim will say to his father: I used to command you in the world and you disobeyed me, but I will not leave you alone today, so take hold of my waist! So he will take hold of his flanks and he will be transformed into a hyena, and when he sees it transformed, he will disown him.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of God, which is His account of Abraham, that when it became clear that his father was an enemy of God, he disavowed him, and that was when he knew and was certain that he was an enemy of God, and he was a polytheist towards Him, and that was when he died in his polytheism.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing.
The people of interpretation differed regarding al-Awah.
Some of them said: It is a supplication.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Al-Awah means supplication.

c: Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Al-Awah means supplication.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah about al-Awah, and he said: It is supplication.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. ... He said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Al-Awah means supplication. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, the same.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan and Israel told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us:
m: I was told on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, he Surat al-Tawbah 9:114 And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him
. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. said: Al-Awah is supplication.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair Al-Laithi, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Al-Awah is supplication.

x: Others said: Rather, He is the Most Merciful.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, he said:
m: Abdullah was asked about al-Awah, and he said: The Most Merciful.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, he said:
m: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrating, on the authority of Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, a blind man: that he asked ʿAbdullah about al-Awah, and he said: the Most Merciful.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, and Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn: that he asked Ibn Mas’ud and said: What is Al-Awwah? He said: The Most Merciful.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn:
m: That he came to Abdullah - and he was blind - and said: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, who do we ask if we do not ask you? Ibn Masoud seemed to feel sorry for him, he said: Tell me about Al-Awwah? He said: The Most Merciful.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah about al-Awwah, and he said: He is the Most Merciful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, he said,
m: Abu Al-Ubaydayn came to Abdullah and said to him: What do you need? He said: What is Al-Awwah? He said: The Most Merciful. ... He said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, a man from Banu Sawa’ah, who said: A man came to Abdullah and asked him about Al-Awah, so Abdullah said to him: Al-Raheem.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi and Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Al-Awah means the Most Merciful.

c: Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Al-Jazzar:
m: That Abu Al-Ubaydayn, a man from Banu Namir - Yaqub said: He was blind, and Ibn Wakee’ said: He was visually impaired - asked Ibn Mas’ud and said: What is Al-Awwah? He said: The Most Merciful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said:
m: Al-Awah means the Most Merciful. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: He is the Most Merciful.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: We were told that Al-Awah is the Most Merciful.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate, he said: merciful. Abdul Karim Al-Jazari said, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, something similar.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The Most Merciful means the Most Compassionate.
