c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn:
m: that he asked Abdullah about al-Awah and he said: al-Raheem. ... He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, who said: The Most Merciful means the Most Compassionate.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The most compassionate is the one who is merciful to the servants of God. ... He said, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Khaithama Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, who said: Al-Awah means the Merciful, in the Ethiopian dialect.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the certainty.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The one who has faith is the one who is certain.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Mubarak, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-Awah means the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia. ... He said, Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Hassan, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Awah means the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said,
m: I heard Sufyan say: The one who has faith is the one who is certain.

x: Some of them said: the one who is certain of the jurist.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Al-Awah means the one who is certain, in the language of Abyssinia.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: It is the certainty, in the language of Abyssinia. ... He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The one who has piety is the one who is certain.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The one who has faith is the one who is certain. ... He said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one who has faith is the one who is certain.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Awwah means certain.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: (Awwah), he said: Trustworthy and certain.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing, he said: The most compassionate means the one who is certain.

x: Others said: It is an Abyssinian word that means believer.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The most compassionate and forbearing, he said: The most compassionate is the believer, in Ethiopian.

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, Abraham was a most merciful one, meaning: the believing, repentant one.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hassan bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The one who has piety is the believer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Al-Awah means the believer, in Ethiopian.

x: Others said: He is the one who glorifies God and remembers Him a lot.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed, he said:
m: Al-Awah means the glorifier.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Yanaq:
m: “A man used to mention God often and glorify Him, so he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: He is a penitent.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, who said:
m: The one who is most devout is the one who remembers God a lot.

x: Others said: He is the one who recites the Qur’an a lot. Mention who said that.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried a dead person and said: May God have mercy on you, you were indeed a recitation of the Qur’an.”

x: Others said: It is from groaning.
Who said that?

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Yunus al-Qushayri, on the authority of a storyteller
m: who was in Mecca, “A man was performing the circumambulation and he kept saying: Surat al-Tawbah 9:114 And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him
. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. ‘Oh!’ Abu Dharr complained about him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Leave him, he is a groaner!’”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakee’ narrated to us, and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Yunus al-Bahili, who said:
m: “I heard a man in Mecca who was originally Roman, narrating on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: ‘A man used to circumambulate the House and say in his supplication: “Oh! Oh!” So he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: He is a groaner!’” Abu Kurayb added in his hadith, saying: “So I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burying that man at night, and he had a lamp with him.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Sulayman, he said, Abu Imran told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabah, on the authority of Ka’b, he said:
m: Awwah, when he mentions the Fire, he says: Awwah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Samad Al-Ami told us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabah, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: Whenever he mentioned the Fire, he would say: Oh.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman, he said, Abu Imran told us, he said,
m: I heard Abdullah ibn Rabah al-Ansari say, I heard Kaʿb say: Indeed, Abraham was a woeful one, he said: When the Fire was mentioned, he said: Woeful from the Fire.

x: Others said: It means that he is a jurist.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Indeed, Abraham was a man of compassion, he said: A jurist.

x: Others said: He is the humble supplicant.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abdul Hamid bin Bahram told us, he said, Shahr bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad, he said:
m: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, a man said: O Messenger of God, what is ‘awwah’? He said: The one who is humble. He said: ‘Indeed, Abraham was humble and forbearing.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The one who is humble and supplicant’.”

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of Abdullah bin Masoud, which was narrated by Zur: that it is a supplication. Rather, we said that this is more correct, because God mentioned it and described His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, with it, after describing him with supplication and seeking forgiveness for his father, saying: “
h
And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him
h
But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God
h
he disassociated himself from him

,” and he stopped supplicating and seeking forgiveness for him. Then He said: Abraham was a supplicant to his Lord, complaining to Him. He was forbearing towards those who insulted him and caused him harm. That is because, peace be upon him, he promised his father to seek forgiveness for him, and to supplicate to God for forgiveness for him, when his father threatened him and threatened to curse him, after he rejected his advice in God and said: “Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham?
If you do not desist, I will surely stone you. So leave me for a long time,” so he said to him, peace be upon him,

“Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever Gracious to me. And I will leave you and what you invoke besides God and supplicate to my Lord. Perhaps I will not be, in my invocation of my Lord, unhappy.”

He fulfilled his father’s request for forgiveness for him, until it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God. God described him as a supplicant to his Lord, forbearing towards those who were foolish towards him. Its origin is from ta’awwah, which means supplication and asking with sadness and compassion, as narrated by Abdullah bin Shaddad, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as narrated by Uqbah bin Amir, the story he told me: Yahya bin Othman bin Saleh Al-Sahmi said, my father told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Al-Harith bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir: that he said to a man called Dhu Al-Bijadayn: He is a penitent!

That is because he was a man who used to do that a lot with the Qur’an and supplication, and he would raise his voice. Therefore, it is said to someone suffering from pain or illness: Do not groan, as Al-Muthaqab Al-Abdi said: If I leave her at night, she will groan, oh, the sad man And from it is the saying of Al-Ja’di: The souls of the spirits follow the paper after they marry, complaining, groaning and bullying Arabs hardly pronounce it as faʿala yafʿulu, but rather they say tafʿala yatafʿulu, such as taʿawah yatawah, wawah yawawah.
The shepherd groaned and his dogs made noise They also said: Oh, you!

i: Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu Al-Jarrah recited to him: Oh, the memory when I remember it, and after that there is land and sky between us He said:
x: And perhaps he recited to us: Faw min al-Dhikr without it, and if fa’al had come from it according to the original, it would have been: Ah, yawwah, ohhan.
Because the meaning of this is: to be in pain, to be sad, and to supplicate, the people of interpretation differed about it in the difference that I mentioned.
Those who said that it means mercy said: That was from Abraham out of compassion for his father, and mercy for him and for other people.
Others said: This was due to his sound faith, his good knowledge of God’s greatness, and his humility towards Him.
Others said: It was because of the soundness of his faith in his Lord.
Others said: This was done by him when he recited the revelation of God that He sent down to him.

Others said: This was done by him when he remembered his Lord. All of this goes back to what I said, and the meaning of some of it is close to some, because the sad person who is supplicating to his Lord, and humble before Him in his heart, this happens to him when he asks his Lord, and calls upon Him for his needs, and these characteristics befall him to which the commentators directed the interpretation of God’s statement: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing.

evidence.text: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried a dead person and said: May God have mercy on you, you were indeed a recitation of the Qur’an.”

x: God Almighty says: And God would not have decreed that you, in your seeking forgiveness for your dead polytheists, were misguided, after He had granted you guidance and enabled you to believe in Him and His Messenger, until He had presented to you a prohibition against it, and you had abandoned it. But before He made clear to you the abhorrence of that by forbidding it, and then you transgressed His prohibition to what He forbade you from, then He does not judge you to be astray, because obedience and disobedience only come from the one who is commanded and the one who is forbidden. As for the one who is not commanded and is not forbidden, then he is not obedient or disobedient in what he is not commanded and is not forbidden from. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things. The Most High says: Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what was mixed up in your souls when God forbade you from seeking forgiveness for your dead polytheists, from impatience over what you had previously sought forgiveness for them before He had preceded you with the prohibition of it, and other than that of the secrets of your affairs and the affairs of His servants and their outward appearances, so He made clear to you His patience in that upon you, so that He may remove from you the burden of sorrow thereby.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: To mislead a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid, he said: God’s clarification to the believers in seeking forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and in His clarification of His obedience and disobedience in general, so do it or leave it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And God would not mislead a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid

. He said: God’s clarification to the believers: that they should not ask forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and in His clarification is His obedience and disobedience in general, so do it or leave it. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not mislead a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid
, he said: God makes clear to the believers that they should not seek forgiveness for the polytheists, in His clarification, in His obedience and in His disobedience, so do it or leave it.

x: God Almighty says: God, O people, has the authority and dominion over the heavens and the earth, and over all the kings below Him. His slaves and servants, their life and death are in His hand. He gives life to whomever He wills of them, and causes death to whomever He wills of them. So do not be afraid, O believers, of fighting those kings who disbelieve in Me, whether they are the kings of Rome, or the kings of Persia and Abyssinia, or others. Invade them and strive against them in My obedience, for I am the One who honors whomever I will of them and of you, and the One who humiliates whomever I will. This is an exhortation from God, the Most High, to the believers to fight every Mamluk who disbelieved in Him, as an enticement from Him to wage war against them. And His statement: And you have no protector or helper besides God, meaning: You have no one who is your ally besides God to support you against Him, if you disobey the command of God and He punishes you for disobeying His command, to rescue you from His punishment, nor a helper, to support you from Him if He intends evil for you. He says: So trust in God, fear Him, and strive in His cause against those who disbelieve in Him, for He has purchased from you your lives and your properties in exchange for Paradise, you fight in His cause, killing and being killed.

The Most High says: God has granted repentance to His command and obedience, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the emigrants from their homes and their clan to the abode of Islam, and to the supporters of His Messenger in God, who followed the Messenger of God in the hour of hardship among them in terms of provision, back-up, provisions and water, after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated, meaning: after the hearts of some of them had almost turned away from the truth, and doubted his religion and suspected what he had suffered of hardship and difficulty in his travel and conquest, then He turned to them in forgiveness, meaning: then He, may His praise be glorified, granted them repentance and returning to steadfastness in His religion, and seeing the truth that had almost become confused for them, He is to them Kind and Merciful, meaning: Your Lord is Kind to those whose hearts were mixed with that because of the hardship and difficulty that befell them in their travel, Merciful that He should not destroy them, and remove faith from them, after They did not do what they did for God as they did for His Messenger, and they endured hardship and distress with him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: In the hour of hardship, in the Battle of Tabuk.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil:
m: In the hour of hardship, he said: They went out on a raid, two men and three on a camel. They went out in intense heat, and they were afflicted with severe thirst that day, so they began to slaughter their camels and squeeze their bellies and drink their water, and that was a time of hardship in terms of water, hardship in terms of back support, and hardship in terms of expenses.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The hour of hardship, he said: The Battle of Tabuk. He said: The hardship, they were afflicted with severe hardship, to the point that two men would split a date between them, and they would suck a single date and drink water with it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Those who followed him in the hour of hardship, he said: the Battle of Tabuk. ... He said, Zakariya bin Adi told us, on the authority of Ibn Mubarak, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, on the authority of Jabir: Those who followed him in the hour of hardship, he said: hardship of the afternoon, hardship of provisions, and hardship of water.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship

, the verse, those who followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk before the Levant in the blazing heat, despite what God knows of the hardship, they were afflicted with severe hardship in it, to the point that it was mentioned to us that two men would split a date between them, and the group would take the date between them, one would suck it and then drink from it, then another would suck it and then drink from it, so God accepted their forgiveness and returned them from their battle.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Utbah ibn Abi Utbah, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas:
m: It was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, about hardship, “Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Tabuk in intense heat, and we stopped at a Surat al-Tawbah 9:117 God has already accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him during the time of hardship after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Then He accepted their repentance. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful. place where we were afflicted with thirst, to the point that we thought our necks would be severed, to the point that a man would go looking for water, and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, to the point that a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its dung and drink it, and put what was left on his liver. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, God has accustomed you to goodness in supplication, so supplicate for us! He said: Do you like that? He said: Yes! So he raised his hands, and did not bring them back until the sky spoke, and it shaded, then it poured, and they filled what they had with them, then we went to look but did not find it had passed the army.”

c: Ishaq bin Ziyadah Al-Attar told me, he said: Yaqub bin Muhammad told us, he said: Abdullah bin Wahb told us, he said: Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Nafi bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It was said to Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him: Tell us about the matter of the Army of Difficulty! Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he mentioned something similar.

x: God Almighty says: God has forgiven the Prophet, the Muhajireen, and the Ansar, “and the three who stayed behind,” and these three whom God described in this verse with what He described them with in what was said, are the others about whom God Almighty said: “
h
And others are awaiting the command of God

, whether He will punish them or forgive them. And God is Knowing and Wise” (al-Tawbah 9:106), so He Almighty accepted their repentance and was gracious to them. The mention of those who said this from the people of interpretation has already been made, so it is unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

The interpretation of the statement then is: God has accepted the repentance of the three whom God left behind from repentance, so He has postponed them from those whom He accepted from among those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as: - Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of someone
m: who heard Ikrimah regarding his statement:
h
And as for the three who stayed behind
, he said:
h
They stayed behind
from repenting.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: As for his saying:
h
They stayed behind
h
they stayed behind

from repentance. Until when the earth, with all its vastness, became strait for them, meaning: with its vastness, out of grief and regret for their failure to fight with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their souls became strait for them, because of the anguish and distress that befell them as a result, and they thought that there was no refuge, meaning: and they were certain in their hearts that they had nothing to turn to because of the affliction that had befallen them from God’s command, because of their failure to oppose the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that would save them from His distress, nor from what they feared of God’s punishment, except God. Then He granted them repentance to His obedience, and returning to what pleases Him about them, so that they would repent to Him, and return to His obedience and abide by His commands and prohibitions, Indeed, God is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful, meaning: God is the Giver of repentance to His servants, the One who guides those whom He loves to guide among them to what pleases Him, the Most Merciful, with them, that He does not punish them after repentance, or let down those among them who wanted to repent and return but did not accept their repentance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And as for the three who were left behind
, he said: Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murarah ibn Rabi’ah, and all of them were from the Ansar.

c: Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Warraq told me, he said: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said: And Murarah bin Al-Rabi’, or: Ibn Rabi’ah, Abu Usamah was not sure.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Amer:
m: h
And as for the three who were left behind
, they said: They were postponed, in the middle of (Bara’ah).

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The three who were left behind, he said: Those who were postponed in the middle of (Bara’ah), his statement:
h
And others are awaiting the command of God
, (al-Tawbah 9:106), Hilal bin Umayya, Murarah bin Rib’i, and Ka’b bin Malik.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And upon the three who were left behind, those who were postponed in the middle of (Bara’ah).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the three who were left behind

, he said: They were all from the Ansar, Hilal ibn Umayya, Murarah ibn Rabi’ah, and Ka’b ibn Malik. ... He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the Surat al-Tawbah 9:118
h
And as for the three who were left behind
, until the earth, vast as it is, became strait for them and their souls became strait for them and they were certain that there is no refuge from God except in Him.
h
Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent
. Indeed, God is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful. authority of Mujahid:
h
And as for the three who were left behind

, he said: those who were postponed. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Yaʿqub, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, who said: The three who were left behind were Kaʿb ibn Malik, who was a poet, Murarah ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya, and all of them were Ansar. ... He said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar and al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, it is said: All of them are from the Ansar: Hilal ibn Umayya, Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and Ka’b ibn Malik.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hashim told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the three who were left behind
, he said: Hilal bin Umayya, Ka’b bin Malik, and Murarah bin Al-Rabi’, all of them from the Ansar.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And as for the three who stayed behind
, until his saying: “
h
Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent

. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful,” Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn Rabi’ah, stayed behind in the Battle of Tabuk. “It was mentioned to us that Ka’b ibn Malik tied himself to a pillar and said: I will not release it, nor will I release myself, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, releases me! The Messenger of God said: By God, I will not release him until his Lord releases him if He wills! As for the other, he had stayed behind on a wall of his that he had reached, so he made it into charity in the way of God, and he said: By God, I will not feed him! As for the other, he rode through the deserts following the Messenger of God, one land raising him and another lowering him, and his feet were dripping with blood.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said:
m: The three who were left behind are Hilal ibn Umayya, Ka’b ibn Malik, and Murarah ibn Rabi’ah. ... He said, Abu Dawud al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Salam Abi al-Ahwas, on the authority of Saeed bin Masruq, on the authority of Ikrimah: And upon the three who were left behind, he said: Hilal bin Umayya, Murarah, and Ka’b bin Malik.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, he said: Kaab ibn Malik said:
m: I have never been in a campaign that was easier for my back and expenses than I was in that campaign! Kaab ibn Malik said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out, I said: I will get ready tomorrow and then join him. So I started preparing my equipment, and I spent the evening without finishing. Then on the third day, I started preparing my equipment, and I spent the evening without finishing. Then I said: No way! The people walked for three days! So I stayed. Then when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived, the people began to apologize to him, so I came and stood in front of him and said: I have never been in a campaign that was easier for my back and expenses than I was in this campaign! But the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned away from me, and he ordered the people to speak to us, and I ordered our women to move away from us. He said: So I climbed over a wall one day, and there I saw Jabir ibn Abdullah, so I said: O Jabir! I ask you by God, have you ever known me to have deceived God and His Messenger? He kept quiet and would not speak to me. Then one day, while I was on the pass, I heard a man saying: Kaab! Kaab! Until he came close to me and said: Give Kaab the good report.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on the Tabuk expedition, intending to attack the Romans and the Arab Christians in the Levant, until he reached Tabuk, where he stayed for a few nights, and the delegation of Adhruh and the delegation of Aylah met him there, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them on the basis of the jizya, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Tabuk and did not go beyond it, and God revealed: God has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship 10:13, and the three who stayed behind were a group, including: Ka’b ibn Malik, who was one of Banu Salamah, Murarah ibn Rabi’ah, who was one of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and Hilal ibn Umayyah, who was from Banu Waqif, and
h
they stayed behind

from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that expedition with eighty-some men. When the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) returned to Medina, those people believed him in their story and confessed their sins, while the rest of them lied. They swore to the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him): Nothing kept them back except an excuse. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) accepted it from them and pledged allegiance to them, and entrusted their secrets to God. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) forbade the speech of those who stayed behind, and said to them when they told him their story and confessed their sins: You have spoken the truth, so stand up until God judges you. When God revealed the Qur'an, He accepted the repentance of the three, and said to the others: They will swear to you by God when you return to them to turn away from them, until he reached:
h
He is not pleased with the wicked people

(al-Tawbah 9:95-96). Ibn Shihab said: Abdur-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik informed me that Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik - who was Kaab's leader from his sons when he went blind - said: I heard Kaab bin Malik narrating his story when he stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. Kaab said: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any battle he fought, except the Battle of Tabuk, except for the Battle of Badr, and he did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from it. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until God gathered them and their enemy without an appointment. I was present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Al-Aqabah, when we pledged to Islam, and I would not have liked to have witnessed Badr in it, even though Badr is more famous among the people than it. My story when I stayed behind from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Battle of Tabuk was that I had never been stronger or more able than when I stayed behind from him in that battle. By God, I had never gathered two camels before that until I gathered them in that battle. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in intense heat, and faced a long journey and deserts, and faced a great enemy. He explained their situation to the Muslims so that they could prepare for their battle, and he informed them of the direction he intended, and the Muslims were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in large numbers, and they were not gathered by a memorizing book - meaning: the register - Kaʿb said: There is no man who wants to be absent except that he thinks that it will be hidden, unless a revelation from God is sent down concerning it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in that battle when the fruits and shade were good, and I was heading towards them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims with him got ready, and I began to go out in order to get ready with them, but I would return without having done anything, and I would say to myself: I am able to do that if I wanted to! This continued to happen to me until the people became serious. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in the morning, and the Muslims were with him, and I had not done anything of my preparation. Then I went out and returned without having done anything. This continued to happen to me until they hurried and the battle was over, and I intended to set out and catch up with them. I wish I had done so! But that was not destined for me. So whenever I went out among the people after the departure of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), it saddened me that I did not see anyone to follow me except a man who was accused of hypocrisy, or a man from among the weak whom God had excused. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. He said while he was sitting with the people in Tabuk: What happened to Kaʿb ibn Malik? A man from Banu Salamah said: O Messenger of God, his cloak and looking at his shoulders held him back! Muʿadh ibn Jabal said: What a bad thing you said! By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing but good about him! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent. While he was like that, he saw a white man with a mirage dissipating behind him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be Abu Khaithamah! And he was Abu Khaithamah Al-Ansari, and he was the one who gave a saʿ of dates in charity, so the hypocrites mocked him. Ka'b said: When I heard that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had set out on his way back from Tabuk, I was overcome with grief, so I began to remember the lie and say: How can I escape his wrath tomorrow? And I sought help in that from every wise man among my family. But when it was said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is about to come!”, falsehood was removed from me, until I knew that I would never escape from it at all, so I decided to tell him the truth. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was returning in the morning. When he returned from a journey, he would start by going to the mosque and pray two rak'ahs in it, then he would sit for the people. When he had done that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to apologize to him and swear to him. They were about eighty-odd men. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) accepted their outward expressions, pledged allegiance to them, asked forgiveness for them, and entrusted their secrets to God. Until I came, and when I had finished, he smiled the smile of someone angry and said: Come! So I came walking until I sat in front of him, and he said to me: What kept you away? Didn't you buy your back? He said: I said: O Messenger of God, by God, if I had sat with anyone other than you from the people of this world, I would have seen that I would escape his wrath with an excuse. I have been given an argument, but by God, I know that if I told you today a lie that would please you, God would soon make you angry with me, and if I told you a truthful story that you would find fault with, I hope for God's forgiveness in it, and by God, I had no excuse! By God, I have never been stronger or more able than when I stayed behind from you! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for this, he has spoken the truth. Get up so that God may decide about you! So I got up, and some men from Banu Salamah rose up and followed me and said: By God, we do not know that you have committed a sin before this! You were unable to apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what those who stayed behind apologized with, for your sin was sufficient for you if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for you! He said: By God, they continued to rebuke me until I wanted to go back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and lie about myself! He said: Then I said to them: Has anyone else encountered this with me? They said: Yes, two men encountered it with you and they said the same as you said, and they were told the same as you were told. I said: Who are they? They said: Murarah ibn Rabi' al-Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi. Then they Surat al-Tawbah 9:118
h
And as for the three who were left behind
, until the earth, vast as it is, became strait for them and their souls became strait for them and they were certain that there is no refuge from God except in Him.
h
Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent

. Indeed, God is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful. mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, and in them I set an example. He said: So I went when they mentioned them to me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, O three, among those who stayed behind. He said: So the people avoided us and changed towards us, until the land became strange to me in my mind, and it was not the land that I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they submitted or sat in their homes weeping, but as for me, I was the youngest and most courageous of the people. I would go out and attend the prayer and go around the markets, and no one would speak to me. I would come to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and greet him while he was sitting after the prayer. I would say to myself: Did he move his lips in return for the greeting or not? Then I would pray with him, and I would glance at him stealthily. When I turned to my prayer, he would look at me, and when I turned towards him, he would turn away from me. When this long period of the Muslims’ coldness had become too much for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of the garden of Abu Qatada, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me, and I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting! I said: O Abu Qatada, I ask you by God, do you know that I love God and His Messenger? He was silent. He said: So I went back and asked him, and he was silent. I went back and asked him, and he said: God and His Messenger know best! My eyes welled up with tears, and I turned away until I climbed over the wall. While I was walking in the market of the city, a Nabataean from the people of Ash-Sham, who had brought food to sell in the city, came and said: Who can point me to Kaʿb ibn Malik? The people began to point him out, until he came to me and gave me a letter from the King of Ghassan, and I was a scribe. I read it, and it said: (As for what follows, it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so come to us and we will console you.) He said: When I read it, I said: This is also a trial!! So I took her to the oven and lit it with it. Then, when forty days of the fifty had passed, and the revelation was delayed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders you to separate from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her, or what should I do? He said: No, rather separate from her and do not come near her. He said: And he sent to my companion about that. He said: So I said to my wife: Go back to your family and stay with them until God decides on this matter. He said: Then the wife of Hilal came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, Hilal ibn Umayyah is an old man who is lost and has no servant. Would you mind if I serve him? He said: No, but he should not come near you! She said: I said: By God, he has no desire for anything! By God, he has not stopped crying since what happened to him until this day! He said: Then one of my family members said to me: Why don’t you ask the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) for permission regarding your wife, since he gave permission to Hilal’s wife to serve him? I said: I will not ask the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) for permission regarding her, and I do not know what he will say to me if I ask his permission regarding her, and I am a young man. Then I stayed for ten nights, and fifty nights were completed for us since the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) forbade us from speaking. He said: Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of fifty nights on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state that God mentioned about us, my soul was constricted and the earth was constricted for me despite its vastness, I heard the voice of a caller, Awfa, on Mount Sala', saying at the top of his voice: O Ka'b bin Malik, be glad! He said: So I fell down in prostration, and I knew that relief had come. He said: And the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) announced God's repentance for us when he prayed the dawn prayer, so the people went to give us the good report, and some of the good report went before my companion, and a man ran to me on a horse, and a runner from Aslam ran before me, and Awfa on the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I heard came to give me the good report, I took off my garment and covered him with it as a sign of his good report, and by God I did not own anything else that day, and I borrowed two garments and put them on, and I went to follow the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). The people met me in groups, congratulating me on my repentance and saying: May God's repentance be blessed for you! Until I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting in the mosque surrounded by people. Talha ibn Ubaydullah ran to me and shook my hand and congratulated me. By God, no man from the Muhajireen got up except him. Ka'b said: So Ka'b would never forget that for Talha. Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, his face shining with joy: Rejoice in the best day that has passed for you since your mother gave birth to you! I said: Is it from you, O Messenger of God, or from God? He said: No, rather it is from God! When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was happy, his face would light up, until his face was like a piece of the moon, and we knew that from him. He said: When I sat before him, I said: O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I give up my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Keep some of your wealth, for it is better for you! I said: Then I will keep my share in Khaybar. I said: O Messenger of God, God saved me because of truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will only speak the truth as long as I live! He said: By God, I have not known anyone among the Muslims whom God has tested with truthfulness since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, better than He tested me. By God, I have not deliberately told a lie since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until this day, and I hope that God will protect me as long as I live. He said: Then God revealed: God has accepted the repentance of the Prophet, until he reached:
h
and the three who were left behind

, until: Fear God and be with the truthful. Ka'b said: By God, God has never bestowed upon me a greater blessing after He guided me to Islam than my truthfulness to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that I would not have lied about him and thus perished as those who lied about him perished. For God said to those who lied, when He sent down the revelation, the worst thing He has ever said to anyone: “They will swear to you by God when you return to them that you will turn away from them. So turn away from them. Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.” Until His saying:
h
He is not pleased with the wicked people

. (al-Tawbah 9:95-96) Ka'b said: We, the three, left behind the matter of those whose repentance the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) accepted when they swore an oath to him, so he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) postponed our matter until God decided on it. So God said about that: And concerning the three who stayed behind, and what God mentioned is not what kept us behind from the conquest, rather it is his leaving us behind, and his postponing our matter from those who swore an oath to him and apologized to him and he accepted from them.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Aqil, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik told me:
m: Abdullah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik - who was Kaʿb’s leader from among his sons when he went blind - said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Malik narrating his story when he stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, and he mentioned something similar.
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I did not stay behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any of the battles he fought except Badr, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik al-Ansari,
m: then al-Salami, on the authority of his father, that his father Abd God ibn Kaʿb - who was the guide of his father Kaʿb when his eyesight was damaged - said: I heard my father Kaʿb ibn Malik narrating his story when he stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, and the story of his two companions. He said: I did not stay behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any battle he fought, except that I stayed behind from him in the Battle of Badr, and then he mentioned something similar.
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik al-Ansari

evidence.text: I read it, and it said: (As for what follows, it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so come to us and we will console you.)
He said: When I read it, I said: This is also a trial!!

x: God Almighty says to the believers, informing them of the path to salvation from His punishment and deliverance from His painful torment: O you who have believed, in God and His Messenger, fear God, and observe Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His limits, and be, in this world, among the people of God’s guardianship and obedience, so that in the Hereafter you will be, with the truthful, in Paradise. Meaning: with those who believe in God, and fulfill His words with their actions, and are not among those who agree with Him, whose words are contradicted by their actions. The meaning of the words is:
h
And be with the truthful
in the Hereafter by fearing God in this world, as God Almighty said:
And whoever obeys God and the Messenger - those will be with those upon whom God has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous

We said: This is the meaning of the statement, because the hypocrite being with the believers is of no benefit to him in any way, unless he does what they do. And if he does what they do, then he is one of them, and if he is one of them, the meaning of the statement should be:
h
Fear God and be with the truthful

. And in order to direct the statement to what we directed in its interpretation, the interpreter of it explained it by saying: Its meaning is: And be with Abu Bakr and Umar, or: with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the emigrants, may God have mercy on them.
Mention of who said that or someone else in its interpretation:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Nafi’,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Fear God and be with the truthful
, he said: with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawayh Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Nafi’, he said:
m: It was said to the three who were left behind: O you who have believed,
h
fear God and be with the truthful
, meaning Muhammad and his companions.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman al-Maharbi, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And be with the truthful

, he said: With Abu Bakr and Umar and their companions, may God have mercy on them. ... He said, Muhammad bin Yahya told us, he said, Ishaq bin Bishr Al-Kahili told us, he said, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim Al-Ramani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding the statement of God:
h
Fear God and be with the truthful
, he said: With Abu Bakr and Umar, may God have mercy on them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Fear God and be with the truthful

, he said: with the truthful emigrants. Ibn Masoud, as was mentioned about him, used to recite it: And be among the truthful, and he interpreted it as a prohibition from God against lying. He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, he said:
m: I heard Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Mas’ud say: Ibn Mas’ud said: Lying is not permissible in seriousness or jest. Read if you wish: (O you who believe, fear God and be among the truthful) - he said: And this is how Ibn Mas’ud read: (among the truthful) - so do you see any concession in lying? ... He said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, he said: I heard Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, something similar. He said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard Abu ʿUbaydah narrating on the authority of ʿAbdullah, he said: Lying is not permissible in seriousness or jest. Read if you wish: (O you who have believed, fear God and be among the truthful) - and it is like that in ʿAbdullah’s reading - so do you see any dispensation for lying?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Lying is not appropriate in jest or in seriousness. Then Abdullah recited: Fear God and be I do not know if he said: among the truthful or with the truthful - and in my book it is with the truthful. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, the same. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, the same.

x: The correct interpretation of this is the interpretation that we mentioned from Nafiʿ and Ad-Dahhak. This is because the scripts of all the Surat al-Tawbah 9:119 O you who have believed, fear God and be with those who are true. copies of the Qur’an agree on:
h
And be with the truthful

, and this is the reading that I do not permit anyone to read differently from it. Abdullah’s interpretation, may God have mercy on him, in this regard, based on his reading, is a correct interpretation, but the reading is different.

evidence.text: Ibn Masoud, as was mentioned about him, used to recite it: And be among the truthful, and he interpreted it as a prohibition from God against lying.

This is because the scripts of all the Surat al-Tawbah 9:119 O you who have believed, fear God and be with those who are true. copies of the Qur’an agree on: And be with the truthful, and this is the reading that I do not permit anyone to read differently from it.
Abdullah’s interpretation, may God have mercy on him, in this regard, based on his reading, is a correct interpretation, but the reading is different.

x: God Almighty says: It was not for the people of Medina, the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those around them of the Bedouins, the inhabitants of the desert, who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, and they were people of faith in him, to stay behind with their families and not have a home, nor to prefer themselves over himself in accompanying him on his journey and fighting with him, and helping him in what he suffered in that battle. He says: This was not for them, because for the sake of them, and because of them, they will not be afflicted in their journey if they were with him, with thirst, which is thirst, nor fatigue, he says: nor exhaustion, nor famine in the way of God, meaning: nor famine in establishing the religion of God and supporting it, and demolishing the beacons of disbelief, nor will they tread a path, meaning: a land, he says: nor will they tread a land, that enrages the disbelievers, their treading it, nor will they gain from the enemy any advantage, he says: nor will they gain from the enemy of God and their enemy anything of their wealth, their lives, and their children, except that God will write for them for all of that, the reward of a righteous deed that He has approved, Indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good, he says: God does not leave a doer of good among His creation who does good in his work and obeys Him in what He commands him, and refrains from what He forbids him, that He will reward him for his goodness, and recompense him for his righteous deed.

Therefore, for those who did that from the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them, what was mentioned in this verse, the reward for everything they did, so the reward for doing that was not lost to them.
The interpreters differed on the ruling of this verse.

Some of them said: It is a ruling, and that was only for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in particular. No one had the right to stay behind if he went on a campaign and sit out, except for those who had an excuse. As for other imams and governors, then whoever among the believers wanted to stay behind him, if the Muslims did not need him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It is not for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to stay behind the Messenger of God or to prefer themselves over him, this is if the Prophet of God goes out to fight himself, so no one has the right to stay behind. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Were it not that it would be too hard for my nation, I would not stay behind a raiding party that goes out to fight in the cause of God, but I do not find the means, so I set out with them, and it is hard for me - or I hate it - to leave them behind me.”

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us,
m: I heard Al-Awza’i, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, Al-Fazari, Al-Subai’i, Ibn Jabir, and Saeed bin Abdul Aziz say about this verse: It is not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God, to the end of the verse, that it is for the first and last of this nation of those who strive in the way of God.

x: Others said: This verse was revealed when the Muslims were few in number, but when they increased in number, God abrogated it and permitted whoever wanted to stay behind, saying: And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once (al-Tawbah 9:122).
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
It was not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God

, and he recited until he reached: That God may reward them with the best of what they used to do, he said: This was when Islam was little. Then when Islam became more numerous, he said: “And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth” (al-Tawbah 9:122), to the end of the verse.

x: The correct statement in my opinion is that God meant by it those whom He described in His statement:
h
And those who had excuses came from among the desert Arabs

, that permission might be given to them (al-Tawbah 9:90). Then He, the Most High, said: It was not for the people of Madinah, who Surat al-Tawbah 9:120 It is not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God or to prefer themselves over him. That is because they suffer neither thirst nor fatigue nor hunger in the cause of God, nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers nor do they gain any benefit from the enemy. They will not be given anything except that a righteous deed will be recorded for them. Indeed, God does not allow the reward of the righteous to be lost. stayed behind from the Messenger of God, nor for those around them from the desert Arabs who sat back from jihad with him, to stay behind him, nor to prefer themselves over him.

This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had urged in that expedition of his, everyone who was able to set out with him, except for those whom he had given permission to, or ordered to stay behind him. So it was not for those who were able to set out to stay behind. So He, the Most High, enumerated those who stayed behind, and revealed the hypocrisy of those whose stay behind was hypocrisy, and excused those whose stay behind was for an excuse, and accepted the repentance of those whose stay behind was negligence, without doubt or suspicion in the matter of God, as they repented from the error of what they had done. As for staying behind him when he is independent, it is not forbidden, if it is not due to his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliking it. This is also the ruling of Muslims today regarding their Imam. It is not obligatory for all of them to rise with him, except when he needs them, because Islam and its people must have their presence, their gathering, and his mobilization of them, and in that case they must obey him.

If this is the meaning of the verse, then neither of the two verses we mentioned abrogates the other, since neither of them negates the ruling of the other in all its aspects, and no report came that directs the argument that one of them abrogates the other. We have explained the meaning of al-mukhmasa and that it is famine, with evidence for it, and we have mentioned the narration of someone who said that in a place other than this, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. As for (al-Nil), it is a noun derived from the saying: (naalni yanalni), and (nalt al-shay fawwa munil). This is if you get it with your hand, and not from (at-ta’al). This is because (at-ta’al)) is derived from (an-nawal), from which it is said: (nalt lahu, anul lahu), from the gift.

Some scholars of Arabic speech used to say: An-Nil is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: He granted me good, he grants me good, and He granted me good, he granted me good. He said: It is as if An-Nil is from the waw, and was replaced with a ya’ because of its lightness and the heaviness of the waw. This is not known in Arabic speech, rather it is the custom of the Arabs to correct the waw of words with a waw, if it is quiescent and what precedes it is open, like their saying: Al-Qawl, “Al-‘Ul,” and Al-Hawl. If what he said were permissible, then Al-Qail would be permissible.

God Almighty says: That is because they are not afflicted by thirst, and all that is mentioned, nor do they attain any attainment from the enemy, and nor do they spend a small or large expenditure, in the way of God, nor do they cross, with the Messenger of God in his conquest, a valley, except that the reward for their work is written for them, as a reward for it, like the best reward they receive for the best of their deeds that they used to do while they were residing in their homes, like:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they do not spend a small amount or a large amount
, the verse, he said: No people increase in distance from their families in the way of God except that they increase in closeness to God.

x: God Almighty says: And the believers should not go forth all together. We have explained the meaning of all with its evidence and the statements of the people of interpretation regarding it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning that God meant in this verse, and what is the group that He disliked for all believers.

Some of them said: They were a group of people who were in the desert. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them to teach people Islam. When the verse was revealed: It is not for the people of Madinah and the bedouins around them to stay behind the Messenger of God (al-Tawbah 9:120), they left the desert to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fearing that they would be among those who stayed behind and among those meant by the verse. So God revealed an excuse for them in His saying:
h
It is not for the believers to go forth all at once
, and He disliked that all of them should leave the desert for Madinah.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once

. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth?” He said: Some of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out into the deserts, and they found favor among the people, and some of the fertile land from which they benefited, and they called whomever they found of the people to guidance. Then the people said to them: We see that you have left your companions and come to us! So they felt uncomfortable about that, and they all came from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God said: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth, seeking good, that they may understand, and hear what is in the people and what God revealed after them, and that they may warn their people, all the people, when they return to them that they may beware.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said in his hadith: Then God said: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth, some went out, and some stayed, seeking good. ... He said, Ishaq told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similar to his hadith on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similar to the hadith of Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah, except that he said in his hadith: We do not see you except that you have abandoned your companion! And he said: So that they may learn, so that they may hear what is in the people.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: The believers would not all go out to their enemy and leave their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once

, he said: They should all go, so why did not a group from every tribe and community go forth, and a group stay behind, that they may gain understanding in the religion, so that those who stayed behind might gain understanding in the religion with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and so that those who stayed behind might warn those who went forth when they returned to them so that they might beware.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, meaning: The believers would not go forth all together and leave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone. Why should not a party from every division of them go forth, meaning a group, meaning the raiding parties, and not set out except with his permission? Then when the raiding parties returned and the Qur’an was revealed after them, those who stayed behind would learn it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They would say: God has sent down a Qur’an to your Prophet after you, and we have learned it. So the raiding parties would remain learning what God had sent down to their Prophet after them, and other raiding parties would be sent out. That is what His statement,
h
That they may gain understanding in religion
, means that they should learn what God had sent down to His Prophet, and that they should know the raiding parties when they returned to them so that they might beware.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, to his statement: that they may beware, he said: This is when the Prophet of God sends out armies, he orders them not to disgrace his Prophet, and a group stays with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to gain understanding of the religion, and a group sets out to call their people and warn them of the events of God with those who came before them.

c: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said,
m: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about the verse:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, the verse, when the Prophet of God went out on a campaign by himself, it was not permissible for any of the Muslims to stay behind him, except those who had an excuse. And when he stayed and the troops were taken prisoner, it was not permissible for them to set out except with his permission. So when a man was taken prisoner and the Qur’an was revealed after him, the Prophet of God would recite it to his companions who were sitting with him. Then when the troops returned, those who had stayed with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say to them: Indeed, God has sent down after you a Qur’an to His Prophet, so they would recite to them and instruct them in the religion, and this is His statement:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, meaning: when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stayed, why should not a party from every division of them go forth, meaning that it is not appropriate for the Muslims to go forth all together while the Prophet of God was sitting, but when the Prophet of God sat, the troops would go forth and most of the people would sit with him.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: These people who went out are not believers. If they were believers, not all of them would have gone out, but they are hypocrites. If they were truthful that they were believers, some of them would have gone out to learn about the religion and warn their people when they returned to them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the statement of
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, is not about jihad, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for years of drought against Mudar, their land became barren, and the tribe among them would come in its entirety until they settled in Madinah out of hardship, and they would claim Islam while they were lying, so they made things difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and exhausted them, and God revealed informing the Messenger of God that they were not believers, so the Messenger of God returned them to their clans, and warned their people not to do what they did, so that is what His statement is: And that they may warn their people when they return to them that they may beware. A third statement was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, until His statement: that they may beware, he said: A group would set out from every tribe of the Arabs and come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him about what they wanted from their religion, and learn about their religion, and say to the Prophet of God: What do you command us to do, and tell us what we should say about our rituals when we go to them? He said: The Prophet of God would command them to obey God and obey His Messenger, and would send them to their people with prayer and zakat. And when they came to their people, they would call out: Whoever accepts Islam is one of us, and they would warn them, so that a man would recognize his father and mother. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would inform them and they would warn their people. So when they returned to them, they would call them to Islam, and warn them of the Fire, and give them good tidings of Paradise.

x: Others said: This is only a denial from God to the hypocrites who caused harm to the Arab Muslims and others, by their failure to oppose the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are among those whom God has excused for Surat al-Tawbah 9:122
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once
. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth to gain understanding in religion and to warn their people when they return to them that they may beware? failing to follow.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed: It is not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God, to Indeed, God does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost (al-Tawbah 9:120), some of the hypocrites said: He who stayed behind is doomed! So this verse was revealed:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together
, to that they may beware, and this verse was revealed: And those who dispute about God after He has been answered - their argument is worthless, (al-Shura 42:16).

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, who said, Sulayman Al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: I heard him say: When the verse was revealed: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment (al-Tawbah 9:39), It is not for the people of Madinah and the bedouins around them to His saying: That God may reward them with the best of what they used to do (al-Tawbah 9:120), the hypocrites said: The Bedouins who stayed behind from Muhammad and did not go forth with him are destroyed!

x: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the Bedouins, to their people to teach them, so God revealed: “
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once

. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth” to His saying: that they may beware? And the verse was revealed: And those who dispute about God after He has been answered (al-Shura 42:16), the verse.
Those who said: “He meant by that the prohibition of everyone going out on a secret mission, and leaving the Prophet, peace be upon him, alone,” differed regarding the two meanings of his saying:
h
So that they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them

Some of them said: He meant the group that stayed behind with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Why don’t a group from each group go forth for jihad, so that those who stayed behind may gain an understanding of the religion and warn their people who went forth in the secret mission when they return to them from their raid?
This is the statement of Qatada, and we have mentioned the narration of that from him, from the narration of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, and:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth to gain understanding in religion? He said: So that those who stayed with the Prophet of God might gain understanding, and warn their people when they return to them. He said: So that they might warn those who had gone out when they returned to them.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatada:
m: h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together
, they said: All together and call upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So that the estranged group may learn more than the one that remains behind, and the estranged group may beware of the one that remains behind.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
