m: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth to gain understanding in religion? He said: So that those who went out might gain understanding, with what God shows them of victory over the polytheists and support, and warn their people when they return to them.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is that it is interpreted as: The believers would not go forth all together and leave the Messenger of God alone. God forbade the believers in Him by this verse from going forth in conquest, jihad, or other matters of theirs, and leaving the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone. But when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out on a military expedition, they should set forth with it a group from each tribe of the Arabs - which is the division - a party, and that is from one to whatever number it reached, as God, may His praise be exalted, said: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth? He says: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth? And this is up to here, according to one of the opinions narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, which is the opinion of Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah.

Rather, we said: This statement is the most correct statement in that regard, because God Almighty mentioned that He forbade the believers in Him from the people of Medina, the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the Bedouins, to stay behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except for an excuse that they can excuse, if the Messenger of God went out to raid and fight an enemy before this verse by saying: It is not for the people of Medina and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God (al-Tawbah 9:120), then He, may His praise be glorified, followed that by saying:
h
And it is not for the believers to go forth all together

, so that was known, since He had informed them in the verse before it of what was required of them from the obligation of going forth, and what was permissible for them to leave it in the case of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raiding and leaving his city to fight an enemy, and He informed them that they were not permitted to stay behind him except for an excuse, after he had mobilized some of them and left some of them behind, that after informing them of that, they should inform them of what is obligatory upon them when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in his city, and others leave it, just as the beginning was with informing them.
The duty is upon its people and some of them are left behind. As for his statement:
h
That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them

, the most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of the one who said: That the rebellious group may gain understanding of what they witness of God’s victory for the people of His religion and the companions of His Messenger over the people of His enmity and disbelief in Him, so that he may gain understanding from his witnessing of the true knowledge of the matter of Islam and its victory over the religions, for he who did not have understanding, and that they may warn their people and warn them lest the punishment of God befall them like that which befell those whom the Muslims had witnessed and witnessed from the people of polytheism - if they returned to them from their invasion - that they may beware, he says: Perhaps their people, if they warn them of what they have witnessed of that, may beware and believe in God and His Messenger, fearing that what befell those whose report they were informed of may befall them.

We said that this is the most correct statement, and it is the statement of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that we narrated from him, because we have previously explained that if nafar is absolute and not connected to anything, then the majority of the Arabs use it in jihad and conquest. So if this is the majority of its meanings, and the Most High said: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth to gain understanding in the religion, then it is known that his statement: to gain understanding is a condition for the nafar and not for anything else, since it follows it and not any other statement.
What do you deny that its meaning is: So that those who are left behind may gain understanding of the religion?

We deny that because it is impossible. That is because if the departure of the departing group was a reason for the remaining group to gain knowledge, then their stay with them must be a reason for their ignorance and abandonment of knowledge. And we know that if their stay had remained and not departed, it would not have been a reason to prevent them from gaining knowledge. And then, He, the Most High, said: And that they may warn their people when they return to them, in conjunction with His statement:
h
That they may gain understanding in religion
. There is no doubt that the fleeing group did not flee except after the warning had come from God to them, and for the warning and fear of the threat they fled.

So what is the reason for the group that stayed behind warning the fleeing group, when they were equal in their knowledge of God’s warning to them? If it were permissible for one of them to be described as warning the other, then the more deserving of being described as such would be the fleeing group, because it had witnessed of God’s power and the victory of the believers over the people of disbelief in Him, what the resident group had not witnessed. But that, God willing, as we have said, is that it warns from its neighborhood and tribe those who do not believe in God when it returns to Him: that what was sent down to those it witnessed from those whom God gave victory to the believers from among their peers from the people of polytheism would be sent down to them.

evidence.text: So when a man was taken prisoner and the Qur’an was revealed after him, the Prophet of God would recite it to his companions who were sitting with him.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: O you who believe in God and His Messenger, fight those of the disbelievers who are your allies, not those who are farther away from them. He says to them: Start by fighting those who are closest to you in residence, then those who are farther away from them. And those who were next to those addressed by this verse at that time were the Romans, because they were the inhabitants of the Levant at that time, and the Levant was closer to Medina than Iraq. But after God opened the lands to the believers, it became obligatory upon the people of every region to fight those of the enemies who are their allies, not those who are farther away from them, unless the people of another region of the lands of Islam were forced to do so. If they were forced to do so, then they were obligated to aid and support them, because the Muslims are one hand against all others.
And since this is true, everyone who interpreted this verse interpreted it to mean that it is obligatory for the people of every region to fight those enemies who are their allies.
He mentioned the narration about them:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Shabib bin Gharqadah al-Barqi, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, he said,
m: I asked Ibn Omar about fighting the Daylamites, he said: Fight the Romans! Ibn Bashar, Ahmad ibn Ishaq, and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you
, he said: the Daylamites.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: That when he was asked about fighting the Romans and the Daylamites, he would recite this verse:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, Imran my brother told us:
m: I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, saying: What do you think about fighting the Daylamites? He said: Fight them and remain steadfast with them, for they are among those about whom God said:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: that he was asked about the Levant and Daylam, and he said:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you
, the Daylam.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said,
m: I heard Abu Amr and Saeed bin Abdul Aziz say: Every people should guard their strongholds and fortresses, and they interpret the words of God:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you

, he said: Those who were near them of the disbelievers were the Arabs, so he fought them until he finished with them. Then when he finished, God said: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, until he reached, while they are humbled (al-Tawbah 9:29). He said: Then when he finished fighting those of the Arabs who were near him, He ordered him to fight the People of the Book. He said: And fighting them is the best jihad in the sight of God. As for his statement:
h
And that they may find in you harshness

, its meaning is: And that these infidels whom you are fighting may find in you, that is, from you, harshness towards them. And know that God is with the righteous, meaning: And be certain, when you fight them, that God is with you, and He is your supporter against them. If you fear God and are in awe of Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, then God is the supporter and helper of whoever fears Him.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That when he was asked about fighting the Romans and the Daylamites, he would recite this verse: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you.

x: God Almighty says: And when God sends down a surah from the surahs of the Qur'an to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then among these hypocrites whom God mentioned in this surah is one who says: O people, which of you has this surah increased in faith? He says: Belief in God and His verses. God says: But as for those who believed, of those to whom this was said, it increased them, the surah that was revealed, in faith, and they rejoice in what God has given them of faith and certainty.
Is not faith in the speech of the Arabs belief and acknowledgment?
Yes!
How did the Surah increase their belief and acknowledgement?

It increased their faith when it was revealed, because before the Surah was revealed, they were not required to affirm it and act upon it exactly, except in the context of their belief that everything that their Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought to them was from God and was true. So when God revealed the Surah, they were required to affirm it exactly was from God, and they were required to believe in what it contained of God’s rulings, limits, and obligations. So that was the increase that the Surah increased in them when it was revealed in terms of faith and belief in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And when a surah is revealed
, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ He said: When a surah was revealed, they believed in it, so God increased their faith and belief, and they were happy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So it increased them in faith
, he said: fear.

x: God Almighty says: And as for those in whose hearts is disease, hypocrisy and doubt in the religion of God, then the Surah that was revealed,
h
It increased their filth upon their filth

, and that is because they doubted that it was from God, so they did not believe in it and did not confirm it, so that was an increase in doubt that occurred in the revelation of God, and it obligated them to believe in it upon them, rather they doubted that, so that was an increase in the filth of their actions, in addition to what preceded from them of filth and hypocrisy. And that is the meaning of His statement:
h
It increased their filth upon their filth
, "and they died," meaning: these hypocrites were destroyed, "while they were disbelievers," meaning: while they were disbelievers in God and His signs.
There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement:
h
Or do they not see
? So the general reading of the regions is:
h
Or do they not see

, with the letter ya meaning: Or do these people in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy not see? Hamza read it as: Or do you not see, with a ta, meaning: Or do you not see, O believers, that they are being tested?

The correct reading for us in this regard is the letter ya, as a form of rebuke from God to them, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters of the regions on it, and the correctness of its meaning. So the interpretation of the statement is: Do these hypocrites not see that God tests them once or twice every year, meaning that He tests them once in some years, and twice in others, and then they do not repent, meaning: Then they, with the affliction that befalls them from God, and the test that is presented to them, do not repent from their hypocrisy, nor do they repent from their disbelief, nor do they remember what they see of God’s proofs and witness of His signs, so that they learn from them, but they persist in their hypocrisy?
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the trial that God mentioned in this place, that these hypocrites will be tempted by it.
Some of them said: This is God’s test of them with famine and hardship.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice
? He said: by famine and hunger.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: They are tested, he said: They are tested, once or twice every year, he said: With famine and hunger.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice
? He said: They are tested with torment every year once or twice.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They are tested once or twice every year
, he said: by famine and hunger.

x: Others said: Rather, it means that they are tested by conquest and jihad.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice
? He said: They are tested by fighting in the way of God every year once or twice.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is that they are tested by the lies that the polytheists spread about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and that those in whose hearts is disease are tempted by that.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Hudhayfah:
m: h
Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice
? He said: We used to hear every year a lie or two, and because of them many groups of people would go astray.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said:
m: They used to tell one or two lies every year.

x: The most correct of the sayings about this is that it is said that God was amazed by these hypocrites among His believing servants, and He rebuked the hypocrites in themselves for their little remembrance and their poor awareness of the admonitions of God with which He admonishes them. It is possible that these admonitions are the hardships that He inflicts upon them of hunger and famine, and it is possible that they are what He shows them of the victory of His Messenger over the disbelievers in Him, and He provides for him from the manifestation of His word over their word, and it is possible that they are what appears to the Muslims of their hypocrisy and the evil of their inner selves, by their inclination to what they hear of the rumours of the polytheists about the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and his companions. There is no report that necessitates the correctness of some of this and not others, from the aspect that must be accepted.
And there is no saying about this that is more correct than accepting the apparent meaning of God’s statement, which is: Do they not see that
h
they are tested once or twice every year
with something that will deter them, then they are not deterred nor take heed?

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: Or do they not see?
So the general reading of the regions is: Or do they not see, with the letter ya meaning: Or do these people in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy not see?
Hamza read it as: Or do you not see, with a ta, meaning: Or do you not see, O believers, that they are being tested?

Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading for us in this regard is the letter ya, as a form of rebuke from God to them, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters of the regions on it, and the correctness of its meaning.

x: God Almighty says:
h
And when a surah is revealed

from the Qur'an, in which there is a fault of these hypocrites whom God Almighty described in this surah, and they are with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they look at each other and argue, Does anyone see you? If you speak or whisper about the faults of the people, he will tell them about them, then they stand up and leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not listen to the recitation of the surah in which there are their faults. Then God Almighty began His statement:
h
God has turned their hearts away

, and He said: God has turned the hearts of these hypocrites away from goodness, success, and belief in God and His Messenger, that is because they are a people who do not understand, meaning: God did this disappointment to them, and turned their hearts away from goodness, because they are a people who do not understand the admonitions of God, out of arrogance and hypocrisy.
The Arabs differed about the interrogative letter al-jalb.

Some of the Basra grammarians said: They looked at each other, ‘Does anyone see you?’ It is as if he said: They said to each other, because their looking in this place was a gesture, and something similar to it, and God knows best. Some grammarians of Kufa said: It is:
h
And when a surah is revealed

, some of them say to each other: Does anyone see you? Another of them said: This contemplation does not mean speech, but it is the contemplation that brings about the question, like the Arabs’ saying: They debated over which of them is more knowledgeable, and They gathered to see which of them is more knowledgeable, meaning: they gathered to see, so this is what brings about the question.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Do not say: We have finished the prayer, for some people have finished and
h
God has turned their hearts away

, but say: We have completed the prayer. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Umair bin Tamim al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say: We have turned away from the prayer, for some people turned away and God turned their hearts away. ... He said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say: We have finished the prayer, for some people have finished and
h
God has turned their hearts away
. Rather, say: We have completed the prayer.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when a surah is revealed
, they look at one another, the verse, he said: They are the hypocrites. Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: “
h
And when a surah is revealed

, they look at one another: ‘Does anyone see you?’” Who heard your report? Did anyone see you? Did anyone tell him? When something is revealed, he tells about their speech. He said: They are the hypocrites. He said: And he recited: “
h
And when a surah is revealed

, some of them say: ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’” (al-Tawbah 9:120), until he reached: “They look at one another: ‘Does anyone see you?’” He told him about this? Was anyone with you? Did anyone hear your speech and tell him about this?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Do not say: We have turned away from the prayer, for God reproached a people and said: They turned away, God turned away their hearts, but say: We have prayed.

evidence.text: If you speak or whisper about the faults of the people, he will tell them about them, then they stand up and leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not listen to the recitation of the surah in which there are their faults.

x: God Almighty says to the Arabs: O people, the Messenger of God has come to you, from yourselves, you know him, not from someone else, so that you would accuse him of giving you advice. He is concerned about your suffering, meaning: He is concerned about your suffering, which is the hardship, dislike, and harm that will come upon them. He is anxious about you, meaning: He is anxious about guiding you from your misguidance, your repentance, and your return to the truth. He is kind to the believers, meaning: He is gentle, He is merciful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves
. Grievous to him is what you suffer,” he said: He was not afflicted with any polytheism in his birth.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Muhammad,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves
, he said: He was not affected by any of the births of the Age of Ignorance. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I came from marriage, not from fornication.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves

. Grievous to him is what you suffer,” he said: God made him from among themselves, so they should not envy him for what God gave him of prophethood and honor. As for his saying: He is concerned about what you suffer, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said: It means: You have not gone astray.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Talq bin Ghannam told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: He is distressed by what you suffer, he said: what you have gone astray.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He is concerned about the suffering of your believer.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He is concerned about your suffering, he is concerned about the suffering of their believers.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of Ibn Abbas. This is because God made the report about the Prophet of God general, that he was concerned about what his people suffered, and did not specify the people of faith in him. So, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the report came from God, he was concerned about what all of them suffered.

How can it be permissible to describe the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as having been dear to them all, while he kills their infidels, mistreats their children, and steals their money?

Their Islam, if they had converted, would have been more beloved to him than their remaining in their disbelief and denial of him, until they deserved that from God. And God Almighty described him as being grievous to Him about their suffering, because it was grievous to Him that they should do what would grievance them, and that is that they should go astray and deserve grievance from God through killing and captivity. As for what in his statement: what you suffered, it was raised by his statement: difficult for him, because the meaning of the statement is what I mentioned: your suffering is difficult for him. As for his saying:
h
He is concerned about you
, its meaning is what I have explained, and it is the saying of the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He is concerned about you
, he is concerned about their lost one, that God guides him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: He is anxious for you, he said: He is anxious for those who have not converted to Islam to convert to Islam.

x: God Almighty says: If, O Muhammad, those of your people whom you have brought the truth from your Lord turn away, and they turn away from you and do not accept what you have brought them of advice in God, and what you have called them to of light and guidance, then say, ‘God is sufficient for me,’ my Lord is sufficient for me, there is no god but Him,’ “there is no god but Him, ‘in Him I have put my trust, in Him I have relied, and upon His help I have relied, and upon Him and His victory I have relied, for He is my helper and supporter against those who have opposed me and turned away from me from among you and others among the people, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, who owns everything below Him, and all the kings are His slaves and servants. Rather, by describing Himself as Lord of the Mighty Throne, He meant to inform us that all those below Him are His servants and are in His kingdom and authority, because the Mighty Throne was only for kings.

So He described Himself as the Possessor of the Throne to the exclusion of all of His creation, and that He is the Mighty King to the exclusion of others, and that those below Him in His kingdom and authority are subject to His judgment and decree.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
But if they turn away

, then say, ‘Sufficient for me is God,’ meaning the disbelievers, they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And this is about the believers. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, he said: Umar, may God have mercy on him, would not record a verse in the Qur’an until two men testified. Then a man from the Ansar came with these two verses: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. It is grievous to him.” Umar said: I will never ask you for proof for them. That is how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih Al-Hanafi, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is Merciful and loves every merciful person. He places His mercy on every merciful person. They said: O Messenger of God, are we merciful to ourselves and our wealth - he said: And I think he said: And our wives -? He said: Not like that, but be as God said: ‘There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
h
But if they turn away
, then say: God is sufficient for me. There is no god but He. In Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.’ I think he recited this entire verse.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd al-Samad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, he said:
m: The last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer,” to the end of the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of my father, he said:
m: The last verse revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf Mihran, on the authority of my father, he said:
m: The two most recent verses of the Qur’an that God revealed are: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer,” to the end of the two verses.

c: Abu Kuraib told me, he said, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abaan bin Yazid al-Attar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, he said:
m: The most recent covenant of the Qur’an with God is the two verses: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, to the end of the surah. The last interpretation of Surat At-Tawbah

evidence.text: I think he recited this entire verse.”
